[h2] Unpacking will be dear to my heart for years to come, and is easily my GOTY 2021 choice, if not my Favorite Game of All Time.[/h2] Unpacking is a wonderfully approachable experience with a story to tell that is highly thoughtful, without ever telling us a word about the life that is unfolding before us. On the surface, it is not a complex game, as all we are doing is clicking and unpacking our boxes and placing items. But underneath it, you will find a very personal story and a world that gradually becomes ours.

Unpacking is disguised as a puzzle game, but this game is fundamentally about growing up as it invites you to explore and fall in love with the constantly evolving narrative that is life; from the fears of the unknown, the hardships of our struggles, and the joys of intimacy.

We see that our character loves art, she loves reading, she loves video games, she loves physical activities. As we get to grow up with her, the objects that she leaves behind, the ones she gains, new hobbies and interests picked up and the rooms that she inhabits; tells us something different if you are willing to read between the lines, as it will give you moments of delight to genuine surprise and sadness. The intimacy she has with her possessions lets us understand how much love and care she has for them, even when they get wear and tear from the stresses of age and the impact they had in different parts of her life.

We don't get to see anyone, all we ever do is place items with each new move. There are small interactions to be had with all the objects if you can find them, from sweet bops to era-appropriate styles and references in abundance at the height of their time. There is nostalgia to be had for everyone who grew up in the 90s, and there is both heartache and joy to be had for those who can relate. 

When I look around my home and see the many items and trinkets that I have carried with me throughout the years, it was mostly because they held a story to me. They tell of the places I have been, the people that I have met, what kind of person I am, they are the memories I want to remember forever. I have lost many things to time, to indifference, to pain; and looking back on them now, it makes me feel silly and melancholic that they aren't here today. Years from now when we drift apart or most of us get lost to the ages, those memories will always be a part of my life, and the new ones that will grow in their place will have something different to tell. It is a story that we are constantly living and constantly telling, it is part of our lives and is continually growing up alongside us. 

As we explore together with our character and see her build a life up from the first trophy to the last triumph; Unpacking wants us to think about the way we live, the decisions that affect us, and the hopes and dreams we carry for the future.

Even if our stories had a happy or sad beginnings, what is lost can't be taken back, but what matters in this moment is right now; because the love and memories we create together still matter long after we are all gone.

尽管利用物品和空间场景的变换来进行叙事的做法在解谜游戏中已然屡见不鲜，但本作贴近生活的选材还是让人眼前一亮，而其赛博搬家的摆放体验同样也能让现实生活中的懒人（比如我）能够畅快地进行解压。

从主角青少年时期至大学期间的居家摆设来看，她大抵是一位热爱绘画、运动、手办和电子游戏（后来还增加了缝纫和尤克里里）的酷姐们，尤其是场景三的物品摆设和关卡结算时的自述，使人由衷地羡慕她对自己所热爱的事物的无限精力与热忱。

然而，这一切关于未来和生活的美好畅想，在场景四中遭遇了一次短暂的阻滞。新识的男友显然是一个自我中心十足的人，这可以从他的家居预陈设中略窥端倪——除了在客厅摆了一堆健身器材和音乐相关的场景物品外，主角随身携带的个人爱好相关物品（游戏机、手柄、微缩建筑、手办、绘画本和绘画工具等）只能被随意地安置在空余的边缘地带，而主角引以为豪的奖状则被轻视地塞到了床下；客厅挂着的艺术品只有新男友自己感兴趣的乐队相关海报，而主角之前家中的挂画则连影子都没有。这让我不由得想到了同样有着自己的数位板、热爱绘画的爱人，倘若一段感情连最基本的尊重和交流都不存在，那么这样的关系又有什么值得维持的必要呢？

好在之后的数幕场景中，摆脱了前男友的主角如愿以偿地走上了她一直以来期望的艺术道路，也找到了属于自己的幸福；而她和她的另一半同等地尊重彼此的兴趣爱好（这体现在空间关系中），这种基于交换彼此的独特体验所带来的情感联系，使得她们的生活空间变得愈加闪闪发光，也使得她们在各自的志趣上日趋纯粹。

游玩本作的过程中种种尝试摆放物品的体验，以及这些体验背后所蕴藏着的、关于主角的思绪，令个人不由得回想起了这些年来漂泊在外、和爱人从异地发展到共居的点点滴滴，可谓是触景生情。希望时过境迁，纵使多年过后世事变迁，我也能和爱人始终维持着这份类似游戏后半部分的、纯粹的情感关系，也能永远保持对生活和爱好一如既往的热枕。

Медитативный, монотонный геймплей ни разу не заставил меня заскучать, ведь игра умудрялась рассказать историю, посредством предметов, а желание закончить ещё одну комнату всегда побеждало над желанием выйти из игры или пойти спать. Пусть история и не была глубокой или проработанной, - она в принципе была довольно поверхностной, но за жизнью главной героини было интересно наблюдать. Приятно смотреть, как из маленькой девочки она превращалась во взрослую женщину, как детское хобби переросло в любимое дело и как строилась новая семья. 

Я совсем не фанат пиксельной графики, но и не брезгую ею, если игра мне действительно интересна. Здесь же пиксели совсем не режут глаза, а придают игре особую притягательную стилистику. Все предметы прекрасно отрисованы и почти сразу становится понятно, что за вещь ты взял и в какую из комнат её необходимо положить (а ведь этот аспект очень важен, на нём строится весь геймплей).
Всё это действие сопровождается приятной, ненавязчивой музыкой. Она мне не запомнилась, но и выключать её посреди игры у меня желания не возникло. 

В итоге разработчикам Unpacking удалось собрать поистине интересный и затягивающий симулятор, в котором приятно провести вечер, когда нужно дать отдохнуть мозгу и просто приятно провести время, не напрягая нервы. Любители выполнять все достижения тоже будут довольны: все они получаются легко и быстро, что не может не радовать. К совсем уже натянутым минусам я могу отнести лишь отсутствие реиграбельности (или же мастерской, к примеру). Но опять же, свою цену игра отрабатывает полностью, что не может не радовать. В итоге имеем приятную казуальную инди на пару часов и однозначную положительную рекомендацию от меня.

[h1]Le jeu[/h1]

Au travers de différents déménagements, grâce à ses objets, on suit la vie de quelqu'un pendant plusieurs années.

Le gameplay est simple, on clique sur un carton pour en sortir un objet, et on le pose où on veut dans la maison. Bon, évidemment, quand tous les cartons sont déballés, si vous avez placé le micro-onde dans la chambre et laisser traîner des chaussettes dans le salon, le jeu ne vous permet pas de continuer au niveau suivant.

Le jeu est entièrement en pixel art, ma foi très convaincant. On peut placer les objets dans des d'autres, ou bien dans les placards, les tourner sur eux-même, ... aucun problème le jeu le gère. Il y a de petits trucs amusants avec quelques objets, 
c'est vraiment bien fait. La musique est tantôt entraînante, tantôt nostalgique, toujours adaptée à la situation. Par contre, parfois elle se coupe, je n'ai pas vraiment bien compris les conditions pour ça.

Si le jeu peut sembler un peu court (environ 5h en prenant le temps), je pense que c'est la bonne durée au vu du gameplay très basique et de l'histoire qui est racontée :).

[h1]Rejouabilité, achievements[/h1]

Si vous aurez probablement une majorité d'achievements juste en terminant le jeu normalement, puis en regardant les noms et les formes des stickers, quelques uns sont un peu plus tricky, il n'est pas toujours évident de deviner quoi faire. Il est possible de revenir dans les niveaux quand on veut pour les faire cela dit, pas besoin de relancer une partie.

[h1]En bref[/h1]

Très bon story telling avec un gameplay plutôt inhabituel. J'ai apprécié.

[h1]GNU/Linux[/h1]

Aucun problème rencontré, le jeu tourne au poil.

A very cathartic experience based on the simple concept of unpacking boxes and arranging the unpacked items around rooms. The music, charming pixel graphics, satisfying grid placements, and silent storytelling are what makes this game really enjoyable. You'll probably like this even more if you're a perfectionist who wants everything to be in its "ideal" place. I found myself moving items all over the apartments/houses to fit my aesthetic, which is probably why I have a longer game time then most.

The only gripe I really have is that I kinda wished the items had names. It took me awhile to figure out that an electrical box with a circle on it was actually a GameCube rather than some sort of portable cooker, and that a board with a pen next to it was actually a fridge whiteboard and not some sort of drawing tablet (since the protagonist is a designer). But at least the game tells you if the item is placed in the wrong location!

All in all, while I did get the game at 40% off, the full price doesn't really bother me for the 10hrs of gameplay I got out of it. Bear in mind that the game was made by a small indie developer, and Unpacking is only its 2nd ever game. But if you're someone who just wants to "complete" the game without caring too much about aesthetics, then maybe wait for a sale before getting this game.

PS: While the game does look like it has the perfect blueprint for Steam Workshop and DLCs, the devs have stated that they're done with this game. So keep that in mind if you're hoping for additional content.

[quote] One of the most unique games of 2021, Unpacking is a masterclass in environmental storytelling, recommended to anyone looking to unwind and relax a bit. [/quote]

Before getting into the review, I want you to take a look around you. Bask in your scenery. Admire the stack of papers sitting on your desk, or your childhood photos decorating your shelf. Perhaps you even have a few souvenirs around your office or room that you can look at. Now, instead of just looking at it, really think about the object. Analyze it. Pick it up if you must. And now, answer me this: what memories come to mind when you think about said object?

The truth is, we are surrounded by our own history. Everything we own has a story to tell. Sometimes, it’s not very interesting, but most often, it is significant. Now picture an entire game where you explore this concept, learning the story behind a whole life just from a person’s belongings. That is the premise behind Unpacking, and I think it’s safe to say that the game does a wonderful job at achieving it with [b]very cute graphics, nice gameplay and an incredible display of environmental storytelling [/b], which will be the focus of this review as it’s easily this game’s strongest asset (at least in my opinion). Now time to get into it, as there’s lots to unpack (heh)!

—------------------

[b]Just a quick note: this review is spoiler free![/b]

“Part block-fitting puzzle, part home decoration, you are invited to create a satisfying living space while learning clues about the life you’re unpacking”. This is part of the description taken directly from Unpacking’s steam page, and it is pretty much as accurate at describing the experience as a single sentence can possibly be.

Your task in this game is simple: unpacking the unnamed main character’s belongings after she moves to a different place. To accomplish that, [b]you click boxes, get items out and store them away.[/b] At the end of a “level”, items that are outside of a proper location (for example, if you decide that the floor in front of the toilet is a great location for your toothbrush) are marked with a blinking red outline. You then have to move stuff around and find space for the object in the correct location. This is the “puzzle” element that was mentioned, but it can be outright skipped if you so desire via an option in the menu that lets you put objects anywhere. [b]The controls are solid, with mostly great snapping. You can also stack objects and move them all together[/b], making it easier to conclude the sometimes herculean task of unpacking an entire life.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2778389984

[b]This gameplay is presented via an isometric perspective, wrapped neatly together with very cute graphics and an extremely relaxing soundtrack that absolutely fits the vibe being offered.[/b] While the presentation is charming and the gameplay is engaging, that is [b]not to say the game is without its flaws.[/b] For example: sometimes, you won’t have any idea what an object is. This results in you having no idea of where the “proper” place for said object would be, which then results in mindless clicking around until it stops blinking red.

Furthermore, the whole system of indicating that you’re trying to put something in the wrong place can be flawed. As an example, think of a common drying dish rack. Would you ever consider putting one on top of a fridge? For me, that makes absolutely no sense. Despite that, the game accepted the top of the fridge as a valid location. [b]Do these issues get in the way of enjoying the game? Not even close, but they do need to be noted regardless.[/b]

Honestly though, in a way, these issues happen due to the [b]overwhelming attention to detail that is presented to us by the developers.[/b] The household objects I can’t recognize are actual objects… They just might not be part of my culture, or it might even just be me not knowing them. The whole reason why they’re there is due to the [b]care the dev team took into making the houses feel accurate to what houses and flats would normally have.[/b] But the attention to detail does not stop there. From items that change with each move (such as a mousepad that has a lot of wear after a few moves, and is eventually replaced) and doors being unable to close if a drawer is open, indicated by the door banging against the drawer… this game has it all. 

But above all else, this game’s attention to detail manifests in its incredible way to tell a tale. [b] The story is not anything special by itself, but the way it’s told is one of the best examples of environmental storytelling I have ever had the pleasure to see in a game. [/b] With every move, you get to see the year you’re now at. With that, you can get an idea of what life stage the person is. And after you beat every level, you get a lovely photo album with the main character’s thoughts written right under the photo. You can even go back to a complete level, retake the picture in another room and get a different text. All of these elements feed us the story in a direct and unremarkable manner, sure, but what maybe goes unnoticed by some is the fact that this direct exposition is only a support for the true manner in which the game tells its tale: the household objects. 

Picture yourself witnessing this situation: someone just moved into their new girlfriend’s house, and during the move, decided to bring a picture of their grandma. It is an item of incredible importance, and they love it… except when they get to the small apartment, there is no room for the picture to be displayed. The person isn’t even allowed to move their girlfriend’s items. And so, the photo ends in a closet. What can you infer about the relationship? I’d say for example that it’s not a very healthy relationship if one party is unwilling to accommodate the other’s most important needs and possessions. Can we, as observers, be sure that’s the case? Nope! But that’s okay. Not everything in life needs confirmation.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2778389926

The example I gave above is not part of the game, but there are plenty of situations that are similar in their concept. If you were to unpack, for example, a piano, you would know your character is into music. Get a magic kit out of the box, and you can infer she’s probably the type to do magic tricks to impress friends. The list goes on, but the gist of it is: [b]through the objects the main character owns, and the places that the game defines as being their proper place of storage, you can find out a LOT about her life.[/b] You discover her hobbies, her degree in university, the trajectory her life took, her religion or lack thereof, her career choice, her trip destinations, some of the companies she keeps, her medical history… [b]By the end of the game, I was surprised by how well I knew this person, despite her having never been even given a name. And that is one hell of a feat.[/b]

At the end of the day, is this game worth it, especially at full price? I would say so, but mostly due to the fact that it truly is a [b]masterclass in environmental storytelling.[/b] However, the game is also very short (3.5 hours or so), so if you are one to equate the duration of the game to its monetary value, waiting for a sale might be needed. But for me, it was worth every penny.

Unpacking in this game felt better than any real move I've ever done 😂

Unpacking is a narrative-focused puzzle game built around placing personal items into new living spaces. It’s quiet, structured, and centred on the small emotional details of moving from one phase of life to the next.

The gameplay feels clean and satisfying. Item placement is smooth, with subtle grid constraints that help things fit without feeling rigid. Each object has its own sound, and the feedback is consistently sharp. There’s no friction, and the interaction loop stays enjoyable the entire time.

I finished three chapters in an hour. I played casually, not worrying about perfection, and still felt rewarded. The game lets you move at your own pace without pressure. There are a few restrictions on where items can go, which pulled me out of the moment at times, but not enough to take away from the overall flow.

The story is told through what the character packs and unpacks. No dialogue, no direct choices. Just details. It’s heartwarming and sometimes heavy, but always subtle. The structure works, and the emotional beats land without being forced.

The pixel art is cozy and clear. The visuals stay out of the way but do their job. The audio is nearly perfect. Every object has a distinct sound when placed, making the whole experience more tactile.

There’s no real replay value. Once you’ve seen the story, it’s done. But that first play-through is solid. If you’re looking for a calm, polished game that delivers a simple concept with surprising emotional weight, Unpacking is worth your time.

Final rating: 7.5/10
Solid, satisfying, and emotionally grounded - even if it’s a one-time experience.

游戏的像素画风跟背景音乐很不错，游玩方式相当放松，随着每次搬家进入新房，都可以从开箱的物品感受到女主角的成长与变化。当然，几次搬家中间的巨大空白，玩家就需要自行去脑补女主角到底经历了什么。严格来说，游戏的剧情确实也是建立在玩家的自行脑补之上。

游戏看似没有故事剧情，却又仿佛在玩的时候默默的给你塞了一个成长故事。从第一个房间到最后一个房间，主角带着从小就喜欢的东西，怀揣梦想，慢慢的到结婚生子等等，这种叙事的方式真的很新颖。玩家正是透过搬家和整理物品的摆放来不断的重新认识女主角当前所处的生活状态，也间接见证了女主角从幼年到成年，到步入婚姻殿堂的历程。这样隐晦的叙事也给玩家带来了小小的触动。

在游戏里并不是把每一个东西随意乱放就行而是每样物品都有一定规范的摆放区域。时常会有系统限制的情况出现，像是书包不能放在地上，把锅铲放在床头肯定也是不行。坦白讲，有时候会玩到有点烦，因为游戏只提示你不能放在这，但不会告诉你要放在哪，需要玩家结合现实去摸索。但总是有些物品看不出来应该摆放在哪，你就要各个房间不停的乱试。

如果这款游戏可以有自定义模式，玩家可以自己打造一个房间，设置各项物品的摆放位置，然后再上传到创意工坊，大家分享互玩彼此的关卡，游戏可能就又升华到更高的层次了。因为现在的通关流程确实有点短，以后应该也不会大幅度更新了，受限于女主角的剧情。

作为一个搬过几次家的人来说，这款游戏真的很有感触，留意到这次搬家留下的物品，或是哪件物品被留到最后，都会深有感概。

짐풀기로 시작하고 끝날 때까지 주구장창 짐만 푸는 사이버 노동 게임

게임 내 여주인공이 커 가면서 다양한 장소로 이사를 가는 이야기가 피상적으로 담겨 있으면서, 게임플레이 자체는 이사를 간 집에서 상자들을 다 뜯어가며 그 안의 짐들을 새 집에 알맞게 배치해주면 되는 방식으로 진행되는 게임이다. 일단, Unpacking 의 장점 하나를 꼽자면 당연히 비주얼일 것이다. 픽셀 그래픽을 사용함에도 불구하고 이 게임은 게임 내 물체들과 방 내부를 굉장히 부드럽게 표현하였으며, 오브젝트들 간 개성이나 생김새도 꽤 자세히 구현을 해 놓았다. 그러나 개인적으로 이 게임을 하면서 느낀 장점은 여기서 멈추었다. 위에서 말한 이 게임의 이야기, 그리고 게임플레이 과정 모두 만족도에 충족하지 않았으며, 이 때문에 이 게임을 심층적인 이야기나 게임성을 기대하고 플레이 한다면 실망할 것이라 단언한다. 왜 이 두 면에서 이 게임에 대해 만족하지 못하였는지 그 이유를 서술해 보자면 :

1. Unpacking 의 게임플레이는 "상자에서 짐 꺼내기 > 해당 짐을 알맞은 장소에 배치하기 (프라이팬은 주방에, 드레스는 옷장에 등등) > 모든 짐을 배치하였으면 게임이 틀린 위치에 배치된 물체를 집어주며, 이들을 정확한 위치에 배치한다면 해당 레벨을 완료하고 다음 레벨로 진행" 의 방식으로 이루어진다. 그리고 이 게임 내 약 8개의 레벨 내내 이 작업을 하게 된다. "아니 힐링게임 장르에서도 반복적인 작업이 나오는데, 왜 이 게임만 이걸 지적하느냐?" 라고 의문을 가질 수 있는데, 일반적인 힐링게임은 간편하고 노동력이 거의 들어가지 않는 작업을 주로 스토리를 진행시킨다면, Unpacking 은 물체를 하나하나 배치해야 하는 마우스 클릭 및 드래그의 반복작업만 모든 물체에 대해 주구장창 진행해야 한다. 여기서 더 끔찍한 점은, 이러한 양상이 게임 끝까지 단 하나도 바뀌지 않는다. 새로운 메커니즘? 플레이어의 예상을 깨부수는 게임플레이? 그런 거 안 나온다. 물론, 단순한 작업만 하는 모든 게임이 지루하다는 건 아니다. 예를 들면, 클리커 게임도 분명히 클릭만 하는 장르인데도 이 장르 내 중독성이 있는 게임들이 한 두개가 아니다. 다만, 과연 Unpacking 이 제공하는 게임플레이의 단조로움에 플레이어가 몰입하고 재미를 느낄 수 있느냐? 라고 질문한다면, 100% 확신에 찬 긍정적인 대답을 할 수 없다는 것이다.

2. Unpacking 의 이야기는 게임 내 하나하나 설명해 주는 게 아니라, 간접적으로 전달된다. 레벨이 지나가면서 주인공은 같지만 나이를 먹어 가며 이삿짐에 들어 있는 물품들이 바뀌는 디테일을 통해 이 게임의 주인공은 어떠한 사람인가? 를 상상하는 과정도 스토리를 알아 가는 하나의 묘미이다. 예를 들어, 어릴 때 벽에 걸어놓은 포스터들을 나이가 들며 줄인다던가, 아니면 반대로 어릴 때부터 침대애 두었던 인형을 성인이 되어서까지 챙기는 점 등등을 보면서 게임 내 주인공에게 몰입을 하고 어떠한 특징을 지녔을지 상상하는 재미가 없는 건 아니다. 그렇다고 해서, 이 게임의 스토리가 흥미로운가? 라고 하면 그건 또 아니라는 것이다. 게임이 진행되는 과정에서 보여주는 주인공의 삶은 평이하고, 이삿짐을 보면서 주인공에 대한 몇 가지 디테일들을 알지언정 그것이 게임플레이를 즐겁게 하는 건 아니고, 모든 레벨을 완료하고 게임을 전체적으로 다시 돌아본다고 해도 스토리가 여운을 남기거나 감동적이었다라고 할 정도는 아니었다고 생각한다. 즉, 게임 내 이야기는 딱 "있는 듯, 없는 듯 하면서도 게임 내 이사를 가는 개연성과 이유를 어느 정도 잡아주는 정도의 기반만 갖춘 스토리" 이다. 문제는 게임플레이에 흥미를 가지지 못했을 경우, 차라리 게임 내 스토리라도 인상이 깊었다면 게임을 재미있다고 느꼈을 수 있었을 것 같은데, 그 방향과는 완전히 반대 방향의 스토리라 실망하였다.


결론적으로, "이삿짐을 풀고 짐을 정리하면서 진행되는 퍼즐 게임" 이라는 아이디어는 나쁘지 않지만, 게임플레이와 스토리가 개인적으로 단조롭고 평면적이라 재미를 느끼지 못하여 비추천한다. 다만, 비주얼이나 사운드 면에서는 아쉽다고 느낀 부분이 없었으니, 만약 트레일러를 보고 재미를 느낄 수 있을 것 같다고 생각될 때 한 번 해보는 걸 권장한다.

여담) 게임의 플레이타임은 약 2 ~ 3시간인데, 정가를 보면 알겠지만 가격 대비 플레이타임이 별로이다. 혹시 구매할 사람들이라면 어느 정도 세일을 할 때 사는 게 돈을 절약하는 데 좋을 것이다.

This game was SO much more than I was expecting.

When I initially purchased it, I was concerned that Unpacking would quickly feel repetitive or like a chore. I am not someone to usually gravitate toward building games, and I thought this would be similar. I am so happy to be wrong! 

The graphics are cute and very aesthetically pleasing, the game function manages to stay entertaining for hours on end, and the storyline is so touching. Unpacking is an instant classic!

How is it that games can be so effective at making menial tasks fun? It will never cease to astound me that there’s an entire flourishing genre of basic labor simulators, where people will pay money for the privilege of driving a bus or chopping down trees. It’s a testament to the developers, I suppose, that they can so effectively gamify work that most people desperately avoid in their everyday lives. That mastery is nowhere more apparent than in the gentle visuals and tactile joys of Unpacking, a lovely little title that simulates the absolute worst parts of moving. The fact that I can even load this game up a few months after unpacking my own new place is evidence of that.

Unpacking takes you on a journey through eight residences as the subject of the story first moves into them. In each locale, you’ll have a selection of rooms rendered in absolutely gorgeous pixel art, blighted by moving boxes that must be, well, unpacked. A whole host of items will come spewing forth from these boxes, from clothes to cutlery, plushies to pills. It’s your job to find a place for each of these, such that the rooms may become a home of at least controlled chaos. Once everything is suitably put away, the game awards you fanfare to let you know your task is done, and that you might move on to the next milestone in this person’s life.

It’s a simple premise with equally simple mechanics. Clicking on a box retrieves an item from it, right-clicking rotates it, and moving it around the room affords you a wide array of context-sensitive locations to place it. The first hint of real genius here is how clever that context sensitivity is. You’re not limited to lining up postcards in a drawer or books on a shelf. As you sweep items around the room, you’ll find you can fold and stack clothes, pin up or roll up posters, keep toothbrushes in cups, and so much more. This is key because it turns what would be a charming task simulator into a journey of discovery to see how few limits you have on where you can place things.

Once you realize how open the game is in this sense, that’s when the real brilliance shines through. The eight scenes that you are tasked with unpacking are not all the same, and some play with those placement mechanics in interesting and logical ways. This all serves the story, which you might have been surprised at me mentioning earlier, given that this is a game exclusively about taking things out of things and putting them on or inside things. Unpacking tells a moving, nuanced story without need of a single word of text, because it does it entirely through context and the environment. You’re sure to notice the items that keep showing up as you move from place to place, as well as conspicuous absences from your belongings. New items can tell stories all on their own, simply from the point in the game where they first appear.

The real wow moment for me was about halfway through the game, where there was a story beat told not by an item, but by the space I had in which to place it. That might sound odd but when I realized what was happening, it hit me harder than so many RPGs or text-heavy adventures ever have. You’ve surely heard the old aphorism “show, don’t tell”, and to me this is the absolute pinnacle of that guidance being heeded. Unpacking does so, so much with just a collection of rooms and items, supported expertly by lush graphics and a moving soundtrack. It’s warm and inviting and meaningful, and so many games with so much loftier ambitions have missed that mark that this game nails.

If it seems like I’m gushing too much over a 3-hour game, that’s because I don’t remember the last time a 3-hour game brought me so much joy. It’s the day after and I’m still running through all the things I did in my head, wondering if I missed any additional significance in a mug or hand towel. There’s a collection of hidden achievements (they exist as adorable stickers in-game) that are awarded for doing specific things while unpacking, and I only got about half of them on a single playthrough, so I’m definitely thinking about going back for those. But even without that extra incentive, I wouldn’t trade my time in Unpacking for anything.

Unpacking offered me the perfect balance between creative freedom and a limiting ruleset. 

You start with a small children's bedroom and a small set of items to unpack from boxes. Once the package is "cleared", the game will indicate if everything is in a place the game considers acceptable. Misplaced items will appear with a blinking red border. You finish a level once the room is tidied up, and the next one unlocks.

You will progress through a variety of [b]levels[/b]. Sometimes they consist of multiple rooms or even stages of a house as we follow the life of our protagonist. The game is not challenging, but sometimes finding a small misplaced item can be tricky. There is a setting to turn off the placement check, allowing you to progress through the levels without adhering to the ruleset if you get stuck or feel stressed at any point.

In general, the game is very [b]accommodating[/b]. You can zoom in and out, increase icon size, change the highlight colour and use keyboard, mouse or controller inputs. There is no time pressure, and the game autosaves at any time.  

The [b]story[/b] is discovered by interpreting the items you unpack and the nature of the apartments you live in. The game takes place from 1997-2018. People who grew up in that time might find many familiar-looking items. Many, if not all, books and other media covers resemble iconic pieces of the time. There are also domestic and religious items that you might not be familiar with. 

The [b]time[/b] it takes to reach the credits depends significantly on your ambitions. Simply unpacking and finding a place that's allowed can be done in 3 hours. It took me 7 and then I started a second playthrough right away (there are 5 save slots) because I had a blast and learned that there is a hidden game mode with a different ruleset for item placement! It's also entertaining to try to complete the game according to a challenge you made up on your own. Like playing the floor is lava or trying to swap the purpose of rooms etc.

The [b]achievements[/b] for this game are visualized and and hinted at by stickersheets in the game. You earn specific stickers for placing or interacting with items in certain ways. 

Lastly there is a [b]photomode[/b] that I didn't make use of but I saw on the community page thst some people create little stories making use of the filters, frames and stickers that the game offers!

[hr][/hr]

Part interior decor, part puzzle, Unboxing creatively delivers what it's like to move houses and how each place has it's own set of memories associated with it.

The game is very simple. You follow the life of a girl from her childhood to adulthood, by unpacking and arranging all of her belongings in every new place she moves into. It sounds just as mundane as the actual real life task is, but the game manages to make it fun and interesting with it's environmental storytelling and attention to detail. 

The game tracks every house or every move with the year that it happened and it is reflected in the items that you unpack. It could be the technology of the time (like the veeery clunky looking PC you'll see in level 2) or it could be trends which will be apparent in her clothes and posters, among other stuff. You also retain some stuff from previous levels, hinting at the character's attachment to certain things or ideas. Each new level might also bring in new rooms to decorate. The first level is just the characters bedroom because as a kid, that'll be the only relevant room as far as unpacking is concerned. You will soon get more rooms or move into places like an apartment or even a two storey house. Sometimes, you might not be able to move certain things because you might not be living alone in that house. Like I said, small, subtle details.

You might initially be put off by the fact that while there is no one specific place for an item, you can't put anything, anywhere you want. But there's a good reason for this. This is where the puzzle aspect of the game  comes in. This helps show the relation the character has to certain items and how it has/will change over the years of her life. Other than the choice of items themselves, where she wants to place certain items helps flesh out her personality a lot and gives us hints to how she feels about the move. 
(There is a toggle in the accessibility settings which lets you place anything anywhere, but I'd only recommend it after you finish the game normally so that you don't miss out on the puzzles)

The game is eight levels long, with gorgeous pixel art and charming music. It's simple yet does what it intends to do pretty well. It's short, but the time you spend organising, reorganising and decorating is fun. You can always go back and redecor it any way you want to, so there is some replayability as well. I would recommend picking this game up at least during a sale, if not at full price. (It does seem a little overpriced when compared to other games, especially because of how short it is.).

I wish the game had more levels or modes or was longer somehow. I loved the storytelling through objects. I played through it and got all the achievements in 3 hours. Short game but very sweet. I wish to see more games by the creators.

Nice little point-and-click game with a unique gameplay.

The character moves from place to place over a period of time (from 1997 to 2018). You have to unpack so many boxes and arrange the stuff at various locations. It's that simple.

There is no narration or voiceover. You will understand the journey of the character by the amount (and type) of stuff you unpack from the boxes. Nice way of telling a story.

The completion time is 3 to 4 hours (with 100% achievements). The gameplay time may vary depending on the player. Some may want to arrange things as neatly as possible, and there are so many ways to do this. So it may take more time.

The sound effect is top-notch. The music complements the gameplay quite well.

It may feel pricey.

I recommend getting this on sale if you want some relaxed gameplay.

Unpacking is one of those rare games that speaks volumes without saying a single word. There is no dialogue, no text-based narrative, yet by the end, I felt deeply connected to the person whose life I had slowly uncovered box by box.
At its core, the gameplay is simple. You unpack items and find a place for them. But this simplicity is exactly what makes the game so moving. Every object tells a story. From childhood toys that stay with you for years, to toothbrushes, posters, and photographs, each item reveals something about the person you are following. Without any text, the game lets you witness love, growth, heartbreak, change, and resilience.
The pixel art is incredibly detailed and warm. The sound design is satisfying and realistic. The ambient music sets a calm and reflective mood. Together, they create a soothing atmosphere that invites you to slow down and truly pay attention.
Unpacking is short, but it stays with you. It does not rush. It respects your time and your emotions. It is the kind of game that feels like a quiet conversation with someone you care about. Personal, intimate, and full of heart.
If you are looking for a peaceful, thoughtful, and beautifully designed experience, this game is absolutely worth your time.

[h1]本以为是一个很短流程的放置解压小游戏，没想到它埋了那么多细节，拼凑出一个令我开心愉悦的女性故事。 [/h1]
游戏玩法，那就是开箱拿出东西，然后再将它们放置到应该在的位置上。从女主童年到大学毕业再到工作，一共开箱了很多次，我恰巧对开箱摆东西少了很多耐心，几乎都是图早点摆好完事，然后就错过很多很多的彩蛋和细节！
[b]如果你对找线索很感兴趣，那么你在完成物件摆放后可以好好研究下房间里的各种东西，会给你惊喜的。 [/b]
[spoiler]女主的童年，还有她的大学生活都很令我羡慕，有自己十分爱好的兴趣，如绘画，游戏(DND跑团和任天堂超级粉丝)，运动等，还有志同道合的朋友。毕业了，被社会毒打后的女主有勇气割舍掉破烂的生活和事业去追寻属于自己的梦想，以及正视自己内心的取向，而不是麻木地过着所谓主流的生活。[/spoiler]
其实这算不上一个很精彩华丽的故事，就是一个普通的女性成长故事碎片集，但它已经足够打动我了。

Today I suggest fighting existential anxiety with a cozy and soothing unpacking simulator - a minimalist puzzle game where you spend three to five hours (or more…) neatly taking things out of boxes after a move and arranging them in a new apartment. Your playtime, I suspect, depends entirely on how feral your urge is to sort books by height and organize socks by color. The game works especially well if the ability to neatly fold a pajama set, tuck it under a pillow, and then place a heating pad under a blanket triggers a warm and fuzzy feeling of control over the boundless ocean of surrounding chaos for you.

For such minimalist gameplay, “Unpacking” does a surprisingly good job of revealing the protagonist's character and life story. It even packs (pun intended) a few unexpected plot twists! One of them hit me profoundly while I was trying to cram a truly astronomical number of bras into a dresser - no other game has ever shocked me with a narrative turn while I was digging through someone’s (clean) laundry :)

Some levels were tricky due to my personal experience. One item left me utterly bewildered; I dragged it all over the apartment - it didn't fit the kitchen, it looked wrong in the bathroom... what is it?! In a fit of frustration, I messaged my friend, who had already beaten the game. I told him I was totally in deepest despair because this one stupid awkward rice cooker is trolling me and doesn't fit anywhere!!!
"Rice cooker?" he laughed. "That’s a game console, dummy." 

A few stressful moments aside, the game wraps you in the feeling of being cradled and promises that if you work hard, fold your socks neatly, go to bed on time, and do your morning stretches, everything will eventually be okay… That’s not necessarily true, but you really want to believe it sometimes.

Unpacking ist ein sehr schönes kurzes Spiel, in dem wir - wie der Name verrät - unser Hab & Gut auspacken UND einsortieren müssen. Ja! Denn es reicht nicht einfach nur auspacken und auf dem Boden legen, man muss die Dinge schon a) in den richtigen Raum und b) richtige Ecke/Regal etc. lagern. z.B. gehört eine Klopapierrolle nicht ins Wohnzimmer oder die Mikrowelle in die Badewanne. Es gibt aber etwas Freiraum. Also ein Bild muss jetzt nicht unbedingt an einem einzigen bestimmten Platz. Bücher können ins Regal, ob oben oder unten, spielt keine Rolle.

Sobald alle Kartons ausgeladen sind, zeigt euch das Spiel die Dinge an, die falsch an einem Ort liegen. Daher hab ich schnell bemerkt, dass es Sinnvoll ist, erst einmal alles aus zu packen und dann ein zu sortieren. Natürlich kann man es vorher machen und später schauen, inwiefern man richtig lag. Im Grunde sollte man locker 80% aller Sachen beim ersten Mal am richtigen Ort legen. Schließlich haben wir alle ein Zuhause und daher sollte man sich da etwas auskennen.

Ich habe das Spiel aus dem Humble Choice November 2023 bekommen. Normal kostet es ohne Rabatt 20€ und ich habe max. 4 Stunden gebraucht. Das wären 5€/h - Recht Teuer!

Unpacking is a short game. A really short game.
But it certainly is one that makes you think for a lot longer!

The game itself focuses around unpacking thingsplacing them in their right (or horribly wrong) places. But there is so much more to this game! It tells the story of a protagonist who you start to get really invested in. During one level I got angry, during some I got extremely excited with and for the protagonist!

Placing and moving things feels great and the artstyle is amazing. The music is super nice as well!

And once I was almost done I jokingly clicked on an object and found out that

Some objects are interactable! With hundreds of more small details and references. 
Also depending on what room you end a level in you get a different bit of lore.

Mas acho um jogo muito curto pelo valor, seria muito legal ver outras histórias, outros ambientes e personagens. 
Depois que joguei Unpacking fiquei desesperada buscando outros que fossem iguais mas nenhum com a mesma proposta, espero que façam mais no futuro.

非常非常非常喜欢这个类型的游戏，看到评论说制作组不打算做续作之类的，去网上搜了下，看到说是作者不理解为什么我们希望出后续，说故事已经讲完了。我觉得制作组可能没理解玩家的意思，故事终究是会结束的这点是没错，但我想大家其实对游戏的玩法也是非常欣赏并且热爱的，空闲放松时刻打开Unpacking玩上那么一关只为了体验整理的乐趣。
我和朋友都买这款游戏并且都玩了，和朋友讨论过，也许并不是说一定要有后续故事才能有后续关卡游戏，可以尝试出额外的附加无剧情关卡，房间布局稍微改动下，比如书架床柜子换换位置，微调下设计，不限制物品放置位置，真正的随意摆放，让玩家自己决定要如何整理出属于自己的家，不也是一种好的玩法吗。
虽然感觉希望不大，但我还是真诚的希望未来的哪一天这个游戏开始制作新的额外关卡，能让我体验更多整理的乐趣！

My own little nobody review, if anyone cares.

Very simple, relaxing, and almost cathartic - but I think the biggest highlight of this game was how the item restriction led to some clever narrative reveals about the character's life, such as having you hide her degree and thus her passion while living with her partner, and then afterwards stashing the photo of both her and her partner from sight in a later vignette. It's for that strength that I recommend not turning off the item restriction requirement if you can help it, although the option being there is really nice :)

说起来蛮奇妙的，玩了这个游戏之后我在现实生活里更喜欢整理东西了。
游戏确确实实很值，非常非常的有趣。
唯一一个美中不足的就是内容太太太少了，我没整理够（泪）。

游戏说实话还不错，但有几个地方及其影响体验。本来我是奔着休闲解压无脑放空来的，结果有些东西居然还规定强制放置的区域。
大家生活习惯都不一样，我就喜欢把我最喜欢的手办模型玩具放在手边，结果系统打咩，不放到人家规定的地方这关就不给过。还有的东西根本就看不出来是啥，也不知道放哪，只能一个个试错，连个提示都没。最恶心的是我玩到第四还是第五关应该是触发bug了，有一张挂在墙上的照片无论我放在哪里都提示错误，搞得我很烦躁一气之下就退款了。
另外就是价格，说实话流程这么短还没有操作性的小游戏70着实有些贵。总的来说见仁见智，可能我脑子不够使感觉被机制嘲讽了，不介意的人可以入手。

Unpacking was low-key one of the favorite games I've played this year. It's about organizing stuff in a house? Yes. And it's fun, frustrating and emotional? YES!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! 

I loved to learn more about the life of the MC through the different houses she lived in and just got really emotional/excited here and there. It was an extremely comfy game and I honestly wish there were more lives for me to pry upon/other games like this.

I heard many great things about Unpacking, being a chill & cozy game, good at calming your nerves while playing it, overall a fun & pleasant game. In my opinion, the game shines the most in its story telling, without telling you.

Through game-play, and with very little dialogue, we get to know the journey of the MC,
"Oh, they seem to be interested in this since little"
"Wow, they kept these things with them all these years"
"Oh no, this relationship isn't gonna work out"
"They are so happy now"

"Show, don't tell" at its finest. 10/10.

太贵了，建议打折入，但我说大概20买差不多。核心玩法就是收拾房间。或者要玩的可以买来2小时以内体验一下吧。也许不是适合每一个人。
游戏流程比较短，也许是我从小到大没搬过家，我没有什么共鸣。我也没想过有一天我从那个我生活了十多年的地方搬走会有多么悲伤。或者是我在家里一直没有属于过自己的空间吧。我很羡慕大多数家庭的小孩，有自己的书桌，电脑桌，可以买自己喜欢的玩意儿摆在书架上，有属于自己的房间，有属于自己的衣柜，鞋架，把房间装饰成自己喜欢的模样。这些我都没有，我甚至在家睡沙发。我在高考完和他们大吵一架。年初的时候我在京东网购了几个箱子来装我的东西，里面大多数是书，从幼儿园的练字本，课本，到现在的大学教材。里面还有许多我的回忆，我幼儿园玩的积木，小学的作文本，初中时候上课的纸条，收集的糖纸，成绩单，我喜欢过的男孩的东西，别人送我的生日礼物，最重要的是从初中在外地读书开始写的一本又一本日记。我很感慨，竟然就三四个箱子就能装下这十八年。也许未来我会有一间属于我自己的房间。
É um jogo muito e relaxante, distrai a mente, mas já terminei de jogar tudo KKKKK, poderia ter mais coisas para organizar, mais cômodos e outras histórias.

Unpacking turns a simple concept into a surprisingly emotional journey. As you organize someone’s life, room by room, you begin to piece together their story in a beautifully subtle way.
It’s a calming, almost meditative experience, with charming pixel art and a soundtrack that complements the cozy, reflective atmosphere.

This is a very short game. I played through all the levels and yoinked all the achievements in about 4 hours.

It is incredibly relaxing, no point system to judge you, no timers, no competitive elements. A real breath of fresh air.

Rooms have very little limitations on the placement of furniture. Anything goes, as long as it makes sense. So a toaster can't go in the bathtub, or toys can't be left thrown on the ground. There are also little details that tell us about the owner of all the furniture. A personal diary needs to be hidden out of plain sight, a certain photo can't be displayed on the cork board. Little details that give us some story and makes it so much more immersive. 

The pixel art is cute and works perfectly with the style of the game. There is so much attention to each individual item, with wear and tear appearing over the years, showing how time has affected them, and new souvenirs that are slowly being collected from holidays abroad. Even the sounds are perfect. Every item has a different sound for every surface it's placed on. I first noticed it with the hot water bottle, sloshing around as I decided where to put it.

It's the perfect game for me. The love, effort, and detail the developers put into creating this, more than justifies the price. I would love to see more ♥

[h1]离别是为了更好的开始[/h1]
当行驶卡车停下，传来一阵门铃声。
你的东西全到了，就装在地板箱子。
你打开一个箱子，有好多事情要忙。
当一切整理完毕，房子就变成了家。
我是一个怀旧的人，每次的搬家都让我惆怅，收拾记忆的碎片，告别认识的朋友，去一个陌生的地方，认识陌生的人。可惜，生活就是如此，有时快乐有时落寞，时光总要推着我们前进，不如日后变得更强，毕竟来日方长。

[h1]不爱整理房间的我，却花了三个小时在电脑上整理房间？[/h1]
Unpacking，顾名思义，开箱，指游戏中搬家之后从纸箱中取出来物品。而游戏中的玩法也非常简单，打开箱子，把物品放到属于它的地方就好了。在摆放上，游戏还算是比较自由的，只要游戏摆到他适合的地方就可以了。不过，作为一个平时基本都懒得整理房间，只要能找到东西就绝对不会去整理东西的死宅，游戏中有些东西的摆放还是让我感到相当迷惑的，顺便游戏中还有大量的女性用品，化妆品之类的，只能大致摆放个位置。顺便，小白板和各种小饰品冰箱磁贴还请注意下，第一次摆放完全不知道是放在那儿，知道无心插柳，才发现这个小白板是放在冰箱前面的。而那些看起来可可爱爱的东西加入不算发卡而是冰箱贴，也许这就是中西文化的差异吧，笔者可不记得冰箱上会加一个小白板。总之，除了几个完全看不出是啥东西的位置不太好摆放外，其他还算顺顺利利了。完成摆放之后，游戏给人整体的成就感还是满满的。比较最难的房间可能摆放的物品要超过200个了，还是相当耗费时间的。不过作为一个不爱整理的人，直到最后笔者的书本和记事本还有游戏卡带还是杂乱无章地摆在一起（笑。当然，如果玩家有心并有耐心还是可以把他们整理得清清楚楚的。

[h1]我愿称之为艺术品[/h1]
游戏虽然有游戏的本质，但是更加倾向于艺术品，或者纪录片，利用整理东西的点点滴滴来给玩家一种全新的体验，并讲述一个完整的故事。故事的跨度相当之大，从1997年持续到了2018年，游戏中以8次搬家为时间节点。从最开始的童年，到初恋，分手，感受到家的温暖，收获爱情，收获家庭，实现梦想。看着游戏中的物品一点一点改变，出现新的电脑，笔记本电脑，3ds，wiiu，ps主机，xbox主机，仿佛可以在游戏中感受到时光的变迁，原来笔者只关注到了游戏机的变化，毕竟我是个游戏宅啊（笑）。
不过游戏中的细节也做得相当到位，比如女主搬家去和男朋友同居的时候，在整理房间的时候，可以看到男生的衣服袜子什么的放的比较凌乱，完全符合大多数男性的特征23333；游戏在在女主和男朋友分手之后搬回到家中，在整理和男友的照片的时候，玩家如果将照片摆放在桌子上，系统之后会提示摆放错误，唯有藏到柜子里面才是正确的方式；有一个最开始就一直在的珍贵玩偶小熊，到后面小熊随着时间已经开始开裂了。

[h1]意外不错的拍照功能[/h1]
在完成整理房间的劳作之后，千万不要急着开始下一个关卡。游戏带有一个相当优秀的拍照APP，带有相框特效，调色效果以及贴纸功能（贴纸需要完成游戏内的）。推荐玩家在完成整理之后在每一间房间都拍一张照片留作纪念，因为通关之后游戏只会把最后完成的那个房间拍照放入相册。

[h1]总结[/h1]
Unpacking是一款温馨休闲的物品放置类游戏，玩家只要将箱子中的物品摆放到合理的位置就可以了。游戏跨度从1997到2018年以八个搬家时间为节点，从侧面讲述了女主的半辈子的故事，有成功有失意，有爱情有亲情，人世间的美好莫过于此。伴随着唯美的8bit音乐与精致的像素建模，一起开始漫漫长路的整理之旅吧~

Unpacking is a comfy and relaxing puzzle game that gives you the satisfactory feeling of unpacking and placing your items on their rightful place when you move to a new place. The puzzles in this game are mostly just block-fitting styled trying to include fun home decoration where over the course of eight house moves, you are given a chance to experience a sense of intimacy with a character you never see and a story you’re never told.

You get to discover the story through the items you place, arranging bookshelves, cabinets and even fridge magnets. There is no rush, no timers and almost full control over where to place items. There are some items that are only allowed in certain rooms and places, but it's quite realistic and I had no problems with most items. I was a little annoyed that some rooms seemed to have not enough space to fit the items aesthetically. There is also very little replayability with this game, and it's finished in just four hours.

I do think the game is worth to be played, since the experience is really good, BUT I don't recommend getting this game at full price, since 20€ is a little much for the amount of content you get, unless they do decide to add more rooms. So get the game at a sale and you'll enjoy a lot of fun times organizing items to your liking.

[h1]90后旅美，漂泊一生[/h1]
很久以前，一个游戏爱好者向我推荐了《Unpacking》，说这是一款禅意十足的益智游戏。那时我看到价格便克制住了下单的冲动，直到今年感恩节促销，才终于入手。

游戏通过拆箱和摆放物品，让玩家一步步窥见主人公前半生的故事与情绪变化。对我来说，这种设定格外动人——从童年的搬家、高中住宿、大学入住宿舍，到出国留学后的频繁迁徙，我与主人公的人生轨迹产生了强烈共鸣，仿佛在每一次搬家中与她渐渐融为一体。

最初多彩缤纷的小房间风格透露着主人公拥有过无忧无虑的童年，作为女孩子的主人公也可以有喜欢踢足球和打游戏的爱好，打破人们对女孩子的普遍刻板印象。我童年时跟随祖母一起搬入新家生活，直到十岁左右才有自己的小小房间。后来买了一堆单机游戏盒和一些小手办，摆放在玻璃柜里以供观赏。我想，那是我童年时代为数不多的快乐回忆。叛逆期提前到来，我执意要买一堆中性运动服取代比较女孩子气的衣服，还剪了短发，以对抗不理解自己的大人们，如今想来也是毫无意义的操作吧，如果回家一看男装摆在那里，肯定会羞愧到想扔掉。

高一时因为对升学有深深的焦虑情绪，担心自己考不上好大学，再加上厌倦了一成不变的生活，想要逃离这种家，于是经过多次争执，才说服家人去某个南方城市借读。那是我第一次离开家乡，独自在异地生活。那段求学岁月，也是我最努力的一年。我那时候在一个本子上写了很多很多读书笔记，然而在毕业后搬出宿舍时却发现丢失了，成为了我心中始终挥之不去的遗憾。从那以后我暗暗地发誓，若有重要事物，无论何时搬家都一定要随身带上。

初入大学时和主人公一样特别兴奋，购买很多生活用品并放在宿舍里，期待着大学生的新生活。我的好朋友打算要搬离大学宿舍，想要让我一起搬进附近的租房里，然后一起生活有个照应，我那时候考虑到距离和时间的问题，一口谢绝了好朋友的要求。我在大学宿舍里布置了比较宅的东西，在上铺放了木质双层桌子，还在周围挂了蚊帐，从此开始悠哉悠哉的死宅大学生生活。

可惜好景不长，大学生活并没有想象中那么快乐，也不尽如人意。因为专业不合自己的兴趣，加之缺乏艺术天赋，我最终决定退学，选择出国留学，转读一个更适合自己的专业，期望通过改变找回自我。初到美国大学，既感到陌生，又充满兴奋。美国的大学宿舍多为双人间，空间更为宽敞自由，可以随意摆放个人物品，不像国内那样拥挤的集体宿舍。怀揣着学成归国的梦想，我开始了留学生涯。后来发现宿舍费用远高于校外租房，甚至一个学期的住宿费足够在外面住上半年甚至更久，于是我决定搬出去租房，由此开启了漫长的搬家旅程。

时光流转，伴随着抑郁与焦虑的起伏。尽管这些年情绪反复无常，又恰逢COVID疫情爆发，我依然在一年搬一次家的辗转中坚持完成了本科学业，并选择留下来工作，与疫情一路抗争。后来因为种种原因，我依旧不断搬家，这才逐渐意识到，自己早已不再是那个渴望新鲜感、想去不同地方生活的年少模样，如今更渴望的是一个可以安定下来的家。

然而即便如此，自己没有绿卡，自身处境愈发窘迫。看着主人公刚刚搬进前任男友家时的整个房间色调偏灰，而且她前任没有给她留下更多属于她自己的个人空间，给人一种压抑的感觉，我不由得想起了自己身处于狭小的单人间，抑郁焦虑的情绪日益加重。此前经历了一场失恋，使此刻的心情更显沉重，仿佛所有积压的情绪都在这一刻倾泻而出。

主人公后来的生活越来越好，开始有自己的房子了，也后来有了理解自己又不会把自己的荣誉奖项放在床底下的伴侣，开始了幸福的同居生活；那大概就是我梦寐以求的爱情和安稳生活吧。反观自己，最近诸事不顺，生活和感情完全没有起色，又没有任何人能够理解自己并给予自己特别需要的支持。通关时我的泪水却不停的掉下来。自己的未来不知何从何去。

回头一看，每次搬家好像没带什么重要的东西，带上的几乎都是自己需要用上的，对自己而言最有纪念意义的事物，无非还是高中生时在国内买的一对耳环，如果没有在酒吧和恋人约会时不慎掉落一只耳环的话，那一对耳环如今肯定会整整齐齐地躺在首饰盒里。

过去在祖父母家时，我见过一堆“古董”家具：笨重的木质抽屉桌、老式衣柜、泛着旧色的褐色行李箱，里面放的都是他们年轻时的衣物。我曾问过他们可不可以把它们扔掉，比较占空间，得到的回应却是“那是爷爷奶奶最重要的回忆，不能扔掉”。如今看着自己身边拥有的旧物并不多，房间里仍然留着重要的人赠送的一些礼物，更加能够理解祖父母即便搬家几次，仍然保留对于旧日时光的美好回忆的心态。

原谅我这篇略显杂乱的小作文，只是情感涌动，有感而发。旅美生活何时才会结束，何时才能拥有一个真正属于自己的家？这些问题，或许只有未来的我才能回答。

"Unpacking" is not what I expected. I thought it was going to be a 'cozy' puzzle game where you move into a room, arranging your belongs to suit your tastes. And, well, I guess it is that, mostly. What I didn't expect was that it would also tell a subtle tale through its mechanics.

Because in "Unpacking", you aren't unpacking YOUR belongings. You're doing the moving for a faceless and nameless protagonist and, in doing so, learning about her likes and life. You pick up quickly that she enjoyed art as a child and she played tabletop role-playing games in college. You can tell her first serious relationship isn't going to end well when her partner gives her practically no room for her belongings. You realize she's made it as an illustrator of a children's book when you unpack a half-dozen copies of the same volume. The game doesn't tell you any of this directly; it only hints at it through what belongings she keeps and discards through her various moves. It's actually rather touching (if a bit voyeuristic).

It's not much of an actual game, though. There's a slight bit of puzzling to it; there's only limited space where you can put all the items, and certain items are only allowed in certain rooms (roach poison, for instance, has to be put in the kitchen). You're still given a lot of leeway, however, and it's never really difficult (the only part that caused me any hardship was figuring out where to put the protagonist's diploma in her 'first relationship' move; there was no available wallspace to hang the thing. The answer was to hide it under the bed. Like I said, that relationship wasn't going to last). It's also not a very long game; I finished it in around two or three hours. You can add some longevity to the gameplay by finding the item combinations that unlock the various achievements, but even then I can't imagine it'd give you more than a couple hours extra.

Personally, I would have preferred --and was expecting-- something a bit more sandboxed and puzzley; an opportunity to make these rooms more 'mine'. Still, even if it wasn't quite the game I wanted, neither can I say I was disappointed with the experience. It was clever, it was sweet and it didn't overstay its welcome. It was an unexpected surprise and while I can't imagine I'll ever play it again, neither am I sorry I spent the few hours I did with the game. It was a nice change of pace from my usual.

[h1][b]ANÁLISIS DE [i]UNPACKING[/i]:[/b][/H1]

La inmensa mayoría de personas hemos vivido a lo largo de nuestra vida una o varias mudanzas. Ya sea porque por el trabajo de nuestros padres hemos tenido que abandonar el hogar donde nacimos y crecimos, por un divorcio, por problemas económicos; por mejorar nuestra situación y poder vivir en un lugar mejor; por independizarnos; por irnos a vivir con nuestra pareja; por comprar una casa más grande porque vamos a ser padres...

Las mudanzas siempre suponen un momento importante en nuestras vidas, ya sea por un buen motivo o por una mala experiencia. No consiste solo en mover nuestras cosas de un lugar a otro, se trata de un nuevo comienzo en otro lugar, acompañados de los bienes materiales más útiles y a los que más aprecio les tenemos, dejando atrás los demás.

Es precisamente de esto de lo que trata Unpacking. Tendremos como objetivo desempaquetar todas las cajas de las mudanzas que vamos a realizar a lo largo de nuestra vida. Con esta sencilla pero original misión, nos cuenta una bonita historia a lo largo de los años. A continuación, os cuento con más detalle.

[h1]Argumento:[/h1] (no contiene spoilers)

En Unpacking no se nos narra una historia de la forma convencional. En su lugar, la tendremos que ir descubriendo e imaginándola mediante los objetos que vamos viendo. Por ejemplo, podremos descubrir el sexo de nuestro personaje viendo el tipo de ropa que usa, la etapa de vida en la que se encuentra, las cosas a las que le tiene más aprecio porque las ha conservado con el paso de los años, las que ha dejado atrás conforme ha ido madurando, sus gustos y aficiones... esta original fórmula de contarnos la historia y de hacer que nos sintamos identificados en etapas de nuestra vida al ver los escenarios y los diferentes objetos. Esto hará que surja la nostalgia, siendo sin duda el punto fuerte de Unpacking.

[h1]Jugabilidad:[/h1]

El manejo es muy ameno y sencillo. Todo se maneja con el ratón (también se puede usar mando, aunque no lo he probado aún). Simplemente hacemos clic sobre las cajas y se abrirán, y de cada una de ellas tendremos que ir sacando los objetos que hay que colocar en cada una de las estancias que se nos muestren. Cada nivel representa un año, una etapa de nuestra vida. Desde nuestra niñez hasta la madurez, viendo pasar una vida y su evolución por delante de nuestros ojos. 

Al final se trata de un juego de bloques en el que podemos "decorar" la casa, pero solo hasta cierto punto porque a la hora de pasarnos los niveles tendremos que colocar los objetos en lugares donde tengan sentido. Este es uno de los problemas que le veo al juego, y es que aunque coloquemos las cosas en sitios donde podrían ir perfectamente, el juego las detecta como erróneas, teniendo que buscar otro lugar que considere correcto. Una vez lo finalicemos si podremos colocar las cosas a nuestro antojo. 

El juego puede parecer que es solo para relajarse, pero en ocasiones ese supuesto relax puede convertirse en agobio al ver que hay muy poco espacio y muchos objetos por colocar, quedando todo el escenario excesivamente sobrecargado en ocasiones y pudiendo generar estrés en el jugador (como ha sido mi caso, que a veces soy algo maniático con el orden de ciertas cosas e igualmente desordenado para otras xD)

[h1]Gráficos:[/h1]

Unpacking tiene gráficos 2D de estilo pixel art con vista isométrica, con unos diseños muy simpáticos y agradables. Escenarios detallados que fácilmente podrían recordarnos a habitaciones y lugares en los que hemos vivido. Podemos girar los objetos para verlos y colocarlos de la forma que nosotros queramos, pero los escenarios son estáticos. De haberse podido ver desde distintos ángulos habría sido mejor, aunque no es algo que se eche especialmente en falta. 

[h1]Sonido:[/h1]

La banda sonora corre a cargo de Jeff van Dyck, con melodías muy agradables y amenas que sonarán de fondo mientas desempacamos, pudiendo cambiarlas por las que suenan en las radios disponibles en los niveles. El problema de este apartado es que hay tramos en los que la música acaba y se queda un largo silencio hasta que comienza de nuevo, a no ser que vayamos a posta a encender antes una radio. Esto me ha parecido un error de bulto, porque aunque los sonidos al abrir las cajas, mover y colocar los objetos están muy conseguidos, además de tener mucha variedad, el silencio de fondo se siente extraño hasta que comienza de nuevo la melodía, que es en gran parte la "culpable" de que jugar Unpacking sea una experiencia que puede llegar a ser emotiva. 

Tenéis la banda sonora completa de Unpacking disponible en el siguiente enlace de Spotify:  [url=https://open.spotify.com/intl-es/album/546P1fkMWTbVjeCMivORqf?si=5RqoNSrxQ_WsoEFqJFQrPg]Banda sonora de Unpacking[/url]

Mi lista de pros y contras a modo de resumen:

[H1][b]PROS:[/b][/H1]

- La estética Pixel Art

- La original forma de contarnos la historia

- Ideal para la gente a la que le gusta tener todo ordenado hasta el extremo

- La banda sonora es muy buena

- Puede llegar a ser un juego muy nostálgico

- Es muy entretenido y ameno

- Traducido al español

- Tiene logros Steam

- Tiene cromos y artículos en la tienda de puntos de Steam

- Tiene guardado de la partida en la nube Steam Cloud

- Se puede conseguir bastante barato en páginas de claves

[H1][b]CONTRAS:[/b][/H1]

- Algunos objetos no se reconocen demasiado bien, poniéndonos más complicado saber donde ubicarlos

- Se puede hacer repetitivo demasiado pronto

- Hay muchos momentos en los que no hay música de fondo, tarda demasiado en arrancar de nuevo

- Aunque puede parecer un juego para relajarse, en mi opinión a veces es estresante y agobiante ver todos los escenarios tan sobrecargados de objetos y sin demasiado espacio donde colocarlos

- Su precio me parece elevado para lo que ofrece, especialmente por su corta duración, solo recomendaría su compra de oferta muy rebajado o en alguna página de keys baratas

[H1]Conclusión:[/h1]
------------------------

Un juego precioso a nivel audiovisual y con un planteamiento muy original. Muy recomendable si te llama la atención la propuesta, eso sí, recomiendo comprarlo solo de oferta ya que su precio habitual me parece elevado para lo que ofrece dada su corta duración.

書籍やゲームの内容が分かる、何を表彰してもらった盾なのか分かる、ノートの中がのぞき見れる、誰の服や靴なのか区別がつく、など、持ち主の性格や思い入れが物からもっと見て取れると良かったなと思う。
国による生活様式の違いで戸惑うのは面白さの一つではある。

[h1]Intro[/h1]
Have you ever moved somewhere else? Or maybe having a habit to reorganize your items several times because of your OCD? [b]Unpacking[/b] can give you that sense of satisfaction by playing it. The game starts as you, someone who just moved to a new house, that need to unpack their items and move them to the appropriate places.

[b]Pros:[/b]
- 8 levels
- Place the items however you want - there are more than one solutions to finish the level

[b]Cons:[/b]
- Some items can be unrecognizable to some people
- You can't move some existing items in one level

[b]Specs[/b]
Intel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650

[h1]Should you buy this game?[/h1]
[b]Yes.[/b]
[i]If you like either to reorganize stuff or simply want to play casual games, buy this game.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h1]In-Depth Review[/h1]

[h3]Visuals[/h3]
Despite using pixelated graphics, [b]Unpacking[/b] doesn't look like a pixelated game at all. It uses a high pixel count, making everything looks smooth at first glance. The shading is done in such a way as to conceal the pixels between the lines. Moreover, environments are varied between each level with numerous items ranging from big and small. The thing is, everything was made in great detail to make it look like the real thing. I couldn't praise the visuals enough for this.

[h3]Story[/h3]
To be honest, the only dialogues that you will see from the game are the one-liners that will be told after completing a level. Levels are spread between several years, indicating a person's life over the years. New items will be brought in after each level, and the old ones will either be replaced or kept. If you have ever watched [b]Toy Story[/b], the game gives a similar vibe to it. You can see the character growing up, leaving all their toys behind except for the ones that they hold dear. It gives some sort of heartwarming feeling to me, especially when you see recurrence items coming out from the boxes. My favorite is the chicken dolls - they always multiply.

[h3]The Game[/h3]
[b]Gameplay[/b]
The game is played just like how the title spells out. You just moved to a new place, and you need to unpack your items to the appropriate places. You have to open card boxes, taking out the items inside until there is nothing left. Each level will take place in more than one location, allowing you to switch between them to put items in other places if necessary. Each location will also have its own card boxes and sets of items, and it's your job to organize them all. The good thing is, you are free to place them wherever and however you want.

Despite your freedom, some items couldn't be placed in a certain place. I mean, you can't place a PC in a bathtub, can you? Well, you actually can, but the game will check the item placements after you take out all items and mark the improperly placed items with red marking. You need to reposition them to the appropriate places to finish the levels.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2647453665

Stacking mechanics make it easy to move some items. You can either place books standing up or lying down, and the game supports both options in its own way. You can put a book in a standing up position between two other books without taking them out, and you also can take out an item stack as one object. This makes it easy to reorganize the items, especially since there are a lot of books to place.

Some objects are just unrecognizable. I'm not sure whether it's because of cultural differences or not, but some items aren't making sense to me. Since I couldn't figure out the items' names nor their use, I ended up brute-forcing these items by placing them in every location that I could find, hoping that the game will accept it. I still don't know what those plier-like items or labeled boxes are, but at least I know where they should be located.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2647453708

[b]Photo Mode[/b]
One of the good things about the game is that you can take photos of your current screen. There are a lot of effects, ranging from simple outlines, filters, and even stickers. While the first two can be used right away, some stickers will need to be unlocked before it is usable. The unlocking requirement is usually simple and tied to an achievement, so you don't have to worry much about it.

[b]Length and Difficulty[/b]
Sadly, the game is very short. I finished all 8 levels in 3.5h and spent an extra 0.1h to get the last remaining achievements. The game isn't hard apart from some unrecognizable objects that you need to place in the correct position. Some levels also have a lot of items that you need to place, and I admit that my solution was kinda messy. I wasn't quite satisfied with how they turned out since I felt like shoving everything in just to finish the levels. Some people might want to spend more time fixing their solutions and making them look better.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2649150452

[b]Problems[/b]
There is one level where you couldn't reposition some pre-placed items. Moreover, you can't swap the same items. It takes longer to organize some items because of this.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
[b]Unpacking[/b] is a casual game for OCD people at its core. You need to love reorganizing items to appreciate them, and the presentation makes it easy to get lost in thoughts. I didn't realize that three hours has passed when I played the game because of the game's slow pacing. Moreover, you don't have to worry about a time limit or anything - you just need to focus on what you want to do. The game doesn't seem to overstay its welcome either. To be honest, I was about to get bored playing the game, but it ends itself soon after.

I could recommend this game to those who enjoy reorganizing items. However, the game is very short, so you might want to either buy it at a sale or play it in [url=https://www.xbox.com/en-US/xbox-game-pass][i]Xbox Game Pass[/i][/url] for a lower price. You don't have to worry about the game's quality though - its presentation surely won't disappoint.

This is a cute and enjoyable experience. It's nice to see the different ways people tackle a common task and something that would normally be a chore is turned into a fun and nearly exciting little game with its fun music and charming art style. For the 3 hours that it lasted, it was definitely interesting to unbox someone's life and perceive a story through their belongings.

However, this game is unfortunately overpriced. While I can always appreciate smaller developers joining the scene, it is also important to know how much an experience is worth. While captivating and intriguing, this game also offers minimal repeatability and does not provide an unforgettable time. The most notable feature of this game is the fact that it is unique, but would otherwise quickly lose it's charm the more that it is explored; especially as a genre.

I do recommend this game as it can be very fun for a marginally definite group of people, but for myself do I not believe it to be worth the amount I paid or the experience it provided. That being said, cool game!

[h1]《Unpacking》——将生活联系，游戏亦为生活[/h1]

[h1]走出“动”来到“静”[/h1]
如果游戏也可以划分动态与静态，那么我想时下主流的游戏大多数都是以[b]“动态”[/b]为主的，多数玩家喜欢动辄刀光剑影血脉喷张的激烈战斗，而我也不例外，我得承认这样风格的游戏更深得玩家欢心。

在这种游戏内，玩家并不需要思考太多，只要消灭挡在前路敌人就好了，它并没有太多弯弯绕绕，所带给玩家的也是极致的动态享受；
玩家虽然不是一刻也不曾停歇，但是基本不是在战斗中就是在前往战斗的路上，在这种高密集高集中的战斗玩家的感觉和感情都被充分调动了起来，身心的注意力也基本都在游戏上，脑海中除了当前游戏的内容或许也想不了其他。
在每一场战斗中，玩家所思考的也是游戏内如何巧妙躲避化解敌人的招式，如何见招拆招战胜敌人，游戏内的动态表现与游戏外的玩家形成了良好的呼应，此时，玩家也是动态的。
我们因为战斗的胜利而喜悦感到爽感，战斗的失败也会产生急切好胜的心情，动态的意味是调动玩家的心神与游戏内协同和一，游戏随玩家而动，玩家亦随游戏而行。
说完动态，那么静态是什么？走进本作，我们或许可以寻找到答案。

[h1]光阴流转于一屋之内[/h1]
在初次进入游戏，我想在很多玩家的心底就已经埋下了名为[b]“联系”[/b]的种子。

[h1]1997年[/h1]的房间是一个面积不大的儿童房，这里的布局是如此简单，仅仅只有书桌、柜子与床铺，但是从当我们从箱子中拿出一件件东西时我们会发现屋内需要摆放归置的东西是如此多，虽然多但是却基本只有两类——玩乐和学习；
除了这两种用途的东西我们很难找到别的用途的东西了，翻出来的玩具和布偶就连展柜也放不下，甚至要放到床上乃至是塞到角落里，随手丢在一边的书包更极了小时候放学回家的自己。
这是一个充满童趣的房间，或许这些无法引起太多共鸣，但是至少在安放这些物品的一瞬间我想到自己小时候屋子内也总是有着收纳不完的玩具。

[h1]2004年[/h1]女主已经进入大学了，与之前的房间内的布置相比如今的房间布置更多透露出一种朴素，虽然仍可以看出一些房间内独有的元素，但是整体看去朴实且无华就是最准确的形容词了。
厨房和独卫，都让我们明白女主是独自租房在外，离家在外，一个人远行东西并不能全部带走，女主已经长大，向着合格的成年人靠拢。

[h1]2007年[/h1]的房间已经变得成熟很多了，这里的房间干净整洁，一切东西都放在它应在的位置，这是一个让人挑不出毛病的房间，但是这里唯独少了童趣。
一个儿童的房间不应该是干净整洁的，或者说喜欢乱摆乱放是小孩的天性，而如今的房间已经明确的告诉我们女主是一个合格的成年人了。

[h1]2010年[/h1]我们搬进了一个新房子，不同于狭小的出租屋在这里空间很大。仅可布置的双人床也说明我们并非一人居住。
我们不再独处，或者说在自己的房间内不再是一个人居住，房子虽大，但零碎的东西很多，女主还是很恋旧，带着自己布偶娃娃、玩具以及儿童读物来到了这里。
但是在此处，这些东西却显得那么格格不入。
这里太规矩了，没有多余的颜色，家里的摆放和公司的桌台如出一辙，整洁且一丝不苟，两种相反元素碰撞的结果是显而易见的，女主离开了这里，带着自己的童真与梦想。

[h1]2012年[/h1]再次回到了最开始的家，小屋的样子也和原来不同，这里不再只有玩具和学习用的纸笔；尽管墙纸还是原来的颜色，屋内很多的玩具也是最初的模样，但是当收拾好了一切，我们发现印象中的房间好像没有这么小，房间在变，我们也在变。
曾经熟悉的地方却有了一丝陌生的感觉。

[h1]2013年[/h1]女主还是离开了最初的小屋，搬进了一个新的房屋内；
带着失意与痛苦女主回到了过去，如今带着梦想与未来女主选择了新的开始。

[h1]2015年[/h1]还是居住在13年的房子，不同的是这里迎来的新的主人，女主再次有了伴侣，从这一刻此处不仅是艺术与梦想之家，更是心灵的避风港；
对比10年居住的同居房我们可以明显看出不同，在物品摆放上几乎处于一个很契合的状态，他们爱好相符，性格互补，生活在一起也会擦除不同的别样的火花。

[h1]2018年[/h1]来到了最后一栋房子，这次的房子很大，是一栋别墅。
除去常规的卧室书房客厅，这次还多了婴儿房。
是的，15年搬进来的新室友与女主一直相处到了现在，他们搬进了新房子，生活也进入了新的篇章，一切是如此美好，阳光依旧。

通关游戏，布置如此多的房间，我最大的感受是游戏带给我的[b]联系感；[/b]
将物品一一摆放，放置在合理的位置，这一种简单的动作想必每个人都进行过无数次，在平常的生活中这一动作可能并不具有多么深刻的意义，只是一种1+1的机械动作，但是在本作中，游戏赋予了这种行为意义——光阴
在游戏内玩家每一次切换地图，都是去到了一个新家或是处于一个新的时间节点，8间房屋，21年光阴，玩家通关游戏也看尽了主角21年的时光，或许游戏内并没有直接的告诉玩家女主有了怎么样的遭遇，遇到了什么开心的事情或是难过的事情，但是通过屋内的格局变化我们其实都可以看出一二；
最明显的就是每一幕都出现的小猪玩偶，在18年的小猪玩偶已经不复光鲜，他暗淡失色，但是表情不变，一直陪伴了主角21年的时光；
每一次所布置的房间是主角生活历程的缩影，但是也未尝不是屏幕外玩家生活的缩影，主角的21年光阴浓缩在房间的布置变化上，而游戏外的我们生活过的房间同样见证了我们的光阴。

如果不是这款游戏可能我不会去想这些，我也不会去环视了我居住良久的小屋，我不会发现我的桌面上已经没有了玩具的踪影，也不会注意到日渐增多的书籍，更不会想到我已经住了数年之久。
屋内的物品在变，屋内的布局在变，屋内的我也在长大，光阴流转，在一屋之内。
正是这款游戏，让我注意到了这些不经意就会忽略的溜走的事物，写到这里，我明白，静态的游戏就是[b]“创造联系，引发思考[/b]”游戏之内与游戏之外通过玩家搭建了桥梁，玩家感受游戏内的情感变化，在游戏外自己的情感也产生变化，这种奇妙的联系正是[b]“静态游戏”[/b]的独有之道。
Лучшая спокойная игра из тех, что я встречал. Жаль, что очень короткая. Очень хотелось бы продолжения

This game is very cute and heartfelt, I just don't feel that it's worth the price. It's very short, I completed it in about 4 hours; I've gotten more time out of cute little games that cost half the price. I bought this game on sale for $8, which I think aligns more with what you get out of it.
o jogo é bem fofo, porém, acaba muito rápido, não vale 60 reais jamais.

Ignore playtime. I played it in offline mode.

Many will scoff at the $20 price tag but I can see the love and devotion put in the game. Sound design and pixel design isn't easy, even in this day and age. The developers put in a crazy amount of sound effects so that putting items in various areas spots makes a different sound. I would certainly hope the $20 contributes to paying the developers, sound artists, and graphic artists a a good wage for their effort in this.

The game is charming and relaxing. The only complaint that I have about the game is that it's short. I certainly would love to see more, as in a different story with different items or something similar to that. The game can be a little finicky when it comes to the placement of different items but it's not hard to figure it out where it needs to go. But sometimes it can feel like it's a bit of a puzzle game to ensure that you're arranging things properly so that everything has its place.

If you're a stickler for organization, there's certainly a chance that you're playing the game a lot longer than average, but it will certainly tickle your categorizing/organizing fancy.

If you enjoy incredible pixel art, this game is for you.
If you're looking for something relaxing and laid back, this game is for you.
If you like organizing and arranging, this game is for you.

To me, it's worth the price. Especially if it means that there's an opportunity for more of this game or a sequel or something. I just want more of this!

All in all 8.5/10

[h1]何とも不思議な感覚が湧いてくるゲーム[/h1]
流れとしては段ボールに荷物が入った状態からスタートして、荷解きして物を部屋に配置する、というもので、単純にパズルゲームとしての要素はステージが進むにつれて部屋数が増え、部屋にあるべき物をあるべき所に配置していくだけで難易度はそれほど高くはない。基本的に荷物はその部屋に置くものが入っていて、時々違う部屋に置く荷物が紛れている事もあるのだが、違っている場合はアイテムがハイライトされるので試行錯誤すればいずれクリアできるだろう。

このゲームを特別なものにしているのは、荷解きを通じて持ち主がどのような人物でどのような人生を歩んできたのかに思いをはせた時にそれは起こる。本棚を見ればとその人がわかるというが、ステージが進むことで数年が経過し、次のライフステージに移った時にどんな荷物が増え、どんな荷物がなくなったのか、自分が引っ越しした時と比べてなにが違って違わないのか。その時生まれる存在しない（もしくはプレイヤー自身の）記憶。
「このゲームについて」で語られるように「直接目にすることもないキャラクターと親密になり、耳にしたこともない物語に触れたように感じられ」たときに、このゲーム体験は特別なものになる。

ちなみに私は部屋が片付けられないので、部屋の片付け経験を積むためにこのゲームを買ったのだが、段々と主人公の父親のような感覚が湧いてきて、「娘を持つ父親はこんな感じなのか～」と思っていたところ、とある展開によって脳が破壊されるような感覚を味わった。世の中の娘を持つお父さんは大変だ。

ボリュームは4～5時間くらいでちょっと物足りない。難易度は前述の通り難しくない。
希望としてはDLCで別の主人公の物語もやりたいな。
It's a nice game, but I recommend getting it on sale as there is not that much content (4h playtime).

You open a box, I open my heart >< 喜欢！老虎和小猪排排坐，冰箱贴和游戏卡带越买越多，带密码锁的日记本放在枕头下面，绿植第一次出现在屋子里，会有人欣然接纳你的爱好...一间只属于自己的房间...一面终于可以挂上你学位证的墙。

收拾的时候也逐渐认识“我”，了解“我”，读过的书，去过的地方，曾经的爱好。每一次打开箱子看到“我”还留有小时候的玩具or物品都会心一笑xD 真好！完全没料到游戏会是这样的展开，之前以为只是普通的收纳小游戏。难怪之前很多v都在播这个，超级适合跟朋友边聊边玩！！

《Unpacking》是一个比较独特的休闲游戏。

标题就是游戏的核心玩法：unpacking，就是将为了搬家而装箱的物品取出，布置在自己的新家当中。没错，就是字面意思，没有什么拐弯抹角，没有什么twists and turns，你要做的就是将各种各样的东西放在你觉得应该放的地方，桌子上、柜子里、窗台上......你不仅需要考虑搭配不同物品和各个房间的功能，还得考虑物品占用的面积、体积，能不能塞得进各种容具，就和现实中的家政一样。

虽然游戏在玩家具体收拾的方式上面，没有过多要求，不过你也不能乱放，游戏还是会检查一下是不是有东西放在了不该放的地方，或者压根没有整理，比如乱扔在地上等。除了比较大的错误之外，游戏应该都是允许的，自由度还是有的。确实是比较独特的一个玩法，虽然没什么“深度”和“挑战”，但作为主打“禅意”的一个休闲游戏而言，本作还是能达到放松的效果的。当然，东西怎么都塞不下，逼死强迫症的瞬间也不是没有，不过大体上还是算休闲了。

本作还有一个比较独特的地方在于对一种新鲜叙事方式的尝试。在游戏剧情中，玩家并不是在扮演自己，而是有一个“主角”，玩家只是以一个可交互的视角，观察这名有着自己的生活的主角所经历的数次搬家。游戏中从没有任何对话，而且几乎没有任何文本，玩家只能根据新家的状况，以及主角的各种生活物品，来推测主角的喜好和生活经历。

这种叙事方式并不常规，甚至能不能说它是一个“故事”，我觉得都还是有争议的，但它确实给玩家表现出了一种别样的感觉。每次搬家，都意味着主角的生活进入了一个崭新的阶段，而玩家通过观察“搬家”这种两个阶段之间的衔接，就能体会到主角生活的种种变化。从主角选择将哪些物品带到新家，哪些又没有，玩家可以看出主角珍视什么，又想放下什么。从新增的物品中又可以看出，主角有了新的爱好，新的人际关系，等等。就和本作商店页面所说的一样，在本作的过程中，玩家从来都没有见过这所谓的“主角”哪怕一面，但却可以通过“搬家”这种方式，对主角产生某种“亲密感”。

不过说到底，你要说本作的故事“平淡”，我也是同意的。本作所描绘的是一个普通人普通的生活中若干细微的切片，采取的又是这种比什么“侧面描写”、“碎片化叙事”都要微妙的叙事方式，确实和一般游戏叙事差距太大了，不是所有人都能接受和理解这种看上去什么也没说的表达方式，这也不是任何人的问题。

总而言之，本作在它的定位上做得是不错的。不过价格确实有点贵了，加上本作也不是那种有大量游戏内容，能够给人带来什么兴奋、刺激的游戏，所以建议入手时好好考虑本作的定位和你的期望匹不匹配。

结论：[b]可以推荐[/b]，建议打折时购买。

[h1]С любимыми (вещами) не расставайтесь![/h1]
Сюжет игры повествует о том, как маленькая девочка постепенно взрослеет и переезжает из дома в дом. Сначала она получает собственную комнату в родительском доме, потом переезжает в общежитие университета. И, в конце концов, получает профессию и приобретает собственный дом, куда и переезжает вместе со своей семьей. И всё это время она не расстается со своими любимыми вещами - игрушками, книгами, безделушками и игровыми консолями, которые она бережно хранит всю свою жизнь.

Основная и единственная механика игры - разложить все предметы после переезда по своим местам. Для этого нужно распаковать коробки и разместить определённые предметы в определённых комнатах. Например, туалетную бумагу в туалете, а одежду в гардеробе или плательном шкафу. В основном, коробки с предметами находятся в правильных комнатах, но в них могут быть предметы и из других комнат. Узнать, какой предмет соответствует какой комнате не особо сложно. Но, если он будет расположен неправильно (не в той комнате или не на своём месте), то, после распаковки всех предметов, неправильно расположенные предметы будут подсвечены красным и их нужно будет расположить правильно, чтобы перейти на следующий уровень игры.

[b]Плюсы игры:[/b]
[list]
    [*]Приятная пиксельная графика
    [*]Приятный саундтрек
    [*]Медитативный и неторопливый геймплей.
[/list]

[b]Минусы игры:[/b]
[list]
    [*]Некоторая нелогичность расположения предметов. Например, некоторые предметы обязательно должны находится в шкафчиках, а другие, наоборот, на полочках.
    [*]Относительно короткий сюжет, который продолжается лишь до взросления главной героини. Хотелось бы проследить её судьбу до самой старости и смерти. А, затем, продолжить игру уже в качестве её ребёнка.
[/list]

[spoiler][b]Особые моменты:[/b]
[list]
    [*]С тех пор, как в доме главной героини появилась вторая зубная щётка, я ждал появления мужской одежды, но этого не случилось. Зато, увеличилось количество женской одежды. И, даже, после появления детской комнаты, этого не произошло. И, только после прохождения игры, авторы дали понять, что она живёт с другой женщиной.
    [*]Радость для фетишистов - в игре можно раскладывать женское белье (трусики, чулки, бюстгальтеры). Только они свёрнутые и их нельзя развернуть и рассмотреть, как следует.
[/list][/spoiler]

[b]Что по итогу?[/b]
Приятная расслабляющая игра, которая проходится за несколько часов.

非常好游戏，建议所有喜欢找点活干然后放空想事情的人来买，感觉在东西慢慢被整理好的时候，我也在其中吸收了精神能量，我称之为阳光游戏。

В целом впечатление полного проходняка. 
Кратко, что ожидалось и получили (имхо):
- ламповая музыка // скучная надоедливая мелодия.
- интересная история // пустые комментарии к фотографиям комнаты ни о чём.
- несколько дней игры // 2 часа активной игры.
- возможность расставлять вещи, как тебе угодно // некоторые вещи уже стоят зафиксированно в квартире, и из-за них общий вид комнаты неопрятный.
- милые и уютные вещички // ГОРЫ МУСОРА, которую героиня перевозит с собой из года в год в разные места обитания.
- отдельно убило, как эта женщина собирает коробки при переезде - зачем миксовать обувь, посуду и книжки в одной коробке? Что это за чушь?

По суперскидке можно купить игру, позалипать.
А я буду мечтать о модах, в которых можно было бы избавиться от всех плюшевых игрушек и прочего мусора, который скопился на полках, чтобы не приходилось перевозить его из одной квартиры в другую.

Увидела превью игры за пару месяцев до выхода и не могла дождаться, когда же можно будет испытать себя. Ожидалось нечто ламповое, но на деле мои ожидания не оправдались. Музыку под такую рисовку можно было бы подобрать более уютную, в итоге играла под свою, потому что в игре она никакая. Обещанная история... А есть ли она? Да, все усмотрели, что девушка жила с парнем, а потом начала жить с другой девушкой, но понятно это только по вещам - при создании "снимка" готовой комнаты пишут лишь пару общих фраз со впечатлениями героини, вроде "Круто иметь собственную ванную!". Но что заставило её это сделать? Без причин и последствия не так уж интересны.

Разочаровало количество контента, казалось, что три альбома - это три истории (или три части одной истории). По факту - нет, игру можно пройти за пару часов.

Я люблю переезжать и обожаю раскладывать вещи так, чтобы они занимали меньше места. Но эта игра была настоятельно против порядка. Почему, почему освежитель воздуха должен торчать на бачке для унитаза, почему его нельзя поставить на пол?
Более того, главная героиня - та ещё мусорщица. Большую часть вещей хотелось выкинуть, а не расставлять по полкам, уже начиная с первого уровня. Ну хорошо, в 1997 она ребенок - но потом, учитывая её количество мусора, она выбирает максимально неподходящую мебель. Например, в ванной к концу игры - открытая полка - пожалуйста, складируйте годовой запас тампонов, аптечку и прочие малопривлекательные предметы в самом видном месте. И проблема была бы даже не в том, что это выглядит неопрятно - эти вещи же ещё и пылиться будут!

Непонятно, почему книжки можно ставить вертикально, а коробку с пластырем - нет.

Некоторые вещи поразили своим "правильным" расположением - ощущение, будто разработчики сами имеют весьма далекое представление о порядке.

Больше всего не понравилось, что по завершению уровня нужно в каждой комнате отдельно щёлкать на звезду, чтобы прочитать комментарий героини, потом возвращаться в квартиру, переходить в другую комнату, снова переходить в альбом и т.д. Когда количество комнат подбирается к 10, это раздражающе скучное занятие, учитывая, что комментарии ничего интересного не рассказали.

И уровни, в которых нельзя менять расположение уже поставленных предметов, просто убивают - если они лежат неудачно, то прочие предметы, разложенные аккуратно, всё равно не смогут воссоздать полноценный уют.

Unpacking is one of the most relaxing and surprisingly emotional games I’ve played.
Just finished it 100% and every achievement felt natural to get while going through each move.

The storytelling is beautiful without using a single line of dialogue you learn about someone’s entire life just by placing their things. The sound design, little details, and cozy atmosphere make every room feel personal.

It’s short, meaningful, satisfying, and perfect if you want something calm but still memorable.

Easily a 10/10 experience.

敘事方法很新穎，透過搬家物品的擺放來不斷認識主角的各種方面，短短幾句話見證了主角從幼年到步入婚姻殿堂。

但說真的，這樣隱晦的敘事給不了玩家多少感動，更何況這其實算是一段平鋪直敘的故事，遊玩的時候擺放也不是隨玩家自由，時常會有系統限制的情況出現，像是書包不能放地上，書本不能放床上之類的，連遊戲機想擺在電視上的櫃子都不行，一定得擺在電視下的櫃子，坦白講有時候會玩到有點煩，因為他只提示你不能放這，但不會跟你說要放哪，有些具體上看不出到底是什麼作用的物品就需要在各個場景各個地方不停嘗試，我洗衣籃就是想放洗手檯旁邊，硬要我放在洗衣機前面是怎樣。

總之算是一款平淡的小品遊戲，美術相當出色，但背景音樂時常播著播著就消失，剛覺得要沉浸到遊戲世界卻又被無BGM跟惱人的強制擺放提示打斷。
特價八折之後算是還能接受的價格，但個人覺得200以下的價格比較合乎這遊戲的內容。

Ждала эту игру с нетерпением после прохождения демки. Когда она только вышла, то я быстро прошла и расстроилась, что очень коротко, хоть и предполагала, что так будет. А также очень раздражало то, что не могу расположить предметы там, где хочу.. Но Боже, я очень рада, что уже после второго прохождение мое мнение начало меняться в ещё более положительную сторону. Прошла раз 7-8, мало того, что это очень расслабляет и мне не надоедает расставлять вещи, так я ещё и с каждым прохождением узнавала что-то новое. Многое можно нажать, включить, открыть, многое можно было повесить, а не просто поставить и так далее. Также по предметам и записям главной героини в альбоме с каждым прохождением я больше понимала увлечения, привычки и жизнь персонажей. Это было очень увлекательно и интересно, я не видела похожих игр. Кстати, оказывается и элемент "головоломки" можно убрать в настройках, т.е можно расставлять предметы так, как ТЫ хочешь и где хочешь, никаких ограничений. Я благодарю разработчиков за эту прекрасную, милую игру и за мои положительные эмоции. С песни вообще в слезы каждый раз. Я очень жду новых ДЛС и проектов от этой студии <3

Sadece yerleştirmek gibi temel bir mekaniği kullanarak yapılmış bir oyun olmasıyla çok enteresan bir narative design çalışması olmuş. Oldukça basit duyulmasına karşın eşyaları ve oyuncuya sunduğu yerleştirme imkanlarıyla enine boyuna hayret verici derinlikte bir storytelling karşılıyor sizi. Çok başarılı bir pixel art icrasıyla görselliği, minnoşluğu da azımsanacak gibi değil. Özellikle sound designını taktir etmeden geçmek olmaz, oyundaki her eşyanın her yüzeye temasına karşı çıkardığı ses özenle entegre edilmiş oyuna; bu detaycılığıyla oyunun kurduğu atmosfere kapılmamak elde değil. Bu kadar dar bir alanda böylesine kapsayıcı bir ton kuruşuna oyunun gerçekten hayret ediyorum, çok çok başarılı bulduğum bir çalışma olduğunu söylemem gerek. 
[spoiler] LGBTQ+ inclusive bir işleyişi olması da pastanın kirazı oldu, [/spoiler] oynarken tüm sinirleri yumuşuyor valla insanın. Etrafı yerleştirmenin verdiği bir verimlilik hissinden, fulfillmentten kaçamıyorsunuz; instant dopamin gibi bir etkisi oldu benim için.
Farmsim, lifesim gibi layout planlamanın oyunun büyük bir parçası olduğu oyunlardan hoşlanıyorsanız ama bu tarz oyunların yeterince "kişisel" olmadığını düşünüyorsanız ya da point and click puzzle oyunlarında sürekli bir etrafı toparlama isteğindeyseniz kesinlikle şans vermeniz gereken bir oyun. Eşyaların customize edilememesi, her eşyayı her yere koyamama gibi tilt edici durumlar olsa da oyunun vaatlerini oldukça başarılı bir şekilde karşıladığını düşünüyorum. Hatta custom designing vadeden birçok oyuna kıyasla yerleştirme olanakları daha geniş; eşyaları stackleyebilme, üst üste koyma, rafa dizme derken hareket alanı beni çok mutlu etti. Yer yer bir puzzle oyunu olduğunu size unutturuyor, oyuncuya içeride atadığı kimlik gerçekten çok kuvvetli. Genre olarak biraz gri bir bölgeye parmak basıyor, bu tarz örneklerin devamını görebilmek dileğiyle...
Gerçekten iç ısıtan dev bir minnoşluk...

Unpacking is a charming and relaxing game with a simple yet satisfying concept: you unpack boxes and organize a new living space. The art style is lovely, and the sense of progression as you reveal the character’s life through their belongings is surprisingly engaging. It’s a refreshing, low-stress experience that offers moments of nostalgia and personal reflection.

However, despite its unique premise and soothing gameplay, the price of £15.49 feels unreasonable for the amount of content. The game is quite short, with a playthrough that can be completed in just a few hours. Given its brevity, it’s hard to justify the full price, and I would recommend waiting for a sale or picking it up when the price drops to a more reasonable £5-8 range. While the game’s concept is fun, the short duration means it may not offer enough long-term value for the asking price.
