 1) Due to it being pixel art, occasionally you can’t tell what something is, and it complains that the object isn’t in a valid location, and of course you have no idea where it goes. So you have to place it in random spots until the game is happy with the placement. I don’t find that fun or relaxing.
 2) The lack of precision for item placement. Everything goes on an invisible grid. And sometimes that leads to frustrating things like:  Cookie sheets cannot be stored on their side, and the only thing you can stack on them are other cookie sheets. Or a pot with its handle, the handle sticking out in a way that takes up a huge portion of the shelf. You can’t turn it slightly so it takes less space. No, it must waste a huge amount of space. There are little frustrating things like that all through out the game.

So while overall it was interesting, and I like how it kind of tells a story without directly telling a story. But the little frustrations stop me from being able to recommend this.

Generally, it's a nice story that I haven't seen anywhere else. Over all, the game has a puzzle element that I haven't seen implemented in this way before, and it is intriguing. I may not highly recommend this game, but given my option of recommend or not, I'd say it's better to have it in your Library than to watch the experience second hand (especially since it's a puzzle game and the way that the pieces are placed is up to the individual playing). 剧情方面，游戏中除了片尾cg没有出现任何角色，因此也没有人物对白出现，每关完成时会有简短的旁白。
不过即便没有多少文字出现在游戏里，我们依旧能从家具中一点点拼凑出主角的人设：她应该是一个喜欢运动、阅读、弹吉他[spoiler]还是贝斯来着[/spoiler]、玩游戏、养绿植，有一点生活小格调，专业是美术相关还拿过奖的女孩。
游戏剧情衔接非常自然，我们就像主角的这只小猪玩偶一样，陪着她从“开心终于有自己房间”的小女孩逐渐成长为能独当一面的成熟人士。

忘记在第几关了，主角跟男友同居之后，家里的装潢档次一下子上去了，不过整体风格变成了冷色调[spoiler]这种装潢风格适合独居，同居的话太没有生活气息了，除非两个人都很喜欢这种风格，不然建议是避开这种风格[/spoiler]，主角在家里的个人空间也一下子所剩无几，她的很多东西都只能收进柜子里。
而对她来说有着一定重要性的奖状，我几乎找不到可以挂的地方，为了通关只能放在床底了。[spoiler]相信不止我一个人通关之后又把奖状拿出来贴浴室上了[/spoiler]
莫名其妙想到朋友前几天和我说的：“现在同龄朋友结婚，虽然我祝福，但是很难真心觉得结婚这件事是幸福的。”对普通人来说，很难预知步入一段关系之后同居是得到的更多还是失去的更多。只不过住过校的朋友们都知道，个人的自由是一定会在集体住宿中被牺牲掉一部分的。
一段感情如果总是需要一方去委屈求全，割舍掉自己最骄傲的那部分，往往会无疾而终。于是这段曾经在冰箱上都贴不下二人甜蜜合照的恋情以失败告终。
在下一关中，主角搬回了自己的家，昔日与前男友的合照也如同放在床底的奖状一样被收纳进柜子。完成这一关的配文是：“小时候总觉得这间房间很大。”，因为她长大了。

当然这个故事最后还是he的，主角喝冰美式之后交往了新的女朋友[spoiler]开玩笑，主角应该是双性恋[/spoiler]，虽然没太看懂两个人相知相识的过程是怎么样的，但家里的装潢很有生活气息，主角的时尚小垃圾和奖状终于又可以放在显眼的地方了。两个人不知道是试管还是领养了小孩，有一间房间是婴儿房。
完成最后一关出现的cg不再是房间照片，而是——[i][b]她抱着吉他，爱人笑着抱着牙牙学语的小孩子，两个人一起坐在院子里看夕阳下的余晖。[/b][/i]
[h2]生活怎么可能跟谁过都是一样呢？[/h2]
谢谢这个小体量游戏两小时给我带来的放松与温暖。[spoiler]也祝耐心看完这条评测的你生活愉快[/spoiler]

This game is way too small.
I paid A$ 28.95 for a 3 - 4 hour game. You can 100% this game in under 10 hours.
I understand that you can only do so much with such a simple concept, but that still doesn't justify the price-to-gameplay ratio being so low.
It doesn't have a whole lot of replayability either. The concept is neat, and the execution is well done. However it needs much more content to be considered a good game.

I suggest the developers build on the concept a little, maybe double down on the puzzle portion in later levels; perhaps some levels the boxes don't start in their corresponding rooms and you have to figure out where they go. Something like that to add some more content. 
I understand that part of the appeal of this game is that is a casual, time-killer, rather than a puzzle game. However I think it's up to the developers to strike that balance between keeping the game core concepts while also adding some more content to the game.

I feel like I'm ranting at this point, but I'm mostly just mad that I spent $30 on a 5 hour game.

unpacking is among the most subtly profound games i have ever played- and i'm an absolute fiend for story games. the game is so damn cute, the colours and the scenery and the absolute beauty in the simple complexity that is unpacking's pixel art style is something i strive for in my own game art creations. 

i played through unpacking when it first came out and it was amazing! i loved it to pieces- and then i played it again, and i focused on the story; the journey out of home, making friends in a wonderful (and incredibly cramped) dorm rooms and apartments and sharehousing units, to moving in with a partner who is not good for you. who stifles and confines you more than the places you've lived. who you pack yourself away for, shoving the degree certificate under his bed. then moving back in with your parents, rediscovering yourself and your passions, building yourself back up, allowing that love to come back to you so then you can give it to someone who deserves it- when they eventually come along.

A moving and unpacking game.
It's not so strict as a puzzle, and you can complete it without worrying too much about where to put all the small items that come out of the boxes. In that sense, the "relaxing" tag makes sense.
It makes you think, "When packing for a move, I should think about unpacking things..." lol
There are dishes scattered all over the place, and you'll be surprised they didn't break. 

While the game involves figuring out where to put small items, furniture, clothes, and other items that come out of boxes, the pixel art of these objects is adorable, so if you like pixel art style, I think the worldview will be enjoyable just for that. The background music is also reminiscent of Super Nintendo music. While unpacking, I often find myself thinking about the owner's hobbies and interests... and for some reason, I suddenly feel like tidying up my own room, so I've stopped playing and started cleaning. 

It seems that there are surprisingly many people who play Speedrun of this game, so if you're confident in your ability to tidy quickly and efficiently, you might want to consider that. lol

세월이 흐르며 이사를 반복하는 주인공이 되어 이삿짐을 알맞은 곳에 배치해야 하는 캐주얼 시뮬레이션 게임이다. 상당히 공을 들인 듯한 픽셀 그래픽과 평화로운 가정의 분위기를 부각시키는 부드러운 사운드트랙이 눈과 귀를 상당히 호강시켜준다. 특히 가구와 사물의 디자인이 대단히 정교해 이삿짐을 배치하다가 공연히 홀릴 정도다. 여기에 짐을 풀어 적절한 곳에 배치하는 게임 플레이는 단순 노동에 가까워 단조로우면서도 묘한 중독성이 있어 현실의 이사와 유사한 느낌을 팍팍 풍긴다. 

이삿짐 상자를 조금씩 풀어 물건을 꺼내고, 꺼낸 물건을 알맞은 위치에 배치해 방을 온전히 꾸며야 한다. 상자에서 꺼낸 사물은 배치해야 할 곳이 어느 정도 정해져 있는데, 이를 모든 사물을 꺼낸 뒤에 알려주다보니 일단 주어진 사물을 적당히 알맞겠다 싶은 곳에 배치하고 이후 잘못 배치된 사물을 교정해나가는 방식으로 게임을 진행하게 된다. 그래도 느낌 가는 대로 배치하다보면 왠만한 사물은 어지간해선 첫 배치에 제자리를 잘 찾아가게 된다. 게임이 점차 진행될 수록 방의 개수가 늘어나고 이삿짐의 종류도 늘어나 까다롭긴 하지만, 어찌저찌 공간을 잘 확보하고 물건의 위치를 궁리하다보면 그럭저럭 해결은 될 정도다. 그래도 이삿짐이 늘어나는 만큼 손이 많이 가는 게임이다보니, 살짝 지루한 노가다를 요구하는 감은 있다. 

상당히 은유적인 스토리텔링을 보여주는 게임이다. 직접적인 설명은 해당 연도의 이삿짐을 전부 푼 뒤 드러나는 단 한 마디 문장 뿐이라 설명만 봐서는 스토리를 온전히 이해하기 어렵다. 그 대신 이삿짐의 종류와 변화를 통해 간접적인 방식으로 이야기를 서술하고 있는데, 이를테면 연도가 지나면서 같은 물건이 점차 낡고 헤지는 모습이 드러난다던가 주인공의 처지가 달라진 것을 반영한 사물이 시기 적절하게 등장한다던가 하는 식이다. 이러한 변화를 이해할 수 있다면 이야기의 의도를 온전히 받아들일 수 있겠지만, 서술이 워낙 간접적이고 은유적이라 이를 제대로 파악하기가 어렵다. 개발사의 의도가 이해가 안 되는 것은 아니나 좀 더 직접적인 서술이 뒷받침됐더라면 하는 아쉬움이 강하게 남는다.

고퀄리티의 비주얼과 아늑한 사운드, 그리고 약간의 반복 작업을 동반한 단조로우면서도 일상에 가까운 게임 플레이는 충분히 매력적이라 할 만하다. 하지만 게임의 분량이 생각보다 짧은 편이기도 하고, 무엇보다 스토리텔링이 너무 간접적이고 은유적이라는 점이 아쉽다. 완성도는 나쁘지 않은 게임이지만 은근히 호불호의 여지가 큰 게임이라 할 수 있다.

Reviewing (mostly) every game (or DLC) in my library, part 53:

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️☆ (9/10 stars)

[i] Unpacking [/i] is a cozy, meditative puzzle game that’s quietly profound. You never see a single face, and yet by the end, you feel like you’ve lived a whole life alongside someone—through childhood bedrooms, college dorms, shared apartments, heartbreaks, and new beginnings. There’s no dialogue, no fail state, and no timer. Just boxes to unpack, memories to rediscover, and a life to piece together—literally.

[b] 🛋 Pros: [/b]
[list]
[*] Environmental storytelling at its best. Every move tells a story. Why is this plushie still here after all these years? Why can’t I put this diploma on the wall in this room? The game trusts you to notice, to feel, and to understand without a single word.

[*] Therapeutic gameplay loop. Unpack. Arrange. Rearrange. There’s something so satisfying about putting everything in its right place and noticing what no longer fits.

[*] Art and sound design are top-notch. Pixel art is warm and expressive, and the sound design is incredibly detailed. Every item has a unique sound depending on what surface you place it on.

[*] Touching themes of identity, growth, and self-worth. The protagonist’s life unfolds across 8 stages, and each new move reflects their growth.

[*] Accessibility-friendly. Relaxed pacing, no fail state, no timers. Great for decompressing at the end of a stressful day.
[/list]

[b] 📦 Cons: [/b]
[list]
[*] Some item placement rules can be finicky. Occasionally, the game insists certain items go in one specific spot. This can be mildly frustrating when you're trying to organize your own way.

[*] Limited replay value for some players. Once you know the story beats, there’s not much incentive to replay unless you’re chasing 100% or just want the vibe again.

[*] Short! I finished in 4 hours and got all achievements. $20 is too steep, I'm afraid.
[/list]

[h1]荷解きってこんなに人生つまってたんだな。[/h1]

一見単純そうな段ボールの荷解き作業の中に、思いがけず他人の人生がつまっていて、生き抜き程度に始めたんだけど思いのほか楽しかった。

俺は人生で今まで7回引っ越ししてるんだけど、荷造り、荷解きってこう・・・ある時は新しい出発だったり、ある時は苦しい事からの逃避だったり・・・結構、黙々作業なんだけど、気が付けば頭ん中でいろんな事考えてやるんだよね。このゲームしてたらその当時の気持ちを思い出して、なんか色々ちょっと泣けてきた。

ゲームもステージをクリアしていくごとに、段ボールの持主の生活＆人生が少しづつ垣間見見えてきて、始めた時はただの荷解き作業だったのに徐々に「あ。オマエまだこれ捨てきれへんのか～？」とか「おいおい、パンツ一体何枚持ってきてんだよっ！？」と、顔も知らぬ持ち主に一人突っ込みしちゃうぐらい親近感が湧いてくる。

ゲーム自体はクリアに３～４時間ぐらい。こだわるタイプならもっとじっくりプレイできると思う。ただ逆に几帳面に整理整頓とかするの苦手なタイプなら、中盤から荷物の数も増えてくるのでちょっとめんどくさい。

基本、俺は３時間ほどでクリアできるゲームには評価が厳しいけれど、セールとかでもう少し買いたい時の書いたし用として買うならおススメ☆個人的には、ノスタルジックな雰囲気もあるから、もう少しBGMが良かったら嬉しかったかなぁ。

Extremely relaxing game, while also managing really well to tell a story... simply through unpacking boxes. I loved the gameplay, loved the pixel art, loved the plot and loved the insanely satisfying sounds when unpacking and moving stuff around (every object makes a different sound and holy hell, I could listen them for [i]hours[/i]).

Honestly, it's easy to think that this kind of game wouldn't have a strong plot, but it does, and it was the thing that surprised me the most. I got into the plot so much that I literally screeched at some plot twists and kept narrating/guessing what was happening to a friend of mine. (Keeping it as vague as possible in order to avoid spoilers) I was cheering for the main protagonist, booing at some flatmates and absolutely approving others.
It's also really nice how you can perfectly see the personality of all the various characters transpire from their objects, and there are a lot of cameos/easter eggs/references to other stuff, both videogames-related and not.

My only complain? It's a short game. When I saw three albums at the beginning, I thought they were for three different stories. Instead they are like three different savefiles for the same story.
Still, a really great game, extremely polished, and worth the price. Hope you'll make more "unpacking stories" in the future, and in general I will keep an eye out for future projects.

Um jogo que representa de forma sútil as fases da vida. 

Game adquirido pelo humble Choice- Novembro 2023

Unpacking é um game sem muito rodeio ou mecânicas diferentes, simplismente nascemos oriundos de um álbum de fotos em um quarto rodeado de caixas, e dali vemos que temos que ir colocando as coisas no lugar até acabar os itens. 
Na minha percepção do jogo ele representa as fases que vivemos na : infância, adolescência, fase de faculdade e vida adulta de casados e solteiro.

De inicio nossa preocupação é ursinhos de pelucia e alguns brinquedos e na ultima parte, estamos com uma casa de dois andares e quarto do bebe. 
Alguns ursinhos serão desde a primeira fase até a final nossa companhia de honra. 

De forma geral o game tera 2 modos, um onde você tem que jogar colocando os itens de forma correta e alguns em locais especificos meio estranhos e outro que só tirar das caixas. 
Para fazer o 100% de todas conquistas, é indicado o segundo modo. 

O game é bem curtinho e facilmente será encerrado. como é tudo tudo simples, ele é um jogo relaxante que as vezes passa despercebido. 

O valor dele de R$29,99 é um pouco alto pelo seu pouco conteúdo; recomendo por na lista de desejo em caso de interesse e esperar ele sair por uns R$10,00 no máximo.

Of course, clearing a level is not easy; the further you go, the more your patience is tested, but at least there is unlimited space for trial and error, and the sound effect upon clearing levels is healing, making all the previous frustrations worthwhile. As for the story, it's only a few lines of text. However, you can infer quite a few details from the items themselves.

Finally, I hope there can be an option that enables displaying the name of each item. It will be great to clear up a lot of confusion like 'what exactly is this thing?', and this feature can even make the game a great tool for learning these words in many foreign languages.

I remembered pulling things out and putting them out in one of the levels. The way how space limited where my possessions got put made my heart sank. In another level, the hopefulness and joy brimming from these beloved possession turned my tear tap on. It is fulfilling. It is heartwarming. It left me with great satisfaction and refreshed, just like I've finished tidying my living space.

On the other hand, Unpacked certainly is not some masterpiece in gaming history. You will finish it in a few hours + it's still a quite expensive game for what you are getting.

I decided to recommend the game but neutral would have been better.

I've been looking forward to this game for a very long time and it did not disappoint! 

The puzzle aspect is nice and zen and it really is just like unpacking your own house after a move but without the physical labour aspect. My usual strategies when moving house all applied (like laying everything out on any available surface to get a feel for how much you have vs what space you have available for it) and it was really fun to just sort and decorate.

But what surprised me a lot is how much I loved the atmospheric story design in this game. You never really get any outside context to the rooms you're unpacking. You have to learn everything there is to know from the available furniture and what you're unpacking onto that furniture. You slowly learn about the person whose life you're sorting through as they grow up and go through the ups and downs of life. You get a sense of pride in your little invisible main character as you see them move from place to place and it's fascinating to see how well you get a feel for their successes as well as their setbacks just from seeing how the items change, where you can slot them in to a new living situation, and so on. 

I highly, highly recommend this game to anyone who likes relaxing zen puzzle games, organizing and decorating, or even just cute isometric pixel styles. A lot of love went into this game and it really shows.

This is one of the most fun, relaxing puzzle games I've played in years! Admittedly, I'm not hugely into puzzles, but if I can find more games like this, I very well might become a fan of the genre!

General praise aside, let's get down to the nitty-gritty: What makes this game so simple, so (comparatively) short, and yet so good? In a word, 'Ludonarrative'--that is, the way the gameplay supports the story, or in this case, the way it *tells* the story. The only text in the game is a single sentence or so at the end of each 'chapter', when you're done unpacking and take a picture of your preferred room to put in your photo album (every room in every chapter has different text, by the way, and they're all really fun and relatable, so I'd recommend reading them all if you're into that).

So, since the game is so text-light, the bulk of the storytelling is done by environmental design and gameplay, and this is executed immaculately. 

First, a quick mechanics review just so we're all on the same page: The game starts you out with a single room to decorate (a very 90's-kid room, appropriately enough) and introduces the basic mechanics immediately: Start opening boxes and grabbing items with left click, rotate items with the right click, and put 'em where you feel like it should go. Once you've emptied all the boxes, then any item that's somewhere it shouldn't be (such as in the wrong room, or on the floor when it should be on a shelf) glows red to let you know that it needs to be moved. And that's pretty much everything you need to know! The simplicity of the mechanics allows for a significant amount of creative freedom (within reason), and just as importantly lets you take in the scene without being distracted by the cognitive load of trying to parse a million little gameplay bells and whistles.

Alright, now to the meat of the thing: How does all this come together to tell a story? Well, first and foremost, you're not just moving colored squares on top of other colored squares. You're unpacking toys and dishes and pillows and electronics and all the other little things that tell you who someone is--you're essentially taking a visual tour through the main character's life and helping her put it all in place. You never see her face, but by the second chapter, you know her well enough to start recognizing her favorite stuffed pig and her art supplies, and this process continues until almost every item you unpack is laden with meaning. You get to handle her computer and sort her socks (Not to spoil anything, but I've never before realized the predictive power of a single rainbow-colored sock), and you start seeing all the little changes wrought by time, all the bits and pieces of life that we pick up or leave behind along the way, from the steady upgrades her computer receives to the new hobbies she acquires.

While the red-outline-system mentioned above can very occasionally be frustrating if you really have no idea what an item is or where it goes, it generally encourages you to put things away in places that make sense, rather than throwing everything onto the floor and calling it a day, which is great because it encourages you to interact with the environment and find creative ways to make things fit, without being so restrictive that it completely stifles your ability to make the place your own--I'm a naturally precise person with a real love of organizing things, so I began by sorting everything into distinct categories and gave every category of item its own drawer/area, color- and style-coded as much as possible. And yet, the longer the game went on, the more I started to feel free to mess things up a bit more and embrace the freedom that the main character herself was experiencing. In other words, I was roleplaying, without a word being spoken or a person so much as entering a room.

The primary caveat to the above is that one chapter in particular is *intentionally* designed to make it hard to find space for all your things unless you're willing to do some serious reorganizing of the stuff that's already there, which is ultimately more trouble than it's worth (which is fantastic ludonarrative metaphor/foreshadowing, by the by).

Speaking of that chapter, it's brilliantly done because in the chapter immediately prior, you were living with roommates who had already set up a lot of their own stuff which you couldn't move. So as soon as you arrive at this new place and can move most things around again, it immediately clues you into the fact that something about the relationship is different here--but it's also obvious from the visual design of everything around you contrasted with your own stuff that you don't really belong, even if you're hopeful that you might be able to make it work.

That chapter then sets the tone for the next (which is brilliantly aided by the music chosen for each chapter) which then further feeds into the chapter after that to create a renewed sense of excitement when the music and scenery changes yet again, and so on and so on until the end of the game.

Lastly, we've arrived at the section I like to call "OMG The Sound Design!" You should absolutely play with the sound on, because it adds *so much* character to practically everything! Every item has a different sound depending on what surface you put it down on, and it all makes perfect sense given the material, weight and shape of the item and the surface. Every place you live has its own exterior soundscape, from highway traffic to the occasional take-off of a plane to the laughter of neighborhood children, and it blends perfectly with the feeling of the interior, which itself is packed with satisfying noises, from the 'tac' of a glass on a countertop to the 'swoosh' of a drawer (or the muted 'clang' of a metal cabinet door swinging open, in some cases).

I apologize for the rambling nature of this review, but I honestly could go on for even longer if the mood struck me, and am refraining from doing so only so that I can say the following: Seriously y'all, experience this game for yourself! It's well worth your time.

When this is revealed, they try INCREDIBLY hard to make it obvious, despite how the rest of the game takes a more subtle tone with its story. Sure, it makes the game "inclusive," but couldn't they have made it more just up to interpretation instead of making it in-your-face? [/spoiler]

The first few houses you unpack in the game are the most fun, since there isn't much of a worry of not having enough space, and it's easier to organize. Later on, though, I found myself more often just putting items wherever I expected the game would want me to, because I was tired of the "No, you can't put that here!" mechanic. The game feels incredibly linear because of this, and you can't personalize the house much, if at all. The developers tried to make each room have just barely not enough space for everything, to try to get you to be more creative with placement, but it just adds another layer of stress.

TLDR; Game is more stressful than intended because of a lack of freedom/space to put stuff, not worth the price to me.

Okay, first things first: if you rate games based on "hours per dollar", Unpacking is probably not for you. There is about four hours of game play here if you explore every single option and replayability is slightly north of zero. You will get to experience Unpacking's very sweet story once and after that, you'll be done with it. So keep that in mind.

Now, with that said, I do recommend this game! As I said, it is incredibly sweet but that's not its strongest suit. The game's strong point is the story that it gently guides you through. You're never *told* the story but if you're paying attention, you can rapidly piece it together from all of the little parts that you're going to be taking out of boxes and putting away. When at a critical moment, you're only given one option to successfully place the protagonist's college degree, for instance, it's devastating as you realize you know exactly what's going to happen next. In the next scene, try to pin a particular photograph on a cork board. Watch what happens to it when you do.

Unpacking is chock full of little moments like this: you're invited to use your imagination to build a narrative that is quite literally bigger than its component parts.

The graphics are nicely done, the music is understated but nice, and the puzzle elements are very clever. One weak point is that there are a couple of achievements that there's no possible way you'll discover without looking up a guide. More care and thought should have been given to ways for the player to figure out some of the more obscure achievements organically. In addition, the art fails here and there when complex objects are rendered as well as probably can be done using the game's pixel art... and there's no way you can recognize what they're supposed to be despite this. Some of the objects probably should have been simplified.

And that brings me back to the game's weakest point: it is expensive for the amount of game play that you get and the story that it tells. It's a wonderful experience, but it will be just as wonderful in a couple of years when you can get it for $7 or $8 instead of $16 or $20. So decide if you should buy it now based on that.

Full disclosure - I know the creative & technical directors of Unpacking so my opinion is biased.

[h2] 是一场告别，也是一次新生。

游戏玩法很简单，每隔一段时间，故事主人公都会迎来一次搬家的经历。而玩家的任务，正如游戏名所示，就是拆开收纳箱，根据物品的属性，结合自己的生活习惯与兴趣，放置在合理的地方。虽然在结算时会有些许的限制，但总体来说，玩家仍然能够在自由的空间里尽情发挥创意，打造独一无二的温馨家园。

综合来看，摆放玩法也许谈不上新颖趣味，甚至刻意要求的摆放位置时常会让人感到气恼，但是这个略显繁琐的过程，是主人公，亦或者玩家对主人公过去、现在和未来的一次思考与体验。在轻松愉快的音乐中，每到一处新的居所，每打开一个箱子，其中或是充满情感与回忆的老旧物品，亦或是新添的生活必需品，一点一滴都能够感受到主人公的生活变迁，从求学到求职，从独立到爱情，一直到最终的幸福，玩家伴随着主人公一起成长，一起见证。而当玩家开始一个个地放置这些熟悉的物件，把那只原来摆在床头的毛绒玩偶安顿在新家的床头，把心爱的书摆放在另一个书架上时，那种重温时光的温馨感会涌上心头，很容易就能感受到这个过程中蕴含的幸福感。那一刻，不仅是故事中的主人公，连玩家都仿佛在打造一个属于自己的幸福角落。每个物件，都是一份记忆，每一次的放置，都是一次情感的表达。所以，尽管有时候麻烦，当到最后玩家看到那个被精心整理过的房间，那些熟悉的布置，立刻能感受到那份独属于自己的温馨，所有的麻烦似乎在此刻也都变得微不足道了。

游戏的最后，主人公都会为精心打扮房间拍照留念，附上自己的寄语。这一时刻，超越游戏界限的情感共鸣会得到最终的升华。也许在一个温暖的午后，我们也会静静地整理属于自己的小天地，回味、告别旧有的回忆，迎接我们新的生活。
Très très bon jeu, très détente, j'y retourne très souvent pour me vidé l'esprit en rangeant !

Unpacking is a casual game of literally unpacking boxes when moving into a new house.  There is an unwritten and unverbalized story told as you unpack your boxes from 1997 to 2018 as you see what the owner is interested in, what they collect, where they've been, and it tells story without telling a story.

Simply put, the puzzle portion of this game is to place the objects in the boxes you are unpacking in the right places.  While the job is not too tedious at the end when the boxes have all been emptied and broken down, items are identified as being in the wrong place.  It is your job to fix those last items in order to finish that move in.

The graphics are pixelated and look cartoony and bright.  They are playful and could definitely make this game well received by both adults and children.  You can zoom out to see more of the rooms you are putting away in, or you could stay zoomed in, the default view, and move the mouse to the edge of the screen to see all parts of the room.  You start out with a single room, then expand to multiple rooms, eventually to an entire house.

The game is short, which is perfect because by the time you get to the final year move it gets a bit too tedious and would become boring and unwieldly to continue.  It's simple game that doesn't overstay it's welcome tells an abstract story and provides some hours of entertainment.  Not highly recommended, but I'm not going to say no.  I enjoy these different type of experiences where continue to play this type of gameplay won't work, but it was just enough for me to enjoy the experience.

"Unpacking" est une expérience enchanteresse qui charme par son originalité et sa capacité à captiver. Son gameplay novateur et son histoire captivante créent un monde où chaque objet raconte une histoire, où chaque déballage dévoile des moments de vie. La tranquillité qu'il offre est remarquable, invitant les joueurs à se plonger dans un rythme paisible et gratifiant.

Cependant, malgré cette immersion enchanteresse, la brièveté du jeu peut laisser un sentiment de désir pour plus de découvertes. Son atmosphère relaxante, accompagnée d'une musique exceptionnelle tout au long du jeu, rend chaque moment mémorable. La touche finale musicale couronne cette expérience immersive de façon magistrale.

En somme, "Unpacking" est une aventure singulière, offrant une expérience méditative et une perspective unique sur la vie à travers des objets du quotidien. Bien que sa durée puisse sembler courte pour les joueurs avides de prolonger ce voyage, son ambiance relaxante et sa narration subtile en font un jeu inoubliable. Recommandé pour ceux en quête d'une expérience différente et immersive.

This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).

[b]Description:[/b]
Unpacking is a short and casual point and click puzzle game where you have to unpack items from boxes and place them in the right place. There are many different types of items that belong to specific parts of the house and specific compartments within that room.

There isn’t a written or narrated story, but the title of each level, the contents of the house and the rooms that are available tell a story by themselves and you can see the progress of the character’s life. This life story seems very personal and auto-biographical and it might be even inspired by one of the developer’s life events.

The graphics are pixel art based, but are very detailed with lots of interesting details and some interactable objects like game consoles and you’ll find quite a few different ones from the 90’s and early 00’s. The soundtrack is nostalgic and relaxing and the sounds of each type of object are realistic and distinct and that is a nice touch. 

The gameplay itself is simple and easy. The correct placing of the objects is easy to figure out with common sense but a few placements seem a bit arbitrary, but, in any case, with just a few tries you’ll figure out the right place for the item. In most levels you also won’t run out of space easily so you don’t have to be very meticulous with the object placement.
   

[b]Achievements:[/b]  
[b]How many:[/b] 25 Achievements.
[b]How much time:[/b] 3 hours, playing at a slow pace and without a guide.
[b]Game difficulty:[/b] Very Easy, it’s easy to find the right placement for the items.
[b]Achievements’ Difficulty:[/b] Easy. Some of the achievements are for completing the levels and the rest are for doing specific things in some of the levels. You can find hints for these within the sticker album inside the same or by checking the global achievement’s page. When I completed the game, I just went back to the previous levels and figured out the missing achievements in a few minutes, so it won’t be too hard, but there’s also a very good guide available. 


[b]Overall opinion:[/b]  
Unpacking is a cute and relaxing P&C puzzle game that is to play in short sessions. It has a very relaxing and nostalgic ambiance and the levels and achievements are easy to complete.

Slightly torn on this one. 

On the one hand I like these sorts of relaxing games which you can play while watching something or leave running in the background if you do something that gives you little bits of time to spare (e.g. code compiling), and on top of that I REALLY enjoy this "genre" of "use simple gameplay loop that then gets turned around to tell a great story". Another example being Spiritfarer, my favorite game of 2020. 

Unfortunately, and this is where it falls flat, while Spiritfarer had excellent writing, great characters, and a very emotional story, the story in this game is fairly anemic. There's a few great little touches like the kinds of decor your character likes to keep around, and [spoiler]how you can't hang up the photo of your boyfriend you broke up with, but can't toss it in the trash either, and have to put it in a cupboard somewhere[/spoiler], but overall it was mostly predictable and by the numbers. Maybe it would affect some other types of people more than me, I don't know. 

That's my main gripe; the secondary one is that it's also very short, which is the opposite problem that Spiritfarer had where it lingered on too long expecting you to finish grindy sidequests instead of ending at the climax, when it's the most touching. This is mixed, because while it's good that it doesn't overstay its welcome (given that the actual gameplay can only carry it so far), it's also not worth the asking price of $20. 

Ultimately I'm giving it a positive rating because I don't feel like price to time ratio should be a death sentence. Just try and pick it up for $5 to $10 instead.

reviews.review:
Unpacking is a story game that doesn't have any story, at least not in the traditional sense. It sounds like a paradox because when you think of stories you'd normally think to the wordiness of games, events, story cues, maybe the various character arcs, but none of those really exist here.

You play as a girl that goes through life 'unpacking', and that alone tells the entire story. There is no narrator, no characters that exist as you see them, and the only time the game ever really says anything to you is through the scrapbook. The story relies on the music, the memories and objects you've pulled out of the boxes. It's a deeply nostalgic feeling even for someone like me who hasn't needed to move as much. Every single item that you pull from the box tells a story, and one that grows slowly with the same pace as the character, and despite it not being your story, you'd see and understand.

You go from a young girl that's still studying, with all the books and toys and fluffy animals keeping you company. To sharing a dorm (with terrible dormmates yuck), that refuse to wash their own dishes, not once even being considerate to each other. To falling in and out of love, coming to terms with it when going home, and even finding another love and starting a family.

If I said that this is all coming from a game where you literally pick up and place objects, and that, that was the entire gameplay, you'd think I'm insane (although I definitely am in some ways or another lulw). But this is definitely a lesson to all other devs to lessen or even outright remove a lot of the wordiness in favor of a more diegetic approach that allows the player to understand the story through sheer context alone.

For anyone that truly wants to reminisce, or tell stories with a stream or even just if you want something that you can take at your own pace. Highly recommended - though I do wish they would legitimately allow you to place objects anywhere.

When I played the demo for Unpacking back when they had one of those big demo event things on here, I immediately wishlisted it. The gameplay and the overall tone/vibe from this game is just satisfying overall. I love the concept of unpacking "through the ages". It tells a story without having to give you any dialogue or exposition.

A lot of people are saying that the $20 (USD) pricetag isn't worth it or that they hope it gets free updates (which I wouldn't be opposed to either), but, there's a lot of detail that went into this game. The sound design in general is phenomenal. You wouldn't normally think that the sound of picking up or putting down an item in a game would be important, but it is. The devs went that extra mile. There's also the music and overall art direction of this game. It gave me a sense of nostalgia that I personally don't have since I didn't experience what this character did, but, it was just so nice. 

I would recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a relaxing game with a heartwarming ending. There is no win or lose state. There are certain conditions to be met to "complete" a level, but it's not like you have to start over. You can also collect stickers by putting certain objects in certain places, some you might get on accident, but they were fun to collect!

Unpacking is a game about…well, unpacking. You unpack your belongings and find a place for everything (or everything its place). With appealing visuals and soothing music, Unpacking can be seen as this almost therapeutic experience as you discover, de-clutter, and reminisce about that SEGA genesis you just took out that box. The game mechanics are very simple—almost too simple—all you need is a mouse, and all you need to do is click, drag, and drop. I highly recommend this game for those that get into their deep cleaning rituals, read Marie Kondo, and get pure joy and satisfaction simply from unpacking and organizing stuff.

[b][u]PROS[/u][/b]
[list]
    [*] Very aesthetically pleasing pixelated visuals
    [*] The 80s-90s nostalgia is real, and it is very nice

[/list]

[b][u]CONS[/u][/b]
[list]
    [*] Pace yourself – easy to get burned out if you play too much all at once
    [*] Has a couple of small glitches, but has been getting regular updates
    [*] Not too much replay value after you beat the game

A very surprising smash hit for me!
It's very simple, so simple you won't believe it.

Basically you unpack your things from boxes and put them places.

However, the simplest ideas are often the best, and what this game offers is so soothing.  There's an incredibly subtle but moving story which you pick out for yourself each time you unpack your things in a new home.  The items often do things (try turning the lava lamp on etc) and have tiny special details to keep the story progressing and hold your interest.

I played this game though several times before realising that you can replay it in 'place items anywhere' mode.  The default mode (and I recommend playing this way first for the challenge) is that you have to put items in specific room and places (no putting your toaster in the shower etc).  After a couple of play throughs I have now used the 'put it where you want' mode and love it.  I've done the challenges and achievements, but now I'm decorating the house my way, and 'putting things wherever I want...yes, I do want the toaster in the shower'!

Игру Unpacking я знаю по восторженным отзывам, её хвалят за расслабляющий геймплей и уникальный способ рассказывать историю через вещи. Рисовка у игры действительно красивая и необычная, в этом ей не откажешь. Многие говорят, что это идеальный вариант для снятия стресса после работы, и я понимаю, почему так считают - [u]концепция гениальная[/u].

Но, честно говоря, у меня совсем не получилось получить от неё кайф. Несмотря на всю её крутость, я не смогла расслабиться во время игры. Вроде бы всё располагает к спокойствию, но есть моменты, которые меня напрягают и вызывают скорее раздражение, чем умиротворение.

Самое сложное для меня - это момент в конце уровня, когда игра подсвечивает предметы, стоящие не на своих местах. Ты вроде бы раскладываешь вещи, стараешься, и кажется, что всё нормально. А потом выясняется, что какой-то предмет стоит неправильно. И хуже всего, когда ты даже не понимаешь, что это за вещь и куда её вообще нужно положить. В этот момент у меня начинается чувство растерянности и непонятки, [b]хочется просто закрыть игру и выдохнуть[/b]. В обзорах эту механику называют "гениальным способом рассказать историю", но для меня она превратилась в [i]источник стресса[/i].

Поэтому играть становилось тяжело, приходилось делать паузы, останавливаться и возвращаться через какое-то время, хотя на самом деле хотелось бы пройти её за раз и закрыть этот гештальт. Но есть и другой момент: из-за этих пауз я иногда теряла нить сюжета, и когда возвращалась, уже не всегда могла вспомнить, что происходило с героиней на этом этапе. Это тоже добавляло дискомфорта.
[hr]
Забавно, но [u]самое настоящее спокойствие приходило ко мне именно после того, как я закрывала игру[/u]. В моменте, когда я выдыхалась и просто выключала её, наступало облегчение. [i]То есть расслабление случилось не от процесса, а от его завершения[/i].
[spoiler]Может быть, если бы в игре были подсказки для непонятных предметов, я бы получала больше удовольствия[/spoiler]
[hr]
[b]Кому бы я порекомендовала:[/b]
[list]
[*]Тем, кто любит спокойные игры без спешки и таймеров.
[*]Тем, кто получает удовольствие от организации пространства и раскладывания вещей по полочкам.
[*]Тем, кто ценит нестандартное повествование и готов сам додумывать историю по деталям.
[*]Тем, кто не расстраивается, если с первого раза что-то пошло не так, и готов переставлять предметы заново.
[/list]
[b]Кому бы я НЕ рекомендовала:[/b]
[list]
[*]Тем, кто, как и я, раздражается от непонятных правил расстановки, когда игра в конце говорит, что предмет стоит не там, но не объясняет, где именно он должен быть.
[*]Тем, кому тяжело играть без подсказок.
[*]Тем, кто хочет расслабиться во время игры, а не после того, как её закроет.
[*]Тем, кто не любит возвращаться к игре после пауз и терять сюжетную нить.
[/list]
[hr]
[h3]Моё итоговое мнение и вердикт[/h3]
[b]Это сугубо моё личное мнение[/b], и я ни в коем случае не отговариваю других от покупки. Игра объективно классная, со своей уникальной атмосферой и историей. Просто, как я могу, я прохожу её в своём темпе, с паузами, и пока что двигаюсь дальше. [i]Может быть, когда-нибудь я дойду до конца и пойму, что оно того стоило[/i].
Мой вердикт такой: [b]Unpacking[/b] - это игра, которую стоит попробовать, если вы любите экспериментировать с необычными инди-проектами и не боитесь, что игра может не подойти. Но если вы ищете стопроцентно расслабляющий опыт без раздражающих моментов, то, скорее всего, она [i]не для вас[/i]. Она скорее на любителя, и этот любитель - не я.
Я бы сказала так: [u]попробуйте, если интересно, но не удивляйтесь, если вместо релакса получите лёгкий стресс[/u].

[h1]A slice of life packed into 8 different lifetimes[/h1]
I got this as part of the [i]Paralives[/i] + [i]Unpacking[/i] bundle. I never usually indulge in "cozy sims" largely because I'm just not the target avatar for those kinds of games. Saying that, I'm a sucker for games with great stories. And while to most people it's a Zen puzzler, [i]Unpacking[/i] rewards those paying attention with a twinkling story.

[h2]FUN[/h2]
I honestly didn't think I would end up spending over 3 hours playing the game. My playtime includes completing all the achievements.

And I genuinely love the achievements. Despite being the metagame, the achievements provide a "hidden" point-and-click experience in that you have to use your intuition to put two and two together, and see how to get them. There are no hints, you simply have to rely on "instinct". If you enjoy figuring things out yourself without any hand-holding, then you'll have a lot of fun attempting to obtain 70-80% of the achievements. I do wish it was a little less challenging, but I guess it's reminiscent to the times when we had to use guides to achieve a challenge anyway.

That's pretty much all there is to the gameplay in terms of replayability and fun. Besides that, all you do is click the left mouse button on things, and make them move around. You'd think this would bore you, but it never does because the...

[h2]LOOK AND FEEL[/h2]
... is [i]fantastic[/i]. Unlike the music, the sound design is intentionally not made chiptune, and it suddenly invokes a kinaesthetic sense in your interactions with the items.

Carry a bag, and you'll feel the plastic squeaking under your grip. You put it down, you'll feel a dull "fump" of the air inside pushing up.

You set different glasses on the table, and each of them would sound different based on the make; some sound like it could break if you set it down again, some sound like they could make your knuckle hurt if it fell on your hand.

And here's the amazing part: when trying to segregate them on the shelves, I could not tell the books from the CD boxes... until I picked them up and set them down to check. If it played a hollow clack of typical plastic, it's a CD box. If it played a thoomish thud, I could literally feel how heavy the book, let alone understood if it's a book or not.

In a way, [i]Unpacking[/i] is one of the prime examples of video games that prove you don't need to make the game *look* realistic to *feel* realistic; that's the difference between reality versus believability, something most game developers AND gamers fail to understand.

[h2]IMMERSION[/h2]
This is possibly the only time I can say that look and feel in a video game does SO much for the immersion factor. And I'll admit: I was so immersed in the game that the idea of getting back to the game just to sort boxes and arrange household stuff after I took an AFK break... made me groan.

Perhaps it worked too well on that regard, and I have to remind myself that this is a game, and there's a reward factor to it... well, some. The only time I did feel like I was getting something valuable from all this ... [i]labour[/i]... were insights about the character that I was, and who they were to other characters.

As I mentioned before, you can only really see the "story" if you're really paying attention and reading between the lines. And in a way, it's really nice to see such a wholesome representation of the rainbow community. It doesn't come in to shove some agenda down the player's throat. It just presents it like it is: just another life, just people hanging about, enjoying life as it is, with their own set of ups and downs. It just so happens that we're looking at the life of someone who's played both sides.

And I think that's the simplest, most honest, and really the truest representation one can create in the community's honour. Whether you support the community or not isn't the point -- it's if you can walk away from the game knowing you can resonate with its story.

And if you did, know that it's because you and I have lived those experiences. If I walked away feeling like someone peeked into my past, then so will you. And the reason why is stupid-simple:

[i]Unpacking[/i] represents the ebb and flow of the mundane yet familiar -- the very claim it promised to deliver. And deliver, it did.

[h1]Verdict[/h1]
There were a few moments where the player seems to have only one choice to make in regards to where to place certain objects.

It made me wonder if the developers left some space for players to explore it in another way, so that our implicit choice could help us interpret it differently. Or if it's intentionally designed linearly to reflect the character's stage of life.

Either way, these moments created an opportunity for emergent narrative to take place. If the intention was what I think, they absolutely nailed it and it was beautifully done, and further cements the representation it means to deliver with respect to the ebb and flow of time, relationships, and love.

[i]Unpacking[/i] is not wholesome for wholesome's sake --  give the game a shot, and you'll see what I mean.

Unpacking is an adorable pixel art game about… Well, unpacking stuff every time you move somewhere new. While the game is awfully simple and easy to play, it also tells a story, which is rather sweet and wholesome.

(Further review might contain spoilers.)

Unpacking allows you to follow the life of the main character by observing how her surroundings change as she grows up. From seeing her childhood bedroom to arranging her own child’s room… And observing her love life, until she finally finds another lady to share the rest of her life with.

While there wasn’t a single line of dialogue during the gameplay, just seeing the new souvenirs from different countries or another diploma hanging on the wall made me really happy for the mc. I was cheering for her success from the very beginning (I did tear up after I finished the game, yes).

Sometimes, despite feeling tired of this game, I kept pushing myself to continue (I guess I just wanted to see the ending). The unpacking itself took me quite a lot of time and it made me slightly frustrated just to get to the decorating and arranging part. While I assumed that this game would make me relaxed, it was quite the opposite. Nevertheless, it was an enjoyable experience. Even though this game gave me a headache a few times, it was only because of my stubbornness to keep going. And hey, you gotta finish the game you bought, right. The money can’t go to waste.

Overall, Unpacking is a pretty good game. It indeed might be relaxing… Not for everyone though. I do encourage you to buy it (once it’s on sale), and enjoy it. And take your time to finish it. Personally, it was a single-playthrough thing for me, and I don’t think I’ll play this game in the near future again. It was a nice experience though.

Ogni livello rappresenta un trasloco in una fase diversa dell’esistenza della protagonista. Attraverso gli oggetti capisci tutto: hobby che cambiano, relazioni che iniziano e finiscono, spazi che si restringono o si allargano. Non ti viene spiegato nulla, ma lo intuisci sistemando libri, peluche, fotografie, console, diplomi.
Il gameplay è semplice ma non banale. Devi trovare il posto giusto per ogni oggetto rispettando una logica realistica. Alcune limitazioni possono risultare leggermente frustranti quando il gioco non accetta una soluzione che per te sarebbe plausibile ma nel complesso il ritmo è rilassante e coerente con l’atmosfera.
La pixel art è pulita, calda, accogliente. La colonna sonora è discreta e accompagna senza invadere. È un’esperienza che punta tutto sulla delicatezza e sulla narrazione ambientale.

Non è un gioco che mette alla prova abilità o riflessi. È un esercizio di osservazione e di empatia.

Voto: 6.5 / 10

Unpacking parece simples à primeira vista, mas é aquele tipo de jogo que te pega desprevenida. Você basicamente vai tirando objetos de caixas e organizando a casa… só que, sem perceber, começa a contar uma história inteira sem usar uma única palavra.

Cada mudança de casa representa uma fase da vida da personagem. Pelos objetos, pelo que some, pelo que aparece e até pelo que não cabe mais, você vai entendendo relacionamentos, escolhas, frustrações e recomeços. É muito sutil, mas extremamente poderoso.

A gameplay é tranquila, quase terapêutica. Não tem pressa, não tem punição, não tem pressão. É você, as caixas e o espaço. Dá uma sensação absurda de conforto, mas ao mesmo tempo bate aquele aperto no coração em alguns momentos… principalmente quando você percebe que nem sempre a vida vai exatamente como a gente planeja.

Visualmente é lindo no estilo pixel art, super delicado, e a trilha sonora combina perfeitamente com o clima do jogo. É aquele tipo de som que te faz desacelerar e realmente entrar no momento.

Jogue se:
Você gosta de jogos calmos e contemplativos.
Curte histórias contadas de forma indireta, sem diálogos explícitos.
Quer um jogo pra relaxar, refletir e sentir (às vezes até demais).

Detalhe importante: não é um jogo longo nem cheio de desafios tradicionais. O foco aqui é a experiência, a narrativa e a sensação que ele deixa depois que acaba.

No fim das contas, Unpacking não é só sobre organizar objetos… é sobre organizar memórias, fases da vida e entender que crescer nem sempre é linear. Um jogo simples, sensível e profundamente humano.

Nota: 10/10
Uma experiência que fica com você mesmo depois de fechar o jogo.

Unpacking is an unexpectedly deep and touching game — all without a single word. At first glance, it’s a simple puzzle game about unpacking boxes after a move. But behind this calm process lies a quiet, intimate story of life, change, new beginnings, and loss.

The gameplay is meditative and soothing: you simply place objects on shelves, in drawers, and around different rooms. Yet over time, you begin to realize that every item tells a piece of someone’s story — full of emotion, memories, and subtle growth. The game speaks entirely through objects, and that’s incredibly powerful.

The visual style is minimalist yet cozy and expressive. The soundtrack is gentle and relaxing, enhancing the nostalgic, almost therapeutic atmosphere.

Pros:
✔ Emotional and atmospheric journey
✔ Unique storytelling through objects
✔ Lovely pixel art and calming music
✔ Soothing, almost therapeutic gameplay

Cons:
➖ Short (but feels complete)
➖ Limited replay value

Rating: 8.5/10 — A heartfelt, quiet game that brings back memories of moves, changes, and new chapters in life. Honest, gentle, and deeply human. Highly recommended for those seeking a soulful experience.

[h1]Une Expérience Minimaliste et Apaisante[/h1]
Unpacking est un jeu qui repose sur un concept simple : vider des cartons et ranger des objets dans un nouvel espace de vie. Pourtant, derrière cette apparente banalité, il propose une expérience unique, à la fois relaxante et empreinte de nostalgie. Le jeu invite à la détente, sans pression ni stress, en racontant une histoire uniquement à travers les objets que l’on manipule.

[h1]Un Gameplay Axé sur la Relaxation[/h1]
Le principe du jeu est accessible à tous. À chaque niveau, on découvre un nouvel espace de vie que l’on doit aménager en sortant les objets des cartons et en les disposant à différents endroits. On traverse ainsi plusieurs étapes de la vie du personnage, de son enfance jusqu’à sa vie d’adulte.

Aucune limite de temps, aucun score, aucune menace. Unpacking se vit à son propre rythme, offrant un moment de calme et d’évasion. Le jeu n’impose que quelques règles de placement pour certains objets, mais il laisse une grande liberté dans l’aménagement des pièces. C’est un véritable jeu « chill », parfait pour se détendre après une journée chargée.

Mais au-delà du simple rangement, le jeu raconte une histoire. À travers les objets que l’on transporte de déménagement en déménagement, on découvre subtilement l’évolution du personnage. Une peluche qui traverse les années, un diplôme qui marque une réussite, un objet qui disparaît d’un chapitre à l’autre... Tout est dit sans un mot, et pourtant, on ressent pleinement les émotions qui s’en dégagent.

[h1]Une Direction Artistique Douce et Immersive[/h1]
L’esthétique en pixel art est particulièrement soignée, chaque objet étant reconnaissable au premier coup d’œil. La palette de couleurs et le style détaillé renforcent l’ambiance chaleureuse et accueillante du jeu.

L’ambiance sonore participe également à cette sensation de bien-être. Pas de musique omniprésente, juste des sons réalistes et agréables : le froissement des cartons, le bruit d’un objet posé sur différentes surfaces, l’écho d’une pièce vide. Tout cela contribue à une immersion douce et apaisante.

[h1]Une Expérience Courte mais Mémorable[/h1]
Unpacking est un jeu qui se vit comme un court voyage introspectif. Une fois terminé, il laisse une impression de sérénité et de mélancolie douce.

Le mode photo permet de capturer ses propres aménagements, ajoutant une petite touche de créativité. Toutefois, l’absence de véritables défis ou de niveaux générés aléatoirement limite la rejouabilité.

Comptez environ 6h pour voir le 100%

一个朋友送给我的生日礼物，竟然成为了我2025年第一个全成就的游戏，她这辈子有了。
画风和玩法都非常可爱的一个休闲游戏，玩家需要把行李中的物品一件件取出来放置在新家里，在我的精心布局下，新房子不能说是井井有条，倒也能说是杂乱无章。
在摆完东西后，系统会提醒玩家哪个东西摆放不合理，对此，来看看我怎么说→
“谁说奖状不能挂厕所墙上？我就喜欢挂厕所墙上。什么，放地上也不行？”
“杀虫剂怎么就不能放地上了！”
“什么，书包居然不能放椅子上！”
“什么，原来这是沐浴露。”
……
诸如此类的错误摆放还有一些，但修正它们不需要用很长的时间，而且将一件件物品放到正确位置的过程本身也很有成就感，虽然仍然称不上美观，但是好歹能叫作有序了。
每次理客厅的时候，我都很羡慕主角家里能一直有游戏机，还有那么多游戏卡带。
顺带一提，有时候拿出来一个物体，我愣是看不出来拿了个什么东西，只能一股脑往抽屉里丢，一般不会出错。

[h1] Nettes Spiel, aber... [/h1] 

Wer ein ganz gemütliches Spiel mit angenehm entspannendem Soundtrack sucht, um nach einem anstrengenden Tag ein bisschen abzuschalten, ist bei Unpacking unter Umständen richtig.

Angefangen in einem kleinen Kinderzimmer, arbeitet man sich schnell durch ganze Wohnungen und begleitet die Geschichte. Eine tolle Idee, besonders da hier und dort auch von eher unschönen Erlebnissen erzählt wird. Manche Dinge gehören einfach an die Wand.

Und hier kommt auch schon mein erstes Problem mit dem Spiel. Denn das Spiel entscheidet, welche Objekte passend oder unpassend platziert wurden. Das ist hin und wieder doch etwas unbefriedigend, da man recht häufig dazu gezwungen wird, den halben Raum umzustellen, um es gemütlich, sortiert und ordentlich zu halten (wenn das dann überhaupt möglich ist). Oftmals kann das aber auch hilfreich sein, wenn man gar nicht versteht, was das Objekt eigentlich sein soll. Gleichzeitig vergisst man so nicht die eine Tasse, die man "nur mal eben schnell" in der einen Ecke abgestellt hat, um einen anderen Gegenstand zu verschieben.

In ein paar "Leveln" ziehen wir offensichtlich mit anderen Personen zusammen oder in eine WG. Und schon ist es dann nicht mehr möglich, alle Gegenstände zu bewegen, auch wenn es sich nur um Deko handelt. Für den ein oder anderen (mich eingeschlossen) ist das an manchen Stellen doch recht unbefriedigend. 

Von der farblich einheitlichen und damit sehr befriedigenden Küche, die auf der Shopseite angezeigt wird, fehlt leider auch jede Spur. Die meisten Räume sind doch etwas zusammengewürfelt und nur schwer farblich (oder thematisch) zu sortieren. Also noch ein Faktor, der den inneren Monk stresst.

Der größte Minuspunkt ist jedoch der Preis. Für rund 20 € bekommt man hier gut 3 Stunden (größtenteils) entspannende Unterhaltung geboten. Zwar gibt es im Hauptmenü die Auswahl zwischen drei Büchern (Spielstände), allerdings sind die Level gleich. Einen Grund, das Spiel also nochmal zu spielen, gibt es tatsächlich erst mal nicht. Nach drei Stunden ist man einfach durch.

"[i]Unpacking[/i]" est un jeu incroyablement cozy et visuellement superbe, avec un concept simple mais efficace : trier et ranger les objets contenus dans des cartons pour aménager différentes pièces. Ce que j'ai particulièrement aimé, c'est découvrir, au fil des niveaux (représentés par des étapes marquantes de la vie du personnage), une histoire subtile et touchante. De l'enfance à l'âge adulte, ces moments offrent une belle dose de nostalgie et de douceur, rendant l'expérience vraiment attachante.

Un des points forts du jeu réside dans la liberté offerte : on peut disposer la plupart des objets à notre guise, ce qui laisse place à la créativité et rend chaque partie unique.

Cependant, le principal défaut reste son prix, que je trouve excessif au vu de la durée de vie du jeu. Même en prenant mon temps, j'ai terminé le jeu en environ six heures pour une partie. À ce tarif, il aurait été préférable d'ajouter davantage de contenu ou de proposer un prix plus abordable.

Malgré cela, je recommande "[i]Unpacking[/i]" pour l'expérience émotive et agréable qu'il offre. C'est un jeu qui mérite d'être découvert, surtout si vous recherchez un moment de détente empreint de douceur.

Ele é um jogo visualmente bonito, interface boa e rodou no meu PC sem placa de vídeo.
Eu comprei ele por 59,99, e acho q poderia ser mais baratinho.
Enfim se você realmente quer comprar o jogo espera uma promoção.
总体时长大概5小时，通过收纳布置不同的房间见证主角的一生，有很多玩具一直陪伴着主角。同时从摆放这些物品的过程中也能看出主角的爱好和职业，主角无论住在多大的房间，总能把房间布置得很温馨。希望大家在漂泊的过程中都能有属于自己的家。

[h3] Вери гуд, вери найс! [/h3]

Очень хороший пример, как рассказать историю с помощью основной игровой механики (при том, что в игре нет диалогов и героя в кадре как такового). Наблюдая за деталями, которые распаковываешь узнаешь подробности жизни ГГ. Проживать историю таким образом - это довольно необычно и интересно.

Сама по себе игра довольно залипательный кликер, расслабляющий и ламповый. Визуально красиво выполненный. Игрушка на пару вечеров, ну либо на один, тут смотря как погружаться.

Esse é um dos jogos mais relaxantes que já joguei, admito que teve vezes que me estressei quando não conseguia achar um lugar para arrumar os itens, mas, de qualquer forma, a gameplay é super leve, os gráficos do jogo são fofos e delicados.
Me arrependo de ter jogado o jogo no mudo, enquanto ouvia música, os sons e músicas desse jogo realmente expressam a vibe do jogo.

Uma coisa que eu gosto é que, ao terminar o jogo, você pode jogar as fases novamente sem o jogo te limitar, como fazia quando você termina de desencaixotar as caixas. Ainda não consegui todas as conquistas, mas, todas as que já consegui são bem diferentes e criativas.
Os itens que se repetem, como os pintinhos, as pelúcias e entre outros, você realmente consegue perceber que ao longo dos anos, no jogo, a pessoa mantém eles independente do lugar que fosse, e eu achei isso um detalhe muito legal.

Mas, um ponto negativo é que o jogo é MUITO curto, eu terminei ele em 6 horas (5,9) sem conseguir todas as conquistas (oque não demoraria muito), então, achei o preço um pouco salgado, mas, realmente vale a pena conseguir ele, melhor ainda se estiver em promoção

Em suma, o jogo vale muito a pena, realmente espero que algum dia o jogo tenha mais conteúdo, ou talvez, um Unpacking 2.

Esse foi um dos melhores jogos que já joguei na minha vida. 

Ele é incrível e faz me sentir melhor sempre que abro (e olha que nem sou tão organizada assim, muito pelo contrário na verdade). Esse jogo me fez refletir e torcer pela personagem. Mesmo que o propósito seja só organizar os cômodos, ao longo dos anos você cria afeto pelos objetos de infância também, pela personagem e suas relações e passa pelas dificuldades juntos, é incrível ver o desfecho de tudo isso. Eu recomendo, de coração.
SO good. I love this game and everything about it. Incredible storytelling and relaxing gameplay. I could play this game over and over. (I have)

[b]Hallöchen![/b] 🐔
Ein Spiel welches ich geschenkt bekommen habe. Ich selbst fand es niedlich, aber dachte immer wozu soll ich denn Dinge einräumen, ich bin selbst sehr oft umgezogen, da habe ich genug geräumt... Aber das Spiel überzeugte mich. 

[b]Schwierigkeit[/b]
Hat keine Schwierigkeit.
Manchmal ein wenig knifflig was das Spiel erwartet, wo man bestimmte Gegenstände hinstellt, aber da kann man sich einfach ausprobieren.

[b]Grafik[/b]
Sehr hübsch und übersichtlich. 

[b]Personengruppe[/b]
Mmh. Alle die Lust haben Zeug einzuräumen? Ich glaube relativ junge Kinder, könnten je nachdem noch Hilfe gebrauchen um die nächsten Jahre (Level) freizuschalten, weil sie vielleicht nicht alles dort hinstellen, wo das Spiel die Dinge haben möchten, z.B. Toaster in der Badewanne. Aber sonst kann jeder einfach einräumen nach seinem Geschmack.

[b]Story[/b]
Die Story spiegelt sich in den Wohnungen wieder. Das ist sehr schön gemacht. [spoiler]Man nimmt auch immer wieder Dinge von der alten Wohnung/Zimmer mit und bestimmte Dinge werden mehr, wie die Plüschtiere, die aber auch wieder abnehmen oder die Notizbücher.[/spoiler] Es gibt nach jeder Wohnung einen kleinen Satz, der dennoch sehr viel aussagt. Denn die Story spiegelt sich auch in den Dingen die man einräumt wieder, ganz toll. Und auch immer eine kleine Überraschung, was man immer und immer wieder auspackt und was man plötzlich vermisst. (Wenn es einem auffällt)

[b]Gameplay[/b]
Naja, bisschen klicken hier, bisschen klicken da. Man hat vorgegebene Dinge, die man in vorgegebene Zimmer einräumt. Man kann zwar selbst die Dinge anordnen, aber das Spiel beschränkt bestimmte Dinge auch. Es achtet auch dass Küchengegenstände, in die Küche kommen (was ja auch irgendwo logisch ist), aber ich hatte auch schon Dinge, wo ich es schade fand, es nicht z.B. in einen Schrank stellen zu können. Das fand ich auch etwas doofi. Aber grundsätzlich macht es Spaß.

[b]Bugs[/b]
Mir sind keine aufgefallen.

[b]Spielzeit[/b]
Ich habe mit allen Errungenschaften 4,3 Std. gebraucht laut Steam. 
Kann auch mehr sein oder sogar weniger, kommt drauf an, wie schnell man einräumt oder ob man es richtig genießt und sich viel Zeit lässt. (Ich glaube ich war ein Mittelding)

[b]Preis[/b]
Zugegeben... ich finde es teuer für den Content. Die Story ist, wie gesagt, sehr schön. Man begleitet eine Frau in verschiedenen Lebensabschnitte und hilft ihr sich einzurichten. Ich verstehe auch den Preis ein wenig. Aber finde es trotzdem viel. 20€ für (in meinem Fall) 4 Stunden, puuuuh. 

[b]Fazit[/b]
Um direkt nochmal auf den Preis zurückzukommen... Das Spiel bietet nicht so viel wie vielleicht erwünscht. Das Spielprinzip ist die ganze Zeit das selbe, ausräumen und einräumen. Das ist ja auch das was wir uns hier aussuchen, wenn wir uns das Spiel holen. Auch die Dinge die man auspackt, sind oft die selben, logischerweise nimmt man Dinge ja auch mit. Aber im Verhältnis zum Preis von 20€ ist das najaaaaa. Die Hälfte denke ich wäre ganz gut für "eine" Person, die man begleiten kann in den Lebensabschnitten. Ich persönlich weiß aber auch nicht wie viel Herz und Arbeit in diesem Spiel drin steckt, vielleicht wäre der Preis dann doch gerechtfertigter... 

Um nun nochmal zum [b]Fazit[/b] zu kommen... wer sich für sowas interessiert (Dinge auspacken und einräumen), dann let's go. Macht Spaß. Aber vielleicht im Sale kaufen. 🐤

🎮 Unpacking to debiutancki tytuł studia Witch Beam, które postanowiło stworzyć coś zupełnie innego na tle współczesnych gier. Gra wyraźnie wyróżnia się na rynku swoją unikalną koncepcją, polegającą na... rozpakowywaniu rzeczy. Wbrew pozorom, ta nietypowa mechanika zyskała sobie wielu zwolenników, oczekujących na spokojną, niemal terapeutyczną rozgrywkę, odmienną od pełnych akcji produkcji. Po kilku chwilach możesz zdać sobie sprawę, że to coś więcej – to emocjonalna podróż przez życie, która skłania do refleksji nad ludzkimi historiami i tym, jak nasze rzeczy odzwierciedlają to, kim jesteśmy.

📖 Fabuła
Nie spodziewałem się głębi fabularnej w grze o rozpakowywaniu pudeł, ale Unpacking mnie zaskoczyło. Każdy etap gry przenosi do kolejnej ważnej chwili w życiu bohatera – od dziecięcego pokoju, przez pierwsze mieszkanie na studiach, aż po współdzielenie przestrzeni z partnerem. Każda rzecz w tych pudełkach opowiadała swoją historię, a ja miałem wrażenie, jakbym układał kawałki układanki życia kogoś innego. Może brakuje tu dialogów, ale przedmioty mówią same za siebie.

🕹️ Gameplay i Rozgrywka
Powiedzmy sobie szczerze – wyzwań tutaj nie ma. Nie znajdziesz w Unpacking wyścigu z czasem, żadnych skomplikowanych zagadek ani przeciwników do pokonania. Gra to powolny, relaksujący kliker, który działa jak lekki powiew wiatru w upalny dzień. Niby proste, ale satysfakcja, jaką czerpałem z układania każdej rzeczy na swoje miejsce, była czymś zaskakującym. Zabawne, jak coś tak prostego może sprawiać tyle radości. Jeśli jesteś perfekcjonistą, lubisz porządek i denerwujesz się, gdy ktoś nie układa majtek "prawidłową stroną", ta gra jest dla ciebie. Przesuwanie kubków, układanie książek czy wieszanie ubrań przynosiło mi satysfakcję, której nie spodziewałem się w tej formie. Choć brak tu prawdziwego wyzwania, Unpacking to relaks w najczystszej postaci.

🖼️ Grafika i Oprawa Wizualna
Grafika w Unpacking jest prosta, ale uderza w odpowiednie tony. Przypomina mi minimalistyczne wnętrza z katalogów IKEA – przemyślane, funkcjonalne i przyjemne dla oka. Każde pomieszczenie, które rozpakowywałem, miało swój własny, unikalny charakter, a dzięki temu gra nie stawała się monotonna. Szczególnie podobało mi się to, jak każdy przedmiot został starannie zaprojektowany, by oddawać klimat danego etapu życia bohatera. Te wszystkie małe detale – od starych figurek z dzieciństwa po wspomnienia z podróży – wciągały mnie coraz głębiej w opowieść.

🎵 Audio i Muzyka
Oprawa dźwiękowa Unpacking idealnie współgrała z resztą gry. Delikatna muzyka w tle, odgłosy rozpakowywania kartonów i stawiania przedmiotów na półkach – wszystko to tworzyło spokojną, relaksującą atmosferę, której potrzebowałem po intensywnym dniu. Subtelność dźwięków nie przytłaczała, wręcz przeciwnie – pomagała się odprężyć.

⚙️ Optymalizacja i technikalia
Gra działała płynnie bez żadnych problemów technicznych. Sterowanie było proste i intuicyjne, a oprawa wizualna, choć minimalistyczna, była wystarczająco szczegółowa, by każdy przedmiot od razu rozpoznać. Na Decku musiałem podkręcić czułość kursora, ten domyślnie jest boleśnie ślamazarny. 

🔄 Regrywalność
Cóż, czy można zagrać w Unpacking drugi raz? Może. Sama fabuła nie jest na tyle złożona, by odkrywać ją ponownie, ale dla tych, którzy czerpią przyjemność z grzebania w bieliżnie, gra zawsze będzie oferować ten sam relaksujący rytm. To raczej tytuł na jedno popołudnie, ale w tych kilku godzinach zapewnia niesamowitą dawkę spokoju i satysfakcji.

📝 Unpacking to gra specyficzna. Nie oferuje dynamicznej akcji ani skomplikowanych mechanik, ale dostarcza coś innego – relaks i emocjonalną podróż przez życie innej osoby. Gdy pierwszy raz usiadłem do tej gry, nie spodziewałem się, że wciągnie mnie na tyle, by zapomnieć o czasie. Czy poleciłbym ją każdemu? Niekoniecznie. Jeśli szukasz wrażeń i wyzwań, możesz być zawiedziony. Ale jeśli potrzebujesz chwili spokoju i refleksji – to jest tytuł dla Ciebie.

猛猛玩了一个下午打通关！评价是好玩儿！我太喜欢了呀，没有任何文本量，但是却完美展现了“我”的故事，从幼儿时期到独居再到两段感情的发展，打住，就不剧透了！
但是有点挑人！如果你喜欢明确的故事主线，清晰明了的任务指引那么你可能不适合这款游戏；如果你喜欢通过探索，自己的想象去完善，窥探故事的来龙去脉，那么你应该会喜欢unpacking这个游戏的。
非常适合一个人待在家安静的慢慢的悠闲的去游玩的游戏，玩得让人heart软软，“我”真的是一个特别特别萌和柔软的小女孩，好喜欢呀！一旦你玩进去了时间就会过的特别快，在摆放物品中时间就不知不觉的过去了，“我”在不同的时间段里面遇到了怎样的人，发生了什么故事，这些都需要你在物品放置的过程中去了解体会，我觉得每次最开心的就是摆放老物品，摆放贯穿着幼年到成年的物品总是让人有一种见到老朋友的欣喜呢！

Unpacking delivers a masterfully crafted experience that transforms the simple act of arranging belongings into a powerful narrative journey. Through carefully curated personal possessions, you witness your character's evolution from childhood to adulthood, their story quietly unfolding through the items they carry from home to home. Each new space reveals chapters of their life - career changes, relationships, family growth, and even heartbreak - all told through the intimate process of finding homes for their belongings.

What makes this game special is how it turns the meditative act of organization into emotional storytelling. Without a single word of dialogue, you piece together life's pivotal moments through objects that carry deep personal meaning. The attention to detail in each item and the satisfaction of finding its perfect place creates a uniquely cozy and contemplative experience.

The game's only shortcoming is that it leaves you wanting more - like a good book you wish wouldn't end, you'll find yourself wishing there were more boxes to unpack and more stories to discover. It's a testament to the game's quality that its biggest flaw is simply that there isn't more of it to enjoy.

Kah aldığı küçük figürlere yenisi ekleniyor (özellikle tavuk ve civcivlerden bahsediyorum) kah yeni bir ülkeye gidiyor ve bir hediyelik getiriyor. Bazen üniversiteye başlıyor, bazen mezun oluyor, bazense sevgilisinden ayrılıyor. Diplomasını başka bir köşeye kaldırmak zorunda kalıyor, başkalarının hayatına kendince dahil oluyor, kendine ona verilmeyen alanı açmaya çalışıyor... 
Hepsinde kendimi gördüm. Küçüklüğümden beri ordan oraya taşınmalarımız, mezun oluşum, erkek arkadaşımın hayatına dahil olmam, beraber bir hayat kurmaya çalışmamız... Oyun gerçekten bende derinlerde bir şeylere dokundu. Bazı eşyalardan hiç vazgeçmiyoruz, bizim kim olduğumuzu ve neler yaşadığımızı hatırlatıyor.

Kısaca oyun çok güzel, çok chill. Herkese tavsiye ederim. İyi oyunlar.

I want to say for the record, while I recommend this game for being a cute, relaxing, satisfying experience, I would NOT recommend getting it at full price. I played through the entire game in one sitting, clocking in 3.8 hours and at least 45 minutes of that if not more was me pausing the game to do some stuff around the house before I forgot. So realistically this is 2 to 3 hours of gameplay depending on how detail oriented you want to be. To me, twenty bucks is pretty expensive for such little playtime. I got it on sale for $10 and even then I feel like I may have overpaid a little. There's only something like 8 levels, the achievements are all locked and they end up being dumb stuff like putting up a poster you find in the room. Definitely an easy game to 100% if one cares enough (I don't). There's no real replay value unless you want to see how many different arrangements you can do or something. It was fun while I played it, the gameplay is addictive, but there's not a whole lot of content. So keep that in mind if you're thinking about buying. Realistically I think this game should have a base price of $7.99 instead of $19.99.

unpacking is a low-five puzzle game which follows the main character as she moves from home to home as the game progresses we see our character grow from a young girl living with her parents and sister in her childhood home through to a grown woman just starting a family of her own every item that we unpack helps frame the story of who this character is and what she values this is unpacking the story explained we meet our character in 1997 when she is unpacking her childhood room she tells us that this is the first room she has had all to herself we later learned that our character's family had moved into a three-bedroom house and that our character has a sister with whom she must have shared a room previously a character was an active child with a love of soccer and the soccer Cute and cozy game of unpacking boxes and figuring out where to put things. It's not a long or challenging game but it's a nice way to spend a few hours.

You learn a lot about the main character during the game without seeing her at all until the ending as she moves between homes at different stages in her life. Seeing her go through low points and high points in her life is quite relatable and seeing what items she holds onto throughout her life was something I definitely connected with emotionally.

Wasn't a super long game, but I really enjoyed it. I also loved going through and seeing the stages of her life, figuring out what happened by the environments and what she was unpacking. A relaxing experience and a joy to figure out how to organize things / change them around a little to fit an aesthetic I liked while they're still in the areas they're supposed to be in. I flipped around back and forth about getting this game and then my husband gifted it to me from his humble bundle, really glad he did from how much joy I got from going through this.

I wanted to like this one, I really did, and with that being said, even this negative review is probably holding back in the severity of the game's issues. 

I love this aesthetic (cozy, casual, cute), this style of story telling (no dialogue or characters, only investigation into another's life/possessions to learn the story), and the concept of relaxing, easy to complete, positive games. I play tons of them!, but I'm no hard critic of them either. I think it's near impossible to do this type of game incorrectly. 

However, Unpacking is so frustrating, whoever marketed this as a relaxing, anti-anxiety or anti-rage game was clearly on amphetamine at the time. The whole concept is to unpack boxes and place the items into the house, learning about the house owner/MC as you do so. The issue I had is that every item had a very specific location it belonged to, removing any aspect of creativity or the ability to design YOUR own room. You have to build the game's version of the room, without any hints or direction, and at many times, without any logic of where a real human would place such an item. 

It also didn't have that positive of a message or story to tell, with some aspects of the game being uncomfortable for me to unpack the rooms of. For example, there's a house the character moves into that belongs to their SO, who very clearly doesn't respect or care for the living space of their partner. That level forces you to find very frugal and constrictive ways to place your items, as to not disturb your SO's items, which just read as icky to me. I wouldn't normally point this type of issue out, but considering the type of people who usually play these games, I think this issue with worth mentioning. 

The game also ran on for far too long, namely just because of the nonsensical and specific level designs. I'm talking TWO hours was far too long for this type of game, like it was really that unenjoyable that a mere two hours felt like eternity and I couldn't have been happier to finally uninstall it. 

The only positive I can give this one is that it is fairly simple to 100%.

The person we become, the people we meet, the people we lose...it's all part of our journey and we will always bring all of this with us in form of memories, photos, plushies, gadgets, etc.

Unpacking is a cute concept game where you set-up your living space each time you move, in which you follow the story of the MC's life through environmental story telling.

Pros:
-Very unique concept that really displays master of "show, don't tell"
-lots of cool continuity details
-A somewhat meditative experience

Cons:
-There is only so much you can do within the concept, game is very short (around 3hrs) and gameplay never gets too much more expansive beyond adding more rooms to do the same thing in.
-Some items need to go in specific places, which is a cool way to add some sort of goal/guiding force to the game, but may feel restrictive to those who prefer to have more freedom in decoration.

Overall I think Unpacking takes an interesting concept and plays it out in a very unique way, unfortunately, it just ends up being limited in terms of what it can offer in terms of gameplay content. I'd say it's a very cool and special experience that they've created here, its just not that fun as an overall game. Indie lovers will adore it for its concept, but those looking to "game" might be better served elsewhere.

Rating: 5/10

[h3] [b] Unpacking is like a heartwarming hug in game form. It's a simple concept - just unpack a series of boxes and organize the contents in a home - but it's executed with such care and attention to detail that it feels like you're putting together a digital jigsaw puzzle of someone's life. 📦[/b] [/h3] 

[i] The minimalist graphics and gentle soundtrack make it a soothing experience, and the gradual reveal of the character's story is like unwrapping a present, one layer at a time. It's the ultimate cozy game for a lazy Sunday afternoon!  [/i]☕️🤗

It feels like taking a hot coffee on a rainy day. Just some quiet and relaxing time organizing your stuff and slowly coming to realize what kind of person the tenant is as you watch them grow up. It is inevitable to feel melancholic as her albums get filled up with memories.

It is a lovely and chill game where you unpack stuff. 
A pleasant surprise was how the story is told: you learn about those people while you organize their stuff after moving to different homes. From childhood, finding a career, hobbies, love interests and how everything connect between the years.

It is interesting how everything feels big during your childhood, how each piece shows you a bit of who you are and developed. Also, how you can feel welcome if you have enough space for yourself.

Personally, it is a fun game, I just can't support the political stuff that is implied towards the end. 
I just like to try and keep my games from that. And to add on, the developers refuse to do anything else for this game that people spent 20 bucks on, for only two hours of play. (I've left my computer on way too many times and forgot, thus resulting in the many hours) It get's a little annoying when they seem to have dropped it as a whole.

I've replayed this game over and over despite it only having a set number of levels. Definitely recommend if you want a nice relaxing game to play. Fun to play with friends despite being single-player, everyone suggesting where items should go is part of my personal Unpacking experience :)

The game isn't for me, but I suspect, for the right player,it is the perfect casual they are looking for. It's the type of game that I would recommend to a nice and mild-mannered friend who doesn't play games all that often and wants to try one to relax.

The game utilizes the medium well to tell a personal and intimate story. It falls into that indie space where everything is cozy and low-stake. There is no larger theme or grand narrative - just a person's life slowly unfolding. For better or worse, there is no "point" to the story which makes it a zen game, I suppose.
