As a puzzler, this game does not deliver much challenge. But as an exercise in environmental storytelling, it's superb. It's up to you how much you want to pay attention to how the items change each move, and what kind of backstory that suggests.

If you rush through this game to get the bare minimum layout requirements checked off, you are going to be very disappointed in the perceived value of your $20.

If you play one episode at a time as an experience to just chill and play house for a bit, enjoy all the attention to the art and sound design, and fill in the blanks to the story, you'll enjoy it a lot more.

I love this game to death. i love the story it follows and just unpacking and placing stuff, just so relaxing, I wish the game was longer with more to do after you complete the story but it is still so fun to play

It is an extremely quick game, and I am glad I bought it during a sale price. I enjoyed it very much, but I think the price is too high. On the other hand, if they release free dlc with more rooms and stories, that would definitely be worth it. 

It's nice and calming :)

A great lite-puzzle/slice of life game about unpacking. If you are looking for a pleasant way to spend an afternoon, this is game fits the bill.

The music, visual story-telling (and how the narrative weaves into the gameplay loop), and art style are all beautiful. Before buying, be aware that this is a ~3 hour game with no sandbox mode, so don't play it expecting more than a few hours of content.
Absolutely loved that game ! Very chill and excellent environmental storytelling :D + very nice graphics and ost :)

OMG好上瘾的理房间小游戏，真的很喜欢
缺点：太贵了（好，其实没钱是我的缺点）以及有些东西不知道是什么导致最后总是不知道放在哪…………

Though this game may be short, it tells a nice, and interesting story through the environment while you solve the puzzle of unpacking things. Definite recommend if you just have some time to burn and want something sweet.

I kinda finished the game in 4 hours. So it's a little easy to finish and I hope there would be more levels in the future!
I love the game, it is very relaxing and opens up a lot of creativity :)

I loved the color scheme, the relaxing nature of the game, and the music. I don't like that there is only a couple hours of game to it and that there isn't any replay value unless you're wanting 100%. If they add more content to the game, as in more story to it, then I'll revisit it. But for now it's gotta get the thumbs down.

An amazing game! Lovely graphics, music, game-play etc. However, the only real thing that bothered me is how short it really was, but it is still new and hopefully more content will be added. Try not to rush through it.
it was a really cute game, seems simple but it kind of has a background story as well through moving houses. andddd i think our character has a gf oml so cute i am gonna cry fr

Not many levels, maybe is not fully worth $20 with how little gameplay. the achievements were fun, but there were a lot of stupid blocks on where items were some allowed to go. I get having a sorting system of where things are belonged, but felt some items had too many rules, limiting my gameplay experience., Good game though, I hope they add more levels or the second version has more.
This game is REALLY REALLY fun I enjoyed it a lot! The sounds, the little details. Truly an amazing game. But I do wish to see it continued and added something more to the story

this game is so fun but it can get frustrating but its really fun to play with friend or even ur self this game is amazing and so is the story behind it! i really enjoyed this game i totally recomened

A compelling game that is both nostalgic and fresh without even speaking a word. I highly encourage those on the fence to buy and play when you want to calm down for the night. I’ve never relaxed and zoned out with a game so heavily.

Lovely and relaxing. I wish there were more places to unpack in, with different kinds of people's belongings.
I would love a game that is an interior design type, but with IKEA furnitures.

Unpacking is a very lovely and entertaining game. Uncovering the story of the protagonist was very satisfying. The sound effects are soothing, the type of items you unpack are very realistic, in general the design of the game is very gorgeous and realistic. 

It's sad that the game isn't very long, with only 1 narrative. HOWEVER, considering everything that's gone into it's design and overall development, and with it being made by an Indie company, I'd say it's fair price. Not Witch Beam's fault for the fact that the game went viral, and that people assumed it was some big company that created an over-priced,  half-assed game. Because, ya know, god forbid a smaller company can actually make something good! Right? (Note: Sarcasm intended)

Lovely Game. Wonderful experience. 0 regrets. Thank you <3

I love this game! Honestly, one of my favorite games I've played in a while. I could probably play this over and over again. If you are not one to sit around and just organize and try to figure things out I would not recommend. But if you are that type of person who enjoys the little bits of interior design I would 100% go for it. Again, I love this game so much.

I would love to play this for the first time over and over. I only hope that there may be more characters that we get to learn about the same way in the potential future.

It's such a relaxing game to play. Just to be able to take your time organizing things into place and learning about the character throughout every move/stage of their life. It's touching to see them grow up from childhood to adulthood through every stages and see what items they collect or keep with them throughout the years. 
And most importantly to me, is to see them overcome obstacles. [spoiler] Such as a bad breakup, moving back home, an injury or disability [spoiler/], and much more. There were some instances that really stick with you, Like when you can see the increasing [spoiler] amount of medications or the cane[spoiler/], [spoiler]having to put their diploma in the closet/under the bed [spoiler/], [spoiler] when their new partner moves in (love the LGBTQ+ representation <3), or when you're setting up the nursery [spoiler/].

Simple, straight forward gameplay. If you like (re)decorating your room you will definitely enjoy this game! 
It's a matter of playing through it once and then going through it again to finish up getting all the achievements, but the storyline truly is lovely to see evolve. Really makes you feel for the main character and their accomplishments in life.

C'est un jeu très satisfaisant, où on peut vraiment aller à son rythme. J'ai beaucoup aimé le cheminement entre les différents espaces et les temps de vie, et toutes ces pistes empruntées par le jeu avec ces objets qui disparaissent, apparaissent, ou qui parfois sont toujours là mais qu'on ne parvient plus à ranger comme avant.Je me suis surprise à être émue et proche de cette femme dont je ne connaissais rien, et de très nombreuses fois je m'arrêtais parce que sa vie ou ses propres affaires me ramenaient à mon vécu. C'était un moment un peu hors du temps, paisible et nostalgique. Je n'ai pas vu les heures passer.

The music and the graphics for this game are very relaxing and nice; it's a good game to play when you just want to unwind but still have to use your brain somewhat. I was a little annoyed with how some objects couldn't stack such as the underwear, but it's a minor thing and it didn't take away from the gameplay.

I genuinely wish this game was much longer or had infinite levels of some sort because of how much I loved playing it. The story is sweet and easy to understand even with minimal wording, and I like that you can learn a lot about the person you're playing as just from the items you unpack. I was weary about this game given that it's around 3 hours of gameplay for 20 dollars, but honestly, I think it's a worthwile game if it's your type of thing. Admittedly I got it as a gift, but regardless I was planning on buying it one way or another and after playing it, I can safely say I wouldn't have regretted buying it.

I love the storyline of this game! Showing the main character going through their life and exploring their own personal identity and hobbies. The achievements are super quirky, too. Such a cute soundtrack and totally worth the money. Got all achievements within 5 hours, definetly a once-playthrough game and a second playthrough to finish up achievements. Not a game to repeat.

Super cute, very calming game. I had a lot of fun playing this, especially during college finals. I do wish that the game was longer and had more content for the price, however. It only takes about 3 hours to play in total. I hope that they update for more content in the future. Besides that, it's a very relaxing game that I recommend!

This game is amazing, especially if you, like me, love redecorating your own room. The graphics are charming as hell and the way through which the story is told is absolutely genius, SO good <3 It is also extremely relaxing. I recommend playing the game through normally the first time, and then, if you still can't get enough, play it with the option enabled to put the objects wherever you like. You, like me, may have some strong opinions about where things should go, haha, but it's worth going along with the game the first time, I think you'll see why. Oh, and, one last piece of advice: if you just can't seem to find the right place to put the iPad: it's not an iPad, it's a whiteboard, for the fridge *facepalm*

Be aware that, after playing this game, you may feel a strong urge to spring clean your own room. And maybe redecorate. It happened to me AND to my roommate, to whom I gifted this game. I cannot buy this game often enough, these developers need to be supported so they can make more like this.

In 6 hours I completed the game twice and got all the achiements. Literally the only negative comment I have is I wish it was longer. I could play this for hours upon hours without getting bored. Controls and everything never annoyed me which is rare in my experience with games. Adorable and I will probably replay this a million times :3

I've been interested in this game since I first saw it on sale. I saw the reviews and they all said that it was satisfying but I didn't want to buy it just because it was on sale and at the time, I wasn't really at the point where I wanted to play it because I was busy playing other games. Few months, and I saw my friend playing it and it looked fun so I bought it. All I can say is, it is so soooo good and I wish there was more. I felt satisfied but I just want moreeeee, more rooms, more stuff, more chapters in their life. Playing this game made me realize how disorderly my life is and Unpacking is my way of somehow gaining control over something. It is very relaxing, and the story telling is great. I love games that tells a story without it being boring by reading tons of text (unless its a visual novel, which is understandable). I highly recommend this game if anyone wants something a bit quick but not very time consuming. I understand if some people aren't as satisfied but for me, it is very nice.
I love this game. It's a comfort game for sure, I play it mostly on freeplay and it allows me to feel in control of things when my anxiety/ocd gets out of control. 10/10 game. Worth every penny.

This game is pure poetry. Learning about and coming to care for, and root for, the narrator through their possessions as you organize their life after every move is one of the most beautiful story telling forms I've ever come across...even if we don't always agree about where certain things are supposed to go in a home.

i wish it was longer, with more customization. maybe more color palettes for different objects or way to make it more unique and individual for every player. right now it just doesnt strike me as being worth 20 euros.

A very relatable and lovely story to go along with the relaxing and fun gameplay! I love decorating games such as Sims and love puzzle games. This game scratched both itches. The art and music was beautiful as well.

Sad that there aren't more levels or different stories but i love the game! 
I do like that they added the dark star mode which makes the game more exciting.
Do recommend :)

Lovely and adorable game. It really calms your soul!
The art is cute and the different "lvls" are just perfect c:

Unpacking is a nice and calm game. The game was designed with love and exudes a beautiful charm with its appearance.
You can exit a level at any time, which makes it a good game for in between. [spoiler]Towards the end, I took more breaks as you had to unpack more and more[/spoiler].
Even if you "just" unpack stuff, you understand the story. I especially loved the way some of the details are built in.
Since the game doesn't last that long, it might be more recommended that you buy it on sale.

This game is just breathtaking, not only does it offer you an escape from irl and the satisfaction of creating a cosy space, but it also features very real and open irl character arcs/storylines. 

This game hit me so hard on a certain level, to include what they have featured in this game, is incredible brave, real world and down to earth, creating such a safe and welcoming environment game that is so relatable. 
Truly a fantastic job by the entire team that worked on this game. The art style and the ever changing music in relation to the story compliments this game so perfectly. Cannot give it more credit!! 

My only negative regarding this game: 
While embarking on the character story and figuring out the life you are leading and all the future developments you become so entangled and captured by their story (especially if you binge play it like I did) to then be met with a "you can't progress because some items are not where they should be" Kinda breaks the immersion and vibes of the game as you then become frustrated that you can't find the exact perfect place for those items to go. This however did not remotely ruin the overall game for me and I will still give it the highest recommendation possible!!!

The concept is interesting as you get to learn more about the character and her what's happening in her life based while helping her unpack. However I echo the sentiments of some of the gamers here that, this is simply not worth the $18.50. I completed the gameplay in 3-4h. Just as I was about to get excited about new maps, new things to pack, the game ended. I was dumbfounded. You're better off buying other type of packing/reno SIMs that can offer the same satisfaction but with more content.

J'attendais ce jeu avec impatiente et je suis totalement sous le charme !
Ce jeu est adorable et j'adore le concept et l’exécution. On suit la vie d'une personne de la petite enfance à sa vie d'adulte, de ses réussites à ses malheurs. 
C'est un fantastique jeu qui, certes, ne change pas une fois qu'on y a déjà joué et ne procure pas une expérience très longue, est charmant et absolument bien fait.
Je le recommande vivement, Unpacking est fantastique !

This game is amazing. It's adorable. You are living life as a female from childhood to adulthood and each scenario that you unpack tells a part of the life story. The twist at the end literally made me cry. One play through takes about 3 hours but you can unlock achievements/stickers so multiple playthroughs are recommended by me. This game means so much to me and once you finish it I think you'll understand why. I don't want to spoil anything by giving more details! <3

Absolutely LOVE this game! I was skeptical at first, of the idea of arranging and organizing items in a game where I can't seem to bring myself to do that in my own life. But as I began to play, and sunk into the story line, the comforting music, and gorgeous graphics, it was impossible not to fall in love. It is fun, relaxing, and the perfect accompaniment to a hot cup of tea on a rainy day.

such a cute game. i was waiting for release for a little while and was NOT disappointed! it's the perfect game for people who like the sorting, organizing or collecting aspects of games. i do wish it were longer but that's always how i feel about my favorites. i'm so excited to see what the creator puts out in the future ^.^

This game is so beautiful. The art style and the music/ambience and the way that the game tells a story as you continue is so amazing and it all works so well. Overall this game the story this game told was wonderful, I'm not sure about the replay ability but I will say that this game is definitely amazing.
A beautiful art style, soundtrack and story, a great game for a quiet night in

A beautiful game with a really good pixel art. It's calm and slow, perfect when you want to chill for a moment or two! Music fits perfectly with type of gameplay. There's even a hint of story involved!

If any game deserves 10/10, it's this game!

Its quite short for its price, but fun and relaxing, id reccommed it for good anxiety relaxtion; but if you got the attention span of having adhd like me you may get bored of it quickly; other than that uts a sweet game.
I realllyyy loved the game. It is a very chill and amazing game where you can organize your own stuff. Sometimes is a little frustrating if you are a very OCD person but the game is totally worth it.
Nice and relaxing game. Some of the items are a bit unusual for some playes so it would be nice to have maybe like a checklist. Also, it'll be great to have more storylines you can play.

The game presents itself as a puzzle game, but it quickly reveals its instead a story through this persons life. Seeing what they bring and what gets added you get to see their ups and downs. I can't convince you if it the price is worth your money, but I can guarantee it is worth your time.

It's difficult for me to know how to rate this game. I think in short that I have to concur with what many other reviewers have said; while the game is very good and fun to play, there is very little content to the game, and little replay potential, and thus the price point of the game seems a bit steep.
I bought this game on sale and ultimately wished I'd waited longer to pick it up, in the hopes of getting a better sale. All in all, though, I did enjoy playing; the art style of the game is cute, the story that unfolds of your character's life, as told through unpacking, is beautiful and often touching. It was always exciting to find cherished items from earlier scenes to unpack and place again. 
Yet ultimately, unless further content is added it's not a game I'm likely to pick up again on a whim. The story felt very self-contained and very much felt like closing a book at the end. 
Ultimately, if this game calls to you, and you think it looks like it would be fun to play, then you are absolutely right and it is; but I would advise balancing the 3-4 hours you'd get out of this game with the current price point.
One thing I do think would improve on the game would be a sort of "infinite" mode with randomly generated items you could set up and decorate, before moving on to another, continuously. Such an addition would add a lot of replay value to the game.

Je vous recommande fortement ce jeu, il n'a beau pas être très long il est très agréable à jouer. La direction artistique ainsi que la bande sons sont très très très bien faite, le jeu arrive à développer une ambiance en très agréable en peut de temps. 
Bref, je vous le conseil fortement.

It's a very cute game! It's super relaxing and really does kill time. Though it's a tad short, it's well worth it to buy the game! The storytelling that's told within each stage of life is subtle and wordless, but the details explain everything that goes on within the main character's life. It had me emotional at the end, but in a good way! I'd love for more games to be like this. Not at all stressful (unless you're like me and stressed over where the heck some items belonged). Calming music with some ambiance of each room playing. Totally recommend!

I love this game so much. It's a super zen puzzle game with some very nice retro to current day-touches, and it has a nice story, if you pay attention.
My only complaint is that there isn't more to unpack. :D
I very much recommend this game.
Fun game, nice and chill can take your time and place things how you like. Fun way to organize the house how you want to! So you can make it different everytime.

I love this pixel styled game so much! I was playing it in a Discord server with a few of my friends and just watching it convinced a majority of them to buy it! We're all obsessed with it! The SFX and visuals are so satisfying and the minimal storytelling was fun to figure out throughout the playthrough! We had so much fun organizing everything and it was just as fun the second playthrough as well! 
I really hope the game devs update the game with more levels! I really wanna play more with more rooms! 
Also, the plants are so satisfying to look at, and that's a *me* thing.

Es ist ein sehr ruhiges und angenehmes Spiel. Die Musik war mir teilweise etwas zu unruhig und ich fand sie nicht so schön. Die Gesichte ist schön. Leider ist Unpacking zu kurz. Es lohnt sich zu spielen aber wenn es am schönsten ist, ist es vorbei.

Very calming and interesting game. This game is kind of a home-decorating sim meets storytelling. It's not intended to do as quick as possible. Whenever I found myself wanting to hurry things up, I took a small break. Really be in the right headspace for this game to work it's magic. Otherwise it takes away from the story. A small point of critique is the motions of grabbing stuff and placing them can get a bit repetitive, especially when unboxing stuff from a different room, and it sometimes frustrated me. Also my OCD brain got a bit frustrated when I had placed everything neatly and then found out there was another [item] that didn't fit on the shelf. 
As for the story, I think it's cute, relatable and a plus is that its LGBT friendly. I want more of this game! And I would prefer more short stories (with small housesspaces), as getting to know the owner of the boxes is what grabbed me the most about the game. In the final levels there was relatively less story and more unpacking due to the bigger houses.

I really enjoyed this game and would recommend :) Now I gotta find something like it!!

This game is one of my favourite games of all time, the story is subtle if you chose to ignore it and the lack of words through the game makes the game understandable even in languages it hasn't been specifically been written for. Whilst the story is subtle the message is a beautiful one and is only accentuated by the phenomenal soundtrack that this game possesses. It has great replay value as you can fine tune your rooms to your liking as your styling changes, you can edit the rooms at any time you wish. 

This has got to be one of the most accessible games of the decade, you can adjust highlight colours alongside the ability to remove all puzzle elements from the game by allowing you to place items anywhere, the lack of written words means you don't even need to be able to hear or read to play this game, the  occasional spoken words are always accompanied by subtitles which makes this game accessible for most people.

The artwork of the game is incredible as well and the reoccurring items bring nostalgia for the previous levels. It's graphics are simple so many computers/laptops will be able to run it without any worries.

Overall this game is incredibly good and I would definitely recommend buying it if you can, this game isn't incredibly long at around 4-5 hours, but the replay ability of the levels means you can go back and re-experience the levels after the fact.

As everyone has already said, the game is definitely far too short, which isn't necessarily a bad thing in my opinion!
I know all the hard work that went into the beautiful art and all the unique sound effects in the game, so if I wasn't naturally frugal with my money, I definitely wouldn't mind the price tag! (I bought the game on sale for ~$16!)

The storytelling is excellent, so much said in just the items you unpack over the years. Such an easy-to-connect story for any young adult or adult going through the wild ocean of life.

I would say that my only negative was that I wasn't sure what some items were and thus sometimes didn't know where they were supposed to go. Which didn't matter too much for the most part, but I sure did feel a little silly when I realized that the rolled up paper that I had assumed was wrapping paper were actually posters, haha.

Super relaxing and immensely satisfying! What a wonderful game.

Good game, very relaxing, fun for people who like to sort or organize things. It also has a nice story going on, as you follow the same young lady from her childhood bedroom, through uni, shared housing, and the trials of young adulthood with each move and adjustment in their life.

The only bad point for this game I'd say is that there is only the one story to follow right now, making the game very short, you can complete it in just a few hours if you don't spend a long time getting your items just right.

I'd love to see the developers add more stories.

Unpacking is always the best part of moving and this game lets you do that without the real world clutter. This has been a rough year and this game has provided a calm respite amidst it all. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Ridiculously short for the price. I've played through twice - once for fun and again to get all the achievements - and it only took me around 5-6 hours(ignore my play time, I left it open by accident). Maybe buy if on sale or something, but definitely not worth £15.49

The game starts off very cute and simple. Unpacking your childhood bedroom and calmly fitting things in place like a puzzle. I had no clue the game was going to tell such an emotional story. Told only through the game play of unpacking the moving boxes throughout a character's life, the narrative is so strongly present. 

Though the gameplay is fairly short, I got really attached to our MC and literally cried several times! I would love to see the additions of new characters and stories in the future :)

Really love the game, but it's so short for the full price. I finished in less than 3 hours. There are 3 save files, which I thought would be different people, but it appears to be the same play through 3 times. I was waiting to get it on sale but it wasn't happening, so I bit the bullet and got it at full price; wish I had waited. However, it's a really good game. During the level where she buys more stuff for herself, I was really excited because I thought she was getting a girlfriend... Disappointed when that wasn't the case haha. Would love to see them add either more levels with aging further, or another person's life. I'm hoping one of those will happen, since it's so new still and getting really good press.

A lovingly designed feel-good game packed with heart and humor.
Perfect for unwinding and exploring. Wonderful soundtrack.

All of the feels! The sound was nice and satisfying when interacting with objects, the soundtrack was relaxing, and the story points were a nice touch~ I would definitely play a 3rd time if not more. c:

un pequeño juego para pasar un rato ameno y olvidarte de lo que esta ahí afuera, si prestas atención a la historia se vuelve mucho mas interesante.
es muy interesante como yo me vi reflejada en la historia de la protagonista y como muchas escenas en verdad son mi vida.
10/10

Ein unfassbar entspannendes Spiel mit viel Liebe zu kleinen Details. 
Das Spiel schafft es, mit nur sehr wenigen Worten eine süße Story zu erzählen.
Ich würde mich auf weitere Games wie dieses und vielleicht sogar eine Fortsetzung freuen! :)

I liked the game, graphically cute, soundtrack isnt annoying or anything.
I would recommend it to anyone, the end was also a lil' cute surprise, i teared up a bit :'')

Tho, I hope there will be more content at some point. There's  few levels to go through.. but it would be nice
if, by any new game, there would be at least a few different paths to go :(

Love from Germany :)

Ein wunderschönes Spielerlebnis! Wer einfach mal abschalten möchte ist mit diesem Spiel genau richtig.
Der Soundtrack ist sehr stimmig und verleiht eine tolle Atmosphäre.
Man kann insgesamt 3 Speicherstände anlegen, so kann mein Partner das Spiel gleich mittesten.
Rundum ein wirklich gelungenes Spiel
Cozy and wholesome game, perfect for relaxing after a stressful day. Loved the story the objects made trough the years. Looking forward to a sequel!

This is a very casual laid back experience that i really enjoyed. No pressure, great pixel art and nice music. The only downside is that it's too short. I wish it had something to do after you finished all the unpacking so that you could come back and play it more.

Cute and relaxing to play. I enjoyed going through each room of the different levels and putting things in order and seeing whats new and what was left behind. But its a very short game. Fun to play. Hope they add more levels though.

This game is calming for me, and as someone who is meticulous, I love the organizational aspect.
The graphics are adorable, and the only part that makes me sad is how short it is, but I still love it.

This game is beautiful. Its one of the most relaxing and calming games that gives Serotonin as you find new ways to place things. 
my only issue is its so short. 20$ does feel like a lot when the story took me only an hour and a half. the replay-ability is there, but i wish they had a free play, where random houses were put there and you could unpack for a mini story. Things could be randomized and you could add new items and take away random ones to make each random house a new experience. 
yet i do understand that the programming and art that would need to take place for this to happen. I'd be happy to wait. 
i guess i just want more; and want to see where else this can go.

The game is incredibly comforting and chill, the story however only follows one person along her moving and is the same every time you make a new save so it can be repetitive if you plan to replay it often.
This is kind of an emotional game, with great character-devolpment, and a sweet ending, it is worth the $20 price tag.

This game was recommended to me by a close friend, and it's exactly what I needed on a quiet evening.
It is relaxing, and the achievement list is fun to complete. There are little surprises, which caught me off guard at first.

Pay attention to your story, and how it has changed you (and your possessions) over the course of your life.
this is genuinely the most relaxing game i have ever played. the ending is really wholesome too and it was so joyful to watch our character's story grow with something as simple as unpacking boxes.
It was a cute game with a nice, somewhat hidden story to it. I do wish there was more overall (other 'storylines' and styles, etc). On sale, this isn't a bad game to pick up!

Unpacking is a game that's simple and a little tricky at the same time.  Finding the right places for things isn't always intuitive, but the music and the process is so nicely calming.  Really, I think the music and the colour palettes are my favourite things about the game as a whole.  The first time I did a full playthrough, I didn't expect the feelings that came with it, but by the end, I felt so happy and so at peace.  It was a great story that unfolded through the process.  Absolutely beautiful.
this game is cute, relaxing, and easy to earn achievements, but it's too short i only spent about 6 hours playing and it ends, hopefully, the developers will update more content.

its a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good game!!! i cried a lot at the ending dude it felt really good to have this kind of cute representation but MAN the game needs more levels!!! it ended so quickly.......... every book being a new save is good but i thought those were different stories!! This game has really good potential!! i hope in the future we will be able to get another stories

Incredibly calming and relaxing to play. The progression through someone's life that you see through unpacking someone's belongings is a really neat concept and I wish the game lasted longer than it did. As much as I loved it, definitely wait for a sale to snag it. The little achievements when placing items in certain places was fun. There were moments where I was trying to place an item, but I had no idea what it was so I struggled trying to place it where it belonged.

[b]Jeu très sympathique, très reposant mais court[/b]. Ce jeu propose de suivre l'histoire du protagoniste au travers de plusieurs déménagement.
Personnellement, j'ai trouvé ce jeu assez émouvant avec un très bonne DA. L'immersion se fait facilement dans un ambiance chill et relaxante (parfait pour après de longue journée de travail :) ). 
Le [b]jeu est très court[/b] donc si vous cherchez un jeu qui va vous prendre des dizaines d'heure ou plus, il ne vous conviendra pas. Heureusement, la qualité d'un jeu ne se fait pas uniquement sur sa durée de vie et je pense que ce jeu vaut ses 20 balles.

When I first started playing, I thought it was going to be a game simply about, well, unpacking your stuff and finding a place for everything. But the more I played, the more I started to understand the protagonist's story and how every move to a new place symbolized her growth as a person. 

And not just in the places but also in her posessions: 

The diploma that hangs on the walls but is stored under the bed when she moves in with her boyfriend. 

The pin going through the ex-boyfriend's face when you try to hang it up on the pin wall and how it's seen as a mistake that it's there and the game makes you store it away where it can't be seen. 

The awards on her Bookshelf in her own apartment that weren't there before, and all the sketches of farm animals slowly turning into a book series.

The rainbow underwear in the drawer when she starts dating a woman.

The visual storytelling is truly stunning, and the song that plays during the credits is so heartwarming!

Apart from that, the game also manages really well to emulate the feeling of "Oh no, where do I put THIS thing now?" and "Why did I pack my undies in with my pots and pans?"

Alll in all, a fantastic game that I will play many times over.

My only criticism would be that it is short. You can complete the game in 2.5 hours but there are achievements, so it does have some replay value. I would have liked more of the "story" and to follow this character throughout their whole life rather than just part of it. But, this is a zen puzzle game so you're expected to relax and take your time. It also has a great art style. I'm sure that it was time intensive to make, so I don't begrudge the cost, I just hope that there will be more content at some point!

Unpacking is so fresh and [i]real[/i], and it hits home as someone who has moved around a lot over the years. It's authentic environmental storytelling, and the devs have clearly put an insane amount of love into the game.

It's visually beautiful. Every pixel is placed with care, and there was never any visual errors or confusion. The little nods to gaming consoles and references were a treat. The sound design is impressive, with over 14k different files for each and every sound, be sure to bounce off all the different surfaces just to appreciate the audio! The ending song is also precious and lovely, and I found it a fitting end to the story.

While it's very much a game that can be enjoyed by everyone, there's also a distinct Aussie feel from the Brisbane-based dev team that I appreciated a lot. Little details that centred the world and really resonated with me as an Aussie player, so kudos to the devs for that.

Witch Beam has handcrafted a beautiful, compelling narrative with the right notes of growing up and finding yourself, and the first playthrough will fly by. But not to worry, as there's achievements and stickers to collect, so you'll have plenty of reasons to revisit Unpacking and truly admire all the love and care that went into crafting this game.

So...this is boring.  I have unpacked a lot in my life..,wasn't fun in real life, not fun in a game.  I figured this would at least be a great story--going through out their whole life...but no.  This game suddenly ends.  I've read other reviews where the reviewer claims to cry at the end, I have no idea why anyone would cry in this short 2.5 hour game.

THE POSITIVE
At first glance, it seems a rather simple game. I had played the demo during LudoNarraCon in April and knew it was a nice relaxing experience but I was totally unprepared for how much more there was. You unpack someone's life and get to experience changes in very creative ways, and I won't say more because it should be a firsthand experience. I will say that this game takes environmental storytelling to a whole NEW level in the best way possible.

Aside from the story, the sound design is so satisfying. At many points, I had to check that the sound of a humming computer wasn't coming from my own, or that birds were not indeed singing outside my window at midnight. Flush a toilet and leave the room and you can hear it in the distance. Pick up a hot water bottle and shake it to hear the water slosh around. Little things like this really add up to gameplay that sucks you in. 

I played through this game a few times to get all of the achievements and found new things each time. I will say that I think the replayability is limited due to the number of things to put away and how tedious it can become depending on how frequently you play it (I played all 15 hours this week so maybe don't do that). 

THE NEGATIVE
I had played through twice and got 100% achievements and that totaled about 15hrs (give or take walking away with the game pulled up). I was fortunate to find this on sale, but I struggle with the idea of $20 for roughly 5-7hrs of gameplay and from what I hear, no DLC is planned. It was a nice story, an innovative gameplay experience, and relaxing. But it was also short-lived.

IN CONCLUSION
So I recommend it based on a great experience, albeit a short one.

tl;dr: puzzle game of finding the right place for stuff; mostly intuitive but a couple of times unclear what the item was; mostly environmental storytelling, not as touching as I expected, more saccharine than miserable; just under 3 hours to "beat", the rest of my playtime is achievement hunting and waiting for the final trading card to drop; the final house is a couple rooms too large; unexpected functionality of unpacking playback and GIF generation.

Detailed thoughts:
Unpacking is a puzzle game (or "game", depending on your view of artsy indie stuff) of opening boxes and putting their contents into fitting spaces, often in rooms other than where the box they came in was. The level of restrictions on items varies, some items you have to get right down to the correct shelf, and some of them you can pretty much leave anywhere short of dropping them on the floor. After your first pass of unpacking every item in every room, the incorrectly placed items get a red outline around them (as do the room icons on the floor plan for rooms with incorrectly places objects in them). For me, it was typically 2 or 3 items per room, so the placement isn't too counter-intuitive or restrictive. After all the items are in their correct place, you can finish the level and move on to the next.

There are about 8 levels in total, if memory serves. The final one was a couple rooms too long, but that could just be my abysimally short attention span talking. I "beat" the game in just under 3 hours. I'll let you decide whether that's long enough for the price. The rest of my playtime is me hunting for the achievements I missed and waiting for the final trading card to drop. Also, considering I got the final achievement at about 3.2 hours and my final playtime is over 4 hours, the time requirement for the final card is a bit too much.

The story is told almost exclusively through environmental clues to be found in all the changing homes and added or removed items you unpack. There are some hints of struggles, successes, etc. Mercifully, the tone is never even close to the utter misery that many indie games (especially the dreaded walking simulators) so love, presumably thinking suffering is somehow profound. If anything, the game might come across as too saccharine for many players. I'm far from cold or emotionally unreceptive to games, so I was rather disappointed I didn't find the game as impactful as the person whose recommendation I followed supposedly did.

The art style is okay, fairly standard indie pixel art, though a couple of times I couldn't quite tell what the item was, causing me to struggle with intended placement.

The game also had some unexpected functionality: you can watch a playback of a level, and even generate a GIF of one of the rooms. The playback was nice, but the GIF generator felt unnecessary.

Unpacking is a short and simple experience that ((packs)) a heartfelt narrative with every item out of the box. Like everyone has said, it’s amazing the attention to detail they put into the sound design. The adaptive plinks and plonks to each surface really help foster the character of the game, taking the roots of its simple sorting puzzle game mechanics and tangling them into the story. The objects you are placing don’t feel like puzzle pieces but parts of the characters life–They hold weight and are characters within themselves, making you want to find places for everything not just to complete the level but because you sympathize with wanting the things you hold dear to be on display. 
One gripe I do have is the game’s soundtrack. It felt that sometimes the music would be seemingly looping randomly and abruptly cutting to a new motif which really made it feel like a shotty DJ with like 4 mp3 files was given too much power in the music department. I’d recommend playing with your own music, or just turning it off if you really want a good immersive experience.

Excellent petit jeu Australien et une très belle surprise !

L'originalité et la simplicité du gameplay, très agréable et sympathique, sans prise de tête, "chill" comme on dit, cache pourtant une discrète couche de narration et de story-telling que l'on attendait pas forcément mais qui donne du coeur au jeu.
En effet, bien que le jeu, qui consiste à déballer et ranger les affaires de la protagoniste dans ses différents "nouveau chez soi" successif à différentes étapes de sa vie, ne comporte aucun dialogue, aucune communication verbale, ni même écrite (si ce n'est une phrase de la protagoniste accompagnant chaque photo de fin de niveau), il y a bien une Histoire, un fil narratif entre chaque niveau.
Mais c'est au joueur de découvrir par lui-même "ce que raconte" chaque déménagement de la protagoniste sur sa vie.

Le tout, grâce uniquement aux objets, souvenirs, ustensiles et effets personnels trimbalés par celle-ci.
Et ça marche superbement bien, nous impliquant dans le jeu au delà du gameplay "point & click" en attirant notre curiosité et en nous incitant à nous demander/essayer de deviner ce que peut être la vie de notre protagoniste sans nom et sans visage.

Niveau gameplay & narration/histoire, c'est fait...
Maintenant, il faut aussi dire que le jeu a une musique discrète mais très calme et agréable et de qualité. On peut retrouver ce côté paisible que certains d'entre nous ont pu connaître en jouant à des jeux bonne-esprit / Life Simulation/Builder, comme les Sims 1, 2 ou 3, tant certains morceaux sont dans le même esprit.

Le sound design est aussi très bon, chaque objet déplacé à son propre son pour vous donner une sensation plus palpable et plus clair de ce que vous êtes en train de déplacer (car vous ne savez pas forcément toujours ce que vous êtes en train de déplacer, puisque aucun libellé ou texte ne viendra vous le dire. Mais heureusement, le visuel de chaque objet est très explicite et identifiable, à quelques rares exceptions près peut-être). Chaque objet d'ailleurs produit un son diffèrent selon l'endroit où vous le déposez. Ce qui peut paraître très anodin, mais c'est agréable à l'oreille.

Enfin, niveau graphisme, les images du jeu, en bande-annonce comme sur les pages du store donnent le ton.
C'est très joli, très esthétique et coloré. Les décors sont très beaux et je me suis même surpris à me dire, après avoir ranger les objets de notre protagonistes dans telle ou telle pièce de cet univers fictif, que : "tiens, c'est une bonne idée de mobilier de rangement / d'agencement de meuble" lol. (réflexion de mec qui n'a beaucoup d'idée de rangement dans son propre chez soi réel, xD...)

Enfin, le dernier aspect que j'évoquerai, et ce sera surement vu comme un défaut pour beaucoup (mais pas pour moi) : la durée de vie du jeu.
Vous pouvez le voir en l'état, j'ai fini le jeu à 100%, avec apparemment 5 heures de jeu au compteur, que j'ai fait d'une seule traite, tellement j'ai kiffé le jeu.

Ce seul point "peut-être" négatif en rebutera surement certain qui se demanderont "5h de jeu,  est-ce que ça vaut bien 20€ ?"
Personnellement, je trouve que oui pour une telle expérience de jeu aussi originale que créative et bien pensé. Et je me dis que j'ai bien mis 14€, au cinéma, pour aller voir 2h de chiasse de film Marvel à mainte reprise... Alors en comparaison, 20€ pour 5h de jeu vidéo où je m'amuse et découvre une petite pépite, c'est une très belle affaire.
A chacun de voir après. :-)

Mais voilà, avis très positif de ma part. Excellent même.

Unpacking is a cute, relaxing organization-based puzzle game that tells a story of growth and self-discovery with a nontraditional method of story-telling. This story is told through the personal belongings of the main character, a nameless and relatively faceless woman, as we follow her from her childhood home to her adulthood. 
(FYI This review is very spoiler heavy and full of rambling).

We never hear her voice until what I assume is her singing in the end credits, which is very a nice song, btw-- but we get a sense of her character through her hobbies and the things she keeps with her from each chapter of her life. She's sentimental in that she keeps her childhood plushies, such as the well-loved pig; she's an unashamed 'nerd' and DnD player as she collects figures, video games, and dice; and finally, it's also clear that she is a proud Jewish woman, who's happily married to another woman and creating a loving, inclusive home in the last chapter. 

The home that we help them build is one that seems harmonious and to be filled with warmth; as pictures line the fridge and they eventually adopt/surrogate/have a baby together in their dream home. I really love this representation and the progression of this relationship, as well as the main character's own growth from what I assume was a really intense heart break from another relationship. This game is sweet in that it shows how she is able to rely on the support of her family as she gets back on her feet and become more confident in herself, as well as her art and art degree-- something that she obviously enjoyed and had conceptual ideas for, but ended up putting to the back burner as she was forced to work a retail job to keep herself a float. 

As an artist, I can appreciate and sympathize with the progression of growing into one's art style and strengths- it's very easy to doubt your skills, especially when faced with the mountain of work that goes into practicing and creating things. With the grind of modern life, it can be daunting to ask yourself: am I going to create work that will support me? Will anyone even like what I make? Am I just wasting my life, chasing a dream that doesn't exist? 

These are hard questions that many face, and looking at history with artist's like Van Gogh- it's clear that not everyone may see or profit from their work during their life time. However, I believe that it's necessary to chase a life that involves/relishes in the things you're passionate about. And this game is a wonderful representation about that passion and aspiration to create. 

TLDR: For all of that, I'm quite happy that I purchased this game- especially given how relaxing it is with the addition of calming music and the cute little sound effects of setting things down. I mean, playing it in-between studying for my finals really gave me some down time- if that attests to how relaxing it is lol. The price IS a bit high for the play time though, but I personally can't gripe too much given how much I enjoyed it and I hope it supports the team behind it.

You really get to learn about the main character and it is amazing how the simple concept of unpacking boxes and putting things on shelves can describe so much about someone's life. I absolutely love this game and hope the developers are considering making more content like this, because I am honestly speechless. The graphics, the soundtrack, just everything about this game was perfect. I loved it. The only thing I would change would be to make certain items more flexible, so players have more of an option when organizing where they would like to place items. Other than that, I love this game. I have played for 5 hours as of this review, and I have completed the main story, but only have 14/25 achievements so I may go back and play through again just to see the little details I may have missed. 10/10, 5 stars, 100% recommend this game to anyone and everyone.

love the art, very relaxing organising everything and anything other than my own life.

do hope there is more content for the price

I absolutely love the simplicity of the game! If you just want to relax playing a game mindlessly, this is the game you want. I had the opportunity to promote this game and absolutely enjoyed every minute of it. The artwork in the game is simple and the story line keeps things open-ended and based on interpretation. 

One small flaw I did bump into is that the music does turn off if you're taking a bit longer on the level, which wasn't too big of a problem to me as I put my own music on after I realized it shuts off. Absolutely beautiful game and highly recommend.

Literally the best cutest and relaxing and semi challenging game ever very worth it for the price and peaceful music items and story line makes it so good 10/10 wish it was longer was very fun to complete

Usually I would be funny with my reviews but this is a very fun game and I would totally recommend this to other people because it is very fun and has some very cool features. It is a kind of short game but you will never not want to hop back onto it just to remember that you played it. You may think it is kinda stupid cause you want freedom but once you finish the game you get as much freedom as you need to fulfill your unpacking dreams without actually moving. Hope you have fun if you get it!

I played this game for 15 hours. I don't know how or why I played that long. I just find myself watching the story over and over again. It brings me a lot of joy.  The graphics are beautiful, and it's really fun to listen to the noises that the items make when you shake them. The items are really adorable and it's fun to see where you can put them.

I've gotten all of the achievements, and I loved to watch myself getting them after I finished the levels, because it looked like I was randomly putting them everywhere. I discovered this game through Vixella on Youtube. 

A lot of people don't think it's worth the amount of money that they had to pay, which is 20 US dollars. I think that it was worth it, as I find myself going back to play it in my downtime. After I finish this review I'm going back into the game.

I wish that there was some more content but NOT because I don't think it's worth it, but because I wanted to see our character through the rest of her life. I wanted to be able to see if they only have one child, or if they have more, and to take care of them as they grow older - by getting more furniture for the kid(s) as they grow older, and having to rearrange the house as the family grows. I think that it would be amazing to see our character's journey until they're old. (I can't handle the idea of the character passing away at the end of the game)

I believe that it took the developers 3-5 years to make the game. I'm so happy that I could play this game. 
At first, I thought that I wouldn't like it since it was just unpacking things but as the time passed I saw the story of our character continue. I loved seeing that. As someone who moved a lot it brought up a bunch of feelings.

Overall, if you like peaceful games where you don't have to think, and allow yourself to relax after a long day... then you will love this game. If you like a game with a small story involved then play this game - it's very easy to get invested in our character's life. 

Thank you "Witch Beam" and "Humble Games" for allowing us to play this amazing game. 

P.S. if you make a sequel I would absolutely play it.
Jeu très mignon, très relaxant. J'espère qu'on aura des DLC, car le contexte est super simple mais tellement apaisant! Je recommande.

I have to agree with the others: It is a nice, soothing game. But it is very short for the money you paid for it. I would wait for a discount.
Maybe they will add more content later.

Super cute game and was really fun to play but knowing now that there is no future content planned is really disappointing. The $20 price is a little ridiculous for how small of a game it is. I had hoped they would add more content to justify the cost. Overall it is still a very well done game if you're okay overspending a bit for it.

While I liked the game and how relaxing it was, there is no way it is worth $20. I played for less than 3 hours and finished the game. There needs to be a lot more content to make the price worth it. The game itself was cute and enjoyable, but the pricetag is atrocious.

This was such an enjoyable and peaceful game, great to play after a stressful day at work, tho it's a bit short for paying $20usd. I hope to see future Free updates if it's to stay at that price as it only took me 2 hours to finish. It lacks content. The story was nicely told with only using unpacking boxes, I liked going through the different stages and seeing the subtle changes and although I feel the price is pretty high for what you get, I don't regret purchasing this at all.

This game is absolutely one of the most chill pixelart experience I had the occasion to live, really recommending it to anyone who wants to relax. You're following the adventures of someone through unpacking their moving belongings. 
A very few words are used, and what the box are containing through the different steps of the story helps you to make hypothesis about what's going on : I really have a soft spot for those kind of games hence a lot of things are said without any written text, which requires a great amount of creativity :D !! 

The amount of efforts that were put into the art is amazing, as well as the background music that seems like chip-generated synth kind of instruments which feels so nostalgic yet calming !! It's crazy how much different sounds effects were made in order for each objet to react logically according to that one specific surface there were put onto ! 

I finished it in two days, and it's an entire re-fill of good vibes :3 ♥ Definitely will follow Witch Beam on my socials and look forward their next game !!

Let me start off by saying that the game itself is really cute and very calming and I've played it a couple of times. 

Pros: 
- Relaxing game 
- Cute, slice of life story
- Free Place Mode 
- Adorable graphics 

Cons: 
- Limited Replayability
- Only one story 
- Pricey (on account of replayability) 
- Free placement mode only after finishing the story once 
- Sometimes you can't tell what an item is or where the game designer actually wants you to put it and you can't progress to the next level without just shoving it in random places. 

tl;dr I really like the game, but it needs other stories or maps or something because just doing the same maps started to get boring.

荷ほどきの手伝いで自分の好きなところに主人公のアイテムを配置していく、レイアウトとパズルが合わさったもので
見た目も可愛らしいドット絵でなじみやすいです。
さらに、ステージを重ねる度に同じ主人公の荷ほどきを手伝うことになるのですが、主人公が少しずつ成長しているのが伝わってきて変わっていくものや、変わらないものが荷ほどきで分かるのも面白いです。
強いストーリー性があるわけではないのですが、しっかり最後に締めくくってくれて少し泣きそうになりました。

Das Spiel ist schön gestaltet und entspannt zu spielen. Allerdings ist die Spielzeit von 3 Stunden viel zu kurz und daher ist der Spielepreis von 20€ NICHT gerechtfertigt. Leider wusste ich das nicht, sonst hätte ich nur 2 Stunden gespielt um eine Rückerstattung zu beantragen.
Leider gibt es auch nur eine Story.
The game needs more levels to play because you can literally beat the game in 3-4 hours.. It should be cheaper.

I absolutely enjoy this game!!!! It is so calming and relaxing though I do wish there were more rooms to decorate and different story lines to play through. Don't get me wrong this is one of my favorite games but playing the same story no mater how many items you can change places with other items gets a little boring. Still very enjoyable to play none the less.

This game is great! I love the storytelling that is embedded throughout the levels along with a weird sense of nostalgia of old doll house flash games. I'm a little disappointed there are only 8 levels (and as amazing as each one is) they don't feel worth the $20 game price.

Unpacking is a puzzle game that tells the story by way of, well, unpacking. Not only is the art attractive, but the gameplay is simple enough that you can grasp the concept fairly quickly: Make sure everything is in its proper place.

Don't let that fool you though. Once multiple rooms start coming into the picture, things can get chaotic. You'll likely have to shuffle things around just to get everything to fit. But it never feels frustrating or impossible to figure out, which I love.

The story itself follows a woman as she grows up and lives her life. I won't go into detail about the story itself, but it's a genuinely relatable and hopeful one that kept me from putting it down from the moment I started it to the moment I had to take a break. I honestly found myself tearing up when I could identify with the character, and I found myself smiling and laughing when things from earlier levels made an appearance.

If puzzles that tell a story are your kind of thing, then pick this up. It's worth the price, and I would love to see more games like it. You can eaily finish it in a day if you have the time to kill, and the number of easter eggs and hidden secrets scattered here and there makes it worth replaying levels later on.

TLDR - This game is good. Buy it.

The game is absolutely beautiful, heart-warming and cozy. The game overall and the ending made me feel great! Everything has been so lovingly created and there is amazing attention to detail! Unpacking has the most interesting story-telling style I have experienced in any medium so far.
I loved the game but it's very short! Finished the game in like 3 hours but could have finished it quicker. Think the price is pretty steep for the gameplay time but brilliant game!

I love the simplicity but addictiveness of the game. The fun little storyline, and the cool things you can do. I love the little easter eggs of things you can put in and the art of the game. It's fun to play with a s/o and to just spend time together. The ending credits legit made me cry, 10/10 "I KNEW THEY WERE LESBIANS" - My girlfriend while I was playing with her. Honestly the work put into this game is amazing, I wish there was more. definitely something to play again <3 One thing I will say, I first thought 20$ would be too expensive for something so small/simple, but the work and art and the indie style game and the amount of love you can tell that was put into the game is honestly worth it. It's the little things that matter. I wish there was more that you could do in the game, but I look forward to further developments of the company and hopefully the game as well. Also I would just like to say, this game releases my stress levels after a long day at school/work, the relaxation and serotonin the game gives me, almost cures my depression

This game is wonderfully calming and seeing the slow evolution of the woman whose life we follow is very well done. Also, the ability to watch back your progress is just a perfect addition. I love this game so much :)

this game was so much fun! I will replay it on days when I need to decompress. I felt very nostalgic unpacking so many familiar things from my childhood, teenage years, uni years, and so on! the aesthetic is sooo beautiful and it is a wonderfully calming game. definitely recommended if you like comfy/cosy games!

Aslında oyunun tek amacı koli açıp içindeki eşyaları yerleştirmek değil. Sürekli aynı kişinin eşyalarını yerleştirdiğimiz için eşyalara bakarak hayatının hangi kısmında olduğunu, nasıl zevklere sahip olduğunu az çok anlayabiliyoruz. Küçük de olsa oyuna hikaye katmaları pek şirin olmuş.

Unpacking is a delicately crafted game made with an immense amount of passion and love. The story of Unpacking is, while the gameplay is incredibly simple, is complex and is up for interpretation. With each stage (years), we as players, are taken through major life events that left me internalising my own memories of similar situations with a variety of emotions; sadness, happiness, excitement, etc. 
Unfortunately, the game is so enjoyable that it was a bummer to have it end so soon. While some others had issue with there be no replayability, I find myself just coming back to Unpacking just to chill out and wind down. The price tag is pretty high considering the short playtime, however, A TON of effort has gone into it.  If you (a perspective buyer) are thinking about picking the game up, I would say, do it.

[h1]Review[/h1]
This game gives you the opportunity to play as a nerdy girl who needs to unpack her boxes after moving into a new place. And you will unpack every single box she has unpacked in her life, every single time she has moved. So stretch that nostalgia muscle, you are going back in time! Learn about the protagonist through the unpacking of boxes! Channel you inner interior designer! Then by all means, please send them back, because who cares about mixing high-end luxurious monochromatic design and cheap old-as-heck colorful appliances in one single room? Not me! And neither should you!

This game is a relaxing experience, as well as the easiest 3D-Tetris puzzle game ever created. But it can also be more than that. It tells the story of its protagonist through its core game mechanic in a very convincing way. You are not simply moving things around: you are moving the memories that stayed with your character... and noticing those that did not. Or those that should not have stayed. Sure, this one stuffed pig is following you around, but what happened to that weird warrior girl figurine? Oh, and remember about that sad grey D&D figurine?

The only actual issue I had with this game was its price, which I find quite steep for the actual play time. Sure, replayability should not be an issue with Unpacking, as the game simply shines at letting you unplug and chill out for a bit unpacking boxes. But some people may be deterred by its price, knowing that the game can be fully finished in around 4h.

[h1]Small pro-tip for the modern pro-gamer[/h1]
Oh, just one more thing since I have seen countless messages online on this matter... If you are under 20, let me just give you a small pro-tip: this is called a GameCube, your older brothers and sisters used to play games on it. And it was a lot of fun.

The thought process to making this game is astonishing. Every single bit of it I love. Throughout the game, the experience of unpacking alone gives you the details to the character's life and how they are, their personality and hobbies. With just numbers of boxes and a series of different places, the game lets you dive into the world of the character and tell a simple story. There are items that make you reminisce the memories, placing them in new places but the value that it holds is all the same, important to your heart. Every item has its story and you're carrying a story through different places, creating more with it, a beautiful story even.

This was such an interesting and touching game, I was disappointed when it ended!

Unpacking sees you, well, Unpacking. Each level as such has you moving to a new house in a new year of your unnamed, unseen character's life. The gameplay itself is as intuitive as it comes, you click a box to pull out a new object, then place it somewhere, be it on a shelf, in a cupboard, on a coat hanger, etc. What makes the gameplay special in spite of its allergy to complexity is the sheer satisfaction that comes with each interaction. Every click on every object is accompanied with a different, perfect sound effect. Plastic spoons clack upon the tiled surface of the kitchen. Books gently thud onto a shelf. Your childhood stuffed pig toy whoomphs ever so softly on to your bed. The grid which each object moves and rotates on as your mouse travels helps to reinforce this almost LEGO-like sensation of things fitting *just* right.

Not only is the gameplay finetuned and refined to an almost infinitely repeatable loop, perfecting tidying into a drug-like activity, the story is elegant in its near-absence. The only writing in the game comes upon the completion of a level, where a photo of a finished room is placed in your album with a caption. Each one is balanced wonderfully between vague and suggestive to stir your imagination, just as the objects you unpack stoke your ideas of what may be the full story. This makes it sound as though there are some great, Dark Souls-ian twists or complexities, but there really aren't. You're following a normal person's life through its ups and downs, but even working out their job, their partner, what they've just achieved feels like cracking a murder mystery.

Ultimately, Unpacking posit the idea that a person's life is at its most understandable and interesting when they're forced to pack everything important to them up and move. A story and a character can be completely described through what they choose to bring with them and what they choose to leave behind, and how those choices evolve from the last move a couple years prior. Why did this person leave those Doc Martens? What about this stuffed pig makes them inseparable for them? How important must their new partner be for them to have given up a treasured possession they've kept with them for twenty years? The fact that this near-speechless game with no visible characters has managed to kindle those questions within my mind is proof enough that Unpacking's hypothesis is true.

There are of course a few wee grumbles. While the pixel art is lovely, consistent and oft adorable, occasionally there is an object which is difficult to interpret, sometimes making the end of a level a slightly frustrating guessing game. This did little to detract though, only becoming an issue once or twice. The music too is pleasant and fits the mood brilliantly, but sometimes the track would end before I was close to finishing, leaving me in silence for a few minutes. And of course, the game is no more than 2.5 to 3 hours long, and with replayability in that the game doesn't change on subsequent playthroughs.

In spite of that though, I think Unpacking is more than worth the asking price. It may be short, but it is entirely unique in how it chooses to present its characters to the player, and each aspect of the game feels crafted to near perfection. This little pixellated game of organising several houses with small clacks and clicks managed to make me feel a great deal, and that is nothing if not impressive.

I'm amazed at how much story they've managed to fit into a game where you only interact with inanimate objects, and a single sentence at the end of each 'level'. It's really heartwarming and peaceful to play, with very satisfying sound effects and music that aren't intrusive or annoying, even when I've spent 20 minutes trying to work out the perfect location for a yoga mat. The gameplay is easy to understand but still challenging enough (some items can only go in certain places, and obviously we all know the pain of not having quite enough cupboard space) to bring it up from being more of an idle sandbox kind of thing. I recommended this to several friends the moment the credits ended!

Unpacking is a game where you - get this - unpack. I went into the game with very high hopes after waiting months for it to release. I did enjoy my time playing the game however I would like to point a few things out before giving the okay to buy. Firstly and probably most importantly, I felt kind of misled by what the trailers showed. I was under the impression that this was more of a sandbox game where you would be able to decorate an array of peoples houses. (sorta like house flipper minus the house flipping) I was excited to go through many different types of houses and living situations. That however is the furthest thing from what this game is. This game is a love poem to the creators significant other. While I am okay with that I am sad to say that there are only 8 short levels that take maybe 3 hours to complete if you are a total spaz and make everything perfect. The game leaves much to the imagination as in most of the "unpacking" situations you are actually only given a small amount of things to unpack while you are unable to interact with the rest of the environment. The first 5 levels leave very little to the imagination as a lot of the objects are already "unpacked" or the rooms you are given are limited and small. The 6th and 7th chapter give you a lot more freedom, however they are basically the same level except in 7 you are just adding more stuff to the 6th. The 8th chapter is where you really get the "unpacking" feel. I enjoyed being able to free decorate the entire house and making it feel personal even tho it was someone else's story. Overall I would give the game a 6/10 This game is not worth the 20$ price tag. If you can find it on sale for less than 10$ I would say yes pick it up but be aware that you are buying a short story game not a game about unpacking. \o/

This game is a short, cute, and relaxing puzzle type game with a story that can be taken as light or as heavy as the player wants to read into it. Personally I feel like the game could have gone on a bit longer and could have included more life themed events after the story "ends" in the game, but I am assuming the developers did not want to get into heavier life themes since the game is supposed to be light and fun.

Major Spoilers below:
The game "ends" when you move in with your partner and have a baby, but I would have liked to see the game continue into your family having a toddler/teenager, and then eventually having to downsize once your child moves out or dealing with in-laws or parents moving in or eventually your spouse dying. It feels like this game was aiming to have a large impact on the player emotionally, but key elements of life events were just missing. It would have been neat and warranted if the end of the game was at the end of the main character's life, especially considering it would have only needed one or two more levels in order to achieve that and would have made for a much more fulfilling ending, instead of the "happily ever after" one we are given when the character is less than halfway through their life.

I will say that I think the game's narrative is very socially important, as it deals with the main character coming to terms with their preferences and moving back in with their parents from a partner that did not suit them, Which can be a scary decision to make, but is ultimately what needs to happen in order to achieve long term happiness for a person in that situation.

Overall I think it is a very well made game and it was very fun to play, but it did leave something to be desired in the feelings department and it could have definitely gone on much longer story-wise than it did for the $20+ price tag.

Despite the others who say this game isn't worth the $20, I wholeheartedly disagree. There are infinite ways to design spaces, and that is what excites me. Puzzling together a room is so worth it when you see the whole thing come together. And as an artist, I can say that this gives me many, MANY ideas on rooms and backgrounds.
I believe I'm almost finished with the game, and I'll come back once I'm done to finish this review off properly.

Update: My heart is so warm and full of joy. Unpacking truly is an experience worth the money, and it can be completed in around 4 to 5 hours. 8 houses, and I'm almost in tears. I'll eventually go back and replay the game to get all of the achievements, but for now, I need to cry from joy. This game is the best I've played this year.

Really really cool game with a good amount of freedom. The story is more of a passive part of the game, and you only have to pay attention to as much as you care to as there is no dialogue or narrator. Instead, you connect the dots through pictures, items, and the soundtrack to determine the phases and life events the character is going through. Its cool to see certain items stick with the character throughout the story, as well as others that reappear after years of being left out. Ultimately you get to decide what type of character you are. Its up to you to decide small things like if you wanna bring your stuffed animals to bed as a twenty year old or if you'd rather store them under the bed. There's pop culture references if you pay close attention to books, magazine, and video game covers as well. It would be cool to play as a guy as well, but that would pretty much be a whole different game so I get it. I really enjoyed level 4 as it made me think about what it would be like to share a small space with someone, and having to make those choices of what to bring. Overall cool game that I think anybody could enjoy.

就如同游戏中一样每次搬家都有会下痕迹，有从儿时的物品一直伴随我们长大的床上的各种娃娃、桌面的小火车、地板的足球、似乎这里也都在见证我们的成长轨迹。但大多物品都更以丢去、更新换代。小霸王、电子宠物已更换成了NS，笨重的大屁股显示器也更换成了更轻薄的显示器，儿时带锁关进抽屉的心事本，也早已不知所踪。

主基调是一款很轻松休闲的游戏，游戏玩法很简单却也很单调，似乎更多的感受是在心境的变化，但我仍觉得的游戏内容与价格并不太匹配，建议等等。[/b]

Unpacking is a beautiful game packed with lots of tiny details. Picking up and laying down items feels… neat.

Interacting with items is very smooth and thought out, like how a piece of clothing can be put on a hanger, or neatly folded and stacked, then the whole stack can be moved. It’s intuitive and seamless. And if I leave a bag in front of a closet door, then I can’t open it anymore because it’s blocked. There’s tiny details in the level like a chipped painting in the path of the fridge’s door, which are a delight to notice. The sounds are on point, each item having a unique sound effect based on size, material, and weight. Pick up and put down a small toy and then a dumbbell and you’ll see what I mean.

The idea of the game lends itself to some great organic storytelling. The story is not some grand adventure or filled with intrigue, nor does it need to be. You’re following a character along the various moves throughout life, like going to college, moving in with a partner, moving back in with parents, etc. It’s grounded, slice of life, and is very relatable.

I think the criticism that the game is too short is unfounded. The game is as short as it needs to be, it doesn’t drag or overstay its welcome. It delivers all the ideas it wants to deliver in a short and sweet package.

Now if you’ll excuse me, there’s a moving truck outside with boxes of my stuff I need to unpack.

The art is stunning, the music is lovely, and the storytelling is perfect - parts of it subtle, parts of it less so, with plenty of little details for you to discover yourself. Gameplay is very satisfying, and the game isn't nearly as picky about where you place things as some other reviews made me think it might be. 

There are so many thoughtful details here that make the experience much more wonderful - from how possessions change over the years, to the game remembering your placement of some things between levels. I enjoyed every minute of my gameplay and plan to replay this game more than once.

I just want to close out this review by saying - I get that taste in games is subjective and that this extremely laidback gameplay isn't for everyone. But I don't agree with the reviews that say the short length of a single playthrough means this game is overpriced, or that you should only buy it on sale. Firstly, the game can easily take you 5-6 hours on a first playthrough depending on how quickly you organize things/how much time you spend reorganizing as you unpack. Secondly - for me, $20 is a pretty great deal for 5-6 hours of genuine enjoyment that I can re-experience any time I want to. It's cheaper than a trip to the movies. If you have $20 to spend on a game, if this game seems appealing to you at all - it's definitely worth that $20.
