Unpacking logra hacerte sentir tan cómodo y pensar sobre todo lo que implica crecer, sin decir ninguna palabra, me parece increíble como un juego logra hablar sobre temas tan complejos como todo lo que implica crecer y todo lo que esto conlleva, sin decir absolutamente nada, para mi este juego es de lo mejor del año pasado y es una experiencia hermosa y emotiva.

Quiero comenzar esta reseña hablando sobre algunos aspectos generales de este juego, en primer lugar todo el gameplay se basa en ordenar tus cosas en las mudanzas, pero a pesar de que uno puede creer que tiene 100% de libertad, en realidad no es tan así, ya que algunas cosas tienen que guardarse en ciertos lugares, como por ejemplo el papel higiénico debe estar en el baño y cosas por ese estilo, por otra parte el apartado gráfico es básicamente pixel art pero con bastantes detalles, ya que si bien muchos juegos indies suelen tener un estilo gráfico de este estilo, me sorprendió en algunos momentos la cantidad de detalles que tienen algunos objetos y ademas de la cantidad de sonidos que tiene este juego, aveces con solo mover un poco un objeto varia el sonido, cosa que me parece un detalle bastante bueno, ya que si eres de esas personas que juegan con audífonos te vas a percatar mas pronto que tarde y otro aspecto a resaltar para mi, es sin lugar a dudas su soundtrack, creo que logra comunicar mucho el soundtrack, dependiendo del nivel que estés y en el lugar que estés, por lo que creo que el soundtrack es bastante bueno, ya que logro hacer mi experiencia mas inmersiva y mas cómoda de cierta manera.

Ahora ya hablando mas a detalle, creo que este juego puede sentirse un poco corto para algunos pero para mi siento que dura lo que debe durar, ya que si bien su precio puede ser algo elevado en comparación a otros juegos, pienso que no se debe valorar un juego por su duración, ya que si el juego se hubiera extendido mas, quizás te puedes llegar a sentir algo aburrido con sus mecánicas, ya que las mecánicas del juego una vez que las aprendes, el resto ya es historia y avanzas mucho mas rápido, por ende creo que el juego dura lo que debe durar. Por otra parte creo que el juego me ha encantado, si bien es raro que un juego no tenga ningún dialogo o tenga una historia como tal, pero si hay pequeños detalles en los objetos que si los vas uniendo, vas a tener una historia que es tan fácil sentirse identificado, ya que vas viendo en cada mudanza como van cambiando las cosas que lleva la protagonista, entonces vez como cambian sus gustos, como cambia todo en si, ya que el cuarto de cada uno es de cierta manera parte de nosotros y por eso es tan lindo, ya que hay detalles que no quiero decir para no arruinarle la sorpresa a nadie y cuando logres encontrar esos detalles, creo que es muy probable que por lo menos sonrías, ya que todos o gran parte de nosotros hemos tenido que mudarnos y cambiarnos de casa y todo lo que esto implica es un proceso que puede ser agotador tanto física como mentalmente, entonces ahí aparece Unpacking para hablarte con otra perspectiva sobre ese proceso y logra hacerte sentir feliz de que has llegado hasta aquí a pesar de todo, por lo que si tuviera que decir en una frase que pienso de Unpacking, esta seria: "Unpacking se siente como un abrazo de alguien cercano y que luego te susurra al oído estoy orgulloso de ti por todo lo que has logrado y en la gran persona que te has convertido"
Apesar de simples, começei a jogar e só consegui parar quando terminou, ótimo jogo pra relaxar.

📦✨ Unpacking – A Cozy, Relaxing Escape… With a Bit of Unwanted Baggage 🎶🏡

✅ Art Style: Absolutely adorable and soothing! Everything is pixel-perfect, with tiny details that make unpacking feel oddly satisfying. 🎨💖
✅ Music & Sound: Soft, calming, and ASMR-worthy—every item placement makes a cute little sound that’s just chef’s kiss 👌🎶
✅ Gameplay: Pure zen—no timers, no stress, just the joy of organizing and discovering a life story through objects. It’s the perfect game to chill and escape reality. 🌿💆‍♀️

❌ What I Didn’t Like: While I loved every bit of the gameplay, I wasn’t a fan of the forced LGBT narrative—it felt unnecessary, like they were pushing an agenda into an otherwise innocent, cozy experience. Also, the ending left me a bit unsatisfied. 😕

🎮 Overall: A fun, relaxing game for those who love cozy, satisfying experiences. Just be aware of the narrative choices. Would I still recommend it? Yes! But with a little side note. 😉✨

I was struck by mixed feelings about this game. On one hand I genuinely enjoyed everything about it - from the design, vague storytelling, relaxing gameplay and the amazing 8-bit soundtrack. On the other hand, this does not justify the price sadly and let me tell you why is that. There are a lot of indie titles out there that offer much more content for the same or lower price. Take „Stardew Valley“ (on sale) and „Celeste“ for example. The comparison between these titles is subjective due to the different genres. However, the question here is about the price-gameplay-hours-ratio which with „Unpacking“ is simply not justified even when on sale. Judging the fact that I have beaten the game in only 10-11 hours. 

If you are short on funds, or simply wish to get as much as possible for the price, then I cannot recommend this title as much as I want to.

Short but impactful narrative about how life changes for an individual from childhood through parenthood. The story implied through the unpacking of belongings caught me off guard because I thought this was just a sorting game. Instead I was met with parallels to my own life that hit me harder than I thought a little game like this might, and it does so quietly. Getting to 2010 and then 2012 will be an emotional moment for most women, I think, because it is such a universal learning experience that you have to go through, and the way the game drives the narrative is just subtle enough to let you realize the circumstance, but without too much obscurity to be only relatable to the very few.

While it isn't the longest game in the world. You won't be mad at yourself for adding it to your library.

TL;DR:
A deeply charming, cozy pixel-art 'puzzler' that tells a surprisingly emotional story without saying a single word. My only real complaint after getting the 100% completion is that it's over way too fast!

Review:
Unpacking is pure, meditative comfort. It does not take much effort to play, it is fun, super cozy, and just a nice 'take this and put it there' drag and drop game. Even reaching 100% is rather easy without getting frustrated. Taking a character's belongings out of cardboard boxes and arranging them across different stages of her life is a strangely personal experience. You learn so much about who she is just through her items. The sound design is top-tier, the pixel art is detailed, and the gameplay is super relaxing. My biggest issue is the length. It took me just about 3.5 hours to fully 100% the game, which felt obscenely short because of how much I was enjoying it. While it's definitely worth picking up on sale for around €4 or so, I was left desperately wishing for extra DLC levels or a sequel, even if the developers have made it clear this is a one-and-done complete story for now.

Verdict:
As stated in the TL;DR, a fantastic, zen-like experience that's well worth playing if you catch it on a discount. It leaves you craving way more content, but the short hours you do get are a total joy!

What a cute and cozy game! You can instantly pick it up and understand what to do, and you have a good amount of freedom to arrange things how you want. Once you're done unpacking everything, there are some super light puzzle solving elements where you would need to adjust some things according to our girlie's preferences or other restrictions.

What I love the most about the game is the subtle storytelling. Although you never get to see our girl or the people in her lives, you can learn a lot about her through following this journey of her unpacking her belongings. It's very nice to see that over the years, she is:
- continuing her hobby of drawing while upgrading her art supplies and equipments, AND making a career out of it! 
- picking up new hobbies (rock climbing, working out, Ukelele etc.) some came from her relationships, some died but some persisted
- traveling places and growing her collectibles (fridge magnets, souvenirs...)
- expanding her closet to have more grown-up clothes and getting perfumes & deodorant
- holding onto her toys, books, games, and posters from her earlier years

The only part that I don't get is the relationships part:
First of all the bf had a super cool looking apartment and it's probably my favorite aesthetics out of all the homes.
However, the game wants us to feel bad about not having space to display our diploma at our bf's apartment, but then in our final home with our gf/wife, we literally also did not give her an office space or even a dedicated desk, and her laptop can only go in the living room ??? Also, her bamboo steamer was put on the top shelf that's out of reach...the whole place feels very much like ours other than some of our partner's clothes & plants, rather than a more equally shared space for two. Aren't we being the "bad" partner here?? idk maybe i'm just making too many assumptions!

Some other things I liked about the game:
- It's so cool that it generates a GIF for the entire unpacking process!
- super easy achievements <3

Efekt na to, zda bude protagonistka rozvíjet svou zálibu v dané oblasti nebo ne to však v posledku nemá, což je patrné hned při dalším stěhování.

[b]2. Hra je velmi krátká.[/b] Já mám tendenci se kochat, ale standardní délka hraní budou tak čtyři hoďky. I s ohledem na výše uvedené mi běžná cena přijde poněkud přemrštěná.

Un petit jeu cozy, court, très simple, mais tellement satisfaisant !

Chaque niveau vous demande de déballer des cartons et d'en ranger le contenu dans une ou plusieurs pièces d'une maison.

D'abord, l'expérience utilisateur est juste parfaite. Les contrôles, les signaux visuels, tout est simple mais tellement ergonomique et bien pensé. On prend un vrai plaisir à placer, déplacer et redéplacer les objets pour parvenir à la configuration idéale et qui nous convient.

Mais c'est quoi la configuration idéale ? Eh bien le jeu laisse libre court à votre imagination pour cela. Alors certes il y a un petit aspect puzzle (vous ne pouvez pas mettre une brosse à dents dans la cuisine par exemple), et vous devrez parfois empiler les objets de manière astucieuse pour avoir assez de place (notamment dans les niveaux plus petits, style appartement), mais ce n'est pas difficile et il est impossible de perdre dans Unpacking - prenez votre temps et rangez à votre rythme.

Enfin, le coup de génie de Unpacking, c'est de nous faire suivre au fil des niveaux la vie d'une personne, qui nous est racontée au travers de ses déménagements et emménagements. Pas de texte, pas de dialogue, non. Juste le gameplay décrit précédemment. Et pourtant en rangeant les objets, on découvre réellement qui est cette personne et les étapes importantes traversées au fil des années.

En résumé, le jeu est un peu court, ne propose pas de challenge, mais chaque minute passée dessus est un plaisir - tout ce qu'on demande d'un jeu cozy.

Unpacking — Le miracle d'un carton bien rangé
Qui aurait cru qu'un jeu dont le concept central est de vider des cartons de déménagement deviendrait l'une des expériences les plus apaisantes et touchantes du jeu vidéo ? C'est pourtant le pari totalement follement réussi du studio Witch Beam avec Unpacking.

Voici pourquoi ce petit bijou méritait absolument son coup de projecteur :

📦 Génie n°1 : Rendre amusant le truc le plus chiant du monde
On va être totalement honnêtes : dans la vraie vie, un déménagement, c'est l'enfer sur Terre. C'est le mal de dos, le scotch qui colle aux doigts, les cartons scotchés à l'arrache et la crise de nerfs quand on cherche ses clés.

Et pourtant, Unpacking réussit ce miracle absolu : rendre le rangement d'un appartement étrangement satisfaisant, drôle et ultra-addictif !

Trouver la place parfaite pour chaque livre, chaque tasse ou chaque petite peluche devient un vrai plaisir presque thérapeutique.

Le bruitage de chaque objet posé (le ASMR du jeu vidéo !) est un régal pour les oreilles.

On passe un temps fou à choisir si le grille-pain doit aller à gauche ou à droite de l'évier, et on adore ça.

📖 Génie n°2 : Raconter une histoire sans écrire un seul mot
C'est là la vraie prouesse du titre : vous raconter toute la vie d'une personne uniquement à travers ses possessions.

Sans aucun dialogue, sans la moindre cinématique et sans même voir le visage de la protagoniste, on suit son évolution de sa chambre d'ado en 1997 jusqu'à sa vie d'adulte :

On devine ses passions qui grandissent (et celles qu'elle abandonne).

On ressent ses coups de cœur, ses doutes et ses ruptures amoureuses juste en voyant quels objets elle garde... et ceux qu'elle doit caser tant bien que mal dans un placard trop petit chez un copain un peu toxique !

On s'attache à elle en découvrant au fil des ans la même petite peluche toute usée qu'on ressort à chaque déménagement.

En résumé : À la fois jeu de puzzle apaisant et récit intime d'une poésie rare, Unpacking est une pépite absolue. Il prouve avec brio qu'on n'a pas besoin d'épées, de dragons ou de fusils pour toucher les joueurs au cœur... parfois, il suffit juste de savoir où ranger ses chaussettes !

An unassuming idea with rich depths. A fascinating journey to have taken. It prompted me to think about what my priorities are, both as a game-player and as a homemaking adult, and to reckon with the gap and the overlap between those two modes of being.

For example: why didn't I find this supposedly "relaxing" and "satisfying" game relaxing or satisfying? Whence this anxiety about the social norms tacit in every object (as silently codified in the win condition)? Why does the "cozy" isometric toy-ification of the world of material possessions make me feel an obscure despair? 

Good and valuable questions for me to have to confront! But I don't think I can describe my experience as "fun."

The relationship between the player and the character is really very odd. I am decidedly not she — based on her stuff I doubt we'd even be friends — so am I supposed to make decorating choices to please [i]myself[/i] or to please [i]her[/i]? Is she even ultimately pleasable?

There's something melancholy about our respective absences from one another's realities. We're just interdimensional poltergeists doomed to  abuse each others' universes. I can do nothing directly about the trend of her life, as she ages and suffers, but I [i]am[/i] responsible for deciding which way her spoons go. "Gosh, is there somehow a way to put the spoons that would improve things for her?" "Ha ha, of course not! Her fate is set in stone; it is for you to witness helplessly from behind glass as you fiddle impotently with these objects. Now show us which way you think spoons go, so that we can tell you whether you do it a good normal way or a weird loser way."

Then again, I feel similar melancholy whenever I reckon with my own material accumulation, its inertness and purposelessness, its alien indifference to the heartbeat of time. All possessions imply a hapless absence; the game just renders that absence interactable, for once, and then calls it "cute."

This was special and I'll be thinking about it for a while. It dismayed me, but in very interesting ways, real-life ways that most games couldn't even touch. There's something to that.

I expected a cozy organization game.

I didn't expect it to make me emotional.

Unpacking tells an incredible story without a single line of dialogue. As you unpack each box, you slowly piece together someone's life—their hobbies, relationships, accomplishments, heartbreaks, and new beginnings. It's amazing how much personality and emotion can come from simply deciding where to place everyday objects.

The gameplay is relaxing, satisfying, and surprisingly addictive. Every room feels like a puzzle, but there's also freedom to make each space feel like your own. Before I knew it, I had finished the game and earned every achievement because I genuinely didn't want the experience to end.

The soundtrack is peaceful, the pixel art is charming, and every move into a new home feels meaningful. It's one of those rare games that reminds you that not every great story needs dialogue or action to leave a lasting impression.

Unpacking is more than a cozy game—it's a beautiful reminder that the little things we carry with us tell the story of who we are.

I can't recommend it enough. ❤️

Unpacking's greatest achievement is in its ability to convey a couple of particularly compelling story beats indirectly through its gameplay. The overall narrative depth isn't anything to write home about, but the way it's done is novel and interesting enough to be worth the time. You'll probably enjoy the game more than me if you intrinsically value the act of decoration and organization, but even as someone not that into that kind of game, I think Unpacking had enough to it relative to the time it took.

Moving through a story without words could be daunting for anyone, but Unpacking does it effortlessly. You follow our main character through her life, hers ups and downs. Tidying, organizing and, yes, unpacking at every step. It's a game that you'll play over and over again.

If you're looking for a short, cozy game with a charming story, great music, and beautiful visuals, I'd definitely recommend it—especially on sale.

Unpacking is one of the coziest games I've ever played.

At first glance, it looks like you're simply unpacking moving boxes. But if you pay attention, every move quietly tells the story of a young woman's life.

From decorating her childhood bedroom, to moving into her first apartment, living with a partner, moving back home after a breakup, and eventually finding happiness again in a beautiful house with a nursery for her own child.

There isn't much dialogue, but the storytelling through everyday objects is absolutely wonderful.

Of course, my inner perfectionist had a few complaints xD

I often wanted to place certain objects in different rooms or arrange them my own way, but the game sometimes limits where things can go. I also wish different kinds of items could be stacked together, because having piles of books and decorations scattered everywhere occasionally made the rooms look more chaotic than cozy.

Still... that's really just me being picky.

Unpacking is honestly a 10/10 experience.

And if you're as obsessed with organizing as I am, don't expect to finish quickly. You'll probably spend hours making sure every single object is in exactly the right place ^^
Genuinely my comfort game. Got me through some of the toughest points in my life so far. It told a story while also being so low maintenance and chill <3

E sabe, eu sou completamente apaixonado por esse jogo, ele me toca de uma maneira que não sei como escrever, ele me da uma vontade enorme de viver e buscar minha vida pessoal e construir uma familia. Unpacking é um jogo que mostra que a beleza da vida está nos pequenos detalhes ao nosso redor, em uma mobília, nas roupas, nos brinquedos, nos livros e etc, e são esses detalhes que mais me encantam nesse jogo, sempre sinto uma paz e tranquilidade jogando.

This game has so much potential for new updates or DLCs, but as it stands, it's an extremely short and somewhat limited game. My actual play time was closer to 3.5 hours, and I've completed the game. The art style is adorable, but sometimes the items were so distorted by the pixelization that I had no idea what I was holding or where it was supposed to go. I would love, love, love if the devs gave us an update allowing 45 degree turns instead of just 90 degree turns. The rules surrounding where an object can or cannot be placed seem random and inconsistent (for example: I was able to place an award on a shelf in one of the levels, but I was not allowed to place it on a shelf in another level and had to put it on a desk). And when your items are in the wrong location, there are no hints to let you know if it's just in the wrong room, or in the wrong spot. I thought it was very cute how the character kept all of her mementos throughout her life, but near the end, her house just felt cluttered with too many toys, an excessive amount of video games, and old laptops piling up in the cabinets. The game was released in 2021, but your unboxing journey ends in 2018, which felt a bit abrupt. Overall, it's a very cute little game and provides a few hours of relaxing fun, but that's about it. 

(Devs, if you're reading this, please consider the possibility of DLCs that include different decorating styles such as gothic/bohemian/maximalism, or starting a new story for the main character's mom that begins back in the 60s/70s and goes up until we meet our main character, it would be so so so cool and I would pay full price for it.)

(It would also be super cool if we were given a "creative mode" where we could choose some premade rooms and decorate them however we want.)

Have to admit I only tried this because it kept popping up in "best of" game lists. But the elevator pitch is both absurdly simple ("unpack"...that's the whole concept and game) and so not my thing. I didn't even get the concept.

...but my pre-game opinion is flat out wrong. What unpacking is, is a game that not so much avoids common tropes within gaming as rather goes in a completely new direction where they don't apply. Your main character is neither well-written nor cliché because there's hardly a few sentences about her. But the sort of non-verbal storytelling is through the roof! You know the main character (and sex, for that matter) by the stuff you unpack, which happens to be the gameplay.
I could say that the gameplay is simple point 'n click with a few slifght puzzle elements, but that's mostly only true in the technical sense. Most stuff you can put pretty much wherever you want and be done with it.

...except you won't. Look...as a CIS male, I can't say I care much about unpacking in general. But this isn't "in general", but it's a game. So my efficiency mode goes places where I don't expect it to, and soon I'm busy neatly stacking all same-colored plates together because...well, because I can, damnit!

And in that immersion, the story plays a subtle but important role. I can't be the only one who noticed something was off when your graduation diploma didn't fit anywhere on the wall. Or, in the next level, where a picture of "a couple" can't remain visible on the board anymore. It says a whole lot without saying anything.

So...what can I say? It's a Marie Kondo simulator. And a damn good one at that. In addition, I'd recommend this for parent-child coop. I've played simple coop games with my 6 year old for a few years now, but this is the first one she completely PLAYS by herself. The coop is more in the sitting next to her and pointing out that that goofy thing is a nintendo DS, that's an old radio, and so on (in fact, I had to break from writing this to give a stray laptop a home within her game ;) ).

Unpacking was a fantastic game that I thoroughly enjoyed from beginning to end. I found it incredibly calming and relaxing, making it the perfect game to unwind with after a busy day.

What I loved most was how the story unfolded without needing a lot of dialogue. Through unpacking boxes and placing items around each room, you slowly piece together the character's life journey, which was both clever and heartwarming.

The gameplay is simple yet engaging, and there's something very satisfying about creating a space and finding a home for every item. It's a beautiful reminder that even ordinary objects can tell an extraordinary story.

Overall, Unpacking is a lovely, peaceful game with a heartfelt story that I would highly recommend to anyone looking for a cosy, stress-free gaming experience.

是一个有一点点剧情，回忆小时候到结婚生子时间线的整理游戏，玩家把快递箱拆开，把每一个对应物品放到合适的位置。很难想象这样一个简单的游戏史低居然还要二十多，我觉得十块差不多了，只能给到NPC。
有几个想提的缺点：一是由于文化差异，很多东西不知道是干啥用的，或者因为个人习惯不同，不知道该放在哪里；二是有很多外形接近的物品，只能猜是干嘛的，比如最后一关有个长得像洗面奶的东西，在浴室折腾半天都不对，最后得放在婴儿房；三是很多物品可以摆在不同的位置，自由度很大，而且每个场景的东西太太太多了。很难不杂乱，收拾完只有一种烦躁，没有强迫症收纳完整整齐齐、干干净净的快乐，让我烦得没有耐心通关后再重新布置。优点也有，那就是收集的贴纸很可爱，成就比较好获取。

Однозначно да, музыка, атмосфера, это всё придаёт некий вайб игре. Сидишь, спокойно распаковываешь вещи попивая чай, раскладываешь всё по своим местам) Мне очень понравилось, спасибо за игру. 
Музыка в конце игры тоже прекрасна. бб

The video on the store page is exactly what this is. Like a zen garden for people who like organizing. There's a light story that. should you pay attention, is touching, but you are never explicitly told what is going on. They let the gameplay do all the work and it helps keep the game focused and engaging cover to cover.

It's also, unfortunately, quite short. I'm not sure they could get much more out of the unpacking gimmick. It's basically the perfect length to not lose your attention, but maybe could have given an opportunity for multiple play sessions if it had more content. If you were RUSHING through the game, you could probably finish it in under an hour. But you'd have to not really care about the minor details and only worry about putting things in valid locations. I suppose that is one way to play, but I doubt you are the type of person to do so if you are considering picking this specific game up. I decided to be very particular about things and organize them how I would in real life. This got me about 5 hours of gameplay.

I'd say you should wait for a sale. As I type this review, the game is $8. I'd say that's a fair price for it. I think I've also seen it go on sale fairly frequently, so you shouldn't have nay trouble getting it for cheap. Personally, I'd say $10 or less would be best. I hate judging a games monetary value, especially since I do respect this game as a great great work of art, but times are tough and it's time to start being a bit more objective.

Excelente jogo e com um diferencial bem interessante: A Narrativa.

O objetivo do jogo é bem simples, apenas organizar seus objetos vindo de mudança, simples, porém muito satisfatório e relaxante. 

Como disse, o diferencial é a narrativa, não são apenas itens que você organiza, ele conta a história de uma pessoa conforme avança os níveis. O seu primeiro quarto, primeira vez morando sozinho e etc. E é bem interessante essa maneira de narrar uma história, não tem sequer nada mais elaborado do que apenas apresentar os seus itens para contar a história.

A gameplay é bem fluida e relaxante, como o jogo propõe a ser, ele cumpre o que é fornecido e de forma muito bem feita.

Destaque também para a música que é simplesmente fenomenal, além do visual dos itens que é muito bem feito. As conquistas também são bem simples e você pode acabar descobrindo sem querer.

Se fosse para apontar um ponto negativo, acredito que estaria no preço base para o que o jogo oferece. Você consegue terminar tudo dele em mais ou menos 5 horas, então acredito que o preço seja um pouco salgado em relação a isso. Mas em promoção compensa bastante!!

A relaxing game with a story told largely through the player's own observations. The object of the game is to unpack boxes and put things in their place. The gameplay mechanism is clicking a box to grab the next item and clicking the spot you want to put it in. (You can also move things around once you've placed them.) Pretty satisfying if you like that sort of thing! There's a light puzzle element to it, but it's not challenging. It's a bit short, but that was not surprising considering the type of game it is and the price. I finished the game in about five hours. I don't think there's a lot of replayability, but I did really enjoy playing it and would absolutely buy an expansion pack or sequel game. You don't need a powerful PC to play this game, by the way. Unpacking is such a cute and cozy little game that’s strangely relaxing to play. At first glance it seems simple, but there’s something incredibly satisfying about unpacking boxes and putting everything exactly where you want it. If you’re the kind of person who loves organising things neatly, you’re going to have an amazing time with this game.

One of the best parts is how it quietly tells a story through someone’s belongings. Watching a person go through different stages of life, seeing what items they keep, what changes and what disappears over time is surprisingly emotional and really interesting to experience.

For achievement hunters, this game is fantastic because you can easily reload levels and clean up anything you missed without replaying the entire game. Some of the achievements are genuinely funny too, which adds even more charm to the experience.

The art style and sound design are cozy and comforting, making it the perfect game to unwind with.

“Unpacking” is a relaxing puzzle and simulation game developed by Witch Beam in 2021. The game tells a story through the act of unpacking boxes after moving into new homes. Instead of dialogue or cutscenes, players learn about the main character’s life by organising her belongings in different rooms over many years.

As players unpack items, for example, books, toys, clothes, and decorations, they discover important moments in the character’s life throughout all life stages. Each object reveals her personality, memories, and experiences. The gameplay combines organisation puzzles with creative freedom, letting players decide where many items should be placed.

The game is recognised for its calming atmosphere, soft music, and emotional storytelling. Its pixel-art style and attention to detail create a cosy experience that encourages players to ponder on themes such as change, growth, and the meaning of personal belongings. Rather than focusing on action or competition, “Unpacking” offers a peaceful, thoughtful exploration of building a life and finding a place to belong.

Pros:

* cosy game for casual players
* cute pixel-art
* easy to get all the archives

Cons:

* not a long game
* If you play it more often, it could feel repetitive

Imagine a whole life being told to you without a single word, solely through the chaos of objects that follow us from apartment to apartment. This is the concept of an original video game ; a melancholy epic set between a box of books that is far too heavy and an old toaster that has survived for way too long. Welcome to the hell of quiet moving, sitting on a lone chair.

Unpacking is an isometric pixel-art game with shimmering colors, where you simply unbox, grab, and set down objects. The concept is disarmingly simple ; you arrange each item in the appropriate room, between closets, shelves, and dressers. Nothing more. And yet, the result is dreadfully addictive.

At the end of each move, you realize you’ve just stepped through a pivotal stage of an existence. You quickly learn that you have to carve out a space for yourself among someone else's belongings, whether in a cramped shared flat or when moving in with a partner for the first time. It is an incredibly bold narrative approach ; the story is felt intuitively, blending the nostalgia of memories with the raw utility of objects.

That is the paradox of such a game, you do the same thing over and over, yet your brain craves its dose of dopamine with every item put away (though, weirdly enough, there are no socks to be found). It’s the surgical satisfaction of tidying up.

For those aiming for 100% completion, it’s nothing too difficult. Aside from a few small secrets hinted at through the collectible sticker descriptions, the challenge remains a bit too easy. A shame.

Note to the Developers: Your game is extremely satisfying, but it sometimes lacks labels for the objects; it’s not always clear if you’re holding a garlic press or an extraterrestrial artifact. It would actually be an excellent way to learn new languages in a playful way.

Story-wise, it would be touching if the journey continued until the very end, with a final "garage sale" style level. There, we would pack away our memories one last time into boxes for the "final journey." Finally, a randomized mode without the story would be perfect to prolong the pure pleasure of organizing.

Unpacking é um daqueles jogos que você inicia sem muita expectativa, que não sabe se valerá à pena o que investiu pagando pelo jogo, mas, ao final, termina com o coração quentinho e achando justo o preço pago pela experiência; sem arrependimentos.

Pois bem, a premissa é muito simples ao ponto de parecer um tanto quanto boba: você desempacota caixas. Só isso; mais nada. Ainda assim, de alguma forma, é uma das experiências mais intimistas que já tive jogando.

O jogo conta a história de uma garota através dos objetos que ela carrega consigo ao longo da vida, sendo mais exata, à cada mudança para uma nova casa; sempre um novo capítulo. Você nunca lê uma única linha de diálogo, nunca vê um rosto, nunca ouve uma voz narrando a história, ainda assim, sabe tudo, ou talvez de muito, o suficiente para o ponto em que se encontra da narrativa. Tu há de saber quando ela está feliz, quando está recomeçando, quando algo deu errado. É um roteiro incrível, amarrado na subjetividade da ambientação.

Algo interessante é que dá pra perceber claramente que a personagem principal trabalha com área criativa, provavelmente Design, Publicidade e Propaganda ou Artes. No início são esboços e cadernos, e, com o tempo, vão chegando tablets, equipamentos, referências visuais. Ver essa evolução profissional acontecer em silêncio, através dos objetos, principalmente o seu local de trabalho, é genial. Me senti representada em vários aspectos, inclusive com o mundo de RPG de mesa.

Tem um momento específico no jogo que me deixou com uma pulga atrás da orelha que simplesmente não saiu da cabeça até o fim. Após uma determinada fase que me deixou com o coração levemente apertado, ela vai morar com outra pessoa, aparentemente uma mulher. Nesse momento comecei à tentar descobrir quem é essa pessoa pela casa, pelos objetos que dividem o mesmo espaço. Romance? Amizade? Não vou dizer, porem quando a resposta veio, não era nada do que eu esperava, mas ainda assim era exatamente o que precisava ser.

Os achievements merecem menção especial. São delicados, coerentes com o espírito do jogo e alguns deles só fazem sentido depois que você termina. E falando em detalhes escondidos: fiquei um bom tempo sem perceber que era possível interagir com certas coisas no cenário, descobri isso só lá pela segunda ou terceira casa. Esse tipo de camada extra, sem nunca esfregar em ti, mas sendo possível encontrar de maneira intuitiva, é o que separa um bom jogo de um jogo diferenciado.

A trilha sonora acompanha tudo com uma delicadeza absurda. Não chama atenção pra si mesma, só existe ali, do lado, como deve ser.

Unpacking é 10/10. Simples na mecânica, impecável no roteiro, honesto do começo ao fim. Se dê a oportunidade de jogar; vale muito à pena, ainda mais em um dia de chuva.

Minha visão sobre Unpacking. É um ‘cozy game’ relaxante onde você organiza seus itens / objetos, em essência é isso, e não há muito o que falar sobre. É um jogo curto, por volta de 4h para finalizar.

  Quero falar brevemente sobre a narrativa. O que [b]  É SPOILER [/b] , então, cuidado. Aqueles que não se incomodam, sintam-se à vontade.
[b] É sério, a partir daqui é SPOILER. [/b]

  É nítido, a todo momento você está organizando um cômodo de sua casa, saindo de um quarto para uma casa inteira, viajando da infância à vida adulta, visitando todos os pontos padrões que idealizam uma vida equilibrada. O primeiro quarto após a saída do berço, a transição para a faculdade, trabalho, a formação do casal e, por fim (na parte narrativa do jogo), a ‘concepção’ de uma nova vida. O que seria o fim do ciclo, a hora zero do relógio, o ponto qual perpetua a existência. 
  Um detalhe sutil, talvez nem tanto sutil, mas bastante emotivo é a formação dos gostos pessoais na infância e como eles são transportados para a vida adulta e transferidos para a prole, não impostos, mas sim incentivados, de forma sutil e carinhosa; no caso do jogo, os troféus da infância e a constante presença da bola de futebol, do primeiro cenário no seu quarto de criança até o último, agora no quarto do seu bebê, deixa isso bem claro. 
Também podemos observar isso na questão do seu diploma, a parte profissional é bem resolvida e possibilita a transformação dos cenários da maneira que é feita. O jogo funciona avançando os anos, não ‘os nossos’, os ‘anos do mundo’.
Quando você percebe que há mais alguém com você, de repente nos vemos organizando itens de caixas estranhas, objetos que não são os nossos habituais e não ‘combinam’ com o gosto que temos - é claro, não existe protagonista que controlamos de modo objetivo, é apenas subentendido, não há textos ou explicações a não ser um breve frase no final de cada cenário, essa parte é explícita permite que compreendamos a ‘história’ - isso gera curiosidade porém logo é compreendido, uma família está se formando, e organizando o quarto do bebê não sobram dúvidas. Ao fim quando finalmente estamos em um casa com espaço para um pet (é o cenário final, a última foto do álbum que montamos ao longo dos anos) isso deixa um sensação de ‘retorno’, de ciclo. Parece que voltamos à nossa casa de infância, tomamos o lugar de nossos pais, e agora como genitores, nossas personalidades serão a base para um novo ser se formar e caminhar pela mesma estrada que caminhamos. Pra mim isso fica claro quando a pelúcia que nos acompanha a partir da infância, e ficou surrada com os anos; quando desembrulhamos a exata mesma pelúcia, agora novíssima, junto da pelúcia que referencia nosso cônjuge. Nesse momento podemos interpretar que nossas preferência não são ‘exatamente’ ou ‘exclusividade’ de nossa vontade individual, foram, influenciadas pelo ambiente, no caso, pelos nossos pais que compartilham conosco não apenas material genético, também gostos, temores, preconceitos, ideais de mundo e tudo aquilo que forma o sujeito em sociedade. A educação de uma vida é algo bastante sério. É claro, só vemos o lado bonito na narrativa e tudo bem, ele não tem como objetivo a reflexão sobre esse tema, e ainda que não seja explícito e talvez eu esteja extrapolando um pouco, há margem para essa leitura.

  Vejo como uma bela narrativa visual. Foi moderadamente emotiva, para mim. Uma história sobre o desabrochar, sobre capacidade e possibilidade de atingir algum objetivo pessoal, profissional ou ambos. O sonho de sair de casa e ser independente. A liberdade financeira. Ser alguém para além de ‘filho de meus pais’. A confirmação da capacidade como indivíduo.  O corte no cordão umbilical imaginário que é viver sob o mesmo teto de seus pais. E, por que não dizer que, seus genitores foram bem sucedidos em criar um adulto funcional que pôde escolher caminhar conforme a própria vontade, por caminhos que desejou, sozinho, mas não abandonado. Família, de sangue ou de escolha, é uma base sólida, quando gerada a partir do amor.

This game is a delight from start to finish, and the only thing I have a complaint about is that I want more Unpacking.

From the moment you open your first box, the world slows down. There’s no pressure, no timers, no overwhelming mechanics, just the gentle, almost therapeutic act of taking items out of boxes and finding a place for them. It’s simple in the best way, like tidying a space while your mind quietly unwinds after a long day.

There’s barely any dialogue, no big dramatic cutscenes, yet somehow, it tells one of the most human, emotional stories I’ve experienced in a game. You follow someone’s life not through words, but through their belongings. A childhood bedroom turns into a dorm, then into shared spaces, heartbreak, independence, and eventually something soft and whole again. The gameplay itself is incredibly satisfying. Placing items “just right” scratches that cozy, organised itch, and the soft soundtrack wraps everything in a calm, comforting atmosphere. It’s the kind of game you can play while half curled up, half zoning out, and still feel completely immersed. Many players describe it as “relaxing and therapeutic,” with a calming loop of organising and decorating .

What I love most is how safe it feels. There’s no stress, no danger, just quiet progress and gentle storytelling. And yet, it still manages to make you feel things. The only downside? It’s short. Most people finish it in around 3–4 hours . But honestly, it feels less like a long-term game and more like a beautiful experience you revisit when you need comfort.

And I'm embarrassed to say it took me a while to realise you [i]could[/i] further interact with some items. You have to right-click to do this, when usually right-clicking is for rotating.

Unpacking is one of those rare games that quietly sneaks up on you. On the surface it’s just about unpacking boxes and putting items around a room, but somehow it ends up telling a really heartfelt story without a single line of dialogue.

As you move through different homes and stages of life, you slowly piece together the story through the objects themselves. Little details — where something ends up, what gets kept, what disappears — say more than words ever could. It feels personal, nostalgic, and sometimes even a little emotional.

The gameplay itself is simple but incredibly relaxing. There’s something very calming about taking your time placing things where they belong and slowly bringing order to a new space. The soundtrack and gentle sound design add a lot to that cosy atmosphere.

This is the kind of game you play when you want something peaceful and thoughtful rather than intense. It’s warm, comforting, and genuinely charming.

Highly recommended if you enjoy relaxing games, thoughtful storytelling, or just want something that feels like a quiet moment in a busy world.

[b]GRAPHICS[/b] The graphics are great — I personally am a big fan of games featuring a 2D pixel art style such as this one, so that was a big plus for me.
[b]GAMEPLAY[/b] The gameplay was engaging and fun, as well as incredibly easy to navigate. Though I usually have a hard time figuring out game mechanics, the basic point-and-click mechanics of this game allow for an easy time, even for non-gamers. Story wise, each level corresponds to a date and a chapter in the life of a person whose boxes you are unloading. 
[b]PC REQUIREMENTS[/b] As someone who runs all my games on a MacBook, I often run into issues with not being able to run games without lag. However, I played this game on my Mac with no running issues, no lag, and no disruption to other applications I had opened simultaneously.
[b]OVERALL[/b] Overall, the game is simple on the surface while also offering an immersive and deep story where you learn about the life of a person as you unbox their belongings in each chapter.

„Unpacking” to jedna z tych gier, które zaskakują swoją prostotą i klimatem. Na pierwszy rzut oka wygląda jak zwykłe rozpakowywanie kartonów po przeprowadzce, ale bardzo szybko okazuje się, że to coś znacznie więcej. Gra opowiada historię bez dialogów, bez tekstu i bez nachalnych wskazówek  wszystko poznajemy przez przedmioty i kolejne mieszkania.

Rozgrywka jest bardzo spokojna i relaksująca. Wyjmowanie rzeczy z pudełek, układanie ich na półkach, w szafach czy szufladach działa wręcz terapeutycznie. Idealna gra do odpalenia wieczorem, kiedy chce się wyciszyć i nie ma ochoty na dynamiczną akcję ani stres. Nie ma limitów czasu, przegranej ani presji – gracz może robić wszystko we własnym tempie.

Ogromnym plusem jest klimat. Muzyka jest delikatna i przyjemna, a dźwięki rozpakowywanych przedmiotów bardzo satysfakcjonujące. Pixel art jest prosty, ale ciepły i dopracowany, a każde mieszkanie ma swój charakter. Zmieniające się lokacje świetnie pokazują kolejne etapy życia bohaterki i potrafią wywołać emocje  od radości po lekką nostalgię.

„Unpacking” to gra, która pokazuje, że nie trzeba skomplikowanej fabuły ani akcji, żeby stworzyć coś wyjątkowego. To idealna pozycja dla osób szukających relaksu, klimatu i nietypowej narracji. Świetna na wieczorek, do herbaty i odpoczynku.

Zdecydowanie polecam.

A very cozy time!

The Settings of the different locations are well done and offer a nice challenge for each unpacking section you do. 

Visually, its pretty cute. Performance was solid throughout and I didn't run into any bugs or glitches. The Art Direction is the perfect match for what this game is going for with its soft colour pallet and really well detailed pixel art. 

Sound and Audio are perfect with the soundtrack being 8-bit ambience and the audio especially when placing items and boxes disappearing is really satisfying. 

In terms of Gameplay, its as casual as you can get. The main gameplay here is just dragging items into locations that you think would fit the environment which honestly is just a relaxing time. I do also like how the game points out what items are in the wrong place instead of having to search very hard cause there is a lot of items that you will be organising. 

Overall, Unpacking is a relaxing time and is very well crafted for what it is!

I bought this game purely because I was bored, had nothing else to play, and figured it was on sale and was well recommended so I may as well give it a try.

This thing left me crying for all the good reasons by the end. It seems like such a simple concept, and it is. You just take stuff out of a box and put it in places. But the devs have done such an amazing job to tell a story of a girl growing up and navigating life through it.  Through every chapter, I found myself smiling like an idiot, constantly going "oh my god she is all grown up now!!!".

I can't even begin to wrap my head around the attention to detail that is needed to make a game like this. Even the tiniest details like what order does the stuff come out of the box tells you something important about the main character.

It's a short game, very simple, but well worth the price. I get that it is 20 dollars for 4 hours of gameplay but for games like this, I feel like you should also factor in how the game makes you feel. Sure, a game like Fifa or 2K will get you 100s of hours of gameplay for like 50ish dollars, but you don't play these kinds of games for the price-to-hour ratio optimisation, you play it for the emotions the story evokes. You wouldn't say a 10 minute song is better than a 3 minute one just because it's more song per song, would you?

I think it is a great game if you are looking for a distraction or something mindful to do. It's well worth playing and I will definitely go back to play through it again! It was a good mix of items that were occasionally unpacked in the wrong room and that you had to put in their correct places. I think you just have to like this game concept and enjoy decorating. The only downside is that I would have been disappointed with the full price. I needed about 7-8 hours of playtime and could probably have stretched it out a bit more since I didn't achieve 100% completion.

As we leave 2025, I thought it'd be nice to play this game as a bookend to last year, and so that I could metaphorically welcome 2026. 

Unpacking is a puzzle game about moving into a new home, and needing to fit your possessions into your new home. I think everyone knows how therapeutic this process can be, basically zoning out thinking about the layout of the place you need to fit your items to. Cleaning is similar!

The basic game loop of Unpacking is that you're given boxes to sort through and figure out where each item goes. It's definitely a little tedious but that's just part of the experience you're buying into; no one said moving would be quick. I WILL SAY sometimes it's unclear where which item needs to go, but that's why we have the internet (the whiteboard goes on the fridge!!). When where these item's go are unclear the game becomes kinda annoying, having to just place the item in random locations until it magically fits. I don't really know if there's a neat solution to this problem, but quickly googling the solution for like 1 minute definitely broke my immersion into the game. I'm willing to forgive the game though cuz for one, I was just impatient, but it's more because the meat of this game comes from it's storytelling! 

Unpacking is "show don't tell" in it's purest form. The aesthetics of the homes you stay at lull you into whatever mindset the character you're playing as is at. The slight differences between growing up and returning to your childhood home, having to place items between the possessions of another person, the ambience!! The ambience is so chill! I might have teared up at the final house a little bit, won't confirm. 

I don't really have much to say about this game. It's a short game you can complete in one day, it executes the gameplay well enough, it's cozy, what else do you need? If you need to relax for a bit and want to zone out with a good puzzle, play this game! 

3.5/5

평가 : 솔직히 정말 단순한 게임이다. 물론 나름의 규칙도 있는 퍼즐 게임이긴 하지만 이사짐을 정리만 하면 되는 게임이다. 이사짐을 정리하면서 누군가에게는 힐링이 될 수 있지만 이게 노동이라 느껴지는 사람도 있었을 것이다. 그래픽은 상당히 괜찮다. 아기자기하고 귀여운 느낌이 많이 든다. 뭐니뭐니해도 이 게임의 최대 장점은 스토리를 풀어내는 방식이다. 게임의 스테이지가 스토리를 풀어내는데 중요한 역할을 한다. 게임이 진행될수록 달라지는 스테이지에 따라 이사짐의 요소들, 집의 크기나 모양들이 달라지는데 사람 한명 없이 그리고 대사 한줄 없이 주인공의 인생을 느껴볼 수 있는 스토리텔링 방식이 굉장히 독특하다. 스테이지를 클리어하면 플레이어의 시간이 흐르듯 게임 주인공의 시간도 흐르고 있다는 것을 보여준다. 물론 이런 독특한 스토리 텔링 방식 때문에 스토리를 이해하는데 어려울 수도 있다. 이 게임의 최대 단점은 가격에 비해 플레이 타임이 굉장히 짧다는 것 솔직히 해도해도 너무 짧다. 정리하자면 굉장히 이사짐 정리라는 퍼즐만으로 한 사람의 삶을 보여주는 스토리텔링은 굉장히 독특하고 좋지만 가격에 비해 너무 짧은 플레이 타임이 흠인 게임. 세일 할 때 한번 사서 해보는 것을 추천한다.

Lovey little cozy game. The gameplay it's pretty straightforward; pull things out of the boxes and organize them as you place them around various rooms.

Спокойная и медитативная игра. Очень понравилась фишка, что через распаковку вещей можно узнать больше об их хозяине и составить полноценный портрет: какие у него хобби, увлечения, достижения и неудачи, отношения с кем-либо и т.п. И всё это только через предметы.

Unpacking surprised me. It’s just you, a pile of boxes, and a new home to fill, but somehow, the whole thing feels soothing and addictive. There’s something about finding the perfect place for every little item that makes you want to slow down and really pay attention. It’s simple, but it pulls you in.

The visuals and sound? Just spot-on. Every room looks warm and real, and even the smallest objects have these tiny details that make them feel special. The soft background sounds—like the rustle of paper or a distant clock—just make it all feel extra cozy. You set your own pace, no timers, no stress. The game nudges you to get creative in ways you wouldn’t expect.

Honestly, what sticks with me is how personal it gets. As you unpack, you’re not just moving things—you’re piecing together someone’s life. There’s no dialogue, but the story kind of sneaks up on you through old photos, worn-out plushies, or trophies from another time. It’s like reading a diary, but you’re the one turning the pages.

Unpacking isn’t just a game you play—it’s an experience you sink into. If you want something calming or just need a break from the usual chaos, this one’s for you. Whether you love organizing or just want to zone out and appreciate the little things, it hits the spot.

10 out of 10. Clear your head, make a space your own, and celebrate those tiny wins. Oh, and if you want to see how neat you can get things, go wild—minimalist bragging rights are part of the fun.

我觉得这游戏最讨巧的地方，就是它把“收纳整理”这件事做得特别有仪式感。
画风是那种3D像素风，看着挺精致，不幼稚。玩法真的简单到没朋友，就是点一下箱子，把东西拿出来，找个顺眼的地方放下。全程没有时间限制，也没有人催你，就听着那个物品碰撞和摩擦的音效，确实很解压，特别适合心情烦躁的时候玩两把。
故事讲得挺细腻的，通过几次搬家，你能看到女主从小时候到成家立业的一生。那个粉红小猪玩偶贯穿始终，最后在婴儿房出现的时候，确实能让人心里一暖，这种无声的叙事挺打动人的。
但咱们得面对现实：体量是真的小。
认真玩也就3-4个小时，手脚快的可能更短。
所以回到那个35元的价格上，我的评价是：不值。
这钱买瓶好点的饮料都不止这点时间了。它更像是一道精致的“餐后甜点”，而不是主菜。

I enjoyed this game a lot, spending a total of 13 hours on it. It was a short game, but if you really take your time trying to unlock every achievement and trying to find the right placement for everything, it can take up more than 4 hours, which seems to be the norm. I liked the storyline of the game even though there were some parts of it that I missed at first until I went back and played it. Here are my pros and cons:

Pros: peaceful, story-based, easy-to-play, not-so stressful.
- This game isn't that stressful, making it peaceful with the music and the sound effects, giving it an ASMR vibe, but sometimes you struggle where to place certain items especially since some don't "belong" in a certain place, leaving you to figure it out. Despite this though, I think it is easy to play, and I love seeing the story progress. 

Cons: Only one storyline, no hints for the achievements, can't move in all directions, pricey, no move mode.
- I wish this game had more than one storyline, you know, different characters with different stories. I would love to see this game in different perspectives and I would love if we can get rid of some items that don't seem useful. Although, I get it, you're supposed to unpack a lot of items for the storyline. Some of the achievements were hard to get and I feel it could've been easier with some hints. Sometimes I couldn't put an item all the way in a corner as it would prevent me from placing it, but it's a puzzle game, so this really isn't much of an issue for me. For the price, I think $20 is kind of expensive for a game that is on the shorter side. I got this game on sale I believe. Lastly, I wish there was an option where the screen doesn't have to move up and down, that you can just zoom in to the area you want, or be all the way zoomed out to view the entire room and not have it move while you play; this is just my preference though. 

Anyway, yeah--I really enjoyed this game. I would recommend it.

4、重新出发，再租房子，这里经历了两集，看得出女主很喜欢植物，然后工作的电脑和画板也越来越多。
5、最后一个巨大房子，还有婴儿房间，但是从前面两集看得出来完全没有男生的衣物。觉得女主应该是跟另外一个女生在一起了，孩子领养的，嗯...   这里观察到女主应该是已经出了自己的画集，有一套一样的书册。

我以为是J人的收纳解压小游戏，没想到是人生治愈诗。

1997年5月，有了自己的第一个房间，可以随心布置，喜欢的玩偶是要陪睡的，上锁的日记是要藏在抽屉的，收音机播放自己喜欢的音乐，玩具和画笔也要整整齐齐。

2004年1月，来到了大学，有个小小的厨房，还有很棒的私人浴室。粉红猪的蝴蝶结这么多年也不知道掉在了哪里，但依然是最喜欢的玩偶；大学依然喜欢画画、踢足球，换了新的随身听和收音机，还有新的游戏机，快乐充实的大学时光。

2007年3月，毕业了，和朋友一起住，朋友是个COSER，家里有手办，还有人台和假毛。但彼此有很多共同话题，可以一同看电影、玩游戏、买冰箱贴。还购置了数位板，将毕业证书高高挂起，并且养了一只甲虫。喜欢健身和户外运动，旅游时会拍好看的照片、买名胜建筑的微缩模型，还买了母鸡和小鸡玩偶来陪粉红小猪。唯二的不足就是需要共用一个浴室和朋友不喜欢刷碗了。

2010年9月，搬进了男朋友家，男朋友喜欢玩音乐和健身，屋子在繁华地段但是很小，衣服是没地方挂的，自己的爱好是没地方搁置的，甚至毕业证只能塞进床底，喜欢的游戏机和卡带也只能胡乱地塞在书柜仅剩的缝隙里，完全没有自己专属的地方，还要给他收拾内裤袜子。刷牙的杯子破了一点，但是依然舍不得丢，尝试了新味道的香水和沐浴露，也给鸡妈妈添了几只小鸡。好处是手磨咖啡很好喝，沐浴间还可以看见美景。

2012年6月，分手了，搬回了家，感觉卧室比之前小了些，但是自在温馨，得了奖的画作和毕业证可以挂在最显眼的地方，用回了原来的洗浴用品，还新学习了缝纫，阳光正好心情欢愉。

2013年1月，在预算范围内找到了一间很好的房子，虽然旧了点，偏远点，但是有自己的专属的艺术空间，有大大的衣柜和大大的床，可以在豆豆沙发上看书看电视打游戏，还可以点上香薰在浴缸里泡澡！

2015年11月，买了新的沙发，事业也有了进展，还遇见了自己的小老虎。她让这个家变得像一个家了，她喜欢养植物，做手工、每个屋里都摆上了多肉，喜欢钢笔记笔记，是个料理好手，有电饭煲、高压锅、柠檬榨汁器、擀面杖、沥水篮、擦丝器、鱼盘、蒜臼子、蒸笼、面食模具、各类调料。还带来了中式香膏和线香的新奇体验，抽屉里塞满了美妆用品，换了新的粉色地垫，衣柜里挂满了漂亮衣服和长筒靴。小老虎是个热爱生活热爱美的女孩子。

2018年7月，搬了新家，有可以养宠物的院子，可以把所有冰箱贴都贴上的大冰箱，能放下两个人衣服的衣帽间，崭新的工作室和浴室，能开晚餐聚会的餐厅。事业有了大进展，粉红小猪和鸵鸟的系列画册出版了，鸡妈妈有了一群小鸡，还给粉红小猪玩偶重新打扮了一下一起期待自己宝宝的到来。

PS：因为小时候经常和妹妹抢浴室，所以女主对浴室有很大的执念，和别人共用时会不太舒服，有美景和浴缸时会很幸福。女主很恋旧，沐浴用品、卫生巾、杀虫剂、锅铲等常用物品都是同品牌型号。

《Unpacking》是一款看似简单，却蕴含深意的“家具布置”模拟器。它的核心玩法就是开箱，然后将箱子里的物品在新家中一一归位。没有繁复的操作，没有紧迫的任务，有的只是从一个个箱子里，整理出一个新家的宁静与治愈。

我特别钟爱这款游戏的以下几点：

1. 复古而精致的像素艺术
游戏的美术风格是极致的细腻像素风。每一件小物件，从游戏机到厨具，从书本到文具，都刻画得栩栩如生，充满了一种复古又精致的质感。这种风格不仅赋予了物品独特的魅力，也让整个整理过程充满了发现的乐趣。

2. 于无声处听惊雷：藏在物品里的故事
这是游戏最绝妙的地方。游戏全程几乎没有文字对话，所有的剧情都通过你拿起的物品、你布置的空间来讲述。

· 成长的轨迹：你能从毛绒玩具、毕业证书等物品中看到主角的成长。而那些逐渐增加的迷你伦敦巴士、巴黎铁塔和比萨斜塔模型，则清晰地记录了她一次次旅行留下的纪念。我习惯把它们都摆在一起，像一个小小的“记忆角”。
· 人生的阶段：游戏巧妙地通过物品的“归属权”来暗示主角的生活状态。比如在合租公寓那一关，只有卧室的东西可以随意摆放，客厅和厨房早已被室友的物品占据，那种初入社会、与他人共享空间的局促感瞬间扑面而来。而搬到男友家时，你会发现他那些已经摆好的音乐设备、唱片你也可以随意移动，这暗示着你们关系的亲密，也给了你“改造”这个空间的权力。

3. [剧透警告] 一次心碎却又充满力量的转折
以下内容涉及关键剧情，请谨慎阅读

! 整个游戏叙事的高潮，发生在我最喜欢也最心碎的一关：主角男友的家。那是一个充满男性气息和音乐元素的小公寓，装修风格与主角此前截然不同。我兴致勃勃地将她的物品与男友的吉他、唱片交织在一起，试图创造出一个融合的、共同的空间。
!
! 然而，下一关的镜头猛地拉回，我们又回到了主角童年时代的房间。一切都变了，又好像没变。在整理时，我发现了从男友家带回来的那张合影——它曾经被贴在男友的冰箱上。我本能地试图将它与其他珍贵的照片一同摆在桌上，但游戏却不允许。几经尝试，最终，只有当我把这张照片收进一个装满旧物的柜子深处时，系统才判定通过。
!
! 那一刻，我恍然大悟：他们分手了。这张照片不再是需要展示的甜蜜，而是需要封存的过去。但故事并未结束于此。我注意到，主角带回了她的尤克里里，还多了几本乐谱和音乐书籍。这意味着，尽管关系结束了，但那段共同经历却在她身上留下了积极的印记——音乐从男友的爱好，变成了她自己的热爱。这种在失去中收获成长的细腻表达，令人动容。

【剧透结束】

总结

《Unpacking》不仅仅是一个整理游戏，它是一次对他人生活的考古，一首由物品写就的无声诗歌。它用最温柔的方式，探讨了成长、独立、爱与失去。如果你是一个喜欢细腻故事、享受宁静时光并乐于发现的玩家，那么这款游戏绝对不容错过。它留给你的回味，远比游戏时长要悠长得多。

Unpacking is one of those rare games that instantly wraps you in a blanket of calm the moment you start playing. There’s something incredibly soothing about opening up each box, placing familiar items in their new places, and slowly shaping a space that feels lived-in and personal. The soft ambient sound effects, retro pixel art, and unhurried pace make the whole experience feel cozy, almost meditative.

What makes Unpacking truly special is how it turns a simple task into an emotional journey. With each room you organize, you learn a little more about the character’s life—without a single line of dialogue. It’s storytelling through objects, and it’s done beautifully.

Whether you’re looking for a relaxing break from high-intensity games or just want something comforting to curl up with, Unpacking is a wonderful, heartwarming experience. It’s calm, it’s cozy, and it’s absolutely worth your time.

[h1]📦Unpacking: Resenha para Garotas Gamers que Amam o Fofo[/h1]
Se você, como eu, procura um jogo para desacelerar e se sentir aquecida, o Unpacking da Steam é uma escolha incrível.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]✨O Charme Fofo e Relaxante[/h3]

[b]Design de Pixel Art:[/b] O visual é o primeiro acerto. A arte em pixel é extremamente detalhada e charmosa, tornando cada item, por mais mundano que seja (uma escova de dentes, um bichinho de pelúcia), uma pequena obra de arte. É um deleite visual que transmite uma sensação gostosa de nostalgia e simplicidade.

[b]Jogabilidade Zen:[/b] A premissa é simples: desempacotar caixas e organizar os pertences em um novo lar. Não há cronômetros, pontuação, nem pressão. Você pode jogar no seu próprio ritmo, clicando nas caixas e escolhendo o lugar perfeito para cada objeto. É um anti-stress garantido, perfeito para relaxar após um dia agitado ou uma partida intensa em outros jogos.

[b]A Satisfação de Organizar:[/b] A mecânica de arrumar cada cômodo (do quarto de criança a uma casa completa) é surpreendentemente satisfatória. Colocar os livros na estante, pendurar toalhas, ou empilhar pratos — cada clique traz uma pequena sensação de realização e ordem.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]💖A História Aconchegante Contada pelos Objetos[/h3]

A verdadeira mágica de Unpacking está na sua narrativa indireta.

Você nunca vê a personagem principal nem ouve a história dela através de diálogos ou longos textos. Em vez disso, a vida dela é contada através dos seus pertences e das mudanças de casa que você organiza.

De 1997 em diante: O jogo te leva por oito fases, cada uma representando uma mudança de casa em diferentes anos (começando na infância). Ao desencaixotar, você vê a personagem crescer: o bichinho de pelúcia da infância que a acompanha por anos, os troféus da época da faculdade, os itens que desaparecem após um término, e as novas coisas que surgem quando ela se muda com um parceiro.

[b]Conexão Emocional:[/b] Você se conecta com a personagem descobrindo suas paixões, hobbies e momentos importantes da vida apenas vendo o que ela guarda e o que ela leva (ou deixa para trás). Por exemplo, ver que um certo item essencial é escondido em uma mudança, e depois volta a ser exposto na próxima, diz muito sobre seus relacionamentos e fase de vida. É uma narrativa sutil e profunda.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]🏆Veredito[/h2]

[b]O Unpacking não é um jogo para quem busca puzzles pesados ou ação. É uma experiência meditativa sobre a vida, o crescimento e a forma como nos apegamos e desapegamos das nossas coisas.[/b]

É um jogo lindo, com uma trilha sonora suave, que vai te envolver em uma história de vida contada com carinho e muitos pixels.

Firstly, I would absolutely recommend playing the game because it is relaxing and comforting but because of the game's length, I just can't recommend paying the full price for it. The game can be 100% completed in just a few short hours, which is great if you want a quick and easy experience, but unless more levels get added or the game gets expanded on to pad out the game's overall length, I can only recommend getting it on discount when the price matches the game length (my general rule is one dollar for every hour I would spend playing)

Absolutely not worth at full price. The game consists of a few chapters of unpacking (no way) and sorting items of our MC, doesn't take too much time, it's a rather small and tedious game. 
Aesthetics - the artstyle itself was not an issue at all, it was consistent and okay, however the MC has got to have the worst taste a human could ever. Barely anything matches, its all just a random mess of items, aesthetically unappealing, makes you think she is actually blind.
Either way, I did enjoy the little story written into the experience. The game allows us to follow the story and growth of the MC through solely unpacking. As we unpack and sort MC's belongings in new areas throughout the years (chapters) we discover new items that expand the collections (like the souvenirs) as well as our old items make their reapperance, sometimes slightly altered, usually aged or worn out (the clear showcase of passage of time was also an enjoyable aspect to experience while playing), this way we can slowly figure out the interests and life story of the MC (requiring the player to hide the photograph with MC's ex in one of the chapters was a clever way to introduce this change in her life without it being said). In the final chapter (which was actually massive btw), we can finally piece together every information we got so far by looking at MC's items throughout the years and make up the entire story in our heads.
I'd like to point out the abundance of notebooks, massive tomes and random booklets. Seriously sorting these was absolutely the worst. Chapter by chapter whenever i opened the boxes with all those books i wanted to quit the game then and there.

[h3]相当意外的是，本作居然还有一点游戏性[/h3]
没有什么特别好评价的，作为近几年火起来的纯粹收纳游戏的鼻祖，在游戏设计上给予了相当大的自由度，但和那些完全自由的“造景”游戏还是有差别的。差别在于有部分物品的摆放位置有一定的限制，就是限制得稍微有些死板，再加上国内外的生活差异，有些国内不常见的家具家电是真的不知道该放在哪里。制作组的制作理念确实是对的，分裂整理、收纳物品并摆放整齐的过程的确可以击中部分人的好球区。因此假如你认为自己算是此类游戏的受众的话，本作还是值得尝试，值得游玩的。
即便本作是有一定设计上的瑕疵的，不过得益于较短的流程，在你产生烦躁感之前往往游戏就结束了。但是不建议长时间连续游玩，每天玩一关左右是比较合适的节奏。鉴于本作的内容量与相对高昂的价格，以及一些小小的dei元素和性别刻板印象，虽然本作值得游玩，但还是建议史低购入。

Unpacking é aquele jogo fofíssimo que transforma a simples tarefa de tirar coisas de caixas em uma viagem emocional cheia de detalhes escondidos. É relaxante, zero estressante e quase terapêutico empilhar pratos, dobrar toalhas e encaixar cada item no seu cantinho perfeito, tudo embalado por uma trilha sonora delicada do Jeff van Dyck. O único “porém” é que às vezes o jogo te obriga a colocar certos itens em lugares específicos (o fiscal da organização aparece!), mas nada que estrague a experiência aconchegante. Recomendo muito para quem ama um bom puzzle suave, decoração e histórias contadas em silêncio... é intimista, bonito e irresistivelmente gostoso de jogar. 📦✨

Unpacking – Small Boxes, Big Emotions 📦

Unpacking genuinely surprised me. At first glance, it looks like a simple game where you take things out of boxes and place them on shelves, in drawers, and around various rooms. But before you even realize it, you start piecing together someone’s life. Every item reveals a little bit of the main character’s journey—childhood, first apartment, challenging transitions, new beginnings. And all of this happens without a single spoken line or piece of dialogue.

The atmosphere is incredibly calm and almost therapeutic—one of those games you launch “just for a moment,” and suddenly three hours have passed while you’re still organizing socks by color. The attention to detail is impressive, and the small discoveries scattered everywhere often bring a smile or spark a moment of reflection.

If you’re looking for something light, beautiful, and emotional, this game is exactly that.

Score: 9/10 ⭐

A short yet relaxing game that can hit you emotionally at the end.

"Unpacking" uses the simple mechanic of taking out items from boxes to decorate a new room/home over time as a subtle way to tell a story about growing up and all the little things, good and bad, that you go through. If you take the time to examine each level, look at the environment and read the story told through it than you get glimpses of the kind of person you're unpacking for and the life journey they take. It's not something profound or life-changing, rather it's something that makes you appreciate the road that life takes you - where every new environment is another chapter.

The graphics are simple, readable and nice. The music is relaxing, and the little bits of interactivity are neat. The achievements are largely easy to get, with some of them popping off by doing the most likely things you would do with a given object.

If you want a game to relax to and perhaps feel a little something at the end, I highly recommend getting this one.

This was such a lovely little cozy game with a unique storytelling approach. As someone who has moved several times in their life and lived with roommates, the story really resonated with me. Specifically, seeing some random (unclickable, therefore someone else's) objects in the [spoiler]roommate stage becoming clickable unpackable items in the next stage[/spoiler]. This was so common with myself and my friends who also lived with roommates; [spoiler]collecting things left behind to add to your sparse stash of home items.[/spoiler] I also appreciated after the [spoiler]MC moved back home as an adult then moved back into her own place, she brought a few more items from her childhood bedroom with her.[/spoiler]

I appreciated the (relative) freedom to place items as it made replays enjoyable. The only thing I would suggest as a QOL thing is an option to see a little description window of what the item is (like if you press SHIFT or CTRL while holding an item it will tell you what it is). There were a couple of items I was unsure of and it made placing them a bit confusing (like the louffa - I legitimately thought it was a ball of yarn and couldn't understand why I couldn't put it in the livingroom lol).

I would love to see (and would happily pay for) more stories to play through. I think this is such an empathetic, emotional yet still lighthearted way of sharing someone's life.

Hello Everyone!

After completing "Unpacking," I thought that I would take the time to write a review for this game. Overall, I would rate this game with FOUR STARS. 

Let's start with the positives.
1.} Playability: I did not experience issues throughout any part of the game. I was able to download, play, and finish the game without running into bugs or other issues. It seems that the Creators took extra care to ensure these types of issues would not happen.

2.) Time Allotment: If you are looking for a game that you can finish quickly or leave in the middle of, this might just be your game. It's not a long game, if you are a player that like to complete the game in one sitting. In addition, if you find yourself being a player that has to leave their game often, I find this game to be okay to do that. I did not run into any issues with my game progress not saving.

3.) Overall - Overall, I would say that this game is a light-hearted and colorful game that, for those like myself who like to organize, is just the right game to play if you need a lift. 

Now, the only negative.
1.) Achievements - As someone who prefers to complete ALL Achievements on the games that I play, I found this game, though simple, to have a few achievements that I had to look at the Spoilers for in order to figure them out. When playing the game, you might expect that all of the achievements or organizational related, but this is not the case. I found myself having to think WAY outside the box as far as the types of achievements that were listed. 

Despite the one negative that I found to the game, I would rate this game highly and would recommend it to others.

如果喜欢整理行李时的那份宁静，或是在布置房间时感到过满足，一定要试试这个游戏。它没有分数和时间限制，也没有失败，只有一个又一个装满回忆的箱子，和一间间等待被赋予“家”的意义的空房间。游戏过程中能感觉到玩家不仅是整理师，也是无声的见证者，通过空间和物品的变化，拼凑出一个完整而动人的成长故事。
非常适合玩几个小时来从快节奏生活中抽离，每次打开一个新的存档，都像是和老朋友重逢一样温暖。

I have played and replayed this game more times than I would like to count. I've deleted saves, restarted, deleted and restarted again. I have not had another game scratch the absolute ITCH that this game has given me. Other games get close... They're cozy, they allow me to organize, progress, etc. But nothing has had the emotional impact on me that Unpacking has. Unpacking skillfully tells a story without outright telling you the story. The actions you take only help to unfold and... well, unpack the story of the character's life. 

To this day, even with my 20 hours on record at the time of writing, I still cry like a big baby at the credits. Every. Time. And maybe that's because when I first played, I was at a time in my life where I was getting ready to move in with my long-time boyfriend. Regardless, I cannot recommend Unpacking enough.

[h1]Unpacking[/h1]
[b][i]Moving in simulator[/i][/b]

[b][u]Gameplay[/u][/b]
A deceptively simple gameplay loop where you open a box, put all the things in the box away where they belong and then the level is finished. Each level has it's own challenges that make you think through what you're doing.

[b][u]Visuals[/u][/b]
Isometric view of rooms in a home. Cartoony without being overly twee.

[b][u]Sound[/u][/b]
The music is a bit samey when you play through the whole story mode a few times, but it is a fitting soundtrack to moving in. There are nice touches [spoiler]when you activate music players in the game[/spoiler].

[b][u]Overall[/u][/b]
I completed this with all achievements in 11 and a half hours according to steam. I bought this on switch as well so I could share it with everyone I know. It's a great little puzzler and it packs an emotional punch. My favourite.

A sweet, if slightly tedious game with surprisingly deep points to make about the relationship between people, home, and possessions. If you've ever gotten a kind of thrill from deciding where to put each item in a new home, you will enjoy this game. There is a puzzle element to deciding where everything will go, especially since, in most of the apartments, it's a bit of tight fit. But mostly this is a game about evoking feelings, such as the unsettled feeling of moving back home as an adult; the freedom of getting your own place (which, though ♥♥♥♥♥♥, feels like home after you've unpacked); the tender feeling of intermingling your stuff with a partner's; the familiarity of unpacking a favorite item that's full of memories.

[i] Unpacking [/i] is a short, cosy and meditative game spread across eight levels, where your objective is to make each house a home by taking stuff out of boxes, then putting them in their respective areas. There are no time limits and the plot is delivered wordlessly through the unseen protagonist, or more specifically their personal belongings. It's a charming and relatable game with a surprising amount of humour and drama. A great game for anyone looking to play something low-stress :)

[b] Very short.[/b] Really good if you get it on sale. I wish it was longer, but it did a good impression and i hope more games like these are made. 

 [i] What is the game about? [/i]
There are rooms, some empty, some already with furniture. You get boxes filled with stuff and decor that you can sort and place (mostly) wherever you want. You can play it the way it is supposed to, or you can (now) sort and place items wherever you want. So it's a game that just makes you feel good about yourself when you find a good spot. It's a game better played when you're not in a rush and take it slow.

 [i] Personal pros [/i]
+ I liked the feature where you can place the items wherever you want, that makes the game re-playable and more fun.
+ Calm and rush-free
+ Cute graphics
+ Has so much potential
+ Simple and straightforward

 [i] Personal cons [/i]
- Way too short for full price :(
- Felt like a demo about to enter real game-play only to end.

Unpacking is one of the most delightful and soothing games I’ve ever played. It’s simple in concept: unpack boxes and arrange belongings in each new living space, but it delivers so much more than just tidying up.

The gameplay is intuitive and easy to understand, making it instantly accessible whether you’re a casual gamer or someone looking to unwind after a long day. There’s no stress, no timers, no enemies. Just the calming rhythm of placing each item where it belongs. The sound design, cozy visuals, and small details make every moment feel satisfying and surprisingly emotional.

For me, Unpacking was the perfect anxiety-reducing escape. It’s incredibly cozy, relaxing, and rewarding. I finished the entire game in a single day, and I even unlocked all the achievements without ever feeling pressured. That’s how smoothly the game flows.

If I had one wish, it would be for more content. I didn’t want it to end! The only downside to Unpacking is that it left me craving more boxes to unpack and more lives to peek into. I’m crossing my fingers for a DLC or a sequel, because I would happily spend hours more with this experience.

Final Verdict:
Unpacking is a heartfelt, relaxing, and perfectly cozy game that I’d recommend to anyone. It’s short but deeply satisfying, and it lingers with you long after the boxes are empty.

[h3]Potentially therapy for hoarders or the organisationally impaired[/h3]

I originally played this game on xbox and I adored it, and I genuinely believe this game could be used as a form of therapy for people who struggle with organisation skills

I do want to say right off the bat, this game needs to be able to be modded, and that's not gonna happen, there's an explanation of why, but I think it'd be well worth remaking the game from scratch with mod support, even if you don't include all the original levels of this game, because this game is pretty short, and as I said, I think it could be a therapy aid, and being able to create your own stories with this game would be an incredibly unique form of storytelling, but also, being able to use this game to create levels specifically designed to help people who struggle with hoarding, organisation, or whatever else, would be incredibly advantageous, I speak from experience

I showed this game to a family member who struggles with organisation and hoarding, they adored it, and after playing they genuinely became noticeably better with their organisation and managing their hoarding, and there's a real lack of tools and resources for people who struggle with that, so this game was kind of huge, but there's a very small amount of levels and they're the same every time, so after a while, the benefits of having played this game didn't completely disappear, but they did decline closer to where they initially were prior to playing

If anyone cares to make a version of this game with more features, a level creator, story creator, and mod support, it could genuinely be lifechanging to some people, and I want to see that happen, I understand why it didn't happen with this game, but I think it's something that needs to happen


This game is fairly short as I said, so do keep that in mind for how much you're willing to pay, I think it's base price is pretty high for the amount of content, but still I think this game is important, and even if you don't need help with organisational skills, this is a lovely chill game, I've been sick recently and that's why I decided to replay it on steam, and it holds up, it's a great sick game, it's a great chill game, it's a great game in general, if you're looking for something intense, of course you won't like it, but if you give it a chance this game is phenomenal and incredibly important

Oh but if you're an anti-woke grifter you should avoid this game, not because the main character is bisexual, but because you don't deserve the joy or relaxation of this game until you grow as a human being

优点：通过整理房间窥探主人公的人生历程别出心裁，适合好奇心旺盛、探索欲强烈的玩家。
缺点：
1..物品没有注释且因为远景的关系，有些很难辨识是什么，无法保证整理逻辑。
比如：
1）主人公拥有大量的书籍，因为远景只能通过封面图案略微猜测书本内容，无法准确分类只能胡乱放在一起，显然不合逻辑。

2.物品摆放并非完全自由，对于各物品大致规定了正确的摆放区域。这本身没什么毛病，但是部分物品的摆放位置不合逻辑，非常别扭。

1）大型盆栽可以大量放在卧室里，显然不利于健康，一般不会这么放。

3）水杯一律不准放在厨房以外的地方？无法理解，边工作边喝个咖啡不是很正常么？

诸如此类。

Unpacking is a simple and cozy game centred around the deeply satisfying task of sorting and organizing. While it includes a light amount of puzzle-solving, the real joy comes from methodically unpacking belongings and finding the best place for them in each new space.

You follow a character’s journey from childhood through young adulthood, with each level representing a major stage in their life. The narrative isn’t overt, but it’s there for those who take the time to notice. Subtle environmental storytelling and item placement hint at important turning points and developments in the character’s life. Some players might claim there’s no story, but in truth, it just isn’t spoon-fed—it’s gently woven into the experience for those willing to read between the lines.

There’s also some replay value, as there’s often more than one way to unpack the same set of items. If you’re the kind of player who likes to sort items by theme, colour, size, or function, you’ll likely take extra time and care, adding to the satisfaction. My playthrough took about 4–5 hours, but you could complete it faster if you’re less focused on precision.

Some reviewers have criticized the game for being too short, but I found the length appropriate for the kind of experience it offers. Not every game needs to provide 75+ hours of content. There are also stickers and achievements to collect for completionists, adding a bit of extra gratification.

If you’re on a tight budget, it might be worth waiting for a sale—but if you’re in the market for something gentle and relaxing, I definitely recommend giving this one a try. It’s a great little game to help you unwind.
