Unpacking is one of the most unique and touching games I’ve ever played. At first glance, it seems simple—you unpack boxes and organize belongings in different rooms. But as you go from one move to the next, you start to piece together a story that’s told entirely through the objects you unpack.

And somehow, without any dialogue or traditional cutscenes, Unpacking tells a richer and more emotional story than many big-budget games. You follow one person’s life across years and locations—through childhood, college, relationships, heartbreak, and self-discovery—just by seeing what they bring with them and where they choose to place it.

The gameplay is calm, thoughtful, and oddly therapeutic. There’s no timer, no pressure—just the satisfying task of putting things in their place. And there’s something incredibly meaningful about recognizing an old object that’s followed you through several moves, or noticing what’s missing after a big life change. Every detail feels intentional.

Visually, the game is charming and cozy, with beautifully pixelated art and subtle animations. The sound design is especially lovely—every item makes a different sound when you place it on wood, carpet, tile, or shelves. It’s a small detail, but it adds so much texture to the experience.

Unpacking is more than just organizing things—it’s about identity, growth, and the emotional weight that our belongings carry. It’s a game that makes you pause, reflect, and appreciate the small things in life.

If you enjoy slow, meaningful games with storytelling done in a truly unique way, this is absolutely one to experience. It’s short, sweet, and incredibly powerful.

This is a neutral review.

I really like the idea behind this chill game, and it mostly works. My issue is that it becomes very tedious (seriously, how many books and articles of clothing are you going to make me unpack every stage?), and some of the items are a complete mystery to me, which makes it very difficult to understand where to place them. Okay, it's a white box with multiple drawers... but I couldn't make heads or tails of where to put it—only through a lot of trial and error did I figure out where it belonged (and I still don't understand what it is). There is something satisfying about placing objects down though and organizing things, though.

In my view, the game would be better with more frequent, smaller levels featuring more varied objects. Everything felt very samey; again, I can only place 21 books before I start to get bored. Why not have a room dedicated to music, for example? Instead, you often get rooms that are just full of objects with no real sense of cohesion.

The achievements were a nice touch—like making me write out a math equation with magnets on a fridge, for example. It is a rather short experience—I clocked in at 3.5 hours played, with every achievement and a little bit of AFK involved. Finally, I feel like $20 is a bit steep for the asking price... again, you'll probably get about 3 hours out of it. Maybe look for it in a bundle or on sale.

しばらく前からプレイしようと思っていたのだが、内容が不十分でフルプライスの価値はないというレビューを読んだ。だから代わりにセール中に買うことにした。プレイを終えて、私はそう思う。リプレイする人もいるかもしれないが、常にリプレイするような作品でもない。

ゲームプレイは極めて単純明快だ。私はOCDだと思うので、アイテムを好きなように配置し続けた結果、必要以上に時間がかかってしまいました。

時間をかけすぎると、それが楽しいと思えるようになるのか、それとも欲求不満によるものなのか。でも、ここで時間を使いすぎると、実生活で部屋の掃除ができなくなりそうだ。

このゲームの特別なところは、遺品を整理している間に湧いてくる好奇心だと思う。持ち主はどんな人なんだろうとか、章を通して何があったんだろうとか。どんなものが残って、どんなものが捨てられたのか。深く考えてみると、結構意味のあることだと思う。見たことも会ったこともないキャラクターが、その人の人生が気になってくる。ちょっと待てよ！これって 「盗み見 」じゃないですか？

[spoiler]ボーイフレンドと同居する章が一番イライラした！あの人のワードローブも整理しなきゃいけないの？彼の家はめちゃくちゃだった。その章が終わったとき、彼女はアルバムに 「ここにやっと自分の身が収まるくらいだった 」と書いている。それがすごく心に響いた。

次の章では、私は彼女が家に戻るのに打ちのめされた...。私は 「えええ？」と言った。ってことは、あの2人は別れたってことだよね？あの男の後始末をしたのが無駄だったことに気づいて、私はイライラした！どういうこと？これは、同棲して別れることになる女子の普遍的な経験なのだろうか。[/spoiler]

最終的に、この絶えず動き続ける人物は幸せを見つける！というわけで、ゲーム全体には満足しています。ニワトリとヒヨコは私のお気に入りのアイテムで、とても気に入っています！それぞれのアイテムが発する音や、さまざまな表面で鳴る音も、聞いていてとても満足できるものでした。

全体的な感想としては、ストレスとリラックスを同時に感じた。でもそれは、彼女の荷物を解きながら、この人の人生を想定することに夢中になりすぎたからだと認め。

Unpacking is a quietly thoughtful game that emotionally impacted me more than I expected. At first glance, it’s just a relaxing unpacking sim, but the subtle storytelling and attention to detail makes it something more meaningful.

The pixel art is surprisingly detailed—you can recognize specific DVDs and items just from tiny visual cues, and that kind of care is everywhere. There’s no dialogue or narration, but the way the character’s life unfolds through their belongings is genuinely touching. It’s peaceful, even a little bittersweet, and makes you reflect on your own life in quiet, unexpected ways.

I earned all the achievements in about 4.5 hours, which makes it a bit pricey for the amount of content, but honestly, the experience felt worth it. Still, I’d recommend grabbing it on sale if you’re hesitant.

If you enjoy calm, cozy games with a deeper emotional core, Unpacking is absolutely worth playing.

A silly little game to satisfy the itch in your brain that craves perfection, Unpacking is a puzzle game all about what the name entails.

Throughout the game, you're given many different scenarios as you live through the character's life and different living conditions. The player has one goal: unpack. These scenarios vary between how many boxes and items the player needs to open and unpack, and how many rooms the player will need to go through to finish the job. And while you might not put a toothbrush in the living room or shampoo in the bedroom, you're given a bit of freedom on how you want the rooms to look with the items given.

While moving and unpacking is a heavy chore to do, Unpacking takes those frustrations and turns it into a satisfying and unique experience.

优点：
- 好像现在玩法目的这么简洁简单的游戏已经越来越少了。很多游戏的“游玩压力”都变得越来越大。但是Unpacking的玩法却十分纯粹，十分放松。
- 没有文本，但通过房间和物品的改变让玩家了解主角生活的变化，可以说是个million dollar idea. (销售额貌似真的有million RMB了）。
- 谈恋爱了搬进来还要给男人收拾房间不然自己的东西都没地方放，甚至奖状（还是证书？）都只能放在床底下。蛮真实的。

缺点：
- 作为一个休闲游戏，配乐好像没有很戳人。
- 可能是我期待太高，当我点击窗户/水龙头/电视等物品发现没有反应的时候确实有点失望。（但好像有些灯可以开？）
- 没有文字label我真的不知道某些东西到底是什么... 
- 过于放松和重复的玩法导致我昏昏欲睡（不过对于失眠的我貌似不算缺点）。这也是为什么现在只玩了3h。
- 我对象骂我说自己房间不收拾在这哐哐收拾变勤快了（jk）

好像这游戏已经没后续了，真的会期待不同角色的Unpacking会是什么样子... ...
非常令人舒适的布置游戏，自由度很高，对爱好收纳整理的人来说特别解压

画风舒适，色彩搭配养眼，配合bgm食用很治愈。操作相对考究，不同拜访搭配过关的自由度还蛮高的，最喜欢是能够通过一些微妙的细节走进主角的内心生活（[spoiler] 比如每次搬家都增多的游戏磁带、从兴趣使然到逐渐变得高端的绘画设备、不断“生小鸡”的玩偶......再比如和前男友同居时无处安放的奖牌只能放在床下、二人分手后只愿意尘封在柜子里的合照、女朋友搬来后家里增添了许多鲜艳的色彩和生机勃勃的植物[/spoiler]）体验下来缺点一是难以判断部分物品究竟是什么，二是流程不长（如果还能有不同主角就好了）。综合而言瑕不掩瑜就是不够玩TT

A true "cozy" game. The trailers and promotional material are all very true to gameplay. This is a game about unpacking a person's story across phases of life. What is kept, left behind, and added all create a narrative through items alone. The details really make this game, and if you play it as just an unpacking simulator, they may be missed. At the risk of sounding super pretentious, this is a visual novel in the form of a game about unpacking boxes.

The $20 base price is pretty steep for the game's content. I recommend getting it on sale, but if you're looking for a zen experience, this does the trick. A well-earned BAFTA award for "Narrative".

First of all, love this game and this is a positive review, but it is NOT worth $20. I got this on sale for $10 and that's how much I think this should be originally, and then still go on sale. There are stop motion or 3D indie games for less than $20 on Steam. I'm a professional animator/illustrator and based on my experience, I'm sure those were more expensive and took more time and more effort to make than Unpacking. 

I finished this game in less than 3 hours (though I will play it again because I liked it) and that is way too short for such a price point. The game play mechanic is very, very simple point and click (though it IS well made and satisfying). And though I do liked the art, it's just pixel art with very little animation. It's cute, but it's the most low effort art you can make (without using unethical AI of course). It's not 3D, it's nothing stylized nor really hand drawn like A Little to the Left which is cheaper and has several DLCs. It's pixel art. Again, I'm a professional animator/illustrator, I expect something more and I know how much (little compared to other styles) effort and talent pixel art involves. Not saying pixel art is bad, just trying to emphasize that it's not worth $20. 

Now, this game is worth playing! It's not just cozy unpacking, there is a story. You feel emotionally attached to the person you are doing the unpacking for. It's super relaxing. It's not buggy. I love all the little elements that make up every move, and the progression and changes that you see. This part was very thought out and what makes this game unique and very playable. 

The actual game play, though simple, is so satisfying! Just opening the boxes, the animation that comes after the click, and the sound effect is satisfying. Clicking and putting an item down is also so clean and satisfying. I would often move things over and over again just to get that clean click. 

Some items I had no idea what they were (probably because the pixel art made it unclear...), so I guessed where to put them (often was wrong). The song at the end was so bad hahaha But it's fitting to the game and music I imagine the devs listen to. I truly imagine the team who made this game is just a bunch of animation or game students like the people I went to school with (animation nerds! :) ), the elements of the game, and all of the items you unpack just felt that way. 

Wish there was more. A DLC of other characters or something. 

Overall, I recommend this as a cozy, relaxing game. I have issues with the price and the art, but I will play this again.

This game is a pretty casual and cozy one, telling a small story through the items you place. You watch the character grow up and how she changes between the places she moves into. The game doesn't take much effort or time to play, and is good for a one day sitting if you want a chill game to play. 

★★★★★

GAME-PLAY-
The game-play for the game is pretty simple. You click things to open or move stuff, and have to put items in corresponding rooms and spots that make sense. The houses are somewhat customizable depending where you put stuff, and gives you a little pit of freedom, but overall it's pretty linear. If you don't put stuff in the right area after everything is unpacked, the items glow red and you have to figure out where they go.

STORY-
The story is pretty simple and mostly told through pictures. It's not a super big part of the game, and it doesn't change your experience very much if you don't pay attention. It's fairly easy to follow though, and I like the LGBTQ+ representation.  The story is small, but it adds a nice aspect to the game.

I don't this the characters names are ever stated, but they might be and I missed them. But through the story and the items you place in these new houses, you get to learn about and feel for the character. In some ways I feel like you can relate to the main character and the way she grows up, even without any narration or obvious storytelling. This makes the game a little more meaningful to me, and I think others who play it could feel the same way.

REPLAY-ABILITY-
I think this game has a little potential to be replayed. You can replay it if you want achievements or when you're really bored, or just want a game to play mindlessly to kill time. It's not a game you'll have 100 hours in, that's for sure, but you can probably replay it a few time without getting too bored.

Unpacking isn't just a game — it's a quiet, pixelated masterpiece. The pixel art is absolutely gorgeous; every tiny object, every shadow and shape is crafted with so much care and love.

But what truly blew me away was the environmental storytelling. I'm a huge fan of games that let the world speak for itself, and Unpacking has instantly taken the number one spot in my heart. There’s something so intimate and profound about learning a person’s story through their belongings. I’ve always believed that a room reflects a person’s soul — their chaos, their dreams, their fears — and this game captures that perfectly.

Without a single spoken word or text-based narrative, Unpacking tells a deeply emotional story purely through objects. A toothbrush, a worn-out plushie — each item carries the weight of years. It’s a quiet, powerful kind of storytelling that sneaks up on you.

I have to be honest: I cried while playing. Real tears. The story is just that beautiful. It reminded me of life’s small, bittersweet transitions, of growth, heartbreak, and self-discovery — all from unpacking boxes.

Unpacking isn't just about organizing things. It’s about finding yourself again and again, and leaving pieces of who you are behind — one box at a time.

Overall
Gameplay - 7/10 (Simple, a point and drag game. Sort them and find the right placement for the right item. Simple, intuitive, effective. For the type of game and story it conveys, perfect controls- seamless progression and can be completed with two hours.)
Story - 7/10 (Nice little story that you piece out from the items. If you rush the games, you'll tend to miss out on the subtle messages from each room and what each item conveys. Still you can get a general sense from a quick playthrough - though the story is conveyed in a very nice way.)
Scenery - 5/5 (Great visuals for the medium. One of the core of the game, its a nice simplistic style that enhances the story it tells and doesn't distract from the gameplay or the story.)
Music - 8/10 (Enjoyed the music throughout. Fit the medium very well.)

Specific
Puzzles - 2/5 (Easy to figure out which items went where, with the only puzzle being your own personal sense of organisation clashing with the games.)

Unpacking is one of those games that feels like a breath of fresh air. At first glance, it’s a pretty simple concept, you’re just unpacking boxes and putting things in their place. But once you start, it’s clear there’s more to it than that. It’s calming, satisfying, and surprisingly enjoyable.

What I really love about this game is how low-pressure it is. There’s no time limit, no goals you have to hit. It’s just you and some boxes, figuring out where everything goes. The simplicity is what makes it so easy to unwind. After a long day, I can just sit back and enjoy the quiet rhythm of unpacking, organising, and sorting things without feeling rushed or stressed.

The game does a great job of showing little bits of someone’s life through their things. As you unpack, you start to see a story unfold, different places they’ve lived, changes in their life, and little details that tell you who they are. It’s nice to see how everything comes together over time.

Unpacking is a perfect game when you just need a break. It’s not about intense action or challenges, just the simple act of arranging items and finding the right spot for them. It’s a game that’s relaxing, easy to get into, and makes you feel like you’ve done something satisfying by the time you finish.

Overall, if you’re looking for a chill, no-stress game to unwind with, Unpacking is a great choice. It’s a perfect way to escape for a little while and just enjoy the peace of putting things in order.

Unpacking es un juego que definitivamente no es para todos, ya que la mecánica es muy repetitiva, simple y la temática es bastante poco llamativa, porque, para ser sinceros ¿quién compraría un juego de desempacar y ordenar?. Pero a pesar de todo lo anterior, es extremadamente divertido el hecho de poder tener control sobre el orden de un espacio sin sentir el agotamiento físico que conlleva esto en la vida real. Lo que me pareció mas interesante sobre este juego fue su narrativa, la forma que tiene de contar historias es simplemente única, al punto donde realmente no te cuenta nada pero con el mero hecho de ver los cambios de espacios, los objetos que uno desempaca y sentir las emociones que transmite la banda sonora, podemos darnos cuenta perfectamente de lo que está pasando y de la linea narrativa que está sucediendo a lo largo del tiempo y eso se siente tan real y tan palpable que te deja inmerso en la dinámica. Nada me ha transmitido mejor la soledad que el ver como se va deshaciendo uno de cosas que le recuerdan a otra persona, cambia de cama de dos plazas a una, se achica el armario, y hasta el mero hecho de tener solo las pertenencias propias y no tener que hacer encajar las tuyas en la dinámica de alguien más, como pasar de tener un vaso con dos cepillos en el baño a tener solo uno o dejar de tener maquinas de café porque ya no vives con la persona a la que le pertenecía. de esta forma uno no solo conoce una historia, si no que conoce al personaje, su evolución, su madurez y hasta pensamientos, llegando a sentirnos dentro del juego, como si nosotros fuéramos los que se cambiaron de casa y tienen que desempacar, ese vinculo que uno crea con el personaje hace valer cada peso que gasté en este juego, el cual si tu lo quieres ver como un minijuego de ordenar y gestionar espacios, va a ser un juego casual el cual no vale lo que cuesta, pero si quieres ir mas allá y centrarte en la forma única que este tiene de contar la historia, lo vas a disfrutar mucho más y va a valer su precio completamente

I love this game so much more than I ever expected too. Generally, it may not be quite worth full price for most people since not everyone will find a lot of replay-ability here. However, if you are a fan of cozy games, organization, and background storytelling then you're sure to at least like this game. I have almost 50hrs in the game, but average playtime is probably closer to four or five hours, at least for a first play-through or to get all achievements. I personally have found a lot of value in replaying the game anytime I need something relaxing, but there aren't any additional content or incentives for this, I just find it fun to see how differently I set up the rooms every few months. 

The art of the game is absolutely fantastic and the gameplay itself is very polished. There are few, if any, things I wish I could do in the game that I currently can't, and there are some things I can do which I never would have expected (like putting the toothbrush in a cup). The pixel art is, again, fantastic and moving items around felt incredibly intuitive, snappy, and consistent. The true way the game shines, at least for those of us not obsessed with organizing, is in its background narrative. It's incredibly endearing and the game consistently does a great job in making you feel exactly the emotions it wants you to. You feel the excitement, discomfort, heartbreak, and freedom that the main character is meant to be feeling simply by moving her things and the ambient storytelling of the room. An absolute master class in taking a simple concept, like moving objects around in a room, and expanding it into something that can actually leave an impact on the player.

This is one of my favourite games. I recently came back to it after completing it a few years ago and playing through a second time adds a whole new level of nostalgia and familiarity.

The gameplay is satisfying and moving items around feels precise and intuitive, unlike some knock-offs whose items feel floaty and don't stay under your cursor/finger. The art is beautiful and it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ joy to zoom in and study all the little details and easter eggs. The sound design and music? Delicious.

The story? C'mon. The devs have put on a clinic in the art of showing, not telling. The depth of what you learn about your protag as you unpack their life through the years is astonishing. From the things they've carried since childhood, to interests they've been introduced to by others, to how their career is going.

I only wish there were more of it. The original story is perfectly wrapped up, but I'd go absolutely feral over new stories about completely different people.

Maybe I'm biased because I see a lot of myself in protag; we share many interests and milestones in life. But man, this game unpacked itself straight into my heart and will be there forever.

In real life, moving is the worst. In Unpacking, described by its creators as a “zen puzzle game,” settling into a new place is surprisingly comforting. Unpacking takes you through a series of homes representing an invisible protagonist’s life from 1997 to 2018, and as it turns out, you can tell a lot about a person by the things they take with them. Though the mechanics are simple and the campaign can be completed in a handful of hours, Unpacking is a memorable, delightful game that shows that there are still new ways to tell stories in video games out there.

You might not think stacking plates and organizing books is compelling, but strangely, it really is. Part of that might have to do with how often you’ve pulled up stakes. For me, it was a lot: between the ages of 18 and 26, I moved more than half a dozen times. Packing and unpacking became an almost annual ritual as I transitioned through a series of apartments in various neighborhoods throughout the Philadelphia area. None of these places ever felt like home until I started unpacking: taping the David Bowie poster with torn edges to the wall, finding a flat surface for my ancient record player, and lining up my Harry Potter books in chronological order on the shelves. Settling into the next place always felt like a new chapter of my life was starting, and that’s a feeling Unpacking captures well.

When you’re getting started, no time is wasted with explanations, tutorials, or cut scenes. You don’t even see the person whose boxes you’re unloading. Instead, we get to know them through the basic point-and-click mechanics that allow you to move belongings from boxes to their proper places in the home, beginning with a single childhood bedroom and eventually moving on to larger, multi-room spaces. There’s no inventory list so you never know what the next thing you’ll pull out of any given box will be, and that makes for a series of sweet surprises that reveals a little bit more about the character. There are also no timers or scores, allowing you to move at your own pace. Because of that, Unpacking is the kind of game in which it’s easy to lose a couple of hours in what feels like only minutes.

I absolutely love this game even after completing it so many times. I find myself coming back again and again when i see it in my library and remember how happy it made me to learn about the character you play as. I love projecting my own personality onto them and i try to give them new quirks every save, giving them a story of my own. Especially while going through some confusing times with my identity as a person and coming into the stage of adulthood, I find comfort in seeing someone figure their own life out and I'm excited to start my new journey.

This game, to me, is very awkward and sometimes uncomfortable when I realize that the spots I place things in can't always stick, things don't always fit when I want them to. And that's okay. Because I'll find another way to make it work, even if it's not going to my own plan.
As a neurodivergent person and someone with associative synesthesia, I experience things that sometimes I don't always understand and the best way i know to communicate is through metaphor and colors. It's why i love games like this. No words to decipher, no perfect narrative to decode, just my interpretation and imagination as I organize for hours.

Visual and vague story telling is one of the most beautiful forms of art to me and I love being pulled in the creator's narrative and being handed the reigns while taking in what they made and adding my ideas. We're writing a story together even across maybe thousands of miles and we're communicating in small ways saying 'look! i want you to see what i did!'. We're having a conversation across worlds, holding hands over tea as we create and share and love what we do.
Giving up specificity to connect with the player/consumer is so intimate to me.

Knowing humans can do this, connect from all over the world to make something beautiful, it reminds me that I'm not alone. It's like a burning fire that you swear you spot pictures in as you sip a hot drink in the cold months, telling someone of your discovery and forcing them to look with you. You both spot your own made up images and talk about how cool it is that fire can make such things.
It's like a soft, dusty yellow that looks almost pink or purple is some light and it's a comfort I want to hold dear for the rest of my life.

I would LOVE another Unpacking, about a different character - I keep looking for games that will scratch the particular itch Unpacking has left me with, and in the end I always come back to replay this one instead. However, it's almost held up entirely by its uniqueness; this is extremely un-replayable. Any attempts to make copycat games would be pretty disastrous, as they wold not be unique. Even this game itself felt like it was dragging on for too long near the end, where the story was finished and the only thing left to do was the relatively unimpressive... unpacking.

Oh the early adulthood first apartment experience with mismatched furniture, a well-worn well-loved blanket, mismatching cups, leftovers from college still serviceable years later. This game lured me in with the promise of cute graphics and satisfying gameplay and kept my attention with a story told entirely through sentimentality and memories held in items. Moving into each new space, pulling familiar items out of boxes and seeing how our main character's life has changed and grown is so special, especially since the game uses no dialogue and does not tell you the story outright. We see our focal character go to college, get into a relationship that failed, rebuild her life, fall in love again and not only move into an actual house with her wife, but also decide to have a child. And the entire time we get to see beloved items return to each new living space, like the pig plushy that not only keeps coming back, but actually shows the passage of time in how it's been worn and torn. It's a game that focuses so strongly on growth and moving forward, but also on sentimentality and nostalgia. It's a beautifully done game and a masterclass in telling a story without having to TELL the story.

It's very good at what it sets out to do, and you end up feeling attached to the main character, though you never even learn her name. This game made me feel the full spectrum of human emotion for a protagonist whose face I never even see.  As I went through each new location and the boxes she brought along, I found myself rooting for her - wanting her to succeed as an artist, hoping she stayed in contact with her D&D crew, shaking my husband's shoulder with joy when she got her own place.  What a journey!

In many ways, I see myself in this game.  Family, school, horrible ex, nerd buddies who helped me find my feet, finding the love of my life and moving thousands of miles away...it's familiar, and I think that's part of what makes this short, simple game so magical.  As I made a point of clearing entire shelves so that my new in-game partner could have her own space for her own things, I looked around the real-world flat my husband and I share and I think of how he did the same for me.  It makes you appreciate what follows you into adulthood, the things we do for love, and how long it can take our dreams to become our reality.  That's a lot to expect from a game that I got for seven quid on sale, but wow, does Unpacking ever pull it off!

浅谈游戏《unpacking》。
这是我第一个达到全成就的游戏，到目前，我的游戏时长为8h。

单从游戏玩法来说，这个游戏非常简单，就是给主人公每次搬家后的箱子进行拆包和整理摆放，对于有整理爱好或者特别喜欢整齐的玩家来说，游玩起来会有一些特别的趣味，但是对于其他玩家来说，游戏体验会稍显单调。

从其他方面讲，这个游戏整体节奏完全由玩家掌控，音乐比较舒缓，画面治愈，在疲劳的生活之余游玩会感到心情很放松。这也是为什么我开始工作后，会在一天下班之后想起这个几年前就走完整个游戏流程的游戏，并重新打开游玩了一遍。

这个游戏比较有意思的一点在于，这个游戏并没有讲什么故事，也没有写什么背景，但是玩家在整理物品的过程中会了解到一个女孩成长到成熟的大人的阶段性变化，也能读到这个女孩人生的每一个阶段所面临的状况和她做出了什么样的选择。这样隐藏在简单的收纳整理中的“故事”别具温馨感，这也是我选择推荐这款游戏的原因。不过这个游戏对于它的内容和游玩价值来说，价格还是略贵了。

Unpacking combines charming pixel art and a calming soundtrack with subtle environmental storytelling and ASMR-adjacent sound effects to create a "puzzle" game which invokes a sense of nostalgia and is easy to get lost in. Simple, non-challenging gameplay is nothing but a positive when it comes to this game. Closer to a form of mindfulness and meditation than a game in the puzzle or logic genre, Unpacking is a gentle story that just so happens to involve some player input. A relatively short title, in name and gameplay hours, it's a low-stakes experience perfect for a cozy and relaxing night in or a rainy day. I give Unpacking a 10/10 for what it is, and was pleasantly surprised when I felt a tug at the heartstrings at some of the more emotional parts of the story. There is limited replay value but I may find myself revisiting the title in the future just for the vibes. Fingers crossed for a sequel sometime in the future.

8/10 Unpacking é um jogo tão imersivo e criativo que fico triste de não poder esquecê-lo para jogar de novo como se fosse da primeira vez.
A ideia de contar uma história através das coisas que uma pessoa leva para cada casa onde mora é genial! Eu gosto muito da quantidade de formas em que podemos organizar cada cômodo nos níveis, apesar de alguns objetos nunca caberem de forma satisfatória nos armários. E com alguns objetos quero dizer as panelas, detesto a parte da cozinha :( Mas bem, organizar uma cozinha na vida real também é terrível.
Não tenho muito a falar sobre a história. Honestamente, sinto que para cada jogador ela vai ressoar de forma diferente. No geral, ela é contada de forma sutil, mas relativamente fácil de entender. 
A jogabilidade também é bacana, apesar de não ter muito o que fazer nesse tipo de jogo quanto às tarefas gerais, nosso trabalho é colocar as coisas no lugar mais conveniente possível. O foco é aproveitar o que os objetos tem a contar. 
No geral, a única coisa que desgosto um pouco sobre o Unpacking é que é um jogo de se jogar uma vez só. Pelo menos pra mim, não tem tanta graça revisitar os itens depois que chegamos ao último nível (por mais que eu tenha feito isso algumas vezes). No fim, temos exatamente aqueles objetos sempre, podemos até entender eles de forma diferente depois, mas eles continuam os mesmos. 
Enfim, jamais vou esquecer a sensação de jogar pela primeira vez, porque foi muito bom, mas não é um jogo que amo com todo o meu coração. No todo, a ideia é fenomenal e muito muito muito bem executada. Vale a pena!

It reminds me that enjoying my time interacting with "games" doesn't always need to involve grinding away at developing white-knuckle aim and PTSD-inducing reaction time. These things can be a way to communicate about the myriad ways people can share our experiences across all the things that might otherwise be used to divide us.

++ Excellent environmental storytelling
++ Intuitive, minimalist interface that never gets in the way of letting you place things where you want

Other notes:
~ Some players might feel shortchanged by the game’s relatively brief run time

I thought this would just be a relaxing game, but it ended up being so much more than that. I found this game very therapeutic, with a beautiful story interlaced throughout. The details of this game, the photographs, how the spaces and things you are unpacking change and develop over the game is a part of the story. The details are beautiful and, as a queer person, its so easy to really start to see yourself in the main character. By the end of the game you feel a sense of truly knowing the characters, feeling proud of their fictitious accomplishments. I also think that the ability to replay the game is definitely there. The underlying story told through subtle subtext and the humorous achievements (eg: the toaster) are a fun bonus; while I can understand the criticisms regarding the game's length/replay value, I respectfully disagree. I bought "Unpacking" today, and I finished it today. I left the game running for a few hours while I did a few chores, so total playtime for me to FINISH the game was actually less, about 3 hours (taking my time/relaxing/enjoying the game.) My biggest fear was the game not being long enough, which it sadly wasn't... However, I enjoyed it too much, ESPECIALLY for relaxing. The storyline is next to nothing, and the game is super easy. I WISH there were DLCs for the game, because even on sale at 50 percent off, I still feel like there wasn't enough playtime there to justify paying even half price for it. Don't get me wrong, the game is fantastic, but since it's so short, it needs more DLC or scenarios to play.

 The concept is super cute... You start out as a "kid" unpacking your childhood room, and continue that... For several years/representing each phase of a child's life into adulthood.  You unpack the boxes and try to fit everything into the rooms that they are supposed to go into. At the end of each scenario, the items you placed wrongly, will be highlighted in red so you'll easily know which ones to fix without hassle. The game overall is definitely re-playable, and I WILL replay it to complete it to 100%, but a game like this isn't for everyone. It's most definitely a "cozy game" and nothing more. Very minimalistic and cute. Don't expect much out of it and heed my warning of it being a pretty short game... It's literally just like the name... "Unpacking." If that concept sounds boring to you, or puzzle games are boring, I recommend skipping out on this one. For cozy/zen gamers, I say watch reviews on Youtube and give it a shot. It made me happy, but not happy enough to justify the price- again, solely because of the short play time.

Update... I went back to finish all accomplishments/complete the game to 100 percent. The "stickers" you find in the game are the additional "hidden" achievements. You can find guides online, they are so easy. It took maybe 10 minutes. I still adore the gameplay, and I know I will replay it sometime soon! Very zen.

For me, this was more than worth it for the price I paid (half off), however it is the sort of gameplay that definitely wouldn't appeal to everybody. It's sort of like a puzzle game but with more creativity to it, but not so much freedom that it could be considered a decorating game. The art and the storyline make the game much more charming and enjoyable, but the core mechanic is a lot of clicking and moving things around, which can get incredibly repetitive. I found the repetition relaxing though, and it made for some effective storytelling each time you see an item repeated (actually made me a little emotional at the end). I agree with other reviewers that the game feels a bit short, I spent pretty much as long as I could on it before it started to feel incredibly tedious but this is a game that could be completed in just a few hours. There is some replay potential but I don't think I would touch it again anytime soon because I got what I wanted out of it by completing the levels and achievements once.

If you like puzzle-esque point and click games, then I would definitely recommend this game, but you might want to wait for a sale since it's pretty short. The story and art are very strong, and the easter eggs make it charming and interesting to try different thigns, but it would've been nice to have a few more levels, or even some DLC exploring a second character's storyline.

Edit: Feb 16, 2025

Finished the game last night. I love how this game doesn't really tell you anything. After each unpacking section there's a less than 10 word summary about that location and it's relevance. But there is so much that the game is showing you with those summaries. You learn so much about the person who is unpacking, and it's entirely through environmental storytelling. The items that stick around between moves, the items that disappear, the way the space expands and contracts. The persistent change of a life over time. It's beautiful.

I also love the simplicity of the game. Pick an item, put the item somewhere, repeat. But the way the items are pulled out of boxes, where similar things are grouped together and largely in the correct rooms, but not always. Where you get to choose how the space looks while you're doing it. You can take as long as you want, or as little time as you want. The items sometimes can do something beyond being put somewhere (turning on a lamp for example) and it's fun to see what can and can't be done.

I loved this game. Not sure what next steps will be for me but for now, I just wanted to expand this comment.

    [*]The perfect game for someone who is not into games. If you want to introduce a spouse, mother, or grandmother to gaming without overwhelming them with mechanics and numbers, this is an excellent place to start.
    [*]Lovely pixel art.
[/list]

[h3]---The BAD---[/h3]
[list]
    [*]Very short and not worth the current full asking price of $20. Wait for a sale.

[h3]---The AMBIVALENT---[/h3]
[list]

This game is 25% puzzle game, 75% environmental storytelling. You follow the protagonist from childhood through starting a family, unpacking and moving her into whatever new place she's living in. I found myself feeling hopeful, sad, frustrated, and happy along with her through each level, which is impressive considering the game's plot is entirely told through the items you get, their current condition from the last time you unpacked them, and where you are able to place them. (Is there enough room? Are they displayed proudly or tucked away in a closet?)

The game's puzzle features aren't strict, which I was worried about prior to playing. You can stack items, place them on whatever shelf or cabinet you want, or display it on the wall or table or windowsill that suits your fancy. So long as they are generally in the "correct" spot you won't be made to move it. (I think you can also force-complete levels, although I've never had to do so.)

All in all, my experience with unpacking has been incredibly pleasant and relaxing, and I see myself playing it through again in the future.

I love this game. It's relaxing and does a great job of telling a sweet story about growing up using only the environment. The levels have different challenges that match the life stage they represent--when the character is moving in with roommates, a lot of space is taken up by the roommates' belongings that you can't move. When she moves in with a boyfriend, his belongings have to be rearranged to make space. It also does a great job of setting the time period each level takes place in and showing the passage of time through things like subtle pop cultural references, different types of technology, and some items showing up in multiple levels with increasing wear and tear. As someone in my mid-30s, who is probably around the same age as the character this game follows, the technological and cultural elements of each level were very relatable!

While there is something of a puzzle element to this game (you have to find places for the items you unpack and you're not allowed to place items in spots that aren't logical, like putting clothes in the kitchen), most of the gameplay is organizing items to your liking, which gives the game some re-playability value. There is also enough detail to make replaying levels fun. I still enjoy going back to this game occasionally when I'm in the mood for something relaxing.

That said, I do think the current price is probably a little high for the amount of content and replay value.

A "cozy" game about moving into new places and having to unpack and put away your belongings.

[hr][/hr]
Unpacking consists of a series of levels of increasing complexity. Each level contains a home shown through a series of screens depicting each available room. Furniture aside, these homes start off being mostly empty, tasking you with arranging various possessions within them in order to finish the level. Said possessions can be taken from a number of moving boxes strewn throughout the homes and placed on any free surface.

While this basic setup may sound benign, the game expects every object to be placed in a valid location, marking up any items which have been placed incorrectly and preventing the level from ending unless everything sits in a logical place. Through this, Unpacking turns into a light puzzle game, with you having to sus out logical places for all items and arrange them in such a way that everything fits into the provided space. This makes for a decent challenge without really ever feeling truly difficult. For some light replay value, there are also a couple of secret interactions spread throughout the levels and items.

Over the course of its levels, the game tells a light story, mostly through implications brought on by the changes in the types of homes and the items you have to move. This setup is used to mix up the basic gameplay, adding some unique constraints in the different homes, such as having to move in with another person whose stuff is already taking up space and can't be moved aside. This adds a welcome bit of variety to the base gameplay and on at least one occasion is also used for some very clever indirect storytelling.

Presentation-wise, Unpacking features a well-executed pixel art look which is detailed and gives the game a welcoming vibe. This is complemented by some neat if mostly forgettable background music and an overall comfortable atmosphere brought on by the gameplay.

You may have noticed that in this review's opening I put brackets around the term "cozy" when describing the game. This relates to the way this game is marketed, being praised as a relaxing experience to unwind and feel comfortable. While I mostly agree with this assessment of the Unpacking experience, I honestly cannot in good faith call the game relaxing, especially when looking at the later levels. The boxes you're unpacking are not perfectly sorted, meaning that item sets may be split up between multiple boxes, sometimes even ending up in different rooms altogether. Combined with the fact that each box essentially acts as a stack of (semi-)randomly items of which you can only ever remove the top-most item before accessing the next one, this makes it quite hard to get an overview of what you still have to place and how you should thus allocate the available space. This will likely lead to you either having to rework your placements multiple times or start each level by taking every single item out of the boxes and throwing them on the floor, creating a massive unordered pile to then systematically sort through.

Combined with the later levels being genuinely massive, this way of playing quickly became exhausting to me, which resulted in me having to take frequent breaks to de-stress outside the game. Some of the later levels were actually long enough to require multiple sessions to get through and I was honestly relieved to be finished by the end of the game. While moving boxes not being ordered well and unpacking taking ages perfectly mirror the experience of moving in real life (in my opinion), I found these aspects to substantially take away from Unpacking's vibe and my overall enjoyment of the game. This sentiment was also backed up by a friend of mine who played the game and eventually stopped altogether due to feeling overwhelmed by busywork.

[hr][/hr]
This last point of criticism aside, I had a good time with Unpacking and enjoyed its base gameplay as well as most aspects the way the game's executed.

well bless my queer lil heart! this was a beautiful 6 hours of therapeutic uNpAcKiNg. yeah, it's short, but I bought it on special and i reeeally enjoyed it so it feels absolutely worth it. will i play it again? not anytime soon, but this will stick with me for a while. i was surprisingly moved by the entire experience. 

it's impressive that such a simplistic game can illicit strong emotion. i'll admit this isn't hard to achieve from me. i've been known to cry during insurance commercials. but if you appreciate being fed tiny doses of feels throughout your gameplay, you'll appreciate this element. but you also have to be looking for it! the subtle detail with recurring motifs as time passes, and the ability to craft a narrative in a visually simple way is pretty damn cool. the ways in which our lives and 'stuff' melds in to others' when we create homes together. it's simple but beautifully poetic and positive outlook on universal human experience. like, the striking visual contrast between the 'toothbrushes'  mutually finding their home in the same cups in some homes, but that option was unavailable in one of the homes with the electric toothbrush...ya know? hmm. i found myself wondering about this character and their life in detail. i'm still thinking about them now. jesus. 

and if you're anything like my autistic ass, romanticism aside, you'll just really enjoy the act of UNPACKING. seriously. i love me some easy point and click. and organising the items satisfied part of my brain without having to THINK TOO HARD. i did have to google the correct location during one chapter because i was stumped (the bloody photo/POSTCARD!) but it was incredibly simple overall so my fried brain didn't even consider rage quitting at any point. i can see how some people would find the game boring, but i'm a simple romantic. this ♥♥♥♥ could never bore me. live, laugh, languish.

[h2]Introduction [/h2]
Unpacking is a unique and charming puzzle game that invites players to immerse themselves in the life of an unnamed protagonist through the act of unpacking their belongings. With a minimalist aesthetic and a focus on storytelling, the game offers a surprisingly emotional experience.

[h2]Story and Setting [/h2]
The game's narrative unfolds chronologically like a photo album. And indeed, each chapter starts with a blank picture in an album with a date and when the level is complete, there is a photo in the album of a newly decorated place. With that you are able to follow the character’s life from childhood, where you could try to understand what the child is interested in, to see hobbies or successes, thorought student life where you have to live with different people to… You should see yourself!
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3301363713

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
Unpacking's gameplay is simple yet engaging. Players are tasked with arranging items within a series of different rooms. The mechanic may look repetitive, but the narrative behind it makes the experience exciting.  Throughout the years you are able to see how different belongings affected (or not at all) the life of this person and to see where it has led the character.
The only thing where I was not 100% about is that some items cannot be put in certain rooms. And after opening all the boxes the game would highlight items which are organized wrongly. In my opinion, the whole idea behind it is unnecessary and ruins the experience. 

[h2]Graphics and Sound[/h2]
The game's visual style is clean and inviting, with a focus on detailed item design. The color palette and overall aesthetic contribute to the game's calming atmosphere. Sound effects are minimal, but effectively enhance the experience.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3301363750

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]
Unpacking is a delightful and thought-provoking game. It offers a unique perspective on the human experience, inviting players to connect with the character on a personal level. The game will be a pure gem for people who themselves were moving to new places, having to survive with different kinds of people under one roof and by accident  [strike]or not [/strike] stealing someone’s else's belongings!

P.S. Couple of weeks ago I moved to a new place and unpacking is still continuing :(

The environmental storytelling is absolutely masterful. It feels like every time I play I notice a new detail. Unpacking will never get old for me, and I highly recommend it.

Unpacking is an absolute gem of a cozy game that will capture your heart from the very first box you open! This game is a delightful breath of fresh air with its soothing and surprisingly engaging gameplay. The concept—unpacking boxes and finding the perfect spot for each item—might seem simple, but it’s bursting with warmth and meticulous detail that makes every moment feel special.

Each level of Unpacking unfolds like a new chapter in the life of its main character, and as you piece together their story, you’ll find yourself genuinely invested and emotionally connected. The nostalgia factor is especially potent, as the items and settings evoke a sense of familiarity and personal memories that make the game feel even more immersive.

The minimalist graphics are absolutely charming, and the calming sound design creates the perfect backdrop for a relaxing gaming experience. There’s something incredibly satisfying about meticulously organizing a room just the way you envision it, and Unpacking captures that feeling brilliantly. It’s the kind of cozy game that not only lets you unwind but also fills you with a sense of accomplishment and joy. If you’re craving a game that celebrates the simple pleasures in life and stirs up a touch of nostalgia, Unpacking is a must-play. It wraps you in its comforting embrace and leaves you with a big smile on your face!

This game was so chill and relaxing! I was sad when it ended. It's definitely not an action-packed game, relax and unpack some items. There's a cute little subplot too if you are paying attention to the level progression. This game has too few levels for $20, however. I recommend buying this game on sale to get a better value. It was only a few hours of gameplay in total.

Es un juego lleno de relajación y nostalgia, gráficos y estetica perfecta, el arte del juego es genial. Muy recomendable si te gusta pasar un rato chill ordenando y desempacando en tu nuevo hogar! 9/10

As someone who enjoys organizing things and decorating in real life, I absolutely loved Unpacking! The game takes just a few hours to complete, so I would suggest buying it when it's on sale. I hope the developers create a sequel some day, because I would gladly play that too!

한 사람의 인생을 따라가면서 그가 이사할 때마다 짐을 정리해 주는 게임입니다.
트로피도 타고, 게임도 하고, wii와 스위치가 추가되고, 새로운 취미가 생기는 것을 알 수 있습니다.
새로운 물건이 생기는 것 외에 여러 번 이사를 하면서도 버리지 않는 손때 묻은 물건들이 튀어나오기도 합니다.
재미는 있는데 플레이타임이 짧은 게 흠이네요.
용도를 알아야 제 위치를 찾아줄 텐데, 도대체 이게 뭔지 알 수 없는 아이템도 있습니다.
2004년의 보라색 물결무늬 네모난 아이템은 여기저기 두어도 제 자리를 못 찾아서 검색해서 공략 보고 해결했네요.

Super cozy game, I completely lost track of time while playing this (in a good way). The story and lore goes deeper than I expected, just wow. I wouldn't get this in full price, but I highly recommend it when it's on sale!

$20 is a huge price tag for the content available, but it's a wonderful game. If you can get it on sale, I recommend it wholeheartedly.

The game tells the story of someone's life as the years go by simply by having you unpack their belongings every time they move. The art is wonderful, the music is feel good, and it scratches the need to organize. I think it's an amazing way to tell a story and it impressively makes you feel some emotions. Not very strongly, but you experience unexpected emotions for the unseen character.

Unpacking is a game where you are unpacking, you are supposed to put things in their place after moving though you are unpacking and through the years you realise you are watching someone elses life told as a story through their belongings, it has a heartwarming ending and has some nice representation. only downside is price i would wait for it to go on sale if im being honest. Yes its a clever story line and method of storytelling though its not worth 28$AUD.  

7.5/10
This game is amazing. It's truly special going through someone's life via amazing environmental storytelling. Just get this game if you are at all interested.

"Unpacking" may not be the longest game, but its story and unique structure make it an unforgettable experience. You accompany a person through various phases of their life, experiencing their emotional highs and lows firsthand. Unpacking boxes and decorating rooms offer a calming and creative experience. I found it particularly touching when familiar items reappeared, creating a deep connection to the protagonist and making her story so relatable.

Some scenes were crafted with such care that I had to pause for a moment to appreciate them. These small, thoughtful details bring so much heart and authenticity to the game. It's this emotional resonance that makes "Unpacking" a truly special experience.

I sincerely hope that there will be new chapters or another game with a new story in the future. I would play it immediately, as "Unpacking" has captivated me with its heartfelt storytelling and artistic design. ♥

I REALLY LOVE THIS GAME. My only issue? For the $20 price tag, it's way too short. I finished this game in 4 hours, and that just felt like too much money for a game I could complete easily in that length of time.
Otherwise, this game is amazing. it's relaxing, the soundtrack is wonderful, and it's a great way to tell a story with no dialogue or characters.

Please do a free update or DLC to add more rooms or another story. It would really make it worth the money. If you can get it on sale, it's worth about $15 or less in my opinion.

i wish it went on forever lol
so much fun, and the "lore" is very wholesome and understandable. Its not too complex to where it confuses you, but has enough details that you fall in love with the story and main character :)
Super cute and definitely a game i will play over and over again.

Unpacking is a simple and satisfying point and click puzzle-ish game. I really enjoyed learning the story of the characters through their things and how you had to treat them. It was very clever! I would imagine it's hard to dislike the game due to it's simplicity, but it never promises more that it offers. It's a wonderful game that is perfect for cozy casual play.

i received a copy of this game to play on stream for stream for a cause's queer indie game showcase in June 2024, i absolutely loved playing this game, at first glance it's just a organizing game however it tells a rewarding deep and meaningful story in the background if you pay close enough attention to it, the story it tells of a woman's growth and life journey is just *Chef's kiss* i absolutely adored this game and highly recommend it

author.personaname: 我只是一隻可憐的土雞

reviews.review:
很有趣很消磨時間的遊戲
能解到主角每個時間段經歷什麼
整理狂魔覺得很棒
關卡有點少
但其實很耐玩 偶爾沒什麼事可以開來玩
背景、結尾音樂也很好聽
整個遊戲下來我最喜歡的遊戲玩偶不是豬豬
是那一組雞
每一次搬家看到小雞有增加就覺得心情很好
結尾看到女主是蕾絲邊覺得超級驚訝
總之就是一個很好玩很治癒的遊戲
所以我玩了13小時

Really nice chill game. Good to unwind after a long day, whether from work or just in general life being life. Can be finished easily in one sitting. There's a decent freedom to decorate so long as the space the item is being place makes sense. Getting the achievements is easy. All in all recommend!

I absolutely loved this game. It is cute and cozy, with the most heart-touching and wholesome story timeline. My favorite part about the game is that even though every item has its room, has its cabinet or shelf, you can still arrange it any sort of way you'd like. Additionally, even if you watch someone else play through the game or play through it yourself, it has insane replayability. Each time is like the first time, and the ending is always like a warm hug to the soul. I love playing Unpacking each night after work, having some sense of order and calm after days of unpredictability and stress.

I really love organizing and i love this game it really is so amazing, i like how u can unpack things and u can choose where things go. Most organizing games don't really give me the satisfying feeling. But this game goes above and beyond, it is for sure worth the money.

Juego de relax. El concepto como tal no da para hacerlo más largo porque si no se haría muy pesado y tedioso, pero unas tres horitas está justo. 

Es entretenido, la músiquita acompaña bien, tiene cierto storytelling, que es algo que ni me acordaba cuando lo compré. 

Lo único que no me gustó es que sólo tiene dos niveles de zoom, el que viene por defecto y un zoom-out y no lo podés regular como querés, lo que a veces hace que no puedas ver con claridad dónde ponés las cosas o qué objeto es el que estás agarrando.

Pero sacando eso, bastante realista en el sentido de "dónde está bien" poner cada cosa; lo cotidiano que se hace acomodar ítems por toda la casa se siente bien por algún motivo, es por eso que le doy un aprobado.

It is literally just unpacking and arranging.  It is a good relaxing game if you are looking for something that you don't have to think to much about.  I played for about 8 hours to discover all of the achievements.

I was able to 100% this in about 8 hours, so definitely short and sweet! It runs beautifully on the steam deck, and I really enjoyed spending a weekend playing this. We all have our own purple cups that we carry through life with us, so that really tugged at my heart strings!
Simple, Therapeutic. And a pretty lovely story unfolds.  It's wonderful to see that some items remain a constant over the years :)

Unpacking was a surprise "puzzle" game that told a beautiful story and completely caught me off guard. I wasn't expecting to get so sucked in by wanting to know what would happen to our protagonist next. This game uses its simplicity to emphasize the differences with each stage and make you think. Not merely about where things might go, but what's happening. It is very re-playable bc there are so many ways to organize the objects fit into their varying rooms.

I could play another billion of games like this. Absolutely stunning creation and phenomenal storytelling through mundane objects that we surround ourselves with as part of our lives. We see no animations, no cut scenes, hear no voices, yet we get to learn of the life of the protagonist and other people in their life so intimately close. Easily one of the newfound forever favourites <3

This game is adorable, I loved the story, the gameplay, the pixel artwork, trying to ID the DVD/Blu Ray/Gamecube/Wii game boxes by their pixel artwork while unpacking, the music, everything is great. I played the 'main story' and the 'hidden story' (start a new album and put every item on every level in the wrong place), got all achievements, and it took me less than eight hours, so its a short one and I don't think I'll be in a rush to replay it, but if there was a DLC with new levels or a sequel I would buy immediately. Pretty sure I got this on a humble bundle, it would be a rough $20 purchase, but it's clear that a lot of love has gone into this. I need an Unpacking piggy plushie.

Tried to find a relaxing game to distract myself from the fact, that i needed to organize my house.
Ended up feeling dread, because i didn't now where to put my pixelated art stuff.

Nice game, very realistic unpacking experience, but i definetely chose poorly.

Backlog Status: Completed

The game has a very unique premise, and fully leans-in to the idea that the entire gameplay loop is opening boxes and re-arranging items in the house(s). I haven't see anything quite like it, and is worth checking out.

The pixel art is also striking. With each item having multiple orientations, the belongings truly feel like they fit where placed. Overall, it's a sentimental journey that doesn't ask a lot of time from the player, yet delivers a premium experience with nothing quite like it.

The attention to detail and storytelling is astounding. Especially seeing the foreshadowing and little details you missed on further playthroughs. 

A lot more puzzly and replayable than I was expecting which was nice. There are some tricky items and there's lots of ways to unpack. 

Absolutely worth it. I just wish it was longer.

Fun but incredibly short. I completed it in 3 hours and even that was with breaks and away doing other things. Rather disappointed it just seemed to stop and seems quite expensive for such a short play time.
I did enjoy it so I would recommend in that sense but I really don't think it's good value for money at all

I would definitely recommend this :>

I like how there is more to the game than just unpacking and organizing things. Every level in the game feels intimate because almost everything has a sentimental value, like with how MC's items or hobbies clings to her like drawing materials and games from childhood even until she met her significant other. I really love the small details that they have added. It makes you look back and contemplate that some things has gone out of age, some stay, some are added. 

Personally, this game would be for you if you like cozy games, wholesome, relaxed-state of environment, and something to have a break from all the stress that is happening. 

Music-wise, it is okay but the calm after the bgm tho is the best. But that's just me HAHAHA

I guess it would have been great if there are more people introduced to unpack things not just our MC. Like maybe in each album available are different stories of different people. It's a nice game/platform to showcase more personal experiences. 

But other than that 4/5. Thank you devs for the experience!

Super cute game with an adorable story told throughout the chapters :)

I appreciate the fact I can mess around with the organisation as much as I like lmao

Unpacking reminds me a lot of those old games where you had to decorate an entire house to your liking. It is way more limited than those, and sometimes it can be quite frustrating when you place an object in another room or in a spot and the game disagrees with you and forces you to put it somewhere else. All in all, the story is interesting and you can see what the MC is going through by the entries in her album. It's a unique experience to get to know a character just by analyzing their belongings.
BUT, this game is NOT worth buying at full price. I believed that each of those 3 albums at the beginning tells a different story, but no, it's just the cover that's different in the actual gameplay, when you place the album around the house. Also, it is quite pricey for less than 5h of active gameplay. I left it open in the taskbar a lot while doing other things on my computer, but the game is shorter than that. 

TLDR: cute, cozy game, but worth buying only if on sale

Took my favorite part of the Sims and made it its own game. Absolutely love, the graphics, the aesthetic, the decorating, etc. I just wish it was longer. I played it all in one night :( and I know I could go on for hours. Maybe if we could create our own houses or choose which ones to decorate apart from the story mode?

An absolutely gorgeous, cozy, insanely well made game with an emotional story. The graphics are adorable and I can spend hours on this game. It's very short, so I'd recommend waiting until it's on sale. One of m favorite things in this game is organizing the books and discs! Anyways pls get this game it will change your life
This game is so freaking chill. I love it. Its great for relaxing. The art is super cute, too. I hope there's more content in the future, or a sequel, or whatever, just give me more! 😅

You don't put toasters on top of the fridge ffs.

I'd also say to wait for a sale. $20 is a bit too much for a puzzle gane imo.

Neat puzzle game otherwise though, but damn is the final level long af.
I've played through this like 3 times on different platforms, and every time is a joy to experience. Such a lovely little relaxing game with a narrative that is extremely touching. Such a joy.

A fairly short, relaxing game about unpacking and putting items in a proper place as the unnamed protagonist moves into various homes throughout her life. It has cute pixel graphics and a chill background music. An enjoyable experience that doesn't overstay its welcome. Get it when it's on sale.

I enjoyed this game it was very relaxing and cute, though I rushed through it a little. I wish there was a bit more content like another story to see the perspective of. Still i'm glad I played it but i do wish i had waited for it to go on sale, sense 20 dollars is a lot considering how short the game is.

One of the most endearing and heartwarming games EVER. Amazing and wholesome story, and the fact, that the game about unpacking somehow tells you a very heartwarming story, is very impressive.  IMO this IS worth the 20$ pricetag.

Unpacking is a relaxing game where you unpack your stuff and... that's about it.
it starts when you're a child, getting your first room. as your character grows up, they move to new places which means more to unpack.

why i recommend this game: it's very relaxing and easy to play over and over again. i own this game on my switch as well, but playing it again i'm not even bored!

if you like cozy games, this might be the one for you.

All the fun of organizing without the stress of packing. My only criticism is the level where you share a space with others and you cannot move their things: realistic, but an absolute nightmare and zero fun to play for an organizational freak like me.

I got this game for free and wasn't expecting much, but in the end I found myself playing it again. At face value this game is just unpacking boxes and organizing them in a home. It's almost like a puzzle in where you place items and sometimes you can't place items in certain areas. However, on a deeper level this is a journey through someone's life. The entire story is told through simply unpacking, but you travel with them from childhood until they start a family of their own. It's a very cute and cozy game. The only thing I can't stand in this game is the Ex-boyfriends house, but I think most of us who have played all agree on that.
Very delightful! Lovely story, lovely music, lovely art style~ I would recommend everyone to play this game! (especially people who have moved homes at least twice in their lifetime)

Unpacking is a good game. You get boxes with lots of items inside them. Your goal is to place all the items in the rooms. Some items can't be placed in a specific room, while other items only fit in a single spot in a room.
The game is very cozy. You unpack a lot of everyday items: toothbrush, coffee mug, headphones, cell phone, clothes and many more. As you progress in the game you start with a teenager room and you don't have a lot of stuff. As you play more – you have more rooms, and more items as you "age" and become a dad (or a mom) yourself.
 The art is descent and while you unpack, or finished a level – you a have a cool camera that allows you to add stickers, play with the lights and adjust different frames. Yet, the game is very very shot – it has only 6 or 7 levels. So for the cost of the game which is more than 10$ I expected a lot more. In a scale of 1 to 10 this game gets 7.

Unpacking offers a relaxing puzzle experience that allows for personal room designs. The game follows a woman's life moving into many different houses, and while the story is cute, I would've preferred other buildings besides home/apartments with other people, as most items you organize are the same between all areas. Regardless of repeating objects, the puzzle allows you to place anything, almost anywhere, with some interactable objects and creative achievements to explore. Overall, I'd recommend the game as the puzzles, for the most part, are satisfying to sort through, but I found some areas in many of the levels repetitive and boring.

Jeu cosy, avec des graphismes et musiques excellent pour ce type de jeu détente. Tous les décors sont vraiment jolis. Gameplay simple et satisfaisant, j'apprécie de découvrir la vie du personnage au fur à mesure qu'on déballe ses cartons. Durée de vie très courte (4-5h pour avoir tous les succès).

This is a very fun cosy game that uses a simple mechanic to indulge in really solid story telling about a girl in various points of her life. I really enjoyed the game and was moved by how the little things in the game can be so impactful to its story telling. The music is light and fits the game and its premise, the sound design gives the game its sense of touch and helps you feel like you are actually moving the things around in your home.

The game also has a lot of replay value, as in my first play through I could not 100% the game and also missed things that I look forward in my future play through's. 

Solid Game 8.5/10 - Would recommend.

es juego muy fácil, relajante y divertido, lo recomiendo a todo el mundo, no hay edad definida para jugarlo XD.... echo de menos actualizaciones,DLC y más cosas para no tener que repetir siempre lo mismo. Un saludo a todos.

It took me by complete surprise how compelling the environmental storytelling in this game is. Not only do you get to play a lovely relaxing cozy game, you get to go along on a journey with a young girl growing up into a fully actualised woman.

I loved this game at first it's relaxing just fun to do something and as every game at the ens after playing for a while it starts to be borning but i really like this game i am done with everything i got all the stickers and cards it took a while but at the end i got everything really fun game and relaxing at a point when you are bored really recommend
Incrivelmente relaxante! A história contada através das mudanças foi cativante o suficiente pra me fazer chorar no final. Definitivamente um dos meus jogos favoritos!!

I love how this game tells a story through unpacking. It's so wholesome and soothing to play. I absolutely love the sound design and pixel art design as well. This game is aesthetically pleasing. Definitely recommend.
Stunning amount of details, great for people who love interacting and sorting! Adorable story line! Love this game so much and wish there were more like this out there <3

It's a cute little indie game where you follow a character through various stages of their life, unpacking goods as they move from one location to the next. The gameplay is just unpacking and organising things, and the story is told almost entirely through the environment. It's very straight forward.

Bearing in mind though, there isn't a lot to it and it isn't very long, so I'd say pick it up on a sale. Good game.

Like Firewatch, the game is insanely short, has a boring ending, and should only be bought on sale. However, Firewatch has engaging plot and characters, this game has neither. While advertised and spread as a relaxing zen puzzle game, I was instead more infuriated and confused by the amount of junk the protagonist likes to carry around. If there were more levels in the game I would've considered money well spent, and I would've given the thumbs up on recommendation. If there was a feature for custom rooms and puzzles on the good ol' Steam workshop it def would've made a good investment.

Anyways, use those 3 hours to clean up your own house instead.
This game is worth every penny. There really needs to be more games like this! Satisfying and does a great job of telling the story without distracting you from the game play.

Es un juego realmente cozy y relajante. Me he ido creando teorías a medida que avanzaba y me iba fijando en los elementos que la protagonista mantenía y en que detalles nos indicaban en qué momento de su vida se encontraba y su relación con otras personas. El final me ha encantado, he llorado y todo, siento que la gente que se muda/ha mudado muy a menudo puede encontrarse identificado/a con este juego.

I played this game twice, and both times I absolutely loved it. I love how clever the storytelling is. I love how cozy and beautiful it is. Above all, I love how powerful of a story it tells without saying a word. Amazing game overall, and one of my favorite ever indie games.

Easy to understand and play. Very satisfying to organize and place items. I absolutely love the unspoken story of time passing and moving from place to place. I replay this when I need to relax and unwind.

so relaxing and lots of game to play but i was still oh so sad when the game had to end
very cute subtle story, very pretty arts, and sweet tunes
also silly achievements
live laugh love this game for realsies
(pls make a sequel/DLC)

It's such a cute and relaxing game! You get to pack and unpack without the stress of having boxes all around you. <3 The subtle inclusion of a story for a game like this was also unexpected but very pleasant.

I indeed like this game! Although, it can be chill and relaxing. Sometimes it's more, just... Work. Honestly, it's a fun game! Something that disturbs me is a lot of times the rooms are packed and crowded, before you even start unpacking. It would be a nice game to listen to some chill songs too. It takes a lot of work to complete some levels. I would much rather it tell you what items are, sometimes I can't tell what an item is! Or don't know. It is cute and cozy, if you listen to some chill songs with headphones on, in a cozy and cute environment <3 The house designs are to my liking. There's a thin line between recommended and not recommended. Consider buying this game when it's on sale. I don't think I would buy for full price! With all due respect to the chill game and the cool mechanics! I would recommend this for sure!

I am in love with this game. Some people complain it's not enough content to justify the price, and I may agree to some extent, but I just love this game and it's mechanics. It relaxes me like no other game I've played before. When I'm stressed I just turn on a podcast and play this. I really do wish there was more content or an extra DLC for purchase, but oh well. I still really enjoy this game and do reccommend it to people!

I have played this game so many times just because it is such a comfort game for me. I reaaaaaally wish there was news about a sequel - I need new rooms and a new storyline! But I definitely recommend this game to anyone with anxiety. <3

Schönes Spiel für zwischendurch. Das Auspacken der Dinge erzählt tatsächlich eine schöne Lebensgeschichte.

Es ist ein Point and Click-Spiel. Etwas nervig bei manchem Wohnungen ist, dass man sich um Gegenstände richtig zuzuordnen teilweise durch mehrere Räume clicken muss. Hilfreich dabei ist aber der jeweilige Grundriss, über den man schneller zwischen den Räumen wechseln kann.

Story rich, relaxing, fun. Very cute and scratches that weirdly specific itch for slow games.

So much beef with the ex. Where the hell are my Doc Martens you ass wipe?!

The one thing I will say: I have finished the game already and honestly I think I wouldn't be happy with it if I paid full price for it. Definitely a game you should get on sale due to it's length.

my first perfect game on steam. i go bananas for a good relaxing, casual play... and this storyline had me hooked. the dedication left me in tears. any and all little guys in the world should experience this when they have the time!!

Beautiful lil game but waaaaaaaaaaay too short! I came into this thinking I could just unpack lots of different rooms to my heart's content, so was a bit disappointed that there was only one storyline to go through. Felt there was definitely scope to include a few more, since on its own the game only makes up just around 4 hours of content. Of course you can just unpack the same rooms over and over in different ways, but that gets a bit repetitive. On the fence, would still recommend but only if you purchase it on sale.

i finished the game quite quickly but LOVED it. it was fun noticing small details and seeing how the plot developed without even requiring dialogue or defined characters. was definitely worth the price, cant wait to see what theyll do next
挺好玩的吧。收纳爱好者。适合平静心情打发时间。画风也不错。能不能出DLC，还想玩新的

Very touching game and different from its genre, I enjoyed getting to know the characters through the objects they own, their writings, their tastes and their many trips. When you move, what you bring with you intimately reflects a part of you and Unpacking allows us to search the characters' belongings without scruples 
(but not in a weird way lol). The only negative thing to say about this game is that it's too short. I want more! I have recommended this game to many friends.
好丸，爱丸，虽然现实里不怎么收拾东西，但这种整理向的游戏一直都很喜欢，而且画风音乐也很不错，内涵故事剧情也是表达得即含蓄又开放，印象深刻的一点是有个照片贴墙上一直会有个人的脸被挡住，换了各种方式找了各种地方都不行，最后放到柜子里感受到了一些不明所以的感情

I love this game! The art is cute, it's easy to understand. The story is all there without a single word every being said, and it's just really fun to replay. It's really soothing to unpack and organize all the things. I hope they make a second! <3

Very unique story telling, the game-play is exactly what it looks like and it get's boring pretty quickly, yet moving on to a new room is always fun and the game is really short.

這款遊戲透過獨特的敘事方式，使用搬家物品的擺設來逐步揭露主角的各種生活階段，從幼年到步入婚姻殿堂的過程被巧妙地包裹在簡單的動作中。每次搬家不僅是物理上的移動，更是時間的流逝和生活階段的轉變。玩家在每一個關卡中，都能看到女主角從少年到成年的成長歷程，這不僅是遊戲的樂趣，更像是在閱讀一部詳盡的人生傳記。

然而，遊戲的敘事技巧並不完美。隱晦的敘事方式雖然新穎，卻沒有給玩家留下深刻的情感體驗，加之系統的強制限制，如書包不可放在地上，遊戲機必須放在特定櫃子等，這些限制經常打斷了遊戲的流暢性和沉浸感。這種強制性的物品擺放，有時候讓人感到煩擾，因為缺乏指導，玩家只能在不停的嘗試中尋找正確的位置。

遊戲中的低潮反映了現實生活的苦澀面，如女主角的愛好和成就被新男友輕視的情節，這深刻描繪了很多人在感情中被忽略或輕視的痛苦。但最終，女主角找到了真正的幸福，與一位懂得欣賞她的人共同生活，這個結局不僅令人感動，也讓人反思真正的愛情應包含尊重和理解。

儘管遊戲流程被評為過短，若能增加自訂模式，讓玩家自由設計房間和擺設，或許能大大提升遊戲的互動性和樂趣。這種改進將使玩家不僅是遊戲的參與者，更是創作者，能在遊戲中分享和體驗他人的故事。

這款遊戲的美術表現出色，儘管偶爾背景音樂的消失可能會打斷玩家的沉浸感，但整體來說，這是一款充滿深度的休閒遊戲，適合家庭一同享受，讓玩家在回憶中找到共鳴，從中發現生活的真諦。

Clever, simple and relatable, Unpacking takes an ordinary experience and turns it into the kind of zen task that creates satisfaction in the act of doing. But more so, while Unpacking isn't a brain-wracking puzzle with absurd levels of complexity, it does very thoughtfully use its game mechanics as the primary mechanism for storytelling -- it's clever certainly, but also a very innovative way to approach a story. Subtle things, like how objects persist and wear over moves, or how old things are replaced with newer ones, or how it feels different claiming a solitary space, versus trying to fit in with others, or trying to make space for someone else -- there's a really powerful emotive quality to this title that can't help but charm.

If you're looking for something relaxing and well curated that doesn't overstay its welcome, a novel take on videogame storytelling, or if you'd just like to play something that isn't overly demanding, this title is absolutely worth your time.

把人生阶段比作关卡的话，房间可能就是最小的地图。在游戏的地图里戳来戳去，像阅读一样浏览着主角的生活，不同的时间和空间给环境带来完全不同氛围，但在变化中却一直能看到很多很多主角在坚持的自我。有些爱好没有了，有新的爱好出现的，有的兴趣变成了工作，新的作品发表了，在感情上碰壁了，创作取得认可了，遇见崭新的人了，去到喜欢的地方了，走了许久，回到房间，小时候的那束光又穿过时间洒在了同样的玩偶上。

可能是刚好站在人生节点上去玩这款游戏，感悟来得更加直接。一遍遍猜测着主角的生活，又有些沮丧，因为意识到并没有这样的机会去整理与回顾自己。你只能通过模糊的回忆，湿漉漉的文字，每一个时间切片下的定格，来勾连起每个时空下的自己。
很解压的游戏，焦虑的时候上来玩一下能让自己平静下来，但是价格有点贵，建议打折的时候入手，我没有很细致的玩大概用了3.6个小时，如果原价买的话会觉得有点不值。
