If there was a way to add rooms, seasons, anything, it would make this game worth every penny. If you can get it on sale - go for it! I would not purchase it at full price, though.

A meditative game that provides a quiet story. I think it can make you a bit sad or nostalgic or excited, depending on where you are in life, or where you've ended up. A really great idea. 

Moving is actually considered one the most stressful events in a life, up there with divorce and death(!), so I think it's amazing that this game came about. I think a big reason these events are considered 'stressful,' amongst so many reasons, is because they always herald great change, and change (good or bad) is scary. 

It is significant to rearrange your worldly possessions for a new life stage, &  even though the circumstances of the move can vary greatly, it does always indicate both a beginning and an end. It can be a time to gauge how far we've come or whether we've maybe taken two steps back. I think that significance can sometimes get lost in the logistics of moving - the costs, the packing, the moving loads of furniture and boxes from one place to another, and then the reorganisation. It's exhausting and mindfulness isn't exactly at the top of the list of things to do. Unpacking shows that, actually, it is the perfect time for mindfulness. The perfect time for self-reflection and planning for the path ahead.

It's a nice game.
This was the most wholesome game I've ever played. 100% Recommend. The only bad thing was how short the game was. But overall it was one of the best games I've played this year.

I agree the game isn't very long and there are some items where it's difficult to figure out what they are/where they go. However, the game is captivating, beautiful, and an absolute delight to play. I started a second play-through almost immediately after the first one (my first play-through was during a storm-induced wifi-outage so ignore the hours played) and any frustrations I had before aren't here now. It really is a delightful story to experience and I cannot recommend it enough for that alone.

This game was amazing i love the concept of it and everything but i feel like this game would be better if u guys started t add new lifes to unpack i completed this game pretty fast and was disappointed at the end to find out i only got to do the one life i will keep this game on my pc for now hoping that new stuff gets added soon cause the game was absolutely amazing stunning but pleaseeeeeeeeeeee add another life to the game this time as a male please please please i will love to continue another unpacking adventure :)
Super cute game!! Very simple and relaxing... Lots of fun hidden achievements and the subtle story telling is amazing!! Only thing to mention is that the game can be completed fairly quickly.
This game is super cute and satisfying you get to see your character grow as a person but its a very short game for the money paid I was under the impression that there would be more to it

Too little content for too much money, and the story doesn't pull through enough to even provide some padding for the price. In addition, not too cozy, as if you do not unpack the items in the very specific places the devs want you to (even if it's a weird place for that item), you can't proceed with the story. At that point it's kind of a lazy, railroaded version of what I wanted it to be.

I havent played for to long, but i do think that this is a game worth buying if you need help to deal with stress and/or you need help training your attention span. At least for me it helps when i need to think of somthing other then real life.
Plus its just a relatable and touching story that the overall game tells.

Ein wunderschönes minimalistisches Spiel zum entspannen und für zwischendurch. Die Pixelgrafik ist sehr schön gemacht und die Eastereggs sind echt lustig. Die Referenzen haben einen schönen Charm.

Das Game ist zwar kurz aber es ist liebevoll gestaltet und gut umgesetzt kann ich nur empfehlen für diejenigen die auf Pixelgames stehen.

Unpacking is a very simple, yet very enjoyable game! I've played it through a couple times, and it helps de-stress after a long day.
I would greatly recommend it to anyone who has OCD or likes to make everything neat. The game gives you so many options of how you would like to organise things, and lets you create your perfect neat space. 

The little easter eggs and achievements are also quite fun :D
it's a very calming game and you can place things in many different places. I use this game to relax and I just enjoy the graphics a lot
Great example of how impactful stories can be told through gameplay rather than cutscenes or heavy-handed exposition. Recommend.
I absolutely loved this game however am disappointed it's not longer!  I hope that in the future there will be more stories and different moves.

When ever I have stressful day or just need to do something to ease my mind, this is the first game that comes to mind, the story is lovely, the art style is amazing and unpacking everything and putting them away, just feels so so soooo nice.
放松休闲，剧情温馨，收纳爱好者不可错过~不过关卡太少，相对来说价格偏高

The game makes me excited for life. You should play this game.

And, if you do, there is a picture after the credits that anyone invested in the game would want to wait for.

游戏是好游戏，全程玩的很开心，但内容太少，4小时就能通关，ed出来只觉得“这就没了？”。总共没几张图，一个关卡做起来应该不难啊，希望后面能出dlc。
50入手有点亏，不差钱的可以考虑。

I forgot to play this game when it came out, but finally sitting down to it, it was really fun! I thought it would go on a little longer, I was a little sad when it ended as I got so absorbed in it. The gameplay is simple but effective, following a person as they move to various houses throughout their life. The little things like some items carrying forwards, and the small items you can interact with, made it a very charming experience. The format of a game worked really well for the storytelling, and the actual process of sorting things made everything very relaxing and satisfying, as the only criteria is to put things away vaguely logically, otherwise there is little guidance and you can be creative with it. Glad I finally played this indie title, I always appreciate seeing new ideas tried out through a video game format. 8/10 calming and satisfying game :)

I was not expecting the CONFIRMED LBGT representation in this. This is so good! 
A fun little game that is very zen and comfy to play. I beat it in 3 hours the first run through. 
I definitely recommend it to enjoy a little relaxing gameplay time without any stress of any kind. 
Almost everything could go and do what I wanted it to. 

My only real complaints were things like why can't I hang up the ukulele when there's a hanging guitar? And some things that can't stack but seem like they should. It's minor. The game is fun in many ways and one of the best things is noticing the details that tell the story as you go through the various stages.

I do wish it was longer for the price paid even on sale. I was very surprised that the last level was the last level.
That said I didn't get 100% of the stickers, so I still have a little replay value left. 

Definitely completely recommend it tho! Very fun. Very zen. Very cute and gay!
I didn't realize this game only had 3hrs of play time. It's a cute game and fun to play, but definitely not worth paying $20 for only 3hrs.

Such a cute game! You can go through the levels pretty fast but I would definitely replay it when I want something non-stressful to play. The story line is easy to follow even though there's no narration/direct story telling. Would recommend to buy when there's a sale.

Very enjoyable but still monstrously overpriced.  I got this at 30% off and it was still a lot for ~3 hours of play.
But to the game's credit it does environmental storytelling very well.  And there's a nice escalation in the amount of friction there is in each scene to get everything placed.  And there's an extra-special type of joy in watching a replay at high speed of your unpacking and tidying.
Es un juego hermoso, muy tranquilo, fácil y entretenido. Lo único malo es que es muy corto. Me gustarían más escenarios, porque lo terminé muy rápido. Recomiendo mucho.

I sat down to play Unpacking, and ended up spending my entire afternoon finishing it. I adore the choice of pixel art style, and the attention to detail was amazing! The subtle story-telling through moving and unpacking someone's life throughout the years really made my playthrough emotional, and I loved learning about the nameless character we play as. Thank you for a wonderful game.

This game may be short, but it is worth every minute spent playing it. It is very relaxing and calming, and I experienced unexpected emotions while playing it. It's not just unpacking boxes, it's unpacking a life.

First of all, the game was really nice and relaxing and it seemed like a great game to pass some time with. And it was! I really enjoyed that you could decide whether you wanted everything 100% perfectly in place or mess around with some items in their respective places. Apart from that it really felt like I was looking at someone going through the phases of their life, based on the stuff that moved with you to the next house/room. This was really well done! The downside is the walkthrough time: Although I must admit I did not check the length of the game beforehand, I expected it to be a little longer. I usually want to spend 1 hour per euro spent on a game and with this game that would mean to play it through 5 times in total. I just would have liked for the game to be a little longer.
It's a brilliant game, beautiful story, and very relaxing to play. gives a lot of variety for where you can put things, and all in all, epic game

genuinely my comfort game. i started sobbing at the end of the story, it was such a sweet ending and it really helped distract me through some tough times. emotions aside, the gameplay is amazing! the music, the graphics, i love this game so much.

It's very a sweet and relaxing game with a pretty interesting story told entirely through the unpacking of various levels. It's a pretty short game so I would recommend getting it while it's on sale because it can be a little pricey for the amount of content you get in the game. Additionally the puzzle aspect can be a little weird? sometimes. It's a bit hard to tell what some of the items they want you to place are and there were a few times I wasn't sure of where they wanted me to put certain stuff like not being able to put deodorant in a bathroom drawer. Other than that it's a very calming  and pleasant experience.

Unpacking ist ein wirklich schönes und entspannendes Spiel. Es macht unheimlich viel Spaß alles auszupacken und für jeden Gegenstand einen Platz zu finden. Schade finde ich, dass es Gegenstände gibt die an machen Stellen nicht liegen dürfen. Dadurch ist man ein wenig eingeschränkt. 

Was ein ganz großer Minuspunkt ist, ist das Preis-Leistungsverhältnis. 4 Stunden Spielzeit, dann war ich durch und dafür sind 20 Euro definitiv zu teuer. Schön wäre es gewesen mehr Wohnungen einzurichten mit unterschiedlichen Gegenständen. Denke ein paar mehr "Level" oder in dem Fall könnte man verschiedene Fotoalben machen wäre sicher möglich und würde den Preis rechtfertigen.

My favorite part is how much story can come out of the atmosphere and setting of this game. As well as the customizability! :) The little achievements or hidden secrets are cutesy! I got quite a bit of them by just playing around and doing goofy stuff! Highly Recommend as a game to just relax with and play!
This game is so relaxing and have surpirsingly good story that I actually tear up a bit. Everytime I have a really bad day I'll come back and replay this game over and over.

Unpacking was very fun and cute, for the ONE STORY it contains. It was 6 or so levels following one person's life from living space to living space, great story telling through environment alone. That being said, this game does NOT contain enough content for the price. Very low replay value.

Honestly really cute and relaxing, but I finished it in about 5 hrs and was really disappointed, especially after spending over $20. If you're looking for a chill organizing type game, it's probably worth it to look for something else that would give you more gameplay for the same price or less.
This game is sooo goood! I love it but the gameplay is really short, sure you can do some challenges but it ha so little levels. I do love playing it but it should have more levels!
this game is adorable and has lots of little hidden messages, i wish it was longer but it also wraps everything up so beautifully i wouldn't change a thing

Having to move and unpack stuff in real life? Awful.
Getting to listen to chill chiptunes and organize a room from an isometric POV? Heckin' pleasant.
The thing that makes moving so stressful in real-life is that you're racing against a time limit. And that can be made even worse if you're a perfectionist as well. Unpacking takes away the worst parts of all that and makes it a pleasant experience.

While it may seem like a rather tame, hum-drum concept in a gaming world filled with strobe lights and loud music, this game is great for people who appreciate good organization, enjoy feng shui planning, or if they are an overall Type-A person. 

There is no time limit and the game mechanics are intuitive. The only learning curve that I had trouble with was trying to figure out what some of the objects were as you unboxed them. So it was a small victory when I realized that the purple, fuzzy thing (that I thought was an oven mitt for more than half of the game) was actually a hot water compress. I'm chuckling as I write this. I recommend this for anyone that just wants to unwind or take a short break.

My only qualm is that the full price for the game a is a bit high for how short it is. But also, the developers worked hard on the game and deserve nice things too. I'm sure you spent more on that custom-made gamepad cozy you got off Etsy. Joking aside, I'd definitely play Unpacking 2 if that happens.
Thought this game was a little pricey for what it offered, but it's very high quality and very enjoyable. The sound design is great, and I think the stickers/achievements you get are very cute.

Ce jeu m'a permis de me détendre et de me concentrer sur autre chose. Je ni joue rarement que très longtemps car cela me fatigue un peu de ranger, mais cela fait toujours du bien de remettre de l'ordre. J'aime aussi l'histoire que nous suivons au cours des déménagements. Je vous le recommande.

So I just finished playing the game. I beat it in about 5 hours would have finished it a bit sooner if it hadn't been for getting caught up on one level due to my sheer stubborness.

Let's get the one and only negative I have about the game out of the way... Simply due to the length of the game I would say that you should not buy this game at it's full price. I know the devs probably put a TON of work into this game, but the length makes it so that, when compared to other games with just as good of a story with similar price points, I can't recommend this game at the $20 price point. If you can I'd say grab it at a sale for about $15. For some that might still be stretching it but I'd say that had I spent $15 on this game I would have personally felt happy with it. I did get the game for less than that on Humble during a sale, but $15 would have been good with me.

Now getting those only two negatives (price and length) out of the way let's move on the part where I compliment the game non-stop.

First and foremost let's talk story. This game... has an amazing little story. Is it complex? Yes and no. The game takes on telling it's story in an incredibly unique way. Almost strictly through objects and moving boxes. There is a sparse amount of dialogue seen only when you take a picture of a room at the end of a level and see what our MC writes in her album under it (tip: you can back out of the album and take a pic of each room before moving on to get the dialogue for each room). Everything else in the game is just told through this womans possessions. 

By placing some of the same objects over and over... and sometimes when you notice an item missing. Like when I placed her cookie jar for the last time and the next level it was no longer there. Implying that this cookie jar that had been with her for so long had finally broken. You can gather the current state of her life based on the condition of some objects, such as her Bard mini and the stuffed pig. Then sometimes it's the placement of items... based on the items around the place she is currently living... or when the game forces you to place something a certain place. The reason I could have finished the game sooner was in the level when she moves in with a boyfriend and I was looking for a place to put a certain object (no spoilers) and I realized... there was only two places I could put it. I put it in one of the two places.... knowing full well that the game would make me choose the one I really didn't want to pick. Sure enough the level ended and I spent a solid additional 20 minutes REFUSING to continue as I desperately looked for ANYWHERE else I could put it. The same thing occurred in that level with a few other objects, that I was thankfully successful in finding far more suitable places for (by my standards) though not ideal. That one object though. I was so angry that I was just saying "No no no no no" to the screen enough that my kid was like "Mama? Why are you saying no?"

The placement of things can mean a lot in this game if you can pick up on the subtle stuff being told here. Though even the stuff that isn't subtle just kinda adds up to an overall story of this womans life. Again. You place some of the same items over and over again to the point that you become very aware of when suddenly one isn't there or when it's condition changes.

You see the things she's forced to give up and the things she fights for.

You'll also notice when suddenly you are placing an item over and over that you weren't before. Like when I realized I had placed heating patches, a cane, and meds several times and I'm like "Oh! She has back problems now. I wonder if it's from being hunched over a desk a lot?"

It is a wordless and really amazing way to tell a story. There was never a moment when I didn't realize what was going on in this womans life because her stuff made it so plain to understand. If you're the kind of person who doesn't get attached to objects and place meaning on them than this game might not be for you. If you are though... you'll enjoy this game.

That damn pig man... I had a stuffed animal I was attached to as a kid that went missing when I was like 13 and I was distraught over it. I never got it back, but I did have another plush that I eventually got that has gone with me on every move I've ever made and always will. My son has a stuffed boa constrictor that goes to bed with him every night. So I get it and when anything happened with that stuffed pig it was a pang in the heart.

This game made me cry.... TWICE. Once during actual game play and once during the credits. Kudos to whoever wrote that ending song it put a sad smile on my face and I loved it.

So now that I'm done talking about how amazing the story telling is in this game. What about gameplay?

I think I covered it pretty well on accident while discussing the story, but if you didn't catch it. The game play is very simple. Unpack the boxes and put stuff away. You follow our MC to different locations in her life and you open boxes and find places for her things. You can *generally* place anything anywhere. With exceptions being that a toothbrush goes in the bathroom, a coffee grinder goes in the kitchen, etc. As well as when the placement of something is impactful to the story and must go a specific place at which point you must figure out where it goes. It's a very zen and chill "puzzle" game. Though the puzzles aren't really puzzles for me. I very easily knew where everything should go. There were only a few items that tripped me up mostly because I couldn't identify WHAT they were supposed to be. Such as a pair of brown headphones that I assumed were able to go just about anywhere. Then I realized they must be sound reducing or sleep headphones because the only place where the game didn't tell me to move it was when I put them by the bed.

And by telling you to move something I mean an item will have a red outline around it to let you know "Hey, move this thing". It's nothing intrusive to the game play.

Last thing I'll talk about the art. I adore it. It's some really well done pixel art and I loved the designs of almost everything. The only time I didn't was, again, when there were things I couldn't identify. One of my favorite things though is the covers of books, games, and dvds. I couldn't peg everything but I noticed some things and it put a smile on my face. Like I'm not 100% sure but I'm pretty sure I that two of the games she has are Animal Crossing and Pheonix Wright. In the blue rays I spotted Jaws and a few other movies. My favorite though, and I might be wrong, is I'm pretty sure that for much of the game she brings the entire Eragon series around with her. Again, might be wrong, but there was a set of book she almost always has that just look like the Eragon series to me. I LOVE stuff like that. It made it fun to sit there and look at the covers of things for a second. Even if it wasn't a identifable series or anything and put stuff together. Like if it was clearly an artbook I'd make sure they all went together.

I treated unpacking her house the way I would mine.

To wrap up.

Unpacking is a short and sweet and wonderful experience for those who want to chill and are able to read into subtle story telling. If you tend to see things at face value than you may not get as much out of the story as I did. If you go by the $1 per hour rule on game prices this game DEFINITELY isn't for you because this game comes out to way more than that. I again recommend pick it up when it's around $15 (though even then it doesn't hit the $1 per hour of entertainment unless you plan on playing the game through multiple times).

Short but charming game. Bit of a missed opportunity that they don't have plans of adding additional content though, especially considering the price and lack of replayability. I'd recommend if on sale

So much fun, loved every second. I wish it was longer or had more options to play, I blew through the whole game within a day of downloading. And, while you get a lot of freedom in where you place items, know that there are a few things that have to be put in a certain place.

A delight to play. Such a nice calming casual game. I played two ways through and am on my third run. The aesthetic just puts me in a relaxed mood. I also enjoy unpacking the boxes, storing the items away, and find it satisfying. Trying to get all the stickers and almost got them.
Very cute little game that gives you the story of someone's life by hints based on the things they own. Great for anyone who likes games where you have to organise things.

Adorable game but a little disappointing. The story is cute, but the gameplay is amazing. It's very calming and kept me hooked. Apparently the devs are super committed to not releasing any additional content. Got through the game in a day and a half of casual playing and loved it but truthfully, if I hadn't gotten it on sale I would've been way more let down by the incredibly short story. I don't understand not making any extra levels and find it a little frustrating. It's SUCH a good game, it's gorgeous, I don't really even care if it has another deep/compelling story, I don't think it's enough game to warrant the price. I play mostly smaller games, I'm no stranger to shorter games. But this was exceptionally disappointing.

hmm.  I'm sorta on the fence with this game.
I kinda enjoyed it?  It's relaxing and I guess I had fun getting the stickers.
I suppose what I find very disappointing is the fact that you only get one story.  Once you play through, you are pretty much done and all the additional journals have no purpose.  They aren't a different story.  For the price tag, there should have been a different story for each journal so you could get some replay action out of it.  
As it stands, it's not a good deal and overpriced.  Absolutely wait for a sale before buying this game.
It's very very cute, really good idea but very short for $20. Rather wait til its 5 or 10, but not worth the $20.

I consider this game to be rather masterclass in telling a story without a single word uttered by any of the characters.  Most of it can be inferred through the gameplay.  By slowly taking out things one by one from the boxes, you understand the character that you're playing as, and the struggles they go through.  It's not a particularly long game, but I find myself going back every now and again just to fix another room and find a new place to organize.

Interestingly, I find that this game also tells you how you organize things when you're unpacking.  Like do you keep all the DVDs together or do you stash them anywhere where you can find room?  How do you take out the clothes before you unpack all the hangers?  And where do you put the plushies!!!!

Its an amazing game there isn't much repeatability but the story aspect of a game where you unpack boxes is insanely cool good game and after a year of not playing gonna play through it again :) also trying to unlock the achievements is fun

BGM和画风都很不错，从每个关卡的房间和物件变化，能看出“我”的人生轨迹，有伴随我一路成长的物件，也有被丢弃了的。
理论上来说这是一款解压游戏，但有些关卡你真的搞不懂那个物品要放去哪里的时候就变成了增压小游戏了。
关卡答案不唯一，强迫症和非强迫症都能找到自己喜欢的摆法，放错位置了也不用怕，说不定有意外惊喜哦。

I base all the games I play if it was worth the price, how many hours it takes for me to beat a game or how many hours I sink into the the game after the fact. I beat the game in less than 4 hours, even getting all the achievements in the process. I still very much enjoy this game, as you can tell by my current 16 hours. I like playing this calming game when I am zoning out a bit on the phone, when my child is needy but wants to watch me play, or just when I wanna play a game and can't decide. It is very calming, a cute little story and a nice polished look to it for what it is. I am inclined to agree with everyone saying the game is too short, because it is. Or if they added other stories, that would be great too.  With how much I enjoy the game, I would love to see more added to it (for free bc of the $20 I paid for it) and to decorate more living spaces! I am usually not someone who cares for decorating games because of how much it will stress me out, but I have the opposite reaction to this game all together. If it is on sale and you are debating on it, I highly recommend it! At the current price, unless you like replaying something, I would avoid it.

I love this game. It is short, repayable ,and such a fun way to tell the story of someone's life. I am terrible at organizing in my own life, but this always makes me want to be better. Absolute gem of a game that I know I will come back to for years to come if only to take a short break, chill, and enjoy unpacking for a bit.
I have never sat down and finished any game in one sitting... Now it's over and I'm ready to play it again. Amazingly peaceful and perfect for the organizers.

A short but fantastic game! Great visuals, storytelling done in such a unique way but easy to follow, and fun little achievements to get. I even went through and did all the 'dark star' endings. Fun little game for taking a load off and organizing

This game has very chill vibes and is a good way to destress. I like the subtle storytelling going on and how you learn about the character you're unpacking as while also able to self-identify and tell your own story. It's especially fun to play with a friend either watching or playing alongside and then comparing how you set up the rooms. I think it's a little pricey, but I got it on sale and I'm super happy with my purchase. I've replayed to already and am not bored. If you're on the fence, I say buy it next time it's on sale!

The art and music for this game are incredible! It's such a fun little game to play through. Honestly, I wish there was more content-- maybe the life story for [spoiler]the wife[/spoiler] told through moving as well, or just a whole new character. I enjoyed the method of storytelling because it felt really personal. I genuinely wish there was more to play!!

I wasn't even playing the game and I enjoyed it.

- A well designed, peaceful and calming game.

- Very well made in terms of the visuals, art style and interactivity with objects and items as well as good storytelling without the use of dialogue. 

- The achievements add to the discovery and charm, not being there just for the sake of it.

- Great sound design and overall refined with no bugs or difficulties encountered.

- The only downside is that this is an extremely short game, taking roughly 4 hours to fully complete and discover all the easter eggs, secrets and achievements.

- Would definitely love to see more content or even another addition to make this a series/franchise.

This game is super calming. some secret challenges that are challenging with cute rewards. you can go in and do it all in one go or take it one room at a time. perfect for the casual gamer and someone who just wants to feel like they're accomplishing something.

Unpacking, Mimimi Games tarafından geliştirilen ve Witch Beam tarafından yayınlanan bir bulmaca oyunudur. Oyuncular, farklı dönemlere ait bir karakterin eşyalarını açarak onları yerleştirme görevini üstlenirler. İşte Unpacking'in temel özellikleri ve deneyimi hakkında bir inceleme:

Basit ve Etkileyici Konsept:
Unpacking, sade ama etkili bir konsepte dayanır. Oyuncular, karakterin çeşitli evlerine taşınan kutularını açarak eşyaları yerleştirirler. Bu sıradan görev, duygusal ve hikaye anlatımı yönünden zenginleşir.

Gizemli Hikayeler:
Oyun, her eşya ve her odanın arkasında gizlenmiş hikayeler barındırır. Oyuncular, karakterin yaşamındaki değişikliklere tanıklık eder ve eşyaların kişisel anlamlarını keşfederler. Hikayeler, oyuncuların bağ kurmalarını sağlar.

Dokunmatik ve Duygusal Deneyim:
Unpacking, sadece fiziksel eylemleri değil, aynı zamanda duygusal bir deneyimi de vurgular. Her eşyanın dikkatlice yerleştirilmesi, oyunculara kişisel bir bağlantı kurma şansı tanır.

Görsel ve Ses Tasarımı:
Oyun, minimalist ve çekici bir piksel sanat tarzına sahiptir. Renk paleti ve detaylar, oyunun duygusal tonunu güçlendirir. Ayrıca, atmosferik bir ses tasarımı, oyuncuları oyun dünyasına çeker.

Rahatlatıcı ve Meditatif:
Unpacking, rahatlatıcı ve meditatif bir oyun deneyimi sunar. Eşyaların düzenlenmesi süreci, oyunculara stres atma ve huzur bulma fırsatı tanır.

Sonuç:
Unpacking, basit bir mekanik üzerine inşa edilmiş derinlikli bir oyun. Görsel tasarımı, dokunmatik hikayeleri ve rahatlatıcı atmosferiyle oyunseverlere benzersiz bir deneyim sunar. Her eşya, bir hikaye anlatır ve her oda, bir yaşam dönemini yansıtır. Bu nedenle, sıradışı bir oyuna ve duygusal bir yolculuğa ilgi duyanlar için Unpacking, kesinlikle göz atılması gereken bir başyapıttır.


Unpacking is a puzzle game developed by Mimimi Games and published by Witch Beam. Players take on the task of unpacking boxes and placing items in various homes belonging to a character from different time periods. Here's a review of the key features and experience of Unpacking:

Simple yet Impactful Concept:
Unpacking is based on a simple but effective concept. Players unpack boxes carried by the character into different homes and arrange the items. This seemingly mundane task becomes enriched with emotional and storytelling elements.

Mysterious Stories:
The game harbors hidden stories behind each item and room. Players witness changes in the character's life and discover the personal meanings behind the items. These stories enable players to establish a connection.

Tactile and Emotional Experience:
Unpacking emphasizes not only physical actions but also an emotional experience. Carefully placing each item allows players the chance to form a personal connection.

Visual and Sound Design:
The game features a minimalist and appealing pixel art style. The color palette and details enhance the emotional tone of the game. Additionally, atmospheric sound design draws players into the game world.

Relaxing and Meditative:
Unpacking offers a relaxing and meditative gaming experience. The process of arranging items provides players with an opportunity to relieve stress and find tranquility.

Conclusion:
Unpacking is a depthful game built upon a simple mechanic. With its visual design, touching stories, and a soothing atmosphere, it provides gamers with a unique experience. Each item tells a story, and each room reflects a life period. Therefore, for those interested in an unconventional game and an emotional journey, Unpacking is undoubtedly a masterpiece worth exploring.

This game is very lovely and relaxing! 
It uses environmental storytelling to its fullest potential, guiding you along the life of our protagonist and the experiences she goes through. 

Its art direction is phenomenal! The interior design is very charming, every level ends up feeling like a home once you are all settled in, and the small touches that show that each room is lived in makes it all so much more tangible, like a place you might have lived in. The colours used in this game are very pretty and light, giving it all the more feeling of coziness, but bright enough to convey joy.

The sound design is absolutely incredible, having ambient music that strengthens the emotions conveyed in each level, from childhood wonder to loneliness and apathy, to ambitious welcoming of new beginnings. Alongside the beautiful soundtrack the sound effects for every interaction with the items in the game are very satisfying and will have you clickling on things over and over just to hear them again! 

The gameplay itself is very straight forward but really enjoyable, very easy to get into. It stays consistent throughout the game, without changing up the way it plays from level to level, but that isn't an issue as it lets the story take priority. It is very fun to interact with every item in the game, and I was very happy every time I discovered an easter egg to the point of giggling with joy. 

All in all, it's a very nice game, a 10/10 for me and I fully recommend it if you want to enjoy a sweet story told solely through environmental design!

Similar to [i]Animal Crossing[/i], roughly 100% of people’s initial reactions to the gameplay of [i]Unpacking[/i] will include the word “chore,” and just like with [i]Animal Crossing[/i], it’s very hard to explain why it doesn’t entirely deserve that label. Even harder, in fact, because [i]Unpacking[/i] is an incredibly pure experience. To wit, you unpack household items and put them in the correct places. That’s it. [i]Animal Crossing[/i]’s engagement came from charm, progression, and personalization, and while [i]Unpacking[/i] has those to some degree, its true specialty is something the other franchise lacks: story. The story itself is mundane as it gets – normal millennial lives a normal millennial life, basically – but the way it’s told is a masterclass of environmental narrative and characterization. Its protagonist is more realistic and well-rounded than most others despite being unseen and unheard.

The game’s microscopic focus allows it to do this – you’d never notice the little details if you had something more important to do – but that’s a double-edged sword. The “chore” spectre is always looming, particularly behind repeated tasks that don’t really change or communicate much. And the more you get into the actual act of unpacking, the more you’ll get annoyed when every book won’t fit on a single shelf or when you can’t stack and arrange things the way you want. You kind of [i]have[/i] to get into the act of unpacking, too, because everything else is designed to be as broadly appealing and unremarkable as possible to minimize distraction. With all that in mind, I don’t feel right giving [i]Unpacking[/i] a universal recommendation, but it’s a unique product that will be completely engrossing to a specific type of person.

Nice game, I like it. Unpacking makes even one of the most tedious necessities known to man quite fun. So you get an isometric view of a room and you click on boxes to get things out of them, rotate them how you want, and click on where you think they should go. You get desks, bookcases, beds, tables, cabinets, wardrobes, drawers, ovens, everything really. The challenge element in this game mainly derives from having to memorise where objects you've previously placed in another chapter went before, as they often go in the same place. But that's not always the case: this game covers different stages of the protagonist's life, and as you progress, they may want to keep older objects hidden or replace them with newer ones. Also, as Unpacking is kind of a block-filling puzzle as well, the placing of objects tidily and sensibly is a game in itself.

I found the game to be reasonably lenient as to where you can place things, but obviously you can't be too silly, like putting a kettle in a wardrobe for instance. Sometimes it can be slightly picky, like when I was struggling to find a space for a small whiteboard and then by luck hitting the jackpot when I put it in (won't tell you). That was quite strange, as when I finally found its spot, the game declared the level complete before I had a chance to tidy up the mess I left on the table. But Unpacking doesn't lose its sense of fun, and it's rarely frustrating, you won't get stuck for long. 

The controls are simple and intuitive, and the game looks nice, although it can be difficult sometimes to determine what some smaller objects actually are (I didn't see a labelling feature). But there's no need for a hint system and won't take you much more than around 4 hours. It's all good.

The game is cute. You get to go through the story of an individual who is unpacking their life due to different life stages.  It's super comfy and cozy, and the soundtrack is pleasant. You do have to navigate between rooms the farther you progress. If that is something that bothers you, I would not play the game. That being said, you do have the option to interact with some of the items to add some flair or momentary surprise. Interacting with the items can lead to hidden achievements!

A neat touch the developers added, I think, is that the caption on the bottom of the album also changes depending on the room you photograph. You do get the option to change the photo to personalize your album after the fact if you did not like the flow.

A suggestion to the devs: it would be nice to be able to zoom in and out the way you want when the photo is taken. I liked the caption change, but I would have liked to photograph some rooms at my own angle instead of the pre-set one.
