While it is short to play through, I'm not mad about it. A wonderful game!

Although this game is fairly short, it does have a lot of charm packed in. I love the story and little easter eggs that are hidden in the rooms. This game truly melted my heart. I do hope the developers come out with more stories to unpack, I would gladly pay for a DLC. Great job!

This game is AMAZING!!!! So fun and super calming, plus the story line is super cute.  Also, love the representation.  I'd reccomend this to anyone, its just so fun.  The way the story is incorporated is just so smart and the graphics aren't overstimulating, which is an issue I find in some pixel games.  
Now I don't know what to do with myself now that I've played the whole thing.  Guess I'll go start again!

Such a cute game with a story that's unexpectedly told so well!!
To play through once, it's not the longest game, but it's something to keep going back to and playing over again :))
it is fun but i hate how we need to put stuff in a certin place i reccemond this it is a fast game but fun i finished it in like 3 days when i usely finish games in like 8-10 days

Wow, I really loved that game. It was super relaxing, with pretty visuals and nice music. Cute story too. My only complaint is it's not nearly long enough. I would love some DLC, or a sequel, or something like that, but since there probably won't be any, I'll just have to play it again!

It's a beautiful game, super relaxing and fun. The story line is amazing. It's a little over priced in my opinion, mainly because the game is super short for the cost.  I kind of wish I would have waited until it went on sale. Otherwise, it's fantastic.

I love this game. It is very fun and relaxing to put everything away. My only complaint is that it only took 3 hours to finish the whole game. I hope they add more content because 3 hrs for $20 is not worth it.

Unpacking is one of those games you never want to end. It does a brilliant job of telling a story just by putting away your characters prized possessions. Its both calming and engaging, and has amazing graphics. The game has a way of portraying the ups and downs of adulthood, and fills you with a sense of hope for the future. I do hope the expand on the game, as I'd love to play it again. My only critique is that the game itself could have been longer. You're spending $20 for about three hours of gameplay, and while you can go back and replay, it's not as fun as the first time. Besides that, this game is one of the best i've played so far, and I'd probably spend an obscene amount of money to play a sequel or spin-off.

This name is so heartwarming. I can't believe the amount of detail and emotions that are conveyed through a game with such bare minimum story line. This game is incredibly intimate and I am so impressed with the way the developers were able to communicate growth and character development so well without dialogue or visible character interaction. 
No idea who these characters are, what they look like, or their names, but I feel so close to them. Watching the main character grow, discover themselves, and have such a beautiful life through nothing but unpacking their boxes has brought me to tears.
The game is short but there is so much to discover. I love that there are so many different ways you can decorate many different rooms and seeing familiar objects move with the characters throughout new or old places. It's so exciting to see new items that the characters obtain through their life and it makes you feel incredibly proud of them. 

I really recommend this game. Very relaxing, warm, and fun. So cute.

This game is really relaxing. This is easily one of my favorite games. Its cute how some of the achievements are obtained. When I first started playing and I had finished putting everything away in the first level, I got the red-outlined thing signaling that something was in the wrong place and all I could think was, "What do you mean I can't put that there? This is my house!!" I just thought it was funny. It is pretty interesting to see where things are and aren't 'allowed' to go. You can also play several times (for me I've got many albums created and so far I have not been given a limit on how many times I'm able to replay). It's so cool to go back and play again to see how I place things differently or to see things that I do consistently throughout albums. The playback feature is also a blast for me, I love watching how my mind worked while placing items but in super speed! Some levels are challenging just because of the amount of objects there are to put in one room, but I wouldn't say its difficult, just makes you think a little bit. The progression of living space and it's size is amazing! The way some items are kept, expanded upon, etc., is so cute and makes it feel like real life when you carry things with you for sentiment.  


TL;DR: I absolutely love this game.
This game is so heart-warming! I loved every second of it. I would have liked that the other albums belonged to other characters, though. It could have been a great feature, but I liked everything!

Very simple, relaxing, and fun!
I like the concept of arranging things, I didn't expect that there would be a story involved in this type of game. The story is nice and heartwarming. I wish there were more levels though, or maybe new story :)
Overall, I'm pretty satisfied, worth it.
It is a very peaceful game, 3 hours felt like 30 minutes and i did cry at the ending. It is so cute and enjoyable, I wish they add more to the game like unpacking the childs life too.
very fun and simple, just wished it was longer for the price, but other than that its good. Just maybe wait till its on a discount

I held off on getting this game for so long because I didn't think there was a story. And now I'm sitting here, having just finished the game CRYING. This game is such a good story, with an interesting and unique story telling device, unpacking.

This is a truly delightful game. It's relaxing to play, and I really enjoyed the art; there's a lot of work put into each little item, and I loved finding homes for everything. The sound design is absolutely wonderful! I found myself picking up each item multiple times so I could hear the noises they'd make as they moved. You can really tell the team was dedicated making this game. Everything feels so thought out. 
The only thing I wish was different was that it was a bit longer. I could see myself sinking a lot of time into a game like this if there was more content or a sandbox mode. It only took me 4 or so hours to complete the game and collect all the achievements. Every second of it was enjoyable, and I really wanted more. It's a fantastic game!

This game is absolutely adorable, the subtle story telling through the possessions that get unpacked from home to home is beautiful and I love it so much! I'd love for a sequel someday! This charming game is worth your time.
Jeux très bien réalisé, de beau graphisme et une petite histoire derrière cependant le jeu est beaucoup trop court pour ma part je l'ai fini en 4h... pour un jeu a ce prix la c'est abusé (20€)

I love it, is such an "aesthetic" game. It's really sad that it only lasts around 3 hours, but it is pretty enjoyable. That is why I find the price a bit high. I believe that this game has so much to offer that 3 hours is really short.

Well, this is one of those games that definitely feels like a very personal journey and if there's one thing I really can not praise enough it's the visual storytelling.  The point of playing this game *is* to interpret and observe this person's world and experiences through what they own, and what they keep.  In this way I have nothing but nice things to say and it's on that basis that I both gave it a try, and that I recommend you do the same.

That said, some critical observations.  On the game play front, it's not always obvious what exactly an item is which, while rare, can lead to some humorous or even lightly annoying "that doesn't go there" moments.  The experience is pretty short but it happened in nearly every move and in one case I literally couldn't find anywhere in the house that would accept it.  Most things can live in multiple places, but in this particular instance I had no idea what the object was or what it wanted from me.  Second, stacking is a bit inconsistent as well.  Some things stack, some things don't and placement can make this person feel a bit psychotic in what they will accept.  That *said*, the fact it didn't happen more does demonstrate some pretty solid conveyance.  There's not a single move where I didn't have to rearrange items, but only once was I like, "WHERE DOES THIS GOI!?"

I will avoid discussing the story too much, but I have to touch on one thing.  We know the protagonist goes through a misjudged relationship where they are, quite literally, having to find a place for themselves.  When you meet your true love you not only have room for everything, all of their stuff compliments your decor.  You literally don't have to move a single thing you own to make room for them in your life.  Oh, and also *you* move their stuff in, you know, because your previous lover couldn't be bothered to make room for you?  And your spouse has different boxes, just in case you can't pick up on on the many visual clues that this stuff belongs to someone with different hobbies and tastes.  It's still full of cute details, and it's wonderfully visual storytelling, but the overt iconography made it feel less substantial, like the writer was really worried someone might not "get it" so they went *really* overboard.  I just felt the details we're left to interpret were the interesting bits, so I guess I wanted it to let me get there without so much hand-holding.

That is not a broad complaint so much as just a personal criticism, maybe other people will find it all more subtle.  I'd still rate it above most indie fare, I enjoyed the story and I'm glad I took the journey.  I can easily recommend it if you are able to patron the arts.

This was the game I looked forward to all year after first playing the demo at LudoNarraCon, and I love the immersion of the final product.  The unique self-driven narrative style of this game is having to quietly piece together the character's life: primarily inferring the backstory through changes in the things the character owns and values, but also the caption that gets scribbled into the photo album when completing a level - the caption changes depending on the room you photograph.  This is also an exquisitely textured game: for example if you shake the mouse cursor with some items you get really rich and responsive sounds.  Furthermore, I love how the soundscape changes for each room you visit, like the hum of appliances, or hints of sounds from the outside world.  Like the preview videos show, many of the objects become interactable after setting them down - some of which are are quite nostalgic - like the PC BIOS boot up screen, the old instant messenger apps on the PC, and the router flickering lights.  One of the things I didn't realize until much later was that completed levels are still editable; you can click on the photograph to revisit a level and change anything you like including trying to complete achievements you may have missed.  Because I didn't know this, I actually played the game twice to get more of the achievements.  Nevertheless there is definitely replay value: the stacking of the objects in the boxes are randomized including randomization between objects being in the wrong room, and the second time round it was easier to strategize about stacking things on the floor first before fitting them into limited shelf space and having to keep moving them around.  As some of the other have suggested, you may spend up fewer hours on this game for the price, but I also thing those are hours well spent and it's nice to have an excellent and unique experience like eating food at a high quality restaurant.  Ordinarily, moving home tends to be ranked high as a stressful event, but it's thoroughly enjoyable in this game.  This is one of the most unique and original games I've played.

My only complaint is that the game isn't long enough! I love the aesthetic, music, and more subtle storytelling. Starting my second playthrough now :)

My only downside is I truly wish I'd paid attention to the price tag versus the amount of time it takes to complete the game. While it says I've played six hours, it's probably closer to 2 to complete the game for me as I left it running while I went on some errands heh. I understand art costs money but I would have waited for a sale.

This game was seriously SO CUTE! I am obsessed! I loved getting to learn more about the character's life and interests. Please give me more!!!! I played all of it in 2 days because I could not stop playing!

Unpacking is that kind of game that makes you feel relaxed while your stimulates your mind with its interesting puzzles as well as the need to organize. Not only that, but those small details, such as the fact that the MC's diploma could only be kept in certain places in certain phases/certain years of their life, tells a story in its own way.

Also, the aesthetic of the game's aesthetic matches the music, and the faint bass tones that you can identify whenever an item is picked up or laid down adds to the overall experience. I had a great time playing the full game, however I hoped there were more. Like there's a phase/stage where the yard/garage is included and playable. Haha!

Unpacking is a unique, relaxing, and enjoyable experience. A simple game but delivers the story well enough. I hope there will be more of this kind. <3

Thank you for making this. I definitely enjoyed it. My heart definitely loved it.

Initially I waited on purchasing this game due to the price in comparison to the length of game playtime. However, after filling every save slot & getting every achievement, just to reset all of my save data to do it over again.. I have to admit that I really love this game. 

The art style is cute and the music is really pleasant. The ending credit song: 10/10! All of the little hidden Easter-eggs and references made (like the Pan's Labyrinth DVD and the way she gradually takes on the same interests and items of her past roommates) in the media were endearing to find. I found myself invested in the character and could relate to the story really well as I share a very similar background as both an artist and a gay woman building her life with her partner and son.

I also understand the feelings of those who purchased this game and were disappointed after completing it in only 3/4 hours the first time around. The thing that some don't seem to realize it that with games like this it isn't supposed to be completed once and never played with again. There are endless different ways to set everything up and beat a level. It's relaxing and fun. (And if nothing else trying to speed-run this game is a lot of fun!)

My only recommendation is that I would love to see workshop content added in, or some DLC that could change up the character's interests with a re-skin of items and books.

This is a calming organizing game which follow a story of a girl moving from one place to another. You get the box and you put your belongings from the box to your room.

The beauty of this game is how you follow a girl journey knowin the story without even a single line of dialogue, everything told by visual, by the place you move in and by the stuff ou bring to the place.

The game itself is very calming and very relatable for the people who move to other place several times in the life. So many stuff, so little space, while looks like you can put your stuff anywhere, but this game is still have some rules about where you can or cannot place your stuff, it makes you thing where the hell you would put your stuff, just like the real life.

Few problems personally, some stuff is so small and so unsusual i can't figure it out what blob of pixel is that? . Then placement rule defined in this game based from the dev society standard, so i could get confused why i can't put some stuff here, for example usually peoples in my place put the body scale on the either bathroom, bedroom or dining room, but this game rules reveal that you put the scale on the freakin kitchen like, what?!! who does that

overall nice little game with not so little price (i bought it on sale btw)
100/10, what a delightful experience. Beautiful, subtle story telling and an ending that had me all weepy and nostalgic. Absolutely needed this <3

It's an amazingly simple game that walks you through the life of a player simply by using rooms and boxes of objects. I've never been told such a well thought out story so well without ever being told it. It's a fantastic game with a lot of fun elements that makes me want to play it over and over. My only complaint would be that it ended too soon. I finished it in around 2 hours and I've been craving more!

This is superlative story telling. What a game. Such a simple mechanic - take stuff and put them in a place. But telling such a powerful story - oh my. It has been a long time since I played a game where the story telling was this good, and has the ability to provide multiple "whoa" moments. And the beauty of this game is that as a player, you will be the one to supply the story. Everyone will have different moments and read the signs differently.
I moved houses quite a bit in the last few years - travelling between countries - and just the simple act of unpacking cups and arranging them brought back such amazing memories. Then there is the joy of discovering some familiar objects through each of the houses, or finding something new.
Play at your own pace, and discover this amazing journey.

PROS-Relaxing, efficient, simple, enjoyable story telling.
CONS- Ended too quickly, not enough of a challenge.
Would recommend this game to anyone who gets satisfaction from organizing or putting things away.

Absolutely amazing game, fun to stream and told a heartwarming story. The only thing that I had struggles with were when there was an item that I wasn't sure what it was and couldn't find the correct spot to place it. (but google can always help with that)! anyways 10/10

Good game - just hope theres some more content coming soon.

Enjoyed playing Unpacking, found the game to be very relaxing and chill.

The game was so cute and was designed with a child's imagination in mind when needed, which added a fun little touch to the types of items and where the right places for them are. While I loved the game, I do wish there was a more for how much the game costs. $20 for about 2 hours of game play, if you aren't rushing or trying to find every little thing. Unpacking is a unique indie game focused on storytelling using a first-of-its-kind mechanic of… Unpacking. It’s a short unique game that anyone could play on any computer since it also has simple but beautiful pixel graphics, created with care and a lot of talent. In a simple world setting that is our own present, we play as a nameless protagonist. From girl to a woman, we as players help her move into new apartments. Each level is a new apartment where we take her belongings out of boxes and organize them in her new space, be it a room, dorm room, bedroom, or a whole house. 

Sounds simple enough and it is, as a gaming mechanic there’s not much to it, but the story unfolds with the items she owns that come with her from place to place as she grows up. As a little girl, we unpack her piggy plush toy, and we continue to do so in each apartment. In her dorm room, we struggle to fit all her new sports equipment into the space. When she moves in with roommates, we can’t move anything in the apartment and are struggling to fit into other people’s spaces. 

In her new boyfriend’s place, while unpacking her mismatched dishes, I felt inadequate next to the man’s designer’s kitchenware. There was no room for our protagonist. Although we’ve seen, by looking at the boyfriend’s belongings, that they have a lot in common - both play music and like video games, the game design lets us know that it’s not perfect. While playing, my heart stung when the only place for the university diploma was hidden in the closet. 

I was amazed at how much emotion the game was making me feel, and I haven’t even seen a character. When I unpacked a bowl I recognized as her roommates I knew she made a friend who gave her a gift. When I stacked new markers on a shelf I was relieved she got back to art. When I saw she has a new partner I teared up with happiness for her. This is a high achievement in storytelling and was a true joy to play.

i LOVE the concept, execution and story of this game but the current content in the game isn't worth the full price for me (if you're thinking of buying wait for a sale), i would love to see additional levels added which would make the price worth it to me.

This game may look like it's just about unpacking boxes but it also unpacks a story! Very well done and well thought out! I loved every detail; to the D&D figures to the growth of hobbies, love and family! Will definitely play again!

A cute little relaxing game that tells a surprisingly deep story through its vignettes and still lives. For $20, it's a bit short/sparse in content, but altogether I enjoyed it and don't regret buying it.

It will seem a bit short, particularly for the price, but it is clear that a lot of thought and heart went into this game.  Hopefully more will come, but it is definitely a case of quality over quantity.

Even if you complete the entire game, you can still go back and complete the puzzles to receive all of the stickers. A common complaint I saw was that there was a lack of levels, and I do agree with that. If you’re looking for a game with a lot of hours of gameplay, this may not be the best value for your money. Overall, it’s a great game. Great to just poke at while relaxing. I’d give it a 7 out of 10.

Es ist ein wirklich super süßes und entspanntes Game ABER es ist meiner Meinung nach viel zu teuer für die Länge & Komplexität des Spiels. A good game.

Being a puzzle game, When you put something in 'the wrong spot' It will flash a red outline around the item, Until you put it in the right spot. Don't worry if you just want this game to place the items, there's a option to remove the wrong spots placings in settings. (Along with changing wrong spot colours)

If your looking for a longer game play, I don't think this game is for you. The game play is only 3-5 hours I'd say,  And there's no levels past 2018. This game is great, I would recommend it for anybody looking for a cute, fun game with a little story line in it.

If I had to rate it out of 10, i would give it a 8.5/10.
In conclusion, Yes! I think you should play this game. ^^

Voilà une nouvelle chose à ajouter à la liste de ce que j'aime faire en jeu vidéo mais pas en vrai : le rangement. Une chose qu'"Unpacking" réussit à rendre agréable, sa musique et ses graphismes pixelisés aux couleurs douces aidant.

Que vous soyez quand même prévenus, au cas où vous ne seriez pas du genre à dépenser vingt euro sans réfléchir : aussi chouette qu'il soit ce jeu est très court. Plus de quatre heures pour le terminer en ce qui me concerne, mais beaucoup l'ont fini en trois petites heures. Ça n'enlève rien à ses qualités, mais ce n'est pas négligeable pour tout le monde.

En bref :
Joli petit jeu, concept original, relaxant, court.
Very chill game. I recommend it! Had lots of fun playing. Not much replay value. I'd get this on a sale. Had a lot of fun 100% this. Hope for more levels soon!
Super cute game with fantastic dialogue-free story telling. A bit short at around three or so hours for the price, but still a good time.

It would also be nice to see a sandbox mode, or something similar, where you can design your own room.

Surprisingly fun for what it is, as well as being short, sweet and to the point. I was also surprised at how well the game manages to tug at your heartstrings. Being able to get a glimpse in from what I'm guessing is the game creators life is really one of those very private things that is also very heartwarming in a way. 

Its also nice to know in some ways that even other individuals lives can be uprooted by circumstances that seem entirely unforeseen. 

This game is easily worth the money and time, considering I got it on a whim when ManyATrueNerd rated it as his game of the year I thought it was absolute nonsense. Now looking back I can see why he rates it so highly.

간단하게 집만 꾸미는게 아닌 집에 물건들을 배치하면서, 주인공의 스토리를 엿볼수 있는 게임.

If I had any complaints it would be that there was not a lot of content, as I finished the game a little under 5 hours. For me personally 20 dollars for 5 hours of content isn't exactly ideal. I hope we get more content in the future. 

Overall I would say its a game worth trying but if you want to get as much content as possible, maybe save this game for another day.

There's no narrative which makes it a super chill game to just play around with, coupled with the sound effects of the objects, makes it a satisfying, casual game. 

It's also impressive how even though there's narration, the environmental factors as well as objects gives you clues on who the character is such as their hobbies, career as well as experiences throughout the years.  [spoiler]For example their breakup with their boyfriend and their girlfriend moving in.[/spoiler] Other than the character themselves, you also get to find out about the people they live with which is quite interesting.

I've played the whole game multiple times and it doesn't really get boring as you notice new things each time you play so it's definitely worthwhile. I do wish there were more chapters/stages because I am addicted to this game but it's a great game =)

I played once and it is done and there isn't enough creative freedom to just unpack again and place things in different spots. I was hoping for more  - or a second story after completing the first. All 3 of my saves have had different outcomes as far as exact items and enough difference to change how I organize things as well. 

Some may find a 20 dollar price tag to be obscene -- However I think its fully justified, and especially if there is any planned added content or other such things... Its a relaxing organizer game.

I personally love it as it's quite cozy and it truly makes you reflect on what your material possessions say about you, and what it means to choose to keep something or to leave it behind.

I don't know how the devs managed to make such an endearing game but I'm excited to see what else they have done and what they have up there sleeves!! I honestly didn't think i would enjoy this game as much as I did and if you are on the fence about getting it I say do it and get ready for a nice time!

The game is very calming and you can play at your own pace. The game weaves an excellent story through the atmosphere, barely uttering a word, allowing the player to fill in the gaps. game is nice, cute, and relaxing. however, i was able to finish the game at around the 3 hour mark. i wouldn't say it's entirely worth the $20 spent unless there is more content added to the game. overall, though, it's a very pleasant game with an adorable art style! the music was also enjoyable :>

so as someone who has ADHD this was fun to play, however there is a few things that i did not like. one would be that yes it is a short game especially for the price. with that said being able to pick if a shirt will be hung or folding is a great concept so the time to make a game (4 years apparently) is kind of understandable, when making sure such things is moving smoothly.  i do hope that more is added tho, i could play this for hours and hours if there was more too it. i hope the developers make more 'levels', or 'stories'. there was a part in the game that infuriated me was that i could not move items that were already there and i found it annoying. i also did not care for having to place items in certain places, when i am the one unpacking, i should be able to place whatever, where ever. it is what it is and will play again, when more is added

Loved this game! Relaxing and got about 5 hours of game play, but can be more or less depending on how particular you are about getting things juuust right. Soundtrack and art style were charming. Didn't think I'd get emotional in a game about organization.

I am a sucker for good environmental story telling and this game does it beautifully! Not only is unpacking and making your space look *perfect* suuuuper satisfying but it was also really cool to figure out who the  person behind the stuff is and where life leads them.

10/10, way more fun than actual unpacking

Short but really lovely and relaxing gameplay.

Unpacking is a zen-like experience in the world of video games, an ode to the simple joy of organization that unexpectedly unfolds into a poignant narrative. This game, developed by Witch Beam, transforms the seemingly mundane task of unpacking boxes into a meditative journey that resonates with anyone who has ever found solace in the act of arranging their belongings.

Visually, Unpacking is a minimalist masterpiece. The pixel art style, paired with soothing color palettes, creates a calming atmosphere. Each item, from childhood toys to kitchen utensils, is intricately designed, inviting players to appreciate the beauty in the everyday objects that shape a person's life.

The soundtrack complements the game's tranquil ambiance perfectly. Subtle, melodic tunes ebb and flow as you meticulously place items in their designated spots, turning the act of unpacking into a rhythmic dance of serenity. The sound effects, from the satisfying clicks of objects finding their place to the gentle rustling of papers, enhance the immersive experience.

Gameplay in Unpacking is deceptively simple yet remarkably engrossing. The challenge lies not in overcoming adversaries or solving complex puzzles but in the thoughtful placement of items. The game encourages a slow, deliberate pace, allowing you to savor each moment and reminisce about the memories attached to the items you unpack.

The narrative unfolds gradually as you progress through different stages of life, from childhood to adulthood. The subtle storytelling is poignant, allowing players to piece together the protagonist's journey through the items they choose to keep and those they decide to let go. It's an emotionally resonant experience that tugs at the heartstrings without being overtly sentimental.

Unpacking's community has embraced its therapeutic gameplay, sharing screenshots of their meticulously arranged virtual spaces and discussing the emotional impact of the narrative. The game has become a digital haven for those seeking a moment of calm in a busy world.

In conclusion, Unpacking is a gem in the gaming landscape, offering a tranquil escape into the art of arrangement. Its minimalist design, calming soundtrack, and heartfelt narrative combine to create an experience that is both relaxing and emotionally resonant. If you're looking for a game that celebrates the beauty in simplicity and the nostalgia of unpacking life's moments, Unpacking is a must-play that unfolds with grace and charm.

J'ai apprécié jouer à Unpacking. La direction artistique en pixel-art est très mignonne et sert le côté nostalgique du jeu. Le principe est très simple : on déballe des cartons puis on place les objets déballés dans les emplacements qui nous semblent les plus judicieux. Le jeu ne vous laissera cependant pas tout placer n'importe où et une fois les cartons entièrement vidés, le jeu vous indiquera en surbrillance les objets mal placés. Certains emplacements ne sont pas évidents à trouver mais vous ne passerez jamais plus de 5 minutes à trouver la solution lorsque cela se produira.

La bande son est assez banal. Ayant joué au jeu presque d'une traite, j'avoue qu'elle m'a un peu cassé les pieds au bout de 2h, je l'ai donc éteinte avant de la remettre en route le lendemain. Il me semble aussi qu'il s'agit de plusieurs pistes qui s'enchaînent sans rattachement particulier à un niveau. J'ai trouvé une piste un peu triste à un moment du jeu qui était plutôt joyeux, c'était bizarre !

Attention aux étourdis : personnellement, je pensais que nous allions suivre le déménagement de plusieurs personnes différentes et donc découvrir à chaque niveau une nouvelle vie, peut-être avec des surprises à la clé mais il n'en est rien. La page du jeu sur le magasin Steam précise bien qu'il s'agit de suivre la vie d'une seule personne le long de 8 emménagements.

Même si j'ai beaucoup aimé jouer au jeu, je regrette cependant son manque de contenu : pour 19,99€, 4 à 5 heures de jeu pour 8 niveaux, cela me semble un peu court.
Je nuancerai néanmoins en précisant que le gameplay étant simple et répétitif (déballer des cartons et placer des objets à l'endroit optimal dans la limite de ce qu'autorise le jeu, rien de plus), je comprends qu'un tel jeu ne puisse pas s'étendre autant qu'un House Flipper ou tout autre jeu de décoration plus poussé.

En matière de rejouabilité, le jeu vous propose à la fin d'explorer à nouveau les niveaux terminés, tel que vous les avez décorés. Cela permet de modifier la décoration, pour votre plaisir personnel, mais surtout cela vous permettra d'essayer d'obtenir tous les succès du jeu. 
Précisons aussi que, à la fin de chaque niveau, vous pouvez prendre 1 photo de l'une des pièces de la maison, 1 seule. La photo viendra alors s'ajouter à un album photo (qui représente votre fichier de sauvegarde) assortie d'un petit commentaire. Ce commentaire change en fonction de la pièce prise en photo : vous voudrez donc peut-être explorer à nouveau votre sauvegarde pour voir tous les commentaires possibles.

En conclusion, je recommande ce jeu aux personnes qui aiment les jeux de décoration et celles à la recherche d'un petit puzzle-game mignon et relaxant mais je vous conseillerais plutôt d'attendre qu'il soit soldé si votre budget est limité.

Unpacking is a very humble and relaxing game. Personally, I rate it an 8/10. The things I like about the game is the visual storytelling and the way the game is. I think it's a bit expensive, but also somewhat worth the price. Worth it for the calming experience, definitely. Another thing I dislike is the zooming. You can only zoom out once from the original view, and I find it annoying. It's a huge difference and I wish there were more zooming options. Another thing I dislike is the boxes themselves. I get it, you're unpacking, but sometimes they cover places where you can put things. I have many cramped rooms because of this. It's a small annoyance. I find the kitchens to be the hardest rooms to complete, as there are so many big objects that appear last for some reason. I've had to reconstruct whole kitchens just because of a random microwave that appeared as the last item. So, for these reasons, the game is a solid 8/10. Just a few small problems. I recommend it.

I never know how I really feel about a game until I try to review it, and then often a lot of Stuff comes spilling out, and then suddenly I want to say that there are relatively few games where People Who Don't Play Video Games are truly and significantly missing out in terms of an artistic/emotional journey that you can only get from this art form, and for me "Unpacking" is definitely on that list. 

There's a lot to unpack with "Unpacking," (sorry), and the short version is that this wonderful and simple game of Taking Things Out Of Boxes In Different Places is a 4-hour concentrated challenge to how you view Stuff and how what we own tells our story when we are not there, and I can't imagine anyone regretting playing it if they know even generally what they're getting into. Does the novel premise of unpacking boxes appeal to you? Do you like super nice pixel art? You will not be disappointed, for once. I love it when that happens.
The long version is that "Unpacking" shows you at length the relationship between the Things we posess and who we are, and it's not something I'd considered at length until it was presented in this effective way that-- again, for once-- actually uses the unique abilities of the medium of video games to convey a story in a uniquely effective manner. There's a lot to say about Environmental Storytelling in games-- the way a game like "Gone Home" or even "Dark Souls" can 3-dimensionally tell a story about a character just by you looking at what they left behind, or even what other say about them-- in text, in a statue,  the *absence* of a statue, anything. And so often it's the space they lived in or the items they owned that tells that story to the point where you develop an image of that person and then eventually realize you've never actually *seen* that character-- you've just seen so much Stuff that the person-shaped, snow angel-style hole in the center of it perfectly outlines who they are or were. "Unpacking" obviously does this, is my point here-- you will learn about the main character and their life and where it takes them, through brilliant game mechanics like when the game lets you touch other people's belongings and when it doesn't, and through attention to detail to a refreshing degree wherein the game assumes you are a non-idiot who is capable of paying attention-- but the game does more than that as well. 

It makes you think about your own Stuff, or stuff in general, and who is at the center of it, and how what we own or even leave behind outlines who we were, and maybe it even challenges how much you hate Materialism-- still bad for its own sake, but there is at least the challenging notion that when we have the power to choose what we own or even just what we can keep, we have the power to exist beyond just ourselves. We all leave a person-shaped hole in the world when we are gone, but how accurate is the outline, how detailed, how well can we be described when we are not there and if we did not otherwise create anything like a body of work or a close family? We all have the right to exist beyond the short decades in which we are literall alive, and maybe the Things we chose to keep are one way to do that. Yeah, it's just Stuff, but the world is just stuff, and a fossilized skeleton ironically tells you less about an individual than their DVD collection does. Materialism for its own sake is still bad, and mansions and luxury cars tell the unsympathetic tale of those who temporarily owned them as they temporarily lived, for their own glory... but simply to choose what we gather around us is valuable and tells our story when we are out of the room. Don't we deserve that? 

As long as the observer does the work to examine such relics, that is, and in "Unpacking" that is you (not that it will feel like work in the slightest). This game does what every Indie game should do: the personal rather than the generic, creative risks instead of safe bets, attention to detail rather than "they're idiots and won't see it anyway so why bother," and constant, human specificity instead of attemtps to appeal to a nonexistent General Audience. And there is no General Audience-- there are are only People, and you are one, and you are very specific, and you will play this game and you will unpack boxes and one or more things will be exactly, f-ing *exactly* like that one thing you have always had in real life, and then you will be IN, you will be hooked, you will get it. For me it was the bus model and the eraser and the pens and the copies of your own book and the wrist brace and the posters I've had for years and the nostalgia and the way we can't control anything beyond the walls we live within so we control that-- we choose what we have, and what we keep, and how long we keep it, and we end up with Stuff and it proves that we existed and how we existed. 

This game in your Steam library is such a small addition to your life, but with an impact so much greater than it looks from the outside. On its own it's just a Thing that many other people have an identical copy of, but in the particular context of your life it tells you so much, and tells so much about you-- like all things.
It's a good game but not worth the price. If it had a little more content it would be better. I would wait till it goes on sale to purchase.

Unpacking is a great experience. Such a cool concept and it was able to tell a real story without getting in the way of the game play. It did get a little overwhelming at times with all of the stuff you have to put away, but that is what it is really like. I would highly recommend it to any casual player.

This would go the same for the completion. Nearly all of the achievements are easy to obtain and if you actually try to ground yourself in the world most of the achievements come naturally.

- 8 / 10

The attention to detail and environmental storytelling is an absolute delight and I loved every second of this. It was a good lesson in empathizing with others as the different situations you end up in bring some pretty poignant "a-ha!" moments. 

Stellar little puzzler with a lot of love.  Highly recommend it.
Very cute, each room tells a progressive story of the character's life. It's a very relaxing game compared to a lot out there, and doesn't require too much focus.

Such a wonderful and cosy-feeling game. It was a lot of fun learning the story as you went along, 'unpacking' the meaning of what you were unpacking and where you could (or couldn't smh) place things. 100% would recommend this game to anyone and everyone.

The game itself is pretty, creative and soothing, although it doesn't have enough content to be worth the 20 euros.

In the future, I'd like to see more stories (maybe two or three additional characters), otherwise great purchase if it's on sale.

The only con would be the game is a bit overpriced (though I see this as a way to support the game devs). Other than that however, its very enjoyable and relaxing. The story is simple and heartwarming. I would definitely replay this if I just need time to kill and wanna get my mind off things.

Here's some suggestions that can make the price more worth:
-A sandbox mode
-Expansion on the story, either the same person, whoever is related to them or just enetirely different person
-Different endings in implementation of how we arrange our stuffs (this falls under expansion of story but I feel like it deserves its own point)

I played for 10 hours, paid 20 bucks. Not too bad, a little overpriced. That said, the game is really fun and relaxing! It was so fun to slowly learn about the person through their belongings. Definitely a unique experience. I really did love it, even though it was a little short for the price. I hope that more content comes out in the future - either a few more levels with the same person, or a new person entirely. The ending was very sweet! I found that even though the premise is so simple, the game had moments that made me a little emotional, and was able to give me a feeling of nostalgia based on items and life milestones I recognized from my own life. Very fun, get it on sale.

Cute and easy,brainless game to play. Only complaint is why can't I put a plant of top of my fridge. Let me put the plants on the fridge. Please.

Fridge plant fiasco aside, nice seeing the story unfold and following what happens to our character with each new chapter.

This is still one of my favorite cute cozy games I have. I have played this game for 39 hours over the past few years, and I am still not tired of it. I absolutely love organising everything the way I would want to. It's so simple, peaceful and calming. Something worth putting hours into if you are looking for a cute indie game where you are in control most of the time. I appreciate the puzzle aspect, and the fact you can toggle it on and off if you wish. 10/10 game, high recommendation.

A relaxing and short narrative game with point-and-click puzzle mechanics. It beautifully tells the story of a young woman moving into different stages of her life, starting with her first private room in her pre-teen years and ending with her own house. The game slowly ramps up the number of tasks one must complete in each stage without ever becoming difficult; imho it gets more pleasant as you progress to freely arrange multiple rooms.

I like this game but I am disappointed. For $20 I was expecting more than one character. Why is there not more than one person to follow? Why is there not a sandbox mode? Why is there not something more for this amount of money. I enjoy this style of game and have many of them. I feel a little cheated. Unless you can get it for $5 or less don't bother. The price tag is too big for what is here.
So heart warming. The attention to detail and storyline are beyond my expectations. So many possibilities and truly makes you think. I was in tears by the end. I adored to game <3!
This game has to be one of my favorite puzzle games! It is adorable and the art style is very heart-warming. I wish the game was longer, but I feel that I has to be the perfect length storywise!

Unpacking has very quickly become one of my Top 5 games. Although it is quite short (especially for the price), it does an exceptional job at delivering meaningful story line through the unpacking of the character's belongings as they move from home to home. I strongly recommend that everybody picks this game up once it goes on sale.
It's so good I cried the whole time playing. Watching the story literally unfold as you unpack things and watching as you grow with your life partner it's just, so beautiful. <3

This is a beautiful game in both the subtle storytelling and the relaxing and satisfying gameplay. It's a wonderful game to wind down with and I highly recommend it for anyone who loves putting everything in its place just so.

Unpacking "packed" an even richer story than I expected. The soundtrack is great while you open box after box and the story unravels. Without any rush it can be completed in 4 hours, and for almost 20EUR, I feel there should have been more in this game. The visuals are not overly complicated and the controls are simple.
I'm definitely going to pick it up and make it 100%, but more stuff to unpack would be awesome! 🐤

A beautiful game clearly made with love! The pixel art is incredibly detailed, if you've enjoyed those children's books where there's lots to look at as a kid, you'll love this! The visual storytelling is out of this world, the replay function is so satisfying, and the story... oh, the story. I'm sure it'll at the very least be a cute, enjoyable story for most people, but for me personally, oh man, this hit way too close to home.

Being vague and spoiler-free: I'm an artist, it's what I do for a living... but things have been feeling very soul-less lately. This game may or may not have given me the boost I needed to find passion in what I do again, I'm sure it's gotta be somewhere in there still.

...Anyway :) I personally did one or two rooms per day at a very chill pace, and so the full game took me 8 hours to finish. I've seen a few comments here and there about the game being "not worth it" due to its length, but I wholeheartedly disagree! Listen, if we are going to accept video games as an art form, we've got to disconnect playtime from good/bad. I can't even begin to imagine how much work went just into the pixel art alone here, along with everything else on top.

A shallow asset flip could take you five times as long to finish, but that doesn't make it any better. Quality over quantity!
I loved every minute of this game. It's not just simply unpacking things, there is a beautiful story. I hope in the future there will be another one.

"unpacking" is such a wonderful, calm experience and a refreshing take on storytelling. Traversing through the life of the main character via the boxes she has to unpack throughout her life is such an immensely personal and introspective look into how much we ourselves put into the little details we decorate our spaces with. 

It is truly enjoyable to go through all of the rooms and unpack things in different ways; the replayability factor is sky-high when you account for the setting to turn off the puzzle aspect of the game and just creatively place things wherever you want. The game makes it fun to unpack! There's so many knick-knacks and little items that allow us as the player to see the scope of how far the main character has grown and progressed as the story goes on, My one main challenge was finding a spot for all of her books! 

There's also so much more interactivity than on first glance. Some of the achievements revolve around these features so I am going to put in spoiler tags for some of this:  [spoiler]Being able to set the time on the microwave, play music throughout the levels using the radios, turning on the game consoles and the computers, all of it is so very thoughtful and honestly adorable to witness.[/spoiler] 

All of this was something I didn't catch on my first playthrough of the game and I'm grateful I went back- it was so pleasant! 

All in all, if you're looking for a comfortable, short, cozy game to play, this is your game. The narration is done masterfully and without even having a real narrator beyond the little captions in the photo album. All of the stickers for the achievements are super cute, as well, so that's an added bonus if you want 100% completion rates! 100/10

A relaxing mix of nostalgia and discovery. I really enjoyed playing through the characters life, the ups and downs of moving, the warm feeling of seeing certain items reoccur throughout each move. 
Its a very relaxing and cute game, the sprites are beautiful, the attention to detail is fantastic. Its a nice cute game with limited playtime. I took my time trying to interact with everything and I was finished within 4 hours. 
While I don't regret purchasing this game at full price, I'd say for those looking for a game with replayability and challenge - this isn't a game you want to buy at full price. If you're like me and just like wholesome 90's aesthetic pixel art, then it's one for the collection and you should buy this game at full price.

This is a really cute game to play and I had a lot of fun with it. Unfortunately, it isn't a very long game and only lasts around 3 hours, which is disappointing for the price. It was still great to play though and I would recommend people to give it a go.

I really enjoyed this game- very peaceful and relaxing, easy to use.

As a warning, I have completed all of the levels in 2.5 hours- I'll probably go back and replay bits to get achievements etc. but I would've liked more content for the money I paid.

beat the game in three hours, it was really relaxing! if you want to wait for a sale, wait. but if you have a spare $20 to drop - get it! either way this game is really well designed and had a very cuter story.

I adore this game because I love organizing things and making rooms look nice. Unpacking lets you arrange and rearrange to your heart's content, with charming little sound effects for every object being set on every surface. The game told a story via environmental storytelling that I found sweet and relatable. I am thrilled to finally own this myself because I want to go back and play it again every so often in the future. I don't know if this game is for EVERYONE, but it's certainly for me. <3
extremely wholesome and relaxing. came for the interior design, stayed for the subtle but rich storytelling and beautiful art.
A very sweet game with some very strong environmental storytelling touches. It's also a great way to get into an argument with your friends over your home decorating methods.
Took about 5 hours to 100% it. Very nostalgic ride through a life from the perspective of material things. SUper unique storytelling, well worth the money.

I liked this game, its got a very nice art style, and its cute and relaxing, apart from the 'things arent where they should be' factor. I would give this game 5/5 if it had a free mode, new objects or at least the freedom to place them wherever without a flashing red outline saying its wrong. This stressed me out a lot, and i originally picked up the game to combat my BPD fits and panic attacks. Nonetheless, i would recommend this game. The developers put a lot of effort into this, and it shows. However, a few more personal addons would make it a perfect game for me.

a delightfully cozy game with wonderful visual storytelling. go through your life going from house to house, placing your possessions in their perfect places. the art of this game is gorgeous and charming.

i reccomend doing your first playthrough with the place anwhere mode in the accessibility settings and go through the game as though it were you unpacking your home in the way youd like, turning this wonderful puzzle game into more of a life simulator.
It's a fun game but I finished it and ended it with all achievements in less than 6 focused hours. I don't regret it tough, only hoped it would have more stories.

A very relaxing game, it is kinda sad how short it is. I recommend playing only a level a night at the most to try and make it last as long as possible. The music is adorable and the game is even more adorable, I hope that some extra content gets added in the future.

Lovely 'cosy' game that had a surprisingly deep narrative subtly woven through it. As someone who loves organising and finding the right place for things, I found this enjoyable and rewarding. I hadn't expected it to have any kind of puzzle logic, so was pleasantly surprised to find that some items do have a 'right' place, or only certain places you can put them. In particular I really loved the little details of the game, like the ability to hang the toilet paper either way ('over' or 'under'), the little rattling noise a DVD or console game makes when you pick up the case (very realistic, great sound design!), and the way certain items 'age' as you progress through the game. I'd definitely recommend this as a chill game - while it's mostly relaxing, it still has some challenging bits where you have to figure things out. The only downside I'd say was that for me personally, some of the rooms still had too much clutter even when everything was put 'away'!

The game itself was great, very relaxing, but I was kind of disappointed that there was less than 4 hours of gameplay when the game cost 20€.  Wouldn't have spent so much if I had realized this beforehand. If you can get it for 10€ or less, go for it, but I would not recommend getting it for full price.
It's a very relaxing game and is also a good puzzle game. It also got my sister hooked after just seeing it once. I would definitely recommend this to others!

Unpacking is a beautiful game with good game mechanics.
The story is lovely, it is definitely as calming as it markets itself as and has nice little ideas for achievements.
While I do recommend this game, the price is quite steep for the playtime, considering I finished one run in less than three hours. 
The only other downside I figured is that I sometimes (rarely but still) had trouble figuring out what an item was supposed to be and therefore had issues knowing where you were "supposed" to place it.
Other than that, it's worth the experience for sure!

I really enjoyed this game - I found it to be very stress relieving. That being said, I think $20 is a lot of money to pay for what you're getting. It only took me 3.5 hours to complete the game, and I do really wish that there was more content for what I paid for the game.

i loved that game you get 3 hours worth of really relaxing gameplay at least thats how long it took me to play through thats my only complain i wish it would be longer
or that you could unlock an book for the babys futur but non the less i lovd the relaxing time it gave me recommend to buy it and try it

This game is so beautiful WOW. I've seen a lot of reviews complaining about the short gameplay for the $20 price, but personally I was able to squeeze about 5-6 hours of gameplay out of it and honestly, the beautiful art and audio make this game an experience that I believe is totally worth the price. I think there is definitely replay value too!

Simples (wenn auch etwas kurzes) Spiel zum relaxen.

Es kann teilweise verwirrend sein wo das als falsch platzierte Item dann tatsächlich hingehört (war aber zum glück nur die Ausnahme).

Ansonsten ein wirklich tolles Spiel :D

Una forma única de contar la historia de una vida, creativa y hermosa. Un pixel art detallado y precioso, una música relajante y pequeños y sutiles detalles sumamente especiales. Me ha encantado, he disfrutado cada momento.

What a lovely game. Very relaxing and fun. I love the developing of storyline and  hope there will be  more to unpack in the future. Definitely would recommend, if you like stress reducing puzzle games. Or Sims. Or anything anime. Its cute.
I had a lot of fun :)

Very good and peaceful game, you just unpack stuff in the new homes the character passes by, which allows for a very original narration. It's poetic and calm, with gorgeous pixel art, and the musics are really incredible, I really like the mixing of guitar with chiptune sounds.

A beautiful game that will take a few hours to complete and will leave you happy, with a super cute ending.<3

Very relaxing and oddly satisfying. I adored the unexpected story that was given to explain the journey this person takes from childhood to an adult with a family of her own. I was disappointed when it ended. I need more of this game!

Unpacking is a rather short idyllic game, despite this, It finds profound beauty in small moments. It examines all of the major moves in a protagonist's life. What I very much love about this type of found object narration is how effective a few trinkets can be to explain who a person is, what culture they are from, and what ultimately will be a step forward for them, or a step backwards.

I very much appreciate the attention to detail, the childhood toy showing wear and tear, chips in old cups, a pair of rainbow underwear. There is such a pointed difference between the feelings of moving in with friends, moving yourself into someone else's space, and the act of making room for someone you love. 

Without ever hearing the characters speak, or even seeing them directly, this game is able to capture some very real feelings through subtle nuance. Bravo.

10/10 more fun to clean than my actual room

I really enjoyed this game!
Good relaxing atmosphere, no time pressure, general freedom of unpacking and arranging the protagonists rooms! Wholesome and you get to see how they change throughout the years! A good game for winding down c:

Only thing that made me frustrated once or twice was when where I wanted to put something somewhere the red outline would come and tell me it's not supposed to be there ;-;

I just want to start off by saying that I think Unpacking is a great game, but $20 is too much to charge people for 5 hours or less of game play. This game looks beautiful and I enjoyed the music, although I do wish there were more songs as they did start to get a bit annoying after hearing the same 2 or 3 repeatedly. When I got the game I thought you could just place everything and decorate however you want.

For the most part, you can put things wherever you want. But then after you open all of the boxes, items are then highlighted red until you put the items in their correct spot. Some rooms were super small so I wanted to put stuff somewhere else where they either fit better or looked better. But the game forces you to somehow squeeze everything into a cabinet or bathroom drawer or you can't move on to the next year. I really did enjoy the game, but I caught myself getting a little frustrated often by having to make sure everything was in the right spot but would look nice to me. I wanted this game to be more relaxing and felt like it was really just a chore.

There is hardly a story at all. Sure, you can kinda get some clues about this person's life by what you unpack, but there's not a lot going on. Every room and every year you go through you're unpacking the same items repeatedly and I started to not like playing the game because of that. While I can see in real life you would most likely have a lot of the same stuff when you move, for a game, it made me want to quit. And after paying $20 for a game that seems more worth $5, I didn't want to quit. It wasn't the story keeping me going, it was just me hoping I would get my money's worth and I don't feel that I did.

So as you can see, I somehow still recommended the game. I understand most of what I said sounds negative. But I do think it's deserving of people playing it. I don't feel like there's enough going on with the story at all or enough content in it that makes this game worth anything near $20. Get this game on sale if you're interested and don't pay full price.

Very good, but very short. Even with taking my time and enjoying everything I finished it in 4.5 hours, so not worth the $20. To make it worth the price they would need to add a few more levels. It's really fun and I recommend it, however in it's current state wait till it's on sale.

I just finished this game, and I already love it to death. Not only is the art beautiful, but the story nearly made me cry at the end. I got surprisingly attached to the main character, helping her move through her life. I got attached to the same items she was attached to, and got excited whenever I noticed new developments through her life. If you're considering getting this game, please do. If anything new comes out for this game I will definitely make sure I grab it.

this game tells a really sweet honest human story, and dose so with cute almost wholesome graphics. i loved the story and the subtle way it was to and i cannot wait to go back through and find all the fun achivements!

Took me no more than 4 hours to complete overall, I love this type of games, I find them very relaxing so I take my time when playing them, but I still managed to finish it in such a short period of time. So for the money you are paying, and for the amount of playtime you're getting, I wont say it is worth it, as you can buy other games that will offer you more, but other than that,as short as it is, the game itself is amazing.
If you pay enough attention to the actual story, and not just on the "arranging stuff", it truly has an amazing and interesting story!
Personally I love the game, as it has a good story and it is amazingly calming,,
the only thing that I don't like is the price it holds, but if you can afford it, I think you should totally pick it up!!

super cute game, really loved the mildly melbournian ambience!!!! i recognised a lot of the sounds i heard and it was probably my favourite part of the game. the art was obviously incredible and the way the whole game fit together was just stunning. story was very simple but i loved it. would definitely want to see more levels in the future!!! finished within 2 days and i want moreee <3

I LOVE this game!! Its so subtle but smart with its story telling so pay attention :) It was fun to visit each place in the character's life! I just wish the game was a bit longer considering the price. It's very well made with lots of detail but Im hoping there will be updates in the future with maybe a new character or just more homes to decorate. It was very relaxing! I just unfortunately finished it in a few hours. I have no doubt that I'll revisit later on just to decorate though.

Overall this game is really soothing and it's developed quite nicely. I think, along with everyone else, we just want more levels. Maybe make multiple stories in the journals and each one is a new story. This game did come out recently so it makes sense that there isn't much. Just hoping there will be an update with more to it for the price I paid!

Very calming, it helped me with my anxiety, and I loved finding out the story as I played through the game.
10/10 would recommend, and it's worth the 20 bucks you pay for it.

Yes, the hype is real! It's worth believing in a team that's willing to commit to releasing a completed project and go "There, it's done". It's worth respecting how much this particular game feels not uncompleted, but rather "oh no, I want to never not be playing this game, help!". It may be short, but it's eminently replayable, has plenty of easter egg achievements, and is simply joyous in an almost retro-feeling way,

That having been said, Unpacking is prime for the mod scene. The devs haven't made a statement about adding the feature, but a lot of people are asking, and it could extend the game life to...well, infinite. Haven't you always wanted to make a mosh pit full of piggy pixel plushies? Pimagine pthe possibilities!

Either way, "I want more" is the only problem you'll face in this deeply pleasant and relaxing experience. Don't miss it, and if you're waffling on your vote, go ahead and hand it over! It earns it.

While simple in mechanics and relatively short in length, this game clearly had a lot of love and care put into an enjoyable and calming experience. I especially admired the more subtle storytelling almost entirely conveyed through visual context and very minor bits of text. Watching the narrator grow, change, and experience life through locations and objects alone caused me to reflect on my own past residences and what items were most important to me in those moments. The pixel art was equal parts adorable and detailed along with the mellow soundtrack really selling that "zen" feeling the game was going for. Overall, Unpacking was a fantastic and tranquil little journey that left me wanting more. I would be ecstatic if this game somehow spawned an entire unpacking/organizing genre. 9/10

This game made me cry, but in a good way. The gameplay may be short but the storytelling and small details are incredible. Moving through the person's life, seeing their possessions (pink pig!) stay with them through the years and seeing photos of them and friends/lovers pop up on fridge magnets is so heartwarming and emotional.

Well done to the makers for creating such an amazing game.

like all new games there will be a few "cons". [h1]Amazing game. Don't be fooled, this is not just about unpacking, it's about how we define the spaces around us.[/h1]

At the start the game is so simple. Unpack the boxes so every item has a home. Forks in the drawer, shirts in the wardrobe and books on the shelf.

But as you unpack more, the game strikes you on another level. It will make you think about the things you own? What objects are so important that they follow you everywhere, like a childhood toy or a cherished photo, and what things are just needed out of necessity?

The game reminds us of the importance of a home, a space where you can truly be yourself. A space that we try to build with colours, sounds and textures that nourish. You decide whether a good home is one that is pristine for visitors, or jam-packed full of life.

The game will ask you questions about how we live with others. How do we compromise over spaces that we share? And, are we ever able to join another's person's life without any cost to them or our ourselves? 

Ultimately Unpacking is about making order of our lives inside, often when order can be hard to find outside. How you order your life, is up to you.

I've played through this game 3x now so I've updated my review...

---{ Graphics }---
Absolutely adorable! I love the retro 90s aesthetic of this game. It reminds me of the life sim games I enjoyed in my youth. 

---{ Gameplay & Story }---
This game is a very calm, no-stress simple puzzle game. You're unpacking boxes and trying to put things in the rooms where they belong, following through the story line of the packer's life. There are some items that are required to go in specific rooms/places but, for the most part, the game allows you to freely place and decorate your rooms however you'd like. 

You're playing as a female illustrator/artist, following her journey...
- Unpacking her childhood room in a new home (1997) 
- Unpacking her first college apartment (2004) 
- Unpacking her items into her post-grad shared apartment, a space that's already cramped with the possessions of her messy roommates (2007) 
- Unpacking her items into the city apartment of her boyfriend, a space where you can move things around but find there's really not enough room for you when you realize you can't put up one of your most prized possessions (2010)
- Unpacking her downsized possessions post-break up into your move back into her childhood home (2012)
- Unpacking her new life into a small apartment of her own (2013)
- Unpacking a few new boxes of things into the same small apartment with items she accumulated from living overseas for work (2017)
- Unpacking into a new home, with her family (2018)

This game is something you can easily play through while you're sipping on a cup of coffee/tea in the morning/evening. I've done so 3x already and still find enjoyment in this game. It's the perfect cozy game when you need to just take your mind off things and play a game that isn't stressful and doesn't have rigorous game play.

---{ Audio }---
Calm, relaxing music. There are some moments where you can interact with items (such as the boomboxes, toys, computer, etc) that make music and noise, which I enjoyed.

---{ Audience }---
I think the target audience best fit for this particular game is adult women, especially millennial women who grew up through the 90s-early 00s. That being said, this game can definitely be played and enjoyed by anyone! I would buy this for yourself if you're an 80s/90s/00s young girlie. If your girlfriend or daughter is just getting into gaming or isn't into typical time-intensive rpg games (yet), this game would make an excellent gift and introductory game for them. 

---{ Difficulty }---
Very easy to learn.

---{ Game Time }---
Approximately 1 to 2.5 hours, depending on what your goal is. If you just want to "unpack" as quickly as possible, game time will be closer to 45 minutes to 1 hour (not recommended). If you want to take your time, get to explore the little quirks of the character you're playing as exploring her rooms and possessions and focus on decorating, then game time is closer to 2+ hours. 

---{ Price }---
Honestly, worth every penny but I would recommend waiting for it to go on sale, simply because there's really only a couple hours of game play.


---{ Recommendations If You Liked This Game }---
If you played through this game and enjoyed it, I highly recommend Assemble With Care (also available on Steam). It's another simple puzzle game that's got a similar feel to Unpacking. I highly recommend both, equally.

---{ Overall Impression }---
***WARNING: SPOILERS AHEAD***
 I ADORE the story line of this game. Going from moving into your own room as a child, to moving into your college dorm, to living with roommates as a new grad, to trying to fit yourself into your boyfriend's apartment, moving back in with your parents when that relationship fails, moving into your very own place, moving into a home with your family - it's the story of a typical Millennial  that I think can resonate with a lot of people. 

It's the little details that I really enjoyed in this game. The mismatched plates, bowls, and cups in your first apartment, realizing there's no where to put your diploma when you move in with your partner (as someone who lived with an emotionally abusive person once upon a time, that part especially got me right in the feels), the little D&D figure that follows you around and doesn't get painted until you move into your own place and rediscover yourself, the postcards that show the people you've gained/lost throughout your life, the little souvenir trinkets that are collected throughout your journey, and (of course) the stuffed pig that slowly gets torn apart and stitched back together, eventually finding it's new home in your child's nursery. It's a very sweet story line and I really appreciated the beauty of it. 

The biggest downside and only major criticism I have of this game is that it's too short. I truly wish it was longer!!! I hope they create an expansion to this or provide an update with more content (such as her journey further into adulthood or maybe a variation where you see her husband or child's life unfold... I mean "unpack").

Unpacking is a short, sweet puzzle game that sounds much more simple than it is. Following the life of one person, you unpack their life over the years, and get to know them through the various objects they bring along each time. A sweet story with a happy ending, unpacking provides a chill yet engaging puzzle. The game has a "right place" to provide a challenge, but if you want to decorate freely, you can change this in settings. If you're looking for a unique puzzle game, this is the one for you.

Ein kurzweiliges Spiel, das subtil eine Geschichte einer Frau erzählt. Die Spielmechanik macht durchweg Spaß. Jeder Gegenstand, der ausgepackt wird, erzählt eine Geschichte. Es wäre schön gewesen, wenn es mehrere Enden hätte, da mir das tatsächliche Ende etwas gezwungen wirkte.

Spoiler:
Mir hat es nicht sehr gefallen, dass hier eine toxische Beziehung mit einem stereotypischen Mann eingegangen wird. Klar, die gibt es, keine Frage und Frauen fühlen sich nach so einer Geschichte vielleicht auch mehr dem gleichen Geschlecht hingezogen. Das wirkte für mein Gefühl jedoch alles zu sehr aufgesetzt. Sie war sich in ihren jungen Jahren, so wie ich das jetzt interpretiere, nicht sicher, wer sie ist. Sie wusste zwar sehr genau, was sie will, jedoch nicht, wer sie war. Mag sein, dass der toxische Kerl ihr die Augen öffnete, aber auch da hätte sie durchaus auch mehrere Beziehungen mit anderen Frauen (Mitsamt Ein- und Auszug) durchmachen können, bevor sie die richtige gefunden hätte. Das Ende war schön. Den Weg dahin empfand ich jedoch als schwierig. Heutzutage sollten solche Stereotypen (auch was die Frau selbst in ihrer Rolle betrifft) nicht in der Form herausgearbeitet sein, Menschen sind nicht einsilbig. Die Vielschichtigkeit eines Menschen wird hier nicht ausgenutzt. (Frau liebt Blumen, Kuscheltiere, malt gerne und spielt gerne Gemeinschaftsspiele und Nintendo, während der "Kerl" anscheinend nur seine Hanteln und Eiweispulver im Kopf hat, wenn er nicht gerade irgendein Kriegsspiel auf seiner (natürlich) X-Box zockt oder oldschool mäßig den Plattenspieler nutzt.
Sehr schönes Spiel um sich mal wieder Kreativ aus zuleben. Für Jeden der sich auch gerne mal stundenlang bei der Raumgestaltung verliert.

marie kondo prepared me for this.

IF YOU LIKE: Animal Crossing, The Sims, A Short Hike, Stardew Valley

PROS:
- HEARTWARMING STORY: never realized how effectively you could tell a story only through showcasing a person's possessions and living spaces, and how much i would like it. [spoiler]lesbians, this game is for u btw.[/spoiler]
- RELAXING: pleasant soundtrack and a no pressure to finish anything quickly. feel free to rearrange your room and furniture as long as it takes, and explore it all. however, i completed the main game in one sitting, <4 hour for one full playthrough.
- DETAILED: incredibly detailed pixel art considering how many different angles every item can be viewed at. i doubt that i saw every sprite the game had to offer even after turning 300+ items in all 4 directions.
- QUALITY > QUANTITY: things like [spoiler]drawers not opening when there's an item in front of it tickled me, and items slowly degrading through the years such as the protag's wall posters developing tears and folds as they're unpacked, or an exe's photograph with a pin through the middle[/spoiler] tells me the devs had some artistic eyes looking into this game. pretty much the embodiment of environmental storytelling. some of the achievements were cute to discover as well.

CONS:
- ...SHORT FOR THE PRICE: considering the full price, i would have wanted more levels to complete. i got this as a gift and therefore for free, but i wouldn't have purchased this at full price. i would be interested to see this game expanded or perhaps done with different characters.
- MOUSE AND KEYBOARD OPTIMIZED: i wanted to play this with my controller and kick back but ended up playing with M+K since some of the precise pointing could only really be achieved quickly with the mouse. totally possible to play either way, and there was no problem to plug and play, but my goopy goblin gamer brain didn't like how imprecise the controller felt.

SUMMARY:
grab this on sale for a cute little game to unwind and experience. excellent gift game, best enjoyed with a warm cup of tea.

There's more story in this game than there is in the entirety of Twilight, and attention to details blew my mind.
I fully recommend this game to anyone that just needs to have some laid back hours and unwind

i would recommend this because the game is so calming and so fun to choose where to place objects and there is a bit of challenge that keep wanting more and the  storyline keeps me always on my toes trying to figure out what makes this person so unique. so overall great game
This game was so much fun. It was short and sweet and I would recommend to anyone. Watching things grow and change was so heartwarming and definitely my favorite aspect of the game.

loved everything about this, it is very cute game with a sweet story alongside it, I just wish it wasn't so short, the game is a bit expensive for what you get if the game had more levels or updates then the price is fine, I do feel that how short the game is it should be cheaper.

3.3 hours to complete the story, and I enjoyed every second of it.

I would not be surprised if Unpacking is used in the future as a star example of environmental storytelling, there are so many depths and aspects of the character and their life that you learn with basically no text.
Seeing what items are brought with them, what new ones are collected, and which ones are left behind.

And this is a REALLY GOOD story, like, I was genuinely surprised how much some of this made me feel and I don't want to spoil a second of it.

Absolutely wonderful little game, there's just enough clutter you have to get creative, but not enough to ever frustrate. Only wish that there was more of it.

10/10

Heartwarming and beautiful. Made me cry a couple of times. Also incredible storytelling for a game without dialogues. Definitely my favorite feel-good game so far. <3
