I wasn't expecting such a subtle yet moving storytelling.

At first I was frustrated to discover that some objects actually need to be place in a specific area in order to be able to move on to the next level. Wasn't the concept of the game to just be able to arrange your stuff as you please? As I moved on to other levels my frustration grew as the limitations multiplied, culminating to a point where I was forced to put very important and meaningful object under the rug because there just was no other place to put it (as well as having to sort out someone else's underwear in order to have an extra drawer...). 
Then it struck me. This game is actually incredibly clever in making you go through the emotions of your character, through different periods of their life. Depending on where you move into, and with whom, the fact that you can or can't arrange the space as you please is a reflection of how much your character is allowed to invest their new living space. Once you stop seeing this game as a random relaxing game but rather as a pleasant puzzle game with very clever storytelling, you'll be able to fully apprecieate how much of a gem this game is.

Unpacking is a truly remarkable game. A completely unique narrative experience that takes full advantage of its unique gameplay mechanic. As of writing this, I've done one playthrough of the game, and have not yet gone back to find all the various nooks and crannies I missed, although I'm sure I will in time.

The game itself is a remarkably personal experience, that manages to perfectly capture a very particular sort of mood. It highlights both the excitement and the tedium of moving into a new place (although the tedium in this case is more just an initial feeling of "Woah, that's a lot of stuff to put away," the actual gameplay is anything but, except in a rare instance when you completely misunderstood what an object was, or when you need to find a place to put that damn colander.) It's truly astonishing just how much character and personality the developers are able to convey through just showing us this person's life, and there's many incredible moments when they manage to convey something incredibly specific without using a single word.

On the negative side, the game is short. I've played for 4 hours and I've already beaten the game, and, while I personally think the game was worth it, it is a fairly steep price for what amounts to not a lot of game. However, if the worst thing you can say about a game is that you wish there was more of it, that's a pretty good problem to have. I suppose I'll just hope for post-launch content for this, or that the developers are planning on  follow-up game. The novelty of this sort of game may wear off at some point, but I'm willing to take that chance.

This is an incredibly cute game. The visuals are very nice to look at, the soundtrack to the game fits well with each level and helps to convey the emotion of the level and to add context to that point in the game. This kind of game falls in the experience category, something that you will likely play once and maybe again in a year or two, or if they add more levels, its something incredibly easy to come back to. The only real issues that I have with the game, are that sometimes when a music track ends there is an incredibly long pause before any music starts to play again, not something that took me out of the game but felt like I should mention it. And what they want you to do with the items and where they are supposed to go isn't always the most clear, and also changes from some early levels into later levels, again not a big negative, but more just something I noticed. The biggest thing to people looking at this game; Is it worth the 20 dollar price point? To me, this was a very fun and pleasant experience, I enjoyed the narrative I was being told about our person and seeing how their life goes on and progress's, I really liked the gameplay, its relaxing and something very different although I would like maybe a freeplay mode or maybe a way to play individual levels over again. I am glad I bought this game, it is a fun, tight, three hour long game that I really enjoyed, and I would say it was worth my twenty dollars, and I am looking forward to whatever they decide to do next.

This game proves that there are still new and interesting ways to make video games out there. I'm amazed at the level of storytelling that was conveyed only through the environment, this is such a special game.

For those of you who enjoy casual games, especially those with a soothing soundtrack and lots of little easter eggs to be found, you owe it to yourself to play Unpacking.  This one comes from a small team at Witch Beam Games in Australia, and is a far cry from their last game Assault Android Cactus, which was a bullet-hell twin stick shooter.  The most action you’ll get in Unpacking is, well, none at all.  

It’s quite a relaxing affair, as you’re able to take your time and sort through your belongings and find each one a new place as you move into your new space.  This plays out over several years, beginning with your first room as a child, then moving to college, and so on, with a new page being added to the scrapbook of your life.  Along the way, you’ll bring some familiar items, and learn a bit more about yourself, your goals and ambitions, your hobbies, and the people you live with.  

The story, as vague as it is, does wrap up nicely at the end, without tying up all the loose ends, which is my favorite type of ending since I can still imagine what happens after this chapter closes.  The gameplay is very pleasing too, with a place for everything, and eventually everything in its place, it’s like if Marie Kondo and Tetris had a baby.  Home decoration on shelves and invisible grids, with very little room for error, but you never feel stressed about it either.  

There are several little easter eggs that can grant you stickers and Steam achievements, if you need something to work on after you’ve finished the game.  It has a nice photo mode to showcase your room after you’ve finished, and a gif maker to show your entire unpacking process in each room.  

In all, I spent about 4 hours playing, and I can't complain about the price.  I pay $12 to go see a 2 hour movie with no replay value, and I actually will probably replay Unpacking a bit to get all the achievements.

I've figured out items I couldn't piece together based on the sound it mad when I put it on a counter. 

[h1] Something important I want to highlight based on other reviews [/h1] 
A lot of people have shown frustrations about the placement requirement for all the items. To me i see this as it's story mode, as this requirement has helped contribute to the story telling of the whole game. To many other people however, this makes the game much harder, much more frustrating, and hard to understand the dev's ideas on what should and shouldn't be placed. 

To this, there is a workaround in the accessibility options. An option to allow items anywhere. Want to be that person to put a toaster in the bedroom? Wanted to show off that brush on the sink instead of the drawer? Just that one option to allow items everywhere fixes that and lets you enjoy the game in a sandbox mode. I hope that this helps people pick up the game if that feature was a dealbreaker.

[h1] TL;DR [/h1]

This game is amazing and can be enjoyed with and without the required item placements, so please give this labor of love from a family dev team a chance.

( Edit 30 Apr 2022: Okay, I didn't know about Dark Star mode until the devs announced it. DEFINITELY gave me more of a puzzle and much more fun to do!!! )

Main problems: same items, same room layouts, can't move furniture around.

What I would like to see:
Anything that brings variety to the layouts and the items. This could be in community-created areas, or user assets, or even something like weekly challenge rooms.

Community-made rooms would be fun, where players can create a room and use furniture from a larger inventory, and submit for others to unpack in. Maybe the items would be selected as well, or possibly with tiers, such as "Minimalist," "Cluttered," and "Overloaded" to indicate the number of items to unpack and store.

It would be nice to have other storylines to explore as well. The main one is cute, but of course... 20 years of someone's life played within 4 hours is a bit disappointing.

Custom rooms and a wider variety of items would add to the replay value. Overall, the game is tied very, very strongly to the storyline of unpacking someone else's life and learning about them from the items they have and the brief notes from their photo album. Once that story is played, there isn't anything else to play. Even with the "block-fitting puzzle," there isn't enough challenge in the rooms other than possibly the year 2010 to make it a puzzle--there's often extra space to place things, so I never felt like it was a puzzle to fit things in. Just a matter of figuring out what the game wanted when items were highlighted in red (which can be turned off).

The gif and photo features may be more fun with additional items in-game. These features are excellent in terms of their aesthetic appeal, but there are not enough places to unpack or enough items for me to feel like I can contribute anything unique.

Negatives:
- shorter game for it's price tag of 20 USD
- I wish that there was more freedom to move preset items that do not come from your boxes.
- Some items don't fit in places they could realistically go (My biggest issue was the nail clippers fighting almost every place in the bathrooms that I chose.) *Not sure if this is a bug or if it's just how the game decides where things should be placed.

While I wish the game was expanded and had more content, that doesn't outweigh the positives for me. I truly think that this game is fun for those looking to unpack a person's home. I've always loved organizational games, and if that's something you enjoy, I recommend. :)

The only Con I can mention is that it's a but short. I love it and want more! It's a great game! Definitely worth the money, and I would love to see where they go from here.

Despite being very short, this game really is fantastic. The visual style is great, and the soundtrack is enjoyable. I haven't encountered gameplay like this before, so suffice to say it is definitely really refreshing to play. Hoping to see more content come from this creator, and DLC.

To be upfront, I turned the puzzle part of the game off before I even played, because I loved the idea of this game and also wanted the complete freedom to put whatever I wanted in each part of the house. I honestly don't think it truly impeded my play, which was great. All in all, this game is absolutely wonderful. The story is beautiful and touching, it's fun to play (even with the puzzle aspect I imagine it's fun trying to figure out where the game wants you to put everything, but I absolutely love decorating games and have since I was a kid, so this was enjoyable and nostalgic for me), and while it might not have much replay value, it's almost inspiring in a way? Like this game showed me that things aren't always going to go well, but in the end it's probably gonna turn out alright and I've just gotta stick around til I get to the good times. This was an incredibly relaxing and enjoyable game for me, and if I could go back and play it again for the first time I would love to. Honestly in a few months when that good ole depression memory loss kicks in I'll find this game again and have just as much fun playing it again. Love the art style, the charm of the little knick-knacks that follow our main character throughout their journey, and the music. Great game. Honestly I would also love if there was just ONE more level to decorate where it really brought you full circle, because [spoiler] it would be so much fun to be able to decorate the child's room as a teenager just like you decorated the main character's bedroom as a kid. If there was even more where we could follow the child's life as well that would be even better. [/spoiler]
Edit: I was right! It's been a little while since I first played and I just played through it again and loved it just as much as I did the first time (and earned some very cute achievements, too). It might be a bit pricey for the amount of game play it actually offers, but it's still an incredibly adorable game and I will love it forever.

Ao mesmo tempo que é um jogo relaxante, é muito viciante.
No momento em que estou escrevendo eu só tenho 4 horas e pouco de jogo, mas já perdi a conta de quantas vezes minha mão dormiu por serem horas seguidas kkkkkk
A arte do jogo é impecável e o jogo te guia caso as coisas não se encaixem, porém não fica super óbvio, o que o torna um desafio!
Super recomendo :)

Игра милая и незамысловатая. Понравилось, как через вещи и детали рассказали историю главной героини, ее предпочтения, а также предпочтения окружающих ее в разные годы людей.  Хотелось бы еще увидеть уровни после рождения ребенка, как меняется обстановка в доме, пока он растет. В последнем переезде есть ощущение, что должен быть уровень с гаражом, но он недоступен. Надеюсь, что игру доработают и откроют новые локации.
Все удивляются количеству трусцов, а меня вот удивило количество лифчиков :D
[spoiler] Не обошлось и без лgбt, ну как в наше время без этого.. [/spoiler]
8 из 10 коробочек для переезда.

A sweet and charming game about unpacking that not only satisfies the desire to be organised, but also gives an underlying story told through the items you place and the spaces you display them in. Very relaxing and with not only a great soundtrack, but amazing foley sound work to enhance the experience! I spent lots of time placing things on every possible surface to hear what each item sounds like. If you think of rearranging your rooms often, or just want a cute art style, I seriously recommend this game. <3

I liked the creativity of the game as well as the consistency in objects. It makes you see the person's life. The only thing I don't like is how short it is. You aren't able to play for very long. You can tell that a lot of time and effort was put into this game but it's just a very short game. Even if you only do one level a day it'll take you less than a week to complete. I couldn't stop playing the game though because it is so good but it only took me 3 days.

Jogo muito legal e relaxante de jogar. No primeiro dia joguei por duas horas sem nem perceber. Em algumas fases, o ambiente pode ser bem desafiador para encaixar tudo no lugar, o que eu achei muito legal. O desenvolvimento da história dá vários detalhes sobre o que a personagem está passando e é muito envolvente passar por cada fase. Além da trilha sonora que é muito gostosa de ouvir, bem relaxante.

I bought this game the day it launched and I've played this game to the end three times already and I plan on continuing to do so! It's such a relaxing experience and I find new ways to organize the rooms each time! This is a must-have for anyone craving an organizational/relaxing game to just pass the time or keep your hands busy while you listen to a podcast or something in the background!
Really interesting no-words-needed storytelling experience! Special thumbs up for just the right length of the game and no drama ending

the game is pretty fun but i dont know if id say $20 fun. i wish you could have more freedom when placing things. i was really excited for the game because i saw it on tiktok but i kinda felt let down to find theres only 7 levels. overall its fun but i hope they come out with more to do.

Oh my goodnesssss
This is such an amazing game. It is so relaxing, so cute, and the story is fantastic. The story telling is so unique, and really made me feel like a part of this person's life as they moved from place to place. I do wish the game was longer. I played it in an afternoon, and although it has a very satisfying ending, I want more! So hopefully, there will be more locations/story in future updates.

Short and sweet little game, completed it in a few hours and was genuinely disappointed that it was over. Played it again start to finish today and finished unlocking all the achievements. Absolutely hope that this game gets expanded on in the future, or that the dev makes something similar, and hopefully a little longer.

I'll echo the sentiments of several other reviews and say that the price is a little steep for the amount of gameplay, but I don't regret my purchase at all.

This game is a very relaxing & fun level based puzzle game. You move through the life of our MC from her very first solo room as a child up to adulthood. As we go through the levels we learn about her through her items & spaces. We see what she values and what she gives up or moves on from which allows us to form a bond with the MC and root for her in her life. This game holds so much realism to the daily struggles some of us face while also being a perfect escape in to something we can have more control over and enjoy.

I hope we get more DLCs or a 2nd game that follows a new character as I loved this style and storytelling.

Honestly an amazing game with an awesomely unique way of telling a story. Been waiting for this to come out since I played the demo a long time ago. Absolutely worth it! Definitely check it out. It's super clear that the developers put a lot of thought and energy into this game. So well done.

Absolutely adore this game, would 100% recommend it.

The game, the style, the storytelling, reminds me a lot of Gone Home, and the games of Angela He, so if you like those, and you like room decorating, and you like story-telling puzzle games, I think you'll like this.

I love puzzle story-telling games, and more than that, I really, really love games that tell a story through objects, and this went for that in a really direct way that worked out very well. No dialogue except the photo captions after a level, no names to put to the characters we meet, and yet, you can create a story in your mind told through the objects you're unpacking, the rooms you're unpacking them into. You feel the hurt, you celebrate the happy. It's a good game.

I also appreciated the thoughtfulness of the accessibility menu and its options, I think a lot of game devs could take note from that.

This is a very short game, though, I played it through in a few hours. I've replayed it several times, though, and I don't mind short story games, anyway. I'd really, really love to see the devs update this with more stories, I think it's maybe a bit high priced for the length of the game currently.

Just a note as I've seen this problem in a few other reviews: This is a puzzle game, not a sandbox decorating game, there are rules as to where certain things can be placed. If you don't like this, there's an option in the accessibility menu to shut this off and play it as a decorating game. That really should not be reason for a negative review, as not only is it clearly stated, but it's also optional.
100% chill. Details matter and tell a story. You can make your own choices where things go - although some things are not allowed (no, you may not store the hair appliances in the sink ;)

Ein wirklich detailverliebtes und entspannendes Game. Es wird nebenbei eine kleine Geschichte erzählt und wer auf Pixelgrafik steht, wird hier auf jeden Fall in den Genuss kommen. Es ist besonders spannend für die Menschen, die in den 90er Jahren geboren wurden, da viele Gegenstände einem bekannt vor kommen.

Man kann sich bei dem Spiel Mühe geben oder es schnell durchspielen, dafür finde ich es aber fast ein bisschen zu teuer. (Habe es geschenkt bekommen und hätte es nur im Sale gekauft).

Amazing game! Very satisfying, and the story-telling was top-notch.

Not much replayability unfortunately. I'm really hoping they add some DLC or something!

I wish there was a middling button. The art is cute, and the process is relaxing. A very enjoyable game, if it weren't only 3 hours long, and also cost as much as it did. I don't think the cost of the game is worth the content available, however, I hope this means they'll be updating and adding more as time goes on.

For an Indie game, I will have to say this is a beautiful, simple and calming game. I know some felt it was short for it's price but to me it felt just right. Seeing the growth of the character through their choices of item and furniture is interesting and reminded me of some items I have kept since childhood till now. I enjoyed this game. Good job to the team!

Great game! Both wholesome and addictive, I always wanted to go back to it to put things in order.  Not too short nor too long. It was nice to pin point things I used to know/own and I think a lot of people can relate to at least a few of the items or to the narrative. I'll most likely play it again. I recommend it.

Sehr schönes Spiel.
Klar kann man das Spiel in 2 Stunden durchspielen, aber ich glaube so ist es nicht gedacht.
Es geht eher darum Sachen auszupacken und sich auch etwas über die Person dabei zu denken.
Ich war etwas verwundert wie der Berg mit unnötigem Kram gewachsen ist....sag sehr viel zu der wirklichen Welt aus.

Was ich besonders schön finde ist das es eine Video Funktion gibt.
Das macht mich immer etwas glücklich wenn man doch bedenkt wo der ganze Kram hin soll.

Ich finde gute Spiele dürfen etwas kosten.
Man darf nie vergessen was hinter so einem Spiel auch für Arbeit steckt :)
I love this game it's really amazing with all the graphics  and the vibes of it are really great I just wish that there would be more levels and rooms to unpack

Man geht den Weg vom ersten eigenen Kinderzimmer bis zur eigenen Familie mit einer kreativen und Fantasy-begeisterten Künstlerin, nur über das auspacken von Kartons. 
Dieses Spiel ist entspannend, schöne Musik, nette Grafiken. Manchmal war es mir ein Rätsel, was die einzelnen Gegenstände darstellen sollten. Ich liebe es zu Sortieren, so liebte ich auch die Einrichtung dieser Zimmer. 
Leider muss ich sagen, dass dieses Spiel recht kurz ist... ich habe es nun in einem Durchgang innerhalb von 4 Stunden durchgespielt. Um alle Sticker zu sammeln könnte ich es jetzt nochmal spielen, aber ich denke das wäre mir jetzt doch zu langweilig. 
Ich gönne dem Entwickler für seine Idee, seine Mühe usw seinen Lohn, aber für knapp 20€ hätte ich mir ein paar mehr Level gewünscht. Raum für mehr wäre da, immerhin geht das Leben ja noch weiter! 
Trotzdem ein sehr schönes Spiel!

Unglaublich wie sehr mir das spielen gefallen hat <3 sehr viele Details und liebevoll gestaltet, und dann auch noch eine schöne Geschichte wird erzählt einfach Faszinierend <3 Ich wünschte mir mehr Levels, es war leider so schnell vorbei :( aber auf jeden Fall das Geld wert <3 <3 <3
Bought this after watching Many a true Nerd's video. This game is a very enjoyable experience, very relaxing and slow. I find playing this game is similar to how I feel when playing townscaper.

Aie Aie Aie ! Difficile de laisser un commentaire sur ce jeu ! Le jeu est beau, bien fait, sympathique et émouvant (on déballe les cartons d'une jeune femme à chacun de ses déménagements et on la suit donc à travers les étapes de sa vie et à au fil de ses emménagements, sans jamais la voir, mais on finit par la connaitre un peu : style vêtements, son métier, ses amours...) mais quand même ! 4 heures de jeu en prenant mon temps... Deux niveaux de plus n'auraient pas été du luxe et m'auraient donné l'impression d'en avoir pour mon argent...
It's a very agreable game to play. Relaxing atmosphere, adorable graphism, simple gameplay, i hope there will be additional "storyline" to follow in the future to enjoy more of this game.

A lovely little game that made me surprisingly emotional. When the credits rolled I was a bit taken aback that it was already over, but then again I'm glad it didn't outstay its welcome. Very cute, very sweet, very lovingly made.

A very sweet, relaxing game. Sometimes figuring out where stuff was supposed to go could be puzzling, but I found enjoyment in organizing and styling rooms. The story is subtle, but truly built into the environment by the game's nature, and packs a good punch when you realize a story beat, made all the sweeter by having to put the pieces together yourself. It's a fairly short game, but there's some good replay value, not just in searching out secrets but also in simply playing through it again and seeing how you'd arrange things differently with another go around. All in all, I'd say it's definitely worth a try, at the very least.
游戏呢是好游戏，休闲治愈。就是你卖70块钱就这么点内容是不是过于坑了，建议实在想玩的立即购买（跟我一样），现在不想玩的等着打折再买吧！还在意犹未尽呢给我整通关了，希望能更新多加点内容！
아기자기하고 귀엽고 재밌어요 정리덕후들 추천~ 가끔 대체 이게뭐지 싶은것들 있음.. 내맘대로 정리하고싶지만 안되는 것들도 있음ㅋㅋㅋ

I loved this game! I for sure thought it was worth $20. Sad that other people didn't agree. I would love if they came out with DLC and maybe had a different family story. I loved the story! There is also so many little details that I think really make this game so amazing! So relaxing and fun! I do agree that there isn't much replayability but I still would recommend this game if you want a super relaxing, organization game! I really loved it!

I enjoyed this game so much. I like how we follow the main characters' journey as well. Whenever we move to a new house, some of their things felt familiar. Love the concept! <3 

It's a very relaxing game, I really adore puzzle games so I got obsessed and attach real quick. Anyways, I hope there will be more! Thank you for making this game!

A delightful light puzzle game where you get to sort things and make pleasant arrangements. Very soothing. And then a playback feature to see all your anxious indecision roll before your eyes! XD Or to make fun stop-motion movies out of. Super cute, super wholesome.

There's a nice little story that creates touching moments and fun surprises. It's affecting because it's taking a long view of a life through moments of significant change, and the game's better for having it, but ultimately the story is fairly safe and isn't the main draw of the game.  It's not a story meant for challenging the audience, showing any particular perspective, or making us reflect on our own lives - except maybe to reflect on our own relationships with the objects we have in our homes. 
Oh, and there are objects specific to certain communities and subcultures, which I really enjoyed seeing crop up. :)

Outstanding visual storytelling through unique gameplay. A fascinating way to tell the story of a person's life through the spaces and the items you unpack. Loved the little details, like a pushpin through the face of a person after a breakup or little damages to items that have been through several moves. Loved the sound design and how different objects interact with surfaces. Absolutely loved playing this and would highly recommend it.

Now to get back to unpacking my real life apartment!

It's EXTREMELY short (beat the whole "story" mode in around 2 hours) and doesn't have anything to add to the replay value such as alternate characters to play with. I'd recommend getting this when it drops down to $10 or even $5.

I just wish there was more content, I finished the entire game, start to finish, went back and rearranged the rooms and unlocked all of the achievements in 4 hours. It was super relaxing to play and I'd love more levels that just feel like puzzles and they wouldn't even necessarily need a story.

Great game. If you want a mentally little bit tiring - bc of the constant thinking it requires - but relaxing chill puzzle game, with amazing story without any narrative, and beautiful pixel graphics, its your game to choose.

The game is relitively short and I finished it in only 3 hours but would definetly play again. 10/10 The main character is gay because they own a flannel and doc martins lol

Very satisfying game! Completed the story and all achievements in a little over seven hours. I became a little obsessed and spent a full hour at a time playing because it was hard to stop. The music, art style and sound effects made it a very chill, relaxing experience.

I have waited for this game for so long, and now that it is finally out I have enjoyed it immensely. The fact that a story can be told by objects is beautiful to me. I will say there are some object placing that are not "correct" that bother me, but I get it you can't just place certain things anywhere. Overall, highly recommend, this game was worth the wait. (side note the music is really calming and beautiful).

7,5/10 - It's nostalgic, beautiful and relaxing

**Spoilers ahead** 

Concept - really really good
Price - well... 

First off- the game is relaxing. It calmed me down since Im pretty much of a clean freak. What I like about this game, is that there are endless ways to organize the items so long they are placed in the right area. I find the background music relaxing as well and does not stress me out in one bit. It's funny how the clutter of other people irritated me though. 

I like the detail were you are not allowed to touch some of the items, so it can be a little challenging where to put your desired items by not moving other people's things. Another detail that I love is that when we moved in with our first partner. it reminds me of how it was moving in my partner as well. I was free to move his things so I could occupy it. I love the fact it's not just a puzzle game because there's a story nestled in the game and it's open to interpretation of what happened throughout the mc's life. 

Sometimes, you quite need to pay attention to some photos and the new items coming in to get a gist of what's going on, but not necessarily. I do recommend this game, the downside is, it wont be for everyone. This game requires a little patience and can get easily mundane since you have the freedom to almost put the items wherever you want. But some of the items' locations just do not make sense to me. As for the pricing, I do not know, where I'm from it costed me 15 dollars. I do not discuss much about the pricing, but I felt like it was good already? maybe- They worked so hard in it, so I do not mind having to own this game forever for 15 usd ;v;

All in all, for me, my 6 hours was definetely well spent. I came to like this game and I would readily buy an exapansion ( if they were to have one in the future )

I really liked how you go through their life story and you get to guess what's going on or build the story yourself. It's just a shame that the game is so short - or maybe I just had such a good time that I didn't see the time pass. Totally recommend it!

I went into this game expecting a relaxing tidying up simulator, but instead I got more of an emotional journey.  Absolutely brilliant subtle storytelling, wonderful sound design, and attention to detail that shows a great amount of care and effort. I bought it on a whim and have never been more pleasantly surprised by a game in my life.

Ich finde das Spiel sehr entspannend und auch teilweise sehr niedlich und interessant was man so alles wieder finde nach dem Umzug aber ich finde für 20 € hat das Spiel zu wenig Inhalt. Ich hoffe sehr das da noch was kommt, in Form von einem Update und nicht einem DLC was man dann auch noch bezahlen müsste.
Also alles in allem ein schönes Spiel aber zu kurz.

It's a chill, simple puzzle game.  No time limit, just making everything fit.

The story at first seems like just an excuse for the central puzzle mechanic, but it's surprisingly poignant and the ending credits are worth listening through. 

The graphics are a simple pixel style, but executed excellently so and the details in the items you're unpacking tell quite a story detailing the life of the person you're unpacking for.

All in all it's an excellent game and well worth the 3 hours or so to play it

The game gave a cute and somewhat emotional 3 hours of gameplay, but I'm not sure it's worth the price point. Maybe grab it while it's on sale?
That being said, it was both satisfying and emotionally compelling. I could particularly relate as lots of the things the character owned, I would have or have actually owned.

Das Spiel macht Spaß, ist entspannend und die Geschichte wird auf eine ganz interessante Weise erzählt.
Ich kann das Spiel zwar auf jeden Fall weiterempfehlen, finde den Preis für ca. 2,5h Spielzeit aber etwas teuer.
Lovely, relaxing game. Finished in 4.5 hours, which is NOT worth the $20 price. But if you can get it on sale, then it might be the game for you. Recommending for when it's on sale.

Super charming and lovely game. The art is fantastic, and so are all of the tiny little audio details! Got a good amount of re-playability as well, I played through the whole game twice back to back to get all of the stickers I'd missed.

I love the subtle story line and the journey experience with the main character. I have played this game 3 times already and it's a pleasant surprise how your friends think when you play with them. I first saw Unpacking the Wholesome Direct, and all I thought it would be was a game where I unpacked random objects for a few different rooms and there'd be some skill involved in getting everything into their places, and room for creativity in how we arranged everything. I got that game, but I also got a lovingly made experience and an inventively told story about a person's life. I will get this out of the way before anything else because it's the one thing I see people bring up in negative reviews: yes, this game is short. I've played it for close to four hours, and while I will definitely go back in to play it all the way through again, I feel like I've gotten the full experience. But I always value a memorable experience over a long game, and I'd much rather play a short game I remember for a long time than a long game that turns into a blur. I will remember Unpacking with far more fondness than a certain MOBA I've spent hundreds of hours in. The point I'm making here is, if you're looking for a repeatable game mechanic with hundreds of levels of increasing difficulty that you can play for several months... this is not that game. It's a short, highly crafted experience that'll be extremely engrossing and moving if you immerse yourself in it, imagine the life of the person whose stuff you're unpacking, and try to put yourself in their mindset as they move into one place after the other. This is my favourite thing about Unpacking. It has about six lines of written story you'll see from beginning to end, but it tells you so many things about the protagonist's life, hobbies, dreams, goals, career and family. It does this through the homes they move into, the objects they keep, the ones that change, where they're putting them, and even which objects they can't move. I don't want to spoil things, but in the middle of the game, I put something from a previous level somewhere else, purely for practical purposes, and immediately felt a deep sense of sadness. Other objects brought a smile to my face, for the developments in the protagonists's life they represented. Micro-narratives develop throughout, and you can imagine scenarios around all of the changes in the objects you're unpacking. I am an artist, like the protagonist, and the kind of supplies I use have changed in a very similar way to theirs. Just from that I could imagine them getting to a point in their career where they thought it was time for an upgrade. The game is full of little progressions like this that garner all kinds of emotions, big and small, and it really does feel by the end that you've unpacked a life. And part of why this is so effective is the love and care that's gone into realizing these objects. You might have already heard that Unpacking has 14,000 .wav files for all its foley sounds. I tested this out at times, and other times was just doing my thing when I stopped, shocked, at how reactive the sound was. Every object makes a different sound based on the surface on which you put it down. Toys and biscuit tins full of sewing equipment make different sounds based on how fast you move them. As a ukulele owner myself, I can confirm that the vaguely musical echo that comes from putting the uke in the game down is entirely accurate. [i]And if you do it in a small space it's louder.[/i] It is a level of attention to detail that could easily have been left out, but I'm so glad it wasn't. This extends to the pixel art as well, where objects large and small are beautifully drawn and rotate perfectly. Objects react to where you place them: books and disc cases stack in different orientations, towels will react accordingly to hooks, racks and flat surfaces, clothes can be folded or placed on hangars, and so on and so forth. Another little detail I love was how space was conserved and respected. This is a 2D game so it'd be so easy for layering to be off and objects to fit where they shouldn't, but if an object blocks a door or drawer it'll open, bump into the object, and close. If there wasn't space to hang a dress because of an object below it, you won't be able to. At no point does the illusion that all these objects share a single 3D space break, and I can only imagine how much skill and effort that took to pull off. The objects themselves are simplified enough to be instantly recognizable, and specific and personalized enough to tell you a lot about the person who owns them. And every last object and room in this game is utterly gorgeous and really gives you a feel for each stage of the character's life. And while the animation in the game takes a backseat, do yourself a favour and stop and look out the windows in each level. Everything I just mentioned comes together to provide a very layered experience. At any given moment while playing, I'm thinking about where to fit each object, where it makes logical sense to go, and what would look prettiest. I'm also thinking about the protagonist, imagining the stories that got them to these objects, and the stories they'll have with these objects. I'm having little relatable moments with their interests and admiring their fashion choices. I'm also enjoying the simple sensation and primal joy of putting things into a neat order. And while all this is happening I'm vibing to the chiptune music. It's a lovely game. It filled me warmth and nostalgia and a little sadness, and gave me a detailed portrait of a character with barely any words. And it was fun! I adore this game, and if a short, charming and lovingly made experience is what you want, you will love it too. I've tried to be balanced and think of what I didn't like about Unpacking, but I genuinely have nothing but positive feelings about this game. I'm sure a few people will find it too short and will think arranging objects is boring, but I'm not those people. I'm so convinced by this game that if it wasn't for its hyper-specific concept I could see Unpacking-likes become an entire genre where we learn about various characters by arranging their stuff. I doubt it'll come to that, but I truly appreciate Unpacking for coming up with another wonderful way to tell stories in a way only a game could. UPDATE: I MISSED SOME THINGS. 1. The game has a replay button which shows a sped up version of you tidying it up! It's so satisfying to watch. 2. A lot of objects react to right clicks (or the B button on your controller) after you place them and oh my god there's so many lovely reactions. Please try right clicking stuff that's been placed, some great stuff happens.

It's a lovely little game where you just unpack things to some nice zen music and watch the story of this character's life unfold through a very well-done visual narrative.

I wholeheartedly recommend that you play this.

I LOVE this game. I sat down and played it all in one day it was that amazing. Music is perfect and you can tell all the little details of the lives you are unpacking. I felt like I was watching them grow and was excited when I could see their accomplishments. The graphics are amazing and it did truly feel like everything had it's place. I would highly highly encourage you to play. I would love a sequel/more games. I would buy anything from these creators.

this game is perfect for my anxiety brain! i love the gentle sounds items make as you place them on different surfaces, and the graphics and music are really charming. i enjoy the different challenge of the levels as you progress - in some rooms you can move others' objects, some you can't; some have many rooms, some have a single room, etc. i can see myself coming back to this a lot when i need a quiet break, so i definitely think it was worth the price. i would love to play more relaxing games like these!

Like others have said before, it is kinda hard to recommend. I was very excited for this game, bought it as soon as I could and I really loved playing it and had a blast, but I was very let down how fast it ended. Its a very fun game, but not worth the $20 in its current form.

This game was so beautiful and delightful. It's my new favorite cozy game. There were so many details that clearly showed this game was a labor of love and that translated beautifully to the player. My heart just absolutely swelled playing this game.

Fun game, seems a little glitchy at some parts, but I'm not totally sure it warrants a $19.99 price tag.
I feel this is a $10.00 game all day, unless they are going to drop more DLC for free, etc.

Cute game, absolutely lovely graphics and mind-blowing attention to sound design! It is short, true, to complete it all it took me about 4 hours, but I've enjoyed each minute of the gameplay :) I've read some comments where people complain that there was no deep story behind it... well, better play again! The story is in every object, in every subtle change and placement of those objects. It was quite interesting experience to get to know the "main character" when we can only look at her belongings and small descirptions in photo albums. Definitely recommending :)

it's a fun, relaxing, short game. There's no time limit, no hard rules, unpack and put stuff around the house then take a picture. There's an underlying storyline about the character that we can deduce from the different places she moved to, photos, and short notes at the end of each level.

Note: there's a setting to allow items to be place anywhere

I love this game, i waited about a month for it to come out. This game has alot of hidden plot the more you notice. this game was the best game ive played in years. I hope they make dlcs or unpacking two soon. Play it as soon asp best game ever!

A simple but sweet game with an incredible amount of care and love put into it, from the art design to the little interactions with some objects to the sheer number of sound effects. The contrast shown between trying to force yourself into someone's space versus making room for the person you've invited in made me tear up (in a good way).
Very calming with a surprisingly lovely story that becomes fascinating to learn. Has a song over the credits that's as good as "Still Alive" from Portal.

Unpacking ist ein wirklich süßes und schönes Spiel, was einen nicht stresst und einen runterholt. Aber 3 Stunden reine Spielzeit sind für 20 Euro mir persönlich einfach zu viel. Über das Spiel kann ich nicht meckern, dass ist wunderbar. Aber ich hätte mir mehr Gameplay gewünscht. Mehrere Leben wären cool gewesen, die sich vielleicht sogar miteinander überschneiden. 

Pro:
-Schöne bunte Grafik
-Kein Stress
-Wunderschöne Geschichtenerzählung
-Am Spiel gibt es nix zu meckern

Contra:
-3 Stunden reine Spielzeit
-Zu hoher Preis

It's a fun puzzle game that still tells a story. I've finished it, but you can still go back and play the puzzles again, or build off of your last solution to try and find some hidden achievements. I've found it to be an interesting way to play a story. 

I do wish there were some more puzzles, or the ability to play as someone else related to the main character to build out some more of the story. I did finish the game pretty quickly, but I still think it's a game worth checking out.

Unpacking ist ein super liebevolles gestaltetes Spiel mit Detailverliebtheit. Dieses Spiel entspannt mit einer angenehmen Musik, lädt zum Erkunden ein und lässt ggf. den inneren Monk hin und wieder etwas verzweifeln. Für alle, die gerne , zumindest digital, aufräumen und anordnen ist dieses Spiel absolut zu empfehlen. :)

Absolutely adored this game. Such a touching and moving story told in a unique way. The level of care and effort that has gone into the art and especially the sound design is impeccable. It's not all about the length of time you spend with an experience, but about how it affects you and connects with you. This isn't a game of puzzles to be solved in a traditional sense, which will frustrate if that's all you expect out of something. Highly recommended.

Absolutely love this game. Didn't expect it to be this much fun but once I started, I couldn't stop! Played it through in two steps- and even went up a bit earlier to continue, the next morning. There is a deep story going on in this game and it's marvelous how it's being told without a single word being ushered. 10/10 from me.

What would also be cool, is if Witch Beam would do another game like this- or perhaps DLC's for events like Christmas etc.
I need more. MORE!!

Kurz aber schöööön. Ein entspannendes Spiel in dem eigentlich nur Kisten auspackt, aber durch das Auspacken wird so wunderbar eine Geschichte erzählt. Genial und mit Liebe gemacht. Davon könnte ich noch zehn Stück spielen. ♥

$20 for under four hours of game play was a little much. I was sad to discover it was also free on game pass after I already purchased it. Super cute, fun puzzles, but not worth the $20 unless they're going to come out with more stories.

An intensely charming little game that is made is a clear amount of craft and love. The sound design in particular is fantastic and has so much hidden detail.

A study in environmental storytelling.

Just such a lovely game. sure, its short, but already in the Demo i had replayed it more than once and re-sorted often the things there.
the Story you get to know when you unpack is good to follow and just so heart warming. 
if you not wanna get it for this prise its ok, i see it as a suport for the developer so more games like this can come out.

정말 재밌어요.. 처음에는 이걸 언제 다하지.. 그랬는데..
생각없이 하다보면 어느새 물건이 다 정돈되어있고 시간 순삭..!!
스테이지가 더 많았으면 좋겠어요 ㅠㅠ 더 플레이하고 싶어요 ㅠㅠ

Ohne Worte erzählt dieses Spiel eine wunder schöne Geschichte. Wer Spaß am umräumen und dekorieren hat wird hier bestimmt auf seine kosten kommen. Ich werde es noch ein paar mal durch spielen da es einfach so unfassbar süß ist.
Für mich eines der besten kleinen Games dieses Jahres.

Short but extremely satisfying, chilling unpacking puzzles, with a subtle layer of narrative behind.
And an incredible sound design (every item has each their own sound depending on the surface they're put on)
Not worth the price but still very lovely - it tells a decent amount of story without actually saying anything. Always annoying fitting pans in the kitchen...

I tend to not leave reviews but I feel the devs deserve a big thumbs up. This game was made with love and it shows.

The atmosphere, the music, the graphics, it's all charming and relaxing. There's story telling via the items. I won't spoil what it is but there's definitely a twist if you start digging deeper. I was surprised and I personally know some people who can relate to the character. And yes, there IS a character! There's no complicated story here... but it's a heart-wrenching one that hits home for many. 

The only bad side is how short the game is. I checked everything out. I collected all the achievements. I went really slow. I finished within two gaming sessions. There's no reason for me to return unless the items in the boxes are random each time. Saying the only bad side is how short the game is might be the best compliment the devs can get. The gameplay isn't trying to be something else. What you see is what you get. And it's oddly addicting! We all want more.

I hope they release DLC (a bit less expensive though I know the devs are a small indie team, still glad to support them!). Maybe show progress further in the character's life. The game is clearly fantastic with very positive reviews despite how short it is. You have some spare money? Buy the game and support the devs. Tight on cash? Wait for a sale. Either way, it's worth an honest look.

Very beautiful and relaxing. The game tells a story is such a unique way. Finding out about the character's interests, milestones, relationships, etc. through the items you unpack and the spaces you put them in was fun. I already expected this to be somewhat short and I feel like I'm nearly finished with the game, but I'm still satisfied with it. This game was worth the wait.

I've been looking forward to this game for a while and it did not disappoint! Everything about it was made with so much love and attention to detail. I'm amazed at the story it manages to tell without using any more words than the ones which are put under each finished level, depending on which room you finish the level in. The story managed to make me angry, hopefull and very happy in the end.
It took me a while to find out how to interact with some of the elements but once I did, I went back to some of the levels that I had completed again to interact with everything I could find. And right now I can't wait to get back into the game, replay some of the levels and make use of the camera and replay functions. 
I've seen a lot of people complain about the price but if given the choice I would play full price again because you can feel how much time and work were put into the game.

overall super simple and relaxing, it could use more places to unpack but for what it is it's good. it's about 4ish hours of gameplay all the way through with a cute, chill soundtrack. it's fun finding out what you have to do to earn all the stickers. i'd recommend getting it, but maybe wait till it's on sale because it's pretty expensive for not a lot of play time.

I love this game and it is worth every penny. Not only is the art and music beautiful, the complex story that unfolds as you unpack each stage of life is beautiful and compelling. I finished the game, but will go back just for the meditative organization, the calming music, and just the beauty that was/is this game.

Such a fun and relaxing game! I love all the hidden small stories, and piecing together the growing and changing character throughout the moves. The use of music and silence adds to the calm vibes, as does the beautiful design. The sweet representation of a queer Jewish woman learning and aging really is something special!

This game has a beautiful story, immaculate sound design, wonderful colors, and overall was something that I got sucked into immediately upon purchase. I love it dearly and will probably replay it many a time in the near future. For someone who loves unpacking/reorganizing their own belongings, this is the perfect game to pass time on for me instead of feeling the need to mess around with my own stuff in boredom.

It's such a great game. It's short but it tells a meaningful story. I love the style and the music!
I do agree that twenty bucks is a lot for this game but I'm glad I played it.

Play the demo, it'll either tell you if this is a 9.5/10 game for you, or a 6/10. For me it was like a dream come true, my only complaint I have is that I had to stop playing it a few times because it was making me too emotional. Which is the softest complaint I think I have ever given.

I really enjoy this game! Its very relaxing, I love that you can decorate with personal freedom and without much limitation to placement. Its quite satisfying. 
Though the game is rather short. I assume, since this game just came out, that there will be more future content though. 
Will love new to unpack the lives of many new characters and their stories! :)

Themed levels would be very fun like Christmas or Halloween, Holiday events in general. 
Someone with a bakery, plant, or pet shop would be very cute :D Maybe a one off/dlc? about an alien, could be very interesting. Lots of ideas!

[h1] Best zen game with a downside [/h1]

First let me say this game is so insanely good. look, this is one of the best calming games I've ever played in my life, and i love how many opportunities there are to create what you want from your imagination. this is what I've been waiting for all my life, and I've already played 16 hours in 2 days... The creators of this game are so talented and my hearts go out to them <3 I've been waiting for this game for a while now, and its even better than i could've expected.

One of the best things about the game is how inclusive and progressive this game is. If you follow the lore, you'll understand that its actually about a [spoiler] lesbian, Jewish woman [/spoiler] :) the whole game is just so heartwarming and cute!! There are so many creative items, and little details hidden throughout to make it a very nice experience for all. i love how some of the objects are moved from level to level, so its not just mindless house creation. This game has a [i] PURPOSE. [/i] My [b] DAD [/b] even liked liked it and played a level, and he's 55 and generally doesn't enjoy video games.

Now lets move on to everyone's issue. The [b] price. [/b] I know you devs works hard on this, and you need money, but there isn't enough content in the game for me to confidently say with my heart that it is worth 20 dollars. i have 16 hours because I've replayed it, but id say it took me like 9 hours to complete it. I personally think it should be 1 dollar for each hour of content. (that's my rule for every game, but obviously the max would be 60) another thing, is that i don't like how i cant put anything anywhere i want. The devs just released an update that added more areas for things, but it still doesn't cover all imaginable areas. The final thing is that i wish some items could be rotated even more, like the knife, or the DS that can only rotate in two directions. I also hope that more rooms will be added in the future, or possibly a new story ( no rush, creating a game is hard lol)

(also wtf is that yellow thing in every kitchen? a nut cracker? it looks like one of those squeezing things to strengthen your hand LMAO)
Fantastic game. It was very satisfying and had a cute story. My only complaint is that the game is very short. The price is a bit high for how short the game is. I finished the game in about 4 hr.

Sad that this game is only 3 hours worth of gameplay. Definitely would recommend purchasing on sale as there is so much you can do in the game. I do agree it is very zen and something to play when you want to zone out. Hope to see some added content in the future!

I really enjoy the zen aspect of this game while still being challenged to piece together a puzzle story. The only thing I do not love about it is the awful blinking red outline of the objects in the wrong spots. It wish it wouldn't blink, its so annoying.

I really enjoyed playing Unpacking.  Its definitely the Zen kind of game it claims to be, it doesn't require you to put things in EXACTLY a single spot, so its nice and forgiving in a good way, but the only complaint I have...its too short.  I finished the whole game in just a few hours. 

If it was $4.99, okay, fine.  But for $20...be prepared to go through it in one evening.

I don't even know where to begin, this game is wonderful. I finished the game over two nights, playing about 2 hours each night. (completed the game in just shy of 4 hours) it's a short game but completely satisfying. it's the perfect cozy relaxing game. the story line is adorable and you can tell the dev's put a LOT of thought behind this game from the story line all the way to the items, designs, the sounds! I am so so sad i finished the game already, I can see this game becoming a huge hit and i surely hope this game gets an update down the line because i dont ever want it to end!! a truly great find, so glad i saw this game advertised by someone on twitter. 

That being said, i'm not sure this game is quite worth the $20 price. the game itself is great and i have no complaints, the price point just doesn't quite make sense to me. however, maybe we'll get some more features in the future as this game is brand new. overall, couldnt be happier with the game, the price point just left me feeling a little unfulfilled when i reached the end.

Absolutely obsessed with this. The kind of calming game I've been looking for for a while now, I would definitely say that it's worth the price. Paying attention to the little things that piece together the character's story is very entertaining as well, plus the little easter eggs are a cute touch! 10/10 soundtrack as well. I 100% recommend this game!

PS: music is amazing

Only thing I'll say bad about it is I feel like for the price paid I would have liked a few more rooms to do so I could get more than 5 hours out of it. Hoping there's more content in the future, I would definitely buy a DLC.

Not to mention there is so much replay value because you can rearrange different rooms and it's so relaxing just working on organizing everything. Lovely music, lovely graphics, everything is just A+.

❌ It is unfortunately very short, and while I think $20 is a somewhat high price for a game that can be beat in 3 hours, seeing as it is an indie developer, and this game took very long to produce and develop, I think it's a fair price.

I went into Unpacking expecting a relaxing puzzle game. What I got was an emotional roller-coaster rich with melancholy and hope. Beguilingly simple in concept - unpack a bunch of boxes, find space for everything, move on - Unpacking crafts a powerful narrative through a combination of devilishly-clever touches. Beautiful to look at and bewitching to listen to, it expertly weaves its story through its simple "unpack item, place item" mechanics. These items combine to paint a vivid picture of their owner: familiar items re-appear on subsequent levels, battered by the ravages of time; new arrivals showcase the relentless march of progress; something mundane triggers sudden realisations. Above all they tell a story. A story of hopes, dreams and brutal realities; of growing up, falling out and moving on; of friendship and family. Yes it's short, but it burns bright and lingers long. In a word, brilliant.
This game is amazing. I only wish it were longer. The music, the graphics, the story, everything about this game is satisfying and adorable. Please buy this game if you like laid-back, cozy games.

Just my kind of Game. Very fun and simple to do. easy to use controls. i love the art style and the music. 
the game for me took 5 hours to complete. i hope there will be other levels in the future. but worth every penny!!
