[h2] Introduction [/h2]

Unpacking is a charming game – one that targets a specific type of audience. Whether you like interior design, or you’re OCD, or you just want to have a relaxing casual gaming experience, Unpacking delivers flawless execution within its niche. The music, pixel art, small interactions, and thought that went into every possible placement makes this game feel “perfect” at what it does. 

[h2] Cost [/h2] 

If there were more interactions, levels, and maybe even custom levels, co-op, etc., it would start to show its worth, but seeing as I 100% the game in 3.1 hours, it’s questionable why the asking price is so high. Not that the game is in anyway bad or not deserving of a high price, but it’s double a blockbuster movie in pricing, or a third of a triple-A game (roughly) - which is something to consider. I could see myself putting in more hours just to get each layout looking picture perfect, but even that would only maybe take an hour or two.

[h2] Gameplay [/h2] 

The gameplay is as it shows: you unpack several boxes, making the house a cluster of different items you have to sort into different locations around the house. Some are obvious where they need to go, others are not. While the game is quite lenient on placement, meaning you could just spam paraphernalia around, there are certain specific story related placements or things that just wouldn’t cross your mind. One in particular, without spoiling anything major, would be a picture you put on a picture board, however you pin it up by stabbing through the face of someone in the picture, giving you a clue as to what you might need to do with this particular item. Also, as you progress, things that were deemed okay placements before, are now seen as bad placements as you get more room to store items. It’s not hard to figure things out for the most part, and all achievements are quite obvious/easy to get. If you take your time, and you really put thought into your design, you should have little-to-no issues, and the game might be even more enjoyable that way. Or you could be like me, and try speedrun each level, ending up with a sense of “chaotic order” by the time you're done with them. 

Unpacking has a lot of LGBTQ+ themes, and I’d argue that while the story itself explores other areas of life, and the overall game is about progressing through life as a whole, the LGBTQ+ narrative is the most overarching. This might be a turn off for you, or maybe something that you’d enjoy – however it’s not obvious, with it being its 15th tag, and subtly hinted throughout each level. It’s up to you whether you care about this or not, but I thought I’d add this to my review, as politically divisive messages like this might not be everyone's cup of tea. 

[h2] Conclusion [/h2] 

Unpacking is a cute and casual game, one that covers a woman’s life, with each object you unpack telling its own story. The music has a certain melancholy to it, giving a sense of nostalgic depression, as you interact with all her belongings – some new, some old, some upgraded, some hidden, some forgotten, and some destroyed. Explore the different hobbies, lifestyle choices, passions, jobs, and relationships, as you organise her into each new house/space. I thoroughly enjoyed my experience, despite how short it was. It made me reflect on my own life and the different objects that have passed through it, and the stories that they tell. 

I recommend getting Unpacking on sale, and spending time with it, not rushing the experience; think about each item, and try to uncover the stories hidden within...

This game unpacks a whole life into simple steps.  You unpack boxes, thinking it will be easy, but then you look at the items your putting out and you see items move from house to house. This game may be short, but it tells a heartfelt story that stays with you forever. Even the simplest gameplay of  unpacking boxes can feel very satisfying as you make each room feel more homey. No matter how many times you relocate in life, the best part is when it's time to unpack.

Is it a short game? Yes. You could easily beat it in one sitting, within about 2-3 hours.
But it's an incredibly charming, unique game. It has an engaging narrative told entirely through the environments you explore and the items you unpack. You start to see familiar items pop up through each year in the timeline, to the point that they become welcome, familiar faces.
Depending on your culture or familiarity with certain objects, you might not know what every item is.
But overall, it's worth playing. If you think such a short game isn't worth full price, try it on the Game Pass or wait to get it on sale or in a bundle.

There is something satisfying about putting things where they belong, and Unpacking has a beautiful visual story of someone's life from childhood to parenthood. The music is also relaxing and there are quite a few puzzles and secret achievements along the way.

It was very short for me, about 5 hours of unique game play, but that being said, my two kids were mesmerized when they saw it and were telling me where to put things, so it does have some replay value ... but it is super relaxing and enjoyable.

I wish I could leave this game with at *least* an 8/10, but the longer I played, the more tired I got.
 
Towards the last few levels, I grew really tired of seeing the same kinds of items like underwear and various small 1 x 1 knickknacks and having to put them away the same ways I had done before. I understand that the counter to this is "It's like this in real life." but to me, it just made unpacking rooms like the bathrooms especially fatiguing.

After the story is completed, there really is no reason to return to the game on a new save file, or return to your previous work because of the nature of the game's story. You know what's going to happen, and a lot of the mystery/shock is really only effective while you're pulling the items from their boxes the first time. 
Some achievements are really charming and require interacting with items a certain way, while others are given out like free candy for doing nothing which makes their existence seem meaningless, and harms a lot of the replay value in trying to earn them post-game. I cleaned up the remaining 5 achievements I had in no less than 10 minutes.

While I think the pixel art in the game is outstanding and a highlight in the indie scene, I was very disappointed in the music. 
For a sandbox-like game, there just isn't any tracks that stood out to me. I couldn't hum anything even if you offered me money, and they don't loop seamlessly, instead going for a few seconds of white noise before looping, making the tracks even more forgettable.

The biggest turn down for me is the asking price. The game does seem to go on sales pretty frequently, but I do not think I can recommend this game for any more than $10 maximum. There are just so many other games I would recommend for that price that offer more meaningful content which really makes me upset.

I really wish there was a complete sandbox mode that alloys you to decorate a room using any items you wish from a selection. Picture Animal Crossing New Horizon's DLC as a widespread example.

As-is, I really wish I could recommend the game, but it I have to squint my eyes a bit too much to give it a thumbs up.
Get it on sale if possible.

🎮✨ UNPACKING: DESEMPACA MEMORIAS PROFUNDAMENTE HUMANAS Y EMOCIONALES 📦💭🧳

Unpacking no es solo un videojuego… es una experiencia silenciosa que te abraza sin decir una sola palabra. 🌈💫
A través de 8 mudanzas, desempacas cajas, recuerdos y pedacitos de vida 🏠📦, acompañando a una mujer desde su infancia hasta su adultez, conociéndola sin verla jamás, solo a través de las cosas que elige conservar.

Cada mudanza es un nuevo capítulo: su habitación de niña 🧸, la universidad 🎓, su primer departamento 🪞, una relación con un chico que no funciona 💔, el regreso al hogar familiar 🏡 y finalmente… una nueva vida junto a una mujer con quien por fin encuentra el amor, un hogar y tiene a su primer bebé. ❤️

No es un título para todos 🎨🧠. Su ritmo pausado y su arte pixel art lo convierten en un refugio para quienes buscan calma, nostalgia y sentido, más que adrenalina o competencia. 🌙☕

Es el juego perfecto para esas noches tranquilas donde lo único que quieres es relajarte, escuchar su delicada música 🎶💤 y dejarte llevar por la historia que se esconde entre cada objeto; aunque a veces no sé si esta mujer tiene más mudanzas vs ropa interior, hahaha.

Unpaking es una historia sobre crecer, amar, dejar ir… y re-descubrir quién eres a través de lo que guardas. ✨
A nice, simple, cozy game to destress playing.

Redeemed this game as apart of Humble Monthly/Choice and it feels like this game would be worth it if it was on sale but 20$ is a lot for how short the game is, game is fun and the story being told by the things you unpack is a neat and interesting detail.

Игра очень зайдет тем, кто любит заниматься именно этим процессом: расставлять красиво и по местам свои вещи в доме. Пиксельная графика, расслабляющая музыка и не напрягающий геймплей, Unpacking отлично подойдет для отдыха на полчаса-час после трудового дня. Em Unpacking a protagonista da historia passara por muitas mudanças na sua vida, e nos somos responsáveis por organizar essas mudanças, e com elas entender a historia do jogo.
A historia não é contada de fato no jogo, com diálogos, ou textos, é necessário que você analise os cenários, entenda onde é possível colocar determinadas coisas e que em alguns momentos você não tem liberdade total.
Os Gráficos junto com a trilha sonora, são o combo perfeito para tornar Unpacking um jogo relaxado e fofo, mas não ache que isso vai durar para sempre, é uma historia bem curta, facilmente terminada em algumas horas, as conquistas são obtidas facilmente, com exceção de algumas que você terá que pensar mais e tentar colocar alguns objetos onde com toda a certeza não é o lugar deles.

The biggest Unpacking sin is the lack of content - many people (you can read it in the reviews) have a great ideas on how to expand this game - add more stories, scenarios, tell story of different type of people, but no, we only got one story that stinks a little bit (Jewish lesbian girl adopts kid - give me a break, so generic in these times that when you reading it and you are a normal person smile appers on your face, but for different reasons than the developers wanted to). Add to it that, you can easly finnish game with all achivements with slow, ponderous gameplay at maximum 5 hours!! Yeah, and the price is quite high cause its 20$, i take it on sale and still don't think it's worth it (I paid about 10$). 

Add to it that, the developers of the game aren't adding any more content, duh, they not even plans to, but that doesn't stop them from making and selling merchandise (?!) from the game such as plushies, posters, stickers, etc., hilarious? Yes, it is. So don't give them your money, or if you really want to play it because you're a fan of chill games, that you can play while listening to some podcast or music, buy it on high discount or play different, better games like Dorfromatik for example, it beats Unpacking in every aspect.

That's it, the rest is good. The music is average, but fits the game perfectly (with the exception of the credits song- it so cringe its giving me crips), pixel art is beautiful and the mechanics are well done, sometimes surprisingly well for a small indie game.

I'm surprised at how short this game was. Taking into account that I've left this game running while doing other things, my play time is actually closer to 4-5 hours. While initially I had fun with this and enjoyed storytelling through objects coming and going, this casual, "zen"-like game got increasingly frustrating, at least for me. The game gives you some flexibility in terms of where or which rooms to put items, but with some objects they give you next to zero freedom. No, you can't leave that on the floor. Yes, it has to go under the bed (which is on the floor). The laundry basket can't go in any room but this one. Toothbrushes and toothpaste have to go in the cup, otherwise you will run out of drawer space or it'll look messy placing all of it on the counter. Incense holder has to go in the bathroom-why? I think it'd look better in the bedroom or living room. Nope, can't do that.

I'm neurodivergent, and the appearance of clutter bothers me a lot. I'm also big on mise en place - everything in its place - so I was thinking this game would be relaxing for me for this reason. While there are designated spots for objects, they aren't without clutter. The bathrooms and bookshelves are good examples for this. Unpacking is not really a puzzle game, it's just an exercise in participatory environmental storytelling. It tells its story via the items you unpack and how you see your life circumstances change, and invites questions about the person's life as they go from child all the way into adulthood.

I didn't really care for it. I'm not going to say it's bad because it lacked certain specific kinds of game elements - I'm evaluating it on what it is and not what it's not - but I just don't think it executed what it was trying to do very well or particularly artfully. 

The questions it invites and the inferences you draw are pretty basic; the game tries to tug on your heartstrings, but it does so with all the subtlety of a dog tied to a knife and loosed in a balloon factory. Often it feels like it's showing you things and nudging you repeatedly with a, "Look, isn't that sad? Isn't this sweet? Look, remember this item from the first place you lived? Don't YOU have something like that you've held onto in your own life? Doesn't that just make you feel nostalgic?" 

There is no real subtlety here. I think people rave about this game because they're not used to encountering this as a means of storytelling, so the *novelty* of it is really enticing to them, but the game does not actually make use of this novelty in a skillful way.

It's also $20 when full price, which is outrageous for a 3.5 hour game, let alone one that isn't especially good.

Après avoir décortiqué Unpacking jusqu'au 100% j'arrive avec un avis qui a mijoté pendant quasiment 4 heures de jeu, ouais j'ai pas trainer, j'avais des cartons a déballer, moi !

Bref ! Pour quelqu'un qui carbure généralement aux jeux qui te secouent dans tout les sens, Unpacking, c'est le bain chaud après une journée de taf. C'est un petit moment tranquille où tu mets le cerveau sur pause et où tu décompresse à fond. Concernant la direction artistique du jeu, c'est assez agréable a regarder, c'est du pixel art a la fois bien travaillé et épuré, c'est propre, c'est net, bref, ça en jette. Bien sur on va aussi parler des OST, mais la... c'est pas vraiment mon délire, mais faut reconnaître que le boulot derrière est bien ficelé. Maintenant, le gameplay ! et c'est là que ça devient sympa. L'histoire, tu la découvres en observant chaque niveau, chaque pièce, t'assimiles l'histoires du personnage à travers des vêtements, des photos, rien n'est là par hasard, c'est du storytelling au petits oignons. Par contre, malgré toutes les idées brillantes, le jeu tourne assez vite en rond. J'ai fini par déballer des cartons de plus en plus vite, histoire de vite finir le jeu et de ne pas m'endormir sur mon clavier. Autres bémol, c'est quand on te force à poser tes objets à des endroits précis de temps à autre. Ça bride ta créativité, c'est comme si on te disait que t'es libre de faire ce que tu veux, mais que tu te rend vite compte que t'as une laisse invisible, et avec des pièces parfois aussi étroites qu'un appartement Parisien, ça peut vite te donner envie de renoncer. Malgré ces petits défauts le plus grand reste la durée de vie : 4 heures pour plier l'affaire surtout que le jeu coûte quand même 20 balles ! C'est presque une agression tarifaire. Mon conseil ? Attendez les soldes, moi je l'ai dégoté pour une poignée de cacahuètes pendants les réducs.

en résumé, Unpacking, c'est sympa, mais faut pas claquer ton PEL là-dedans. Attends les promos et prend le seulement a ces moments la.

Such a gorgeous game that does what games as a medium can do uniquely - makes you feel and discover a story through inputs and actions. Unpacking is about exactly what it sounds like: unpacking your stuff in a series of places as your character moves through life. But the developers had an intuitive understanding of the ways in which this universal experience can tell us such specific things about a person. What items travel through a person's whole life and which fall away as the years pass tell us about a person's priorities and the direction of their growth, while the places they move to mark major life milestones. I'm pretty sure I've made every one of these moves, from going off to college to navigating space with roommates to coming home again, until eventually you find the right path and take decisive steps forward. Mechanics like whether you can move another person's possessions when you're moving into their space (roommates: no, boyfriend: yes) are a clever way to change the mechanics of the puzzles while alluding to the way it truly feels to inhabit others' spaces - and to have one all our own. It was emotional and satisfying to see this unnamed character taking new paths in life and finally moving from cramped spaces where things had to be shoved into every nook and cranny to larger abodes where she had more room to breathe. Our homes - and our possessions - are ultimately what constitutes our lives, and the intimate exploration of one person's stuff was a moving and joyful experience.

[h1][b]滿足整理、裝飾癖好，悠閒且療癒的溫馨小品。[/b][/h1]

[h2][b]前言：[/b][/h2]
 《Unpacking》是以拆開大量封箱物品並其作為各式家具、擺設，只要將對的物品擺放在對應的房間，可隨喜好布置的解迷小品，美術為像素風格，但在細節上相當用心，物品的擺設很自由，可以依照常理擺放，也能發揮創意；故事以「相簿」形式記錄女主角每次搬家、重新裝飾家裡的心境變化，可愛的畫風結合溫馨的故事，讓本作是具有療癒感受的作品。

[hr][/hr]

[h1][b]留有空白，讓人去想像的故事[/b][/h1]

  遊戲劇情以相簿日誌的形式，從女主角小時候佈置兒時的房間開始，在到大學第一次擁有自己的專屬套房，開始工作、和人交往同居、最後成立家庭的點點滴滴，透過循序漸進的方式，藉由每個時期的房間佈置來瞭解女孩當下的情況；遊戲沒有什麼台詞與對白，故事的細節都藏在每一關的環境物品、拆開紙箱拿到的擺設裡來讓玩家拼湊，你會發現有些布偶是女主角從小到大，不論搬家幾次都捨不得丟掉的紀念伙伴，而有些照片則是女主角不願再看見的回憶，玩家就隨著這些物品漸漸認識女主角的故事。

  每一關都會有數量不等的房間和可作為家具的物品，有時候打包會把不同房間的物品擺在同一個箱子內，玩家拆開紙箱後需要依據物品的功用來擺放，全都放到正確的房間後就能推進下一關，擺放方面能按玩家的喜好佈置，還能拍照留念；同時遊戲也藏有不少彩蛋，像是符合那個年代的流行元素，又或是遊戲迷會知道的玩意，但有些物品的外觀辨識度不足，或是日常比較少見，會難以判別它屬於哪種房間類型，這種情況就只能逐一測試。

[hr][/hr]

[h1][b]遊戲優缺點一覽[/b][/h1]

👍 療癒人心的美術風格與音樂
👍 能滿足整理癖好的佈置玩法
👍 溫馨，讓玩家探索與拼湊的小故事
👍 還原1997～2018年代的元素

👎 部分物品的外觀難以辨識功用是什麼
👎 玩法變化不大，連玩幾關可能會有點煩躁感

[hr][/hr]

[h1][b]結論：喜歡解謎小品可買，有整理癖好必買～[/b][/h1]
[b]個人評分：8.5/10。[/b]

  現實中「開箱」會讓人有種新興奮感，而本作是能讓你瘋狂拆紙箱並盡情整理與佈置的小品，遊戲時間不長，4個小時左右就能全破與全成就，符合下列推薦的話，值得考慮看看！

[h3]推薦對象：[/h3]
[list]
[*]有喜愛整理、佈置房間的癖好
[*]喜歡溫馨、可愛的小品
[*]遊戲時間較少，希望是短時數的作品
[/list]

I'm mixed on this. Like I'm in between 'like' and 'dislike' and since there's no in between choice, I'm going to put it as NOT a reco game and the reason/explanation why is this:
Before everything else, I just wanna say this first game I had (and only game so far) that I only needed to use a mouse to play the game—which is what I love about it (me when I'm just lazy but wanna be entertained without using too much effort). And art is cute too. Buuuut:

1. Let's say there's 3 rooms to decorate. The boxes per room most of the time has something that doesn't apply on that room. And people need to guess where it's supposed to go. And it's not just 'what specific room'; it's where the exact place in that specific room it's acceptable to place it before the system accepts it. And that's the easy part. Imagine doing the guessing on a 7 room home.

2. Achievements is a guess game too. It's hidden which some people who loves achievements may find it annoying [again]. Example, let's say placing a glass of water near a socket (poof, hidden achievement given suddenly. You have to guess basically what the achievements are gonna be).

3. Huuuuge turn off for me and the reason why I leaned on not recommending it is cuz of the "game level". For a mid range price game, it only has maybe 10? 15? level and the game's done. You start on 1st level again if you wanna try getting the achievements you didn't guessed the 1st time around. I could buy a better game with the same price that would keep me entertained far longer and not 'stuck' on 15 levels before I'm forced to just repeat it all over again if I wanna try to get the most of the game.

This is the only time in my life I’ve actually enjoyed moving house. There are no heavy boxes, no broken mirrors, and zero sweat—just the pure, therapeutic dopamine of finding the perfect spot for a digital toaster. It’s incredibly relaxing; the "thud" of a book hitting a shelf is basically ASMR for the soul. It turns out my true calling isn't a career, it's organizing someone else's socks.

Unpacking is a game about taking things out of boxes… and somehow discovering an entire person’s life while deciding where to put a toothbrush.

There are no enemies. No timers. No explosions. Just you, a bunch of cardboard boxes, and the quiet pressure of figuring out where this one random spoon belongs.

At first, it seems simple: take item → place item → feel productive.
But then the game hits you with emotional storytelling through objects.

You start noticing things.
“Why do they still have this photo?”
“Why is there only one pillow now?”
“Why is there NO SPACE for their stuff in this apartment??”

Suddenly you’re not organizing items you’re analyzing life decisions.

The gameplay is incredibly satisfying. Everything has a place… except when it doesn’t, and the game silently judges you by refusing to accept your questionable interior design choices. “No, the toaster does NOT belong in the bathroom.” (You tried. Don’t lie.)

The pixel art is beautiful, the sound design is cozy, and the act of placing items becomes weirdly addictive. You’ll spend five minutes rotating a mug like it’s a critical life choice because it is.

10/10 Came to unpack boxes. Stayed to unpack feelings.

Unpacking, karakterimizin hayatında 20 yıl boyunca ilk evinden son evine kadar giden taşınma süreçlerine şahit olduğumuz bir oyun. Oyunumuza kendimize ait bir oda ile başlayıp yıllar ilerledikçe yeni evlere yelken açmaktayız, Yelken açtığımız her yeni ev bir öncekine göre hayatımızdan daha fazla iz taşımaktadır. Oyunun ana konusu taşındığımız evlere karton kutularla getirdiğimiz malzemeleri güzelce yerleştirmek olsa da 20 yıllık bir serüvenin izlerini karton kutulardan çıkan malzemelerle görmekteyiz. 1-2 saat sürecek rahatlatıcı bir oyun deneyimi sunan Unpacking ev düzenlemeyi seven veya genel olarak sakin oyunları arayan oyuncular için oldukça ideal bir oyun.

Eğer ev düzenleme oyunlarına ilginiz varsa ve Unpacking'den farklı olarak 3 boyutlu bir dünyada tüm evi düzenlemek istiyorsanız aşağıdaki oyun da tam size göre: https://store.steampowered.com/app/613100/House_Flipper/

Unpacking é um jogo muito interessante e relaxante ao mesmo tempo, a OST é incrível, a arte do jogo é muito bem feita e bonita. É realmente um jogo que enche os olhos e dá pra se divertir bastante enquanto joga. Mas ainda acho que pelo preço que eles oferecem é muito superestimado, ainda mais quando se cobra 60 reais por um jogo que tem somente 8 fases com 35 cômodos pra decorar. Simplesmente acho que não vale, ainda mais pra nós brasileiros, em que 60 reais é muita coisa pra um mero joguinho.
Desde o dia que lançou, eu esperei por muito tempo para que ele ficasse com 40% de desconto e ainda assim, acho que paguei muito pelo que ele oferece. Aos que estão em dúvida ou que querem comprar logo de cara, eu recomendo que esperem que ele fique abaixo de 40 reais pra menos antes de comprar. O jogo vive em promoções de 20%, mas esperem que um dia o desconto chegará pra mais. Não vão no impulso de comprarem logo se estão com esperanças dele ser um jogo longo, porque definitivamente não é. Eu levei em torno de 5 horas pra terminar, mas aposto que dá pra fazer em 2 ou 3 horas, ou até menos. As conquistas são facilmente conquistáveis também (se você ler o guia do jogo, é claro). E de verdade, por mais divertido que foi, eu não sei se jogaria de novo, mesmo fazendo tudo diferente, porque querendo ou não, o jogo se torna repetitivo, não dá pra fazer muito.
Eu realmente esperava que ele tivesse um modo livre de jogo, com cômodos aleatórios pra decorar e uma infinidade de novas possibilidades, com muitos cômodos novos e diferentes, expandindo a criatividade pra cada jogador. Eu realmente espero que no futuro, os desenvolvedores coloquem mais fases e mais cômodos, porque é justamente o que se espera de um jogo que custa 60 reais. Mas infelizmente, acho que o jogo só ficará em torno disso e não acho que eles vão colocar conteúdos adicionais (não duvido que coloquem uma DLC caríssima e sem muito conteúdo pra aproveitar também).
O conceito do jogo literalmente prometeu tudo, mas entregou pouquíssimo (ou talvez nada). Eu amei muito jogar Unpacking, mas eu esperava muito mais pelo tanto que paguei. Acho que por 20 reais, ele estaria muito bem pago e com certeza eu recomendaria, mas por 60 reais e o tanto que ele oferece, eu definitivamente não recomendo.

The music was great, items come out of their box with a satisfying rustle, and people bind this game managed to encapsulate the feeling of organizing things until they look nice and fit where they belong is without the stress that normally accompanies doing so.

It's a game about unpacking and life progression over the years of a girl's life. There's a story that's in the background that you can piece together as you move forward in time. The amount of things you can interact with blew my mind, and all the achievements were a blast to try and figure out. I know a lot have complained about how quick the game is to complete, but if you're meticulous about organizing like I am and enjoy cozy vibes at your own pace, you'll really like this game. I've gone through five hours already and have yet to get all the achievements or try a second run through the game to get them. I'll definitely be replaying this one, just to see how things can be organized differently.

What really changed my opinion is the developers’ attitude toward the player base. They have made it clear they are finished with the game and have no interest in expanding it further. According to them, they spent years on it and it is no longer “fun” to work on, and they believe they do not owe players anything beyond what already exists.

I understand that developers are people and can choose their direction, but this is still a business. Customers are actively asking for more content and expansions, yet the team has chosen to move on to projects that no one but them are interested in. It feels like they had something special and decided to walk away from it despite strong support from the community.

The game itself is good. The problem is the lack of longevity and the dismissive tone toward players who helped make it successful. Buy it on sale if you are curious, but do not expect ongoing support or future content.

When I stumbled upon Unpacking on the steam store I wasn't sure if I'd enjoy it. I was pleasantly surprised. 

Without saying too much, it tells a story in an amazingly subtle way which allows for the player to fully ignore it should they want to. It's a great game to sit down and relax, given that you find organizing relaxing. 

One of the only things I found that I disliked about the game was that (to my knowledge) there is not a key that allows for easy room switching and forces the use of the mouse. For most people I'd say this won't be an issue, but as someone who uses fairly low DPI and has a non-ideal setup for ergonomics, I found it a bit straining to move to the sides of the display to switch rooms. Especially if I happened to be switching rooms fairly quickly and moving back and forth.

To give it a bit of nit picking, I do wish that you were allowed to fully reorganize rooms instead of having to squeeze your new items in with pre-existing ones. This would be cool as a toggleable option in a future update. (Assuming that any plans exist for expanding the game)

[b]TLDR[/b]

Unpacking is a relaxing experience that subtly tells a story, allowing the player to ignore said story if they prefer. With a few hours or so of content, it'll be a worthy purchase if this kind of game is something you enjoy.

I won’t spoil anything, but the narrative you unravel as you unpack boxes is complex and intersectional. It’s hard to discuss the ways the game tackles human experience without giving things away, and much of the initial pleasure of the game is figuring things out for yourself. I’m not someone who replays games very often, nor sinks hundreds of hours into procedural games, nor do I speedrun. I’ve also mostly cured myself of completionism. That said, I think Unpacking really rewards replaying - not in the stickers and achievements (although those are fun!), but rather in elements like how which room you complete a move on determines what musing from the character you’ll get to read. Replaying also allows you to spot details you missed the first or the third time you played - the houses are nearly as full as real houses, so familiarity helps reduce the overload and lets you study other bits of the rooms. The stickers and album functions are massively fun, but they aren’t that interesting on a first play through - you need to know the character first to really get a kick out of some of the stickers you can use. 

Witch Beam have put in impressive artistic work, individually creating every item and every sound in minute detail. This is a game that is most enjoyable to those who admire excellent craftsmanship. If you’re looking for something that will feature DLC and new levels and hundreds of hours of play, you’re going to be disappointed. If, instead, you’re looking for a beautifully wrought, curated experience, this is going to be easily worth as much as you’d pay to go see a movie in theaters (when it’s not a pandemic…). Accessibility won’t be an issue for most players - while sound is certainly a highlight of the game, it’s not strictly necessary for gameplay, and likewise neither is reading. Witch Beam have taken the time to support control remapping and gamepads, as well as making the game playable one handed and with a single button for interaction, if needed. Players can entirely turn off the light puzzle aspects, and change the color of the “wrong position” outline. The game saves when you open a menu or exit to the main screen, so you can pick up where you left off at any time, and keep your play sessions as short as you want.

Deeply melancholic to play. While the story is obviously subtle for a game with no dialogue or visible characters for the most part, the story is excellently told. There are so many little things to pick up on as you go, like [spoiler] finding back pain patches as the years pass, or the mug with the toothbrush being cracked after a while, or how the number of souvenirs keeps increasing, or how in his apartment the only stuff of his you're allowed to move around are cookware and underwear, and all of his decor stays put, or how, in the final level, you can put your laptop inside of the cabinet and that's fine because you just aren't using your old laptop anymore.[/spoiler]

All of that puts aside the bigger, more obvious beats that are much easier to catch but still tell a story very well, like [spoiler] the only place in his apartment you are allowed to place your degree is over the toilet, and the very next level you've moved back home.[/spoiler]

TL/DR: A masterwork of subtle storytelling. No other game could give me melancholic pangs over clicking on a cardboard box and retrieving a gray towel.

[b]Unpacking[/b] is a very original and [i]very[/i] well made little puzzle game that I just so happen to be [b]writing a negative review on.[/b] Now [i]you might be wondering [b]“why is that?”.[/b] [/i] [i]Is he stupid?[/i] probably, but [i]even though I can appreciate the finer details[/i], I just never found the core gameplay of unpacking boxes to be all that interesting; along with a number of other issues. Let me just make it very clear: [b]the game is actually pretty amazing,[/b] [i]it’s just not my thing.[/i] So, with that said, [b]let’s start this unboxing video. [i]like and subscribe!! !! !! ![/i] [/b] [spoiler]…...please?[/spoiler]


[b]Unpacking[/b] might be one of the most [i]aptly named[/i] video game titles in recent memory, because [b]that’s [i]exactly[/i] what you do:[/b] [spoiler]unpack stuff.[/spoiler] Aside from games like the DS horror [b]Touch the Dead[/b], [i]you can’t get much more literal than that.[/i] The story follows a young woman and her journey through life, with the “levels” being the most pivotal years and changes. 1997 is when she and her family move and [i]she finally gets her own room.[/i] 2004 is when she graduates high school and [i]moves into her college dorm.[/i] 2010 is when she [i]gets married to some dude.[/i] [b]And so on [i]and so forth.[/i] [/b] The gameplay is extremely simple: [spoiler]unpack stuff.[/spoiler] And [i]unsurprisingly[/i] for a super casual puzzle game, [i]it’s super duper easy.[/i] [b]barely an inconvenience[/b]. There is a little bit of strategy involved, mostly boiling down to [b]common sense[/b]; you gotta put things in the right place and keep it tidy, and [i]no matter how hard you try[/i], [b]you can’t flush your stuffed animal collection down the toilet.[/b] [spoiler](you CAN, however, hang your high school diploma above the toilet. what an accomplishment!).[/spoiler] The later levels are typically just more of the same, [i]only [b]even more[/b] [/i]; more people, more rooms, and [i]more and[/i] [b]more boxes to unpack. [i]isn’t this so much fun.[/i] [/b] While you might miss it if you’re not paying attention, the real star of the show is the story, [i]told almost [b]entirely[/b] through visuals.[/i] There’s the obvious stuff of moving through life and becoming an adult, but there’s also [i]so much said[/i] with so little, being told in the background with what shows up in later levels, to what [i]doesn’t[/i] show up again; all painting a full picture of this woman’s life, and making her a three dimensional character. It’s honestly brilliant; and again, (practically) [b]no dialogue.[/b] [spoiler](not to mention you don't even know what the protagonist looks like until the credits)[/spoiler]. But [i]is all of this worth folding and sorting approximately[/i] [b]281 pairs [i]of underwear?[/i] [/b] you’re the judge here. Either way, [b]get that laundry done, bub![/b]   


If there’s one thing we can all agree on here, it’s that [b]Unpacking[/b] is a [i]good looking game.[/i] The intentionally limited [i]yet[/i] hyper detailed pixel art style looks [b]incredible[/b]; so soft, colorful, and [i]adorable.[/i] [b](almost)[/b] Every single sprite and prop, [i]no matter if it’s a mouse pad, butter dish, or fridge magnet,[/i] is instantly recognizable, even with the blocky look. [b]Heck[/b], I’ll take that a few steps further, and point out that even [i]the movies and video games[/i] within the game can be identified. Our girl has a Nintendo Gamecube! [b]Awesome![/b] [i]Look at them games;[/i] [b]Wind Waker, Double Dash, [i]Midway Arcade Treasures 3??[/i] [/b] very specific, but [i]very cool.[/i] [b]I love Hydro Thunder.[/b] One of her roommates is a big monster movie fan! [b]Epic![/b] [i]Look at them movies;[/i] [b] Jaws, Shin Godzilla, and [i]Up.[/i] [/b] ...y’know, [i]the Pixar movie…[/i] that’s not really a monster movie, ain’t it. [b]whatever. [i]everyone loves Up![/i] [/b] The subtle detailing of age and wear on some of the objects is [i]really good.[/i] You probably know of the stuffed pig on the game’s Steam page, [b]yeah?[/b] He’s by your side your whole journey, and he looks a [i]liiitttle[/i] more worn out each and every passing year. And [i]if you keep your eyes peeled[/i], you might see a lot more objects like that [spoiler](ma’am, please, just throw away that broken coffee cup….or glue the pieces back together. yeah, great idea).[/spoiler] I love how the game sounds, too. [b]“wow, this game sounds great!! why did this random guy on the internet give it a negative rating?” [i]you ask.[/i] [/b] Well, [i]I’ll be happy to tell you![/i] First of all, and I say this [i]as a fan of slow, casual games[/i], [b]this game is far too slow and casual.[/b] [i]at least for me.[/i] Really, I’m the kind of guy who could spend three hours straight on [b]Balatro [i]like nothing[/i] [/b], but getting through [b]Unpacking[/b] [i]felt like a [/i] [b]chore[/b] [spoiler]..because, y’know, it’s literally like a bunch of chores.[/spoiler] It’s difficult to tell what some of the items are even supposed to be, but I blame that [i]less[/i] on the art style and more on [b]I’m a guy and I don’t understand girly things.[/b] There’s this thing that [b]-to me-[/b] looked like [i]an oversized [b]stapler[/b] [/i], but it was only allowed to go in the bathroom for whatever reason. Unpacking : By Triple F

"Unpacking" by Witch Beam is a unique, zen-like puzzle game that combines elements of organization with storytelling, inviting players to unpack and arrange belongings in a series of rooms across different stages of a character's life. Rather than relying on dialogue or text, "Unpacking" tells an evocative story through the objects you unpack, allowing players to piece together details about the protagonist's journey, relationships, and personal growth. It’s a simple premise, but "Unpacking" takes this simplicity and weaves it into a poignant experience that feels intimate and nostalgic, with a deep appreciation for the little things that make up a life.

The gameplay revolves around a series of life events, starting with the protagonist’s childhood bedroom and progressing through various moves into shared apartments, dorm rooms, and eventually into more personal living spaces. As players open boxes filled with personal belongings, they must organize and find suitable spots for each item within the space, arranging them in ways that feel logical and aesthetically pleasing. The satisfaction of organizing items to fit seamlessly into their new environment creates a calming, almost meditative experience. With each move, players witness the changes in the protagonist’s belongings, which subtly reveal the evolution of their tastes, career, relationships, and identity over time.

One of the game’s strengths is its attention to detail. Each object, whether it’s a well-loved teddy bear, a stack of art supplies, or a kitchen appliance, feels authentic and meaningful. The items aren’t just decorations; they’re relics of the protagonist’s past, hints at their personality, and symbols of their growth. As the protagonist moves from one stage of life to another, certain items reappear, some remain in storage, and new ones emerge, creating a strong sense of continuity. This careful choice of items makes each move feel personal, and over time, players grow attached to these objects, seeing them not just as pieces to be arranged but as cherished parts of the character’s life.

"Unpacking" uses its minimalistic art style to great effect, creating vibrant yet cozy environments that feel inviting and realistic. Each room is presented in pixel art, with a charming, handcrafted aesthetic that captures the warmth of the protagonist’s various homes. The color palette shifts subtly with each new setting, conveying the mood and significance of each stage in life, from the excitement of a first apartment to the warmth of a shared home. The art style, though simple, is highly detailed, with each object easily identifiable and rich with character, encouraging players to look closely and appreciate the small touches that bring each room to life.

The game’s sound design enhances the immersive experience, with satisfying audio cues for placing items on different surfaces, from the muffled thud of clothes in a drawer to the clink of dishes on a countertop. Each sound is distinct and carefully chosen, creating a tactile feel that makes organizing each room immensely satisfying. Additionally, the game features a gentle, ambient soundtrack that remains unobtrusive, allowing players to settle into a calm, focused rhythm as they unpack. This audio design serves to amplify the meditative quality of "Unpacking", making each action feel purposeful and grounding.

Where "Unpacking" truly shines is in its narrative subtlety. The game tells its story not through dialogue or explicit storytelling, but through the evolution of the protagonist’s belongings and the spaces they inhabit. As players handle each item, they learn about the protagonist’s relationships, career, and emotional states. For example, the appearance of certain objects like a partner’s mismatched belongings, or an item that remains in a box due to lack of space, reveals more about the protagonist’s life than any text or voiceover could. This approach requires players to observe, reflect, and empathize, making the game’s storytelling approach highly personal and impactful.

One minor drawback is that "Unpacking" is a relatively short experience, with most players able to complete it within a few hours. Additionally, the game’s linear structure may limit replay-ability, as the story unfolds the same way each time. However, this brevity can also be seen as a strength, as it keeps the experience tightly focused and prevents the game from overstaying its welcome. The length and structure allow players to fully engage with each moment, making the story’s impact feel more concentrated and meaningful. For those who appreciate immersive, emotionally resonant narratives, "Unpacking" provides a short but powerful experience.

In conclusion, "Unpacking" is a beautifully crafted game that takes a simple concept and transforms it into an exploration of identity, memory, and personal growth. Through its intuitive gameplay, detailed art, and innovative storytelling, the game offers a gentle yet profound look at the journey of a single life, told entirely through the belongings we carry with us. It’s a game that invites introspection and empathy, celebrating the quiet moments of reflection that come with every move. For anyone looking for a relaxing, heartfelt experience, "Unpacking" is a testament to the storytelling potential of games and a reminder that sometimes, the smallest details can tell the biggest stories.

Unpacking é simples, mas viciante. O objetivo é desempacotar caixas e organizar objetos, mas cada item conta uma pequena história da vida das pessoas que você está “visitando”. É tipo terapia em forma de jogo: relaxante, satisfatório e cheio de charme.

O visual é acolhedor e colorido, o som dos objetos sendo colocados é super satisfatório, e a narrativa acontece de forma sutil, só pelos itens que você organiza. No fim, é um jogo que faz você se sentir bem, tranquilo e curioso sobre cada detalhe da vida dos personagens.

Just wanted to write a little review because I saw that I neglected to do so long ago. Unpacking is one of the most special games I've ever played and I've been chasing the "high" of the understanding the story with each move. I could likely credit this game with being partially responsible for helping me unearth a part of my identity. I'll never forget how sick I felt in that one apartment level and how stressed I felt trying to fit all my (the main character) possessions in the space. I'll never forget when I realised who I was sharing that space with and how I vowed to NEVER do this in real life, lol. It was EYE OPENING and UNFORGETTABLE. The last move of the game was also incredibly unforgettable. The whole game!!! This is one of the best and I'd recommend it to anyone. It's important to hear and experience stories like this to gain new perspectives. I'd make this required gaming for the whole population! I really hope this studio has more stories to share. I had a great time playing this game. It made me realize just how bad I am at organizing things. I have to admit, it gets a bit frustrating when I am unable to find the right spot where to place an object. Some objects were also unfamiliar to me, and I had no idea where they were supposed to go (like the orange peels, the red ruler-looking thing, and the purple sack). It would be helpful if there were an option to identify items, and a bonus if there are descriptions to help what the objects are for.

As you play, you gradually uncover the main character's life story. I found myself getting emotional as I unpacked from the first level to the last—it reminded me of my own life, the things I had when I was younger, and what I have now as an adult.

Lastly, while playing, I felt an overwhelming urge to tidy up my room. The emotions I experienced in the game carried over into real life. It’s an incredibly relaxing game that lets you play at your own pace. Absolutely would recommend it. 10/10!

Unpacking tells so much with just objects and rooms. The story is beautiful, the art is amazing, the game is both relaxing and satisfying. It has replay potential (I've played at least 4 times) because the objects you place do not have that "one" perfect place to put them. Every time I played a little differently and tried new things.

It's not challenging, but it's not trying to be. It allows the player to immerse themselves in a story and to just unpack a few things here and there. You can perfect it as much as you want or you can half-ass it a little (there are some constraints). It's a perfect game to enjoy for a few hours with a hot tea. The coziness-factor would land it a 10/10 in my book for sure.

As I said, I hope there's a second part, because I'd like to do this over and over and over again, just maybe with new things and new rooms.

I actually couldn't put the game down and 100% it all in a day. I do like organising irl so for me the gameplay was super satisfying. Overall, no complaints. It's relatively short, though, especially if you're not going back in to find the secrets. So, grab it on sale if you're hesitant about the price. As a creative and someone who understands the game-dev process, however, the base price is worth it as it's a [i] beautifully-crafted [/i] game.

Unpacking is a casual, at your own pace game that has you unpacking boxes of household items and placing them in the correct locations around each house. It’s fairly simple and relaxing to play, has a very mellow soundtrack to listen to, but the game is quite short (easily finish in a few hours) and might be worth picking up on a sale if you don’t like paying full price for a few hour’s enjoyment. I’m not sure exactly who this game is meant to be marketed too, but might be worth a look if you just want to play something that’s short and relaxing which won’t tax your brain.

[B]Story[/B]
For a story, there’s not much, you help unpack the un-named protagonist’s belongings for each of her major life events, moving away for college, moving in with her boyfriend, breaking up and moving back home, moving to a small apartment, moving in with a new partner and then setting up a house with a baby on the way.

[B]Gameplay[/B]
The gameplay is quite simple, each room has a few boxes of items, and you have place each of the items in a location that suites it (eg dishes in the cupboard, books on a shelf, ect). If you get anything wrong (and it’s easy enough to do as there’s no description for items), then they are highlighted red and need to be moved to the correct place. Some items can be interacted with (which is where most of the achievements come from), but it’s all about finding the correct place for each item. Much easier than in real life, and slightly more enjoyable. Most of the time it makes sense, and it’s much easier than doing the housework I should be doing.

[B]Graphics[/B]
The games low res pixel graphics make the rooms fairly easy to explore, items that need to be placed have a white highlight (so you can see them), and can be rotated or sometimes flipped or stacked on top of each over, rooms flash red if there are any incorrect items in them, and when everything is correct a golden star appears in the corner that allows for the game to progress. Some objects are hard to figure out what they are (dishrag looks exactly like a hand towel), and why would a diploma need to go under a bed? 

[B]Music[/B]
It’s been a long time since I’ve listened to such a mellow soundtrack, but it perfectly suites this game. There’s lots of acoustic and mellow chiptune tracks and the ending credits song couldn’t be more poignant about moving in with someone and placing of your life’s mementoes together and what that means. I especially like the hidden soundtracks in the game (that you unlock for getting every object in every room wrong). I can’t say I’d heard of Jeff van Dyck before playing unpacking, but I’d be tempted to keep an eye out for other games where he is the composer.

[B]Achievements[/B]
All of the achievements are super easy to get, I’m surprised that this game doesn’t have like 80% of players unlocking the rarest achievement

とある一人の女性の荷物を荷ほどきしていくパズルゲーム。シンプルな操作性でゲームがあまり得意じゃない方や普段ゲームをそれほどしない人でも無理なく楽しめる作品だと感じました。データを３つ作れるので、家族や友達とどんな配置にしたのかを見比べてみるのも楽しい遊び方だなと思いました。最後、自分のプレイ映像を早送りで見れるのも嬉しいポイント。

ダンボールから次々と出てくるアイテムを正しい位置に置いていくのが楽しかったです。ゲームをしていくうえで説明などはないものの、家が変わったりダンボールから出てくるアイテムが変わってくることで、主人公（？）の生活が垣間見えるのが面白かったです。大人になっても子供の頃ものを大事にしてるんだな、とかこの人はこういう趣味を持っているんだろうな、とか想像しながらプレイしました。あとものすごい音へのこだわりも感じました。物を置くときの音が気持ちよすぎる。

一気にクリアするのもいいですが、私はあえて毎日少しずつ荷ほどきして癒されるのがここ最近の日課でした。終わってしまって悲しいので、ＤＬＣや続編に期待しています。

真的是一个很可爱的小游戏！
游戏的玩法特别简单，就是把物品从箱子里面拿出来，摆到你想摆的位置，最后检查一下摆放的区域有没有出错，就可以进入下一关了。看着非常简单休闲的小游戏，但是整体轻松的氛围中又隐藏着主人公的人生转折和情绪的起起伏伏，很多很细腻的情感都藏在零零碎碎的物件背后，加上游戏本身的文字引导非常少，玩家很容易就可以和游戏的主人公产生情感连接。Unpacking真的是一个非常适合平静心情的游戏，简单的游戏模式竟然也能让玩家不知不觉进入心流。游戏的bgm也非常优秀，并且会随着主人公的境遇起伏改变成对应的氛围，不过总体而言一直是轻松愉悦的。
游戏中会有很多可可爱爱的小成就，把物品放在意向不到的地方或者按特殊的方式拜访，说不定会获得奇奇怪怪的小惊喜~
结束最后关卡的我只觉得世界真美好……如果你正处在不是很积极的情绪中，可以试着玩一玩Unpacking，这里没有打鸡血式的鼓励，但是能和主人公一起分享发自内心的幸福。

Unpacking é um joguinho indie bem relaxante e com a proposta de fazer você relaxar ao som de uma trilha sonora legal e organizar cômodos de diversas casas, que vão desde a sua infância, até a sua vida adulta. Enquanto arrumamos os diferentes cômodos em diferentes momentos de nossas vidas, vamos notando o quanto nosso personagem está crescendo e o quanto ele já cresceu. É um belo jogo e eu recomendo muito!

Tato fajná oddechová hra je balzám na duši. Relaxační hra na jedno dopoledne, u které se nemusí ani tolik přemýšlet.

Sledování života jisté slečny, která dospěje a nakonec má i miminko byl vlastně takový zajímavý příběh hry, který byl velmi originálně a vkusně podán tím, jaké předměty vytahuji z krabic. A také hodně napoví samotné byty a místnosti. Poznáme, že bydlí u rodičů, v garsonce, že měla rozchod s partnerem a také narození potomka a pořízení celého domu.
Samotnou ženu poznáme až na samotném konci hry. Byť pouze na fotce proti Slunci a z profilu.  

Odměnou za splnění jsou i zajímavé samolepky, které doplňují achivimenty.

Co se grafiky týče, jedná se o krásný pixel-art doplněný skvělou hudbou, která doprovází jednotlivé levely. Jak už zaznělo, někdy je problém poznat jaký předmět právě umisťuji.

Poslední věc, co musím na konci pochválit jsou předměty, které odpovídají herní době. V roce 1997 máme tamagothi a v pozdějších letech máme konzoli Wii a Xbox :) Slečna je velká herní fanynka.

Pro: Stylová grafika, soundtrack, velké množství objektů, stylizace příběhu a celkový nápad hry.

Proti: Poměrně krátké.

İyi bir hikaye anlatmak için kelimelere ihtiyaç olmadığını anlatan oyunlardan biri Unpacking. Kullandığı bu anlatım tarzı hikayenin oyuncunun hayal gücüne bırakılmasını sağlayarak kişisel olmasını sağlıyor. 
Mekanik açısından ise bu kadar basit görünen bir mekaniğin bu kadar eğlenceli ve rahatlatıcı olması apayrı bir başarı. 
Etkileşimli eşyalar oyuna ayrı bir hava ve eğlence katıyor. Yerleştirdiğim eşyaların gerçekten çalıştığını görmek şaşırtıcı ve mutlu ediciydi.
Kendi şahsına münhasır bir oyun Unpacking, oldukça kısa sürmesine rağmen damakta çok güzel bir tat bırakıyor ve oyuncu daha fazlasını istiyor.

Extraordinarily cute and relaxing game, and putting together the pieces of the characters life (I'm assuming AFAB based on the period products but I won't assume any pronouns) and their progression on self expression and love is very very cool. I genuinely would love to have more games exactly like this but with different characters and stories because of how connected I got with a character strictly through them moving between spaces in both the real world and in their personal life. And being able to interact with different items based on personalities and lifestyles would be soooo much fun I would spend all my money to support that if someone would make it happen.

I played this while streaming in discord to a friend and he and I really got into it. Speculating where the story was going to go was very very fun.

In terms of the actual gameplay, 100/10 so freaking satisfying. It definitely tickled that one part of my brain that craved organization (the part of my brain that refuses to interact in my actual life btw). So having everything click and snap in place, the sound design, the UI, everything was fantastic.

Complaints and cons: genuinely, there were some frustrating things. I understand that to really set in a more "realistic" approach, placing things in "wrong" spots would make the level incomplete. But there were definitely some choices that I PERSONALLY did not agree with and did not understand why they were wrong. I think having a more free placement of items would make the game more enjoyable but it is a game, so therefore to make it seem more like a puzzle and less like a chore I understand the reason for these placement wrongs and rights. 
I also was so frustrated with the lack of space yet somehow the MC had like...seven million items to place? And not being able to stack certain items, or place them in a spot that exists but isn't visible (like the cups on the shelves, there's space in the way back but because it's not visible you can't access that space so it limits how much ACTUAL space you can utilize). Again, as it is a game I understand there are constraints within the space and the way you can organize things especially since it's an 8-bit so whatever faults I found I ended up consolidating with purely because I understand the style does not hold the same standards as a real space does. 

TL;DR: 10/10 game, very cute and fun. Would highly recommend. I got it when it went on sale but I would buy at full price with no regrets.

이삿짐을 풀어 정리하는 게임입니다. 시작하고 한두 스테이지는 재밌었는데, 중반부터 반복작업으로 느껴져 지루해져 갔습니다. 내방꾸미기 게임인 줄 알았는데, 한정된 공간의 인벤정리 게임인 점도 별로였구요.

 풀어야 하는 상자 수가 점점 많아지고 품목 구분 없이 마구잡이로 포장되어 있어서, 상자 하나씩 까서 정리했다간 기껏 정리해둔 거 다시 옮겨야 되기 십상입니다. 그래서 상자 다 까서 바닥에 물건들 늘어놓은 다음 정리를 시작하게 되는데, 이 사전작업이 상당히 귀찮았습니다. 스테이지 넘어갈수록 기존의 이삿짐에 새로운 물품이 추가되는 식이라 계속 같은 물건을 보게 되는 것도 질리게 만드는 요인 중 하나였구요. 생각보다 물품을 마음대로 배치하지 못하는 점도 별로였습니다. 충분히 둘 만한 장소인 것 같은데 여기 아니라고 빨간불 들어오고, 맞는 위치 찾으려면 거기 둔 물건 또 다른 데 옮겨야 하고, 그러면 또 옮긴 자리에서 빨간불 들어오고, 이거 상당히 짜증났습니다. 물건 둘 공간 자체도 넉넉치 못했구요. 후반으로 갈수록 한정된 공간에 정해진 물건을 우겨넣는 게임이 되어갑니다. 
 다른 문화권이라서인지 이 물건이 왜 여기 있어야 하는지 이해되지 않는 부분도 많았구요. 몇몇 물품은 이게 도대체 뭔지 알 길이 없는 것도 있었습니다. 

 스토리는 뭔가 디자인쪽 일을 하는 것 같은 주인공의 이야기를 이사하는 장소와 이삿짐으로 짐작하는 방식으로 표현되는데, 중반까진 그냥 흔히 있는 만남과 이별 등 감성 자극하는 분위기로 가다가, 갑자기 동성결혼으로 건너뛰네요. 어째 아기방 준비하면서도 이상하게 남성용품이 안 보인다 했더니, 너무 뜬금없어서 좀 황당했습니다. 예상치 않던 임신을 해서 중간에 얘기나온 언니네 집에 얹혀사는 건가 했는데, 엔딩 보니 그건 아닌 듯하구요.

通过沉浸式整理房间，一点一点了解了女主。就像是intro中写到的，这是一个禅意游戏，累的时候，云整理房间还是比较治愈的，只不过感觉游戏的彩蛋是，通过整理房间，一点一点窥探到女主的感情之路的变化。[spoiler] 最后发现女主是个同性爱情，是真的没想到。 [/spoiler]

一开始在自己的房间生活，照片上的那句话是“我终于有了自己的房间了”，青春期有自己的小秘密，希望有独立的生活空间，这一点真的戳到我回想到自己以前的童年生活。

第二阶段，有了自己不大的独立的小空间，到第三阶段搬到了一个更大一点的空间，在这个过程中，女主换了电脑，买了更多的画册，有了更多的工具，就像我们不断为自己的生活奔波奋斗，累，可能也会有快乐。

终于，女主找到了自己的男朋友，并且很快搬了进去，和男主一同生活，就到了第四个阶段。在这个阶段感觉女主的生活比较压抑（从色彩来看没有那么活跃了），而且可能女主和男友的社会阶层也不同（这里纯属猜测，就像开头说的，这好像也是游戏的一个彩蛋，不同的人眼里有不同的哈姆雷特），男友的东西是不可以被调整摆放位置的，只能一点一点的把自己的东西小心翼翼的塞进去，连自己的奖状只能放在床底。在厨房中最后照片留下的留言是”原来咖啡也可以不是速溶的“，可能这也暗示了这段感情最终BadEnding了。所以女主分手后只能默默搬回了自己的家，但是在自己的家里，色彩又明亮了起来。可以把自己喜欢的画和奖状随意摆在任何位置。唯独……和男友的合照，只能放到柜子里面。

后来女主可能是做好了重新开始的一切准备，所以她又租了个房子，相册里面的留言是”终于自己拥有一张大床了“

在下一个阶段，有一个人搬进来了，刚开始以为是交了个新的男朋友，后来整理卧室衣柜发现。。搬进来的是一个女孩。而且小猪和小老虎并排放在一起的时候，触发了爱情❤的成就，因此就发现，原来[spoiler] 女主找到的爱情并不是新的男友，而是女朋友！ [/spoiler]。可能也是女主终于可以按照自己内心真实的想法来生活了吧。

最后跟女友一起搬进了二层小楼，过起了幸福的生活。

这个游戏在休闲之余，让我们一点一点了解到了别人的生活和心路历程，是个挺有意思的休闲游戏，没有生涯、没有战争、没有任务，自由度相对可以。

但是不足的是，画风中一些东西，只是猜到了放在什么地方，但具体是什么，很难辨别。。。

总体还是比较推荐，可以在正念时间多一点休闲

Unpacking is an enjoyable, relaxing and charming game.  It feels so rewarding to empty your moving boxes and find a home for every item, and I often lost track of time while I reshuffled everything until my home was just how I wanted it.  There are several possible places for each item, meaning players can choose which things they want to show off and which should be tucked away out of sight.  I enjoyed building a picture of the mover's live based on their belongings, and it was interesting to look back when it was over and spot little clues that I missed as I was going through.

HOWEVER, the game is quite short.  Within 7.5 hours I had finished each level, completed all of the achievements, and arranged every room to my satisfaction.  If the game included one or two more "campaigns" with different stories, or else a handful of one-off short stories, I think I would like it a lot more.  Perhaps DLC of other stories will come out eventually, or someone will make a mod to tell their own story.  I suspect such a thing would be a lot of work, though, so I won't begrudge the developer if it doesn't happen.

I strongly recommend this game if a) it's your thing AND b) it's on sale.

(If only it was as easy to unpack my own moving boxes and get everything squared away)

[b]Могут ли о человеке рассказать его вещи?[/b] [i]Могут.[/i] 

[code]Каждую вещь, которую приобретает человек, он наделяет смыслом. С течением времени вещи начинают сами рассказывать истории о своем хозяине, обретая собственное звучание. Таким образом мы можем понять не только вкусы человека, но и прикоснуться к его душе. Прекрасная интерактивная игра, в процессе которой вы познаете историю одной жизни. Здесь не будет долгих диалогов, а в качестве персонажей выступят личные вещи молодой девушки. Их интересно разглядывать, как отдельные осколки истории, выстраивающиеся в единую картину. Увидев одну книгу, вы узнаете о хобби, которое перерастет в любимую профессию, а увидев часть белья узнаете о личностном развитии персонажа и выборе, что ему удалось сделать. Фотографии, статуэтки, элементы одежды и игрушки - всё в этой игре несёт свой собственный смысл приоткрывая с каждым разом новые стороны истории одной жизни. После прохождения возникает вопрос ко всем игравшим и не только: "А что обо мне смогут рассказать мои вещи?". Мне было бы интересно узнать это пожалуй..[/code]

Here is the explanation; (No Spoliers) 
  Most of the bad comments are about the short playtime. Even though that's true, it depends mostly on you. There are no rules, no set challenges, you can just rush through and finish it within 2 hours, easy.  
 However, if you like immersive stories, and I really do mean immersive, if you want to experience a game almost as real as real life, and experience it truly from another person's eyes, YOU'RE GOING TO LOVE IT!

At first you don't notice it. As you'll progress along, the game slowly starts to make sense. But you need to play it like real life, not like a game. Like if you've moved to a new house,  where would you put the kettle in the kitchen? What do you reach at the first thing in the morning? Do you have an order when you're doing laundry?
You start by putting things the way you're used to irl, but that will change if you pay attention. That's the challengeing part. and you'll love the game for it.

[h1] A Short and Sweet Life Story[/h1]

[i]Unpacking[/i] is primarily advertised as a meditative and calm puzzle game that consists of us sorting through boxes of furniture and personal knick-knacks and arranging them into the room or the house we're moving into. However, as you go further along, you'll realize that [b]these small trinkets and tokens all give insight into the character of the person we're unpacking for, revealing a surprisingly story-driven aspect into the game[/b].

The premise of [i]Unpacking[/i] is fairly simple: unpack boxes of things into the rooms available to you to finish a level. But as you take each item out of the boxes, you'll find yourself caught up on tiny details that bring nostalgia, happiness, sadness, and an entire array of emotions you never thought you could get from unpacking a virtual room.

One of the beauties of [i]Unpacking[/i] is its minimal amounts of text, which means less reading and more doing. A result of this, however, is that there aren't any labels for the items you pick up, so sometimes you'll be confused by what this blob of pixels you just picked up really is. This is where [i]Unpacking[/i] becomes [b]a slight guessing game[/b]. Oftentimes, you'll recognize what exactly it is you picked up, after all, a computer from the '90s is fairly hard to not recognize, but sometimes you won't be able to tell. At these moments, just have the item in your hand and hover over different surfaces, and sometimes the change in angle or placement will be just enough to let you know what it is you're holding.

As such, [i]Unpacking[/i] is a surprise all on its own. It can be a short hours of adventure but it has so much to be appreciate in it. Opening up boxes and sorting the items into a house never sounded fun or engaging to me at first but it prevailed by having such [b]a unique way of telling its story, finding a simple way to be compelling[/b].

Pour ma part, j'ai bien aimé ce jeu.
En effet, ce n'est pas un jeu de grosse action, c'est plutôt un jeu grande détente.

Bien entendu, le but est très simple, vous devrez défaire les cartons et placer vos objets dans un endroit de votre choix.
Par contre, certains objets ont une place particulière. Vous ne pourrez pas ranger les ustensiles sur le comptoir.  Il est donc nécessaire de les placer dans l'endroit adéquat pour réussir votre déménagement,  certaines choses seront mélangées dans les boîtes. 

J'ai trouver son agréable qu'il ait une petite histoire progressive et que certain objet vous suive tout le long et d'autre s'améliore. À la fin par exemple, vous aurez vraiment beaucoup de jeu de console. 

Les succès, ou autocollant dans le jeu, sont agréable a chercher, certain objet ont une petite interaction, comme la radio peut vous jouer de la musique.

C'est un jeu sans temps, donc vous pouvez réfléchir autant qu'il vous plaira avant de placer un objet.

Le prix est un peu cher par contre. La durée du jeu n'est pas très longue. Je vous conseille d'attendre un rabais, pour acquérir ce titre si vous aimez les jeux de détente sans stress.

I'll probably revise this review when I finish it, but I feel a strong need to give it support in the form of a review already. I've played the first 3 hours or so with my wife, and we were both taken aback by how deeply emotional and meaningful the story here is. If you're expecting a long game with difficult puzzles then that's not what you'll find here, but to me that's in no way a negative. This is a meditative game that lingers on feelings about some of the most turbulent moments in our lives when everything changes, and asks you to personally and thoughtfully arrange the pieces that make up those moments. It's a shining example in the "show, don't tell" principle, except it makes you show yourself. You just have to be receptive to what it wants you to see.

I'm not going to spoil anything, but the 2012 chapter made both my wife and I break into tears as we reminisced about having been in similar situations. This game can hit really hard depending on what kind of person you are and what kind of life you've had, although I do think everyone can take something from it. You will probably connect deeper and more personally with the story if you've been through a lot of changes in your life, if you've been in spaces that feel like home and spaces where it feels like you're an intruder, even if your cohabiters are loved ones—but if not, then this still has the qualities of all the best deeply personal stories: It puts you firmly in the shoes of someone else, and makes you experience their life at their most vulnerable.

I'm really excited to finish this game and thankful to Witch Beam for the great experience so far. I promise this is well deserving of the asking price if it sounds like something you'd connect with.

[h1]Unpacking - Une histoire racontée sans un seul mot[/h1]

Unpacking c'est un jeu zen de rangement développé par Witch Beam, sorti en 2021. Sur 8 déménagements successifs, on déballe des cartons et on range des objets dans de nouveaux logements - sans jamais voir le personnage principal, sans jamais lire une ligne de dialogue. L'histoire se raconte autrement.

[h3]Mon avis perso[/h3]
C'est un exemple à suivre de narration environnementale, et elle est ici parfaitement réussie. Le jeu arrive à nous raconter une vie entière d'une vraie profondeur sans prononcer un seul mot, sans jamais montrer son personnage principal. Il utilise simplement les différents environnements et les objets à ranger à chaque déménagement - notamment ceux qui nous suivent au fil des années - et franchement c'est une énorme réussite. C'est hyper relaxant de ranger tout ce chantier en découvrant petit à petit la vie de cette personne au fil des déballages de cartons.

[h3]Les points faibles[/h3]
Le jeu est peut-être un poil court et manque de rejouabilité. Mais c'est clairement chercher la petite bête - ce n'est pas le propos du jeu et ça ne gâche rien à l'expérience.

[h3]Les points forts[/h3]
La narration environnementale, la direction artistique pixel art charmante, et cette capacité rare à créer de l'émotion et de la nostalgie avec si peu de moyens narratifs. Un modèle du genre.

Often introduced simply as a relaxing game, Unpacking is so much more than a stress reliever.

   If you're like me, and you're here to find something chill and new for the weekend. Not only does this game offer it's calming side, it will tell you a charming story trough it's many items, all pulled from moving boxes. Through every level you watch someone grow up through snapshots of their life. Every time they move into a new place in their life's story it feels as though you accompany them in a short part of the journey. An adventure of life which warmed my heart to experience.

   Witch Beam is not a developer I've heard of before purchasing Unpacking. I'm thankful to have had such a delightful introduction to their work. I'm extremely impressed by the creative talent behind this title. The ability to create a tale by showing rather than telling is becoming an increasingly rare ability. From today forward, I'll be sure to pay great attention to this developer and their future works!

Is this a short game? Yes. However, in my opinion that's missing the point. The care that's gone into Unpacking's creation and, if you look for it, the attention to detail in each new location speaks volumes about the developers Witch Beam. There's a wonderful, zen-like feel to the game, that lends itself to being very much a "pickup and chill" type game.

Whilst some may want additional levels, it would detract from the story each successive move is telling us about our unseen protagonist. That being said, there is replayability here if you're one for re-arranging things when stressed (like I am) without the need to completely re-arrange your actual house which would take some actual effort. An ultimate win if you ask me!

Some may see this as overpriced but I wholeheartedly disagree. There's depth and care here that is often missing in some bigger more bombastic titles from bigger developers. Moreover, it's great to see something different hit the shelves and be executed so well.

O jogo te convida a acompanhar a vida de uma pessoa por meio da tarefa aparentemente mundana de desfazer caixas de mudança. Cada item que você posiciona diz algo sobre a protagonista: seus gostos, seus sonhos, seus momentos de transição e até suas frustrações. E o mais incrível é que você entende tudo isso apenas observando.
A ambientação é maravilhosa: os cenários são cheios de detalhes, a pixel art é impecável e a trilha sonora tem um tom suave e aconchegante que combina perfeitamente com o ritmo tranquilo do jogo. A sensação de nostalgia, descoberta e intimidade é constante.
Não é um jogo desafiador no sentido tradicional, mas é profundamente recompensador. É sobre se reconectar com memórias, criar ordem no caos e refletir sobre os momentos de mudança na vida.
Narrativa ambiental sensível e poderosa
Pixel art linda e cheia de personalidade
Trilha sonora relaxante
Jogabilidade intuitiva e meditativa
🔹 Veredito:
Unpacking é uma obra de arte interativa que toca o coração com sua simplicidade e humanidade. Se você gosta de jogos que contam histórias de maneira criativa e emocional, esse aqui é imperdível.
⭐ Nota: 9/10 – Um jogo que me fez sentir muito mais do que esperava.

Alright, first off all I'm not writing this review to attack the developers. Being a small development team, I've think that the devs have done a great job on this game. I really like the concept of unpacking a house and think the idea is very innovative itself. The small details included within the game, such as being able to turn on the computer and solve the Rubik's cube are simply amazing and add some depth to the game. The photo mode good fun in itself as well, with numerous frames, filters and unlockable stickers to edit your screenshots.

Why the negative review though? Well, this review is not so negative, it's more of a mixed review. But there is one flaw that kills the game for me. There's little to no replay value.

There's a total of eight levels within the game, and although most of those levels are large and spacious, once you complete those eight levels.... that's it. You finished the entire game. The only small elements of replay value within the game are replaying the same levels, unlocking the rest of the stickers you didn't unlock throughout your playthrough and using Photo Mode to create screenshots, but even they can become dull eventually. 

I might sound a bit harsh considering the devs worked three years on this but in all honesty, $20 for around 4-5 hours of narrative gameplay with no replay value is not acceptable. Why not add an actual sandbox mode into the game? You know, where players can choose what items they want to place in the room from a list of items, allowing them to have more creativity when it comes to creating screenshots or playback GIFs. I understand that from one of the devs videos, the devs tried to avoid the "sandbox" element within the game as it ruins the immersion of you being an "unpacking ghost" of this unseen female protagonist, therefore you don't actually choose what items are present in a level as you don't actually play as said protagonist. Still, an inclusion of a proper sandbox mode would improve the replay value of the game by a considerable amount for some players.

I know that there is an Accessibility Mode in the game that let's you place items where you want them but that still doesn't count towards an actual sandbox mode, it's just a setting that affects the way you play the game.

Overall, I love the premise and art style of the game and I appreciate the devs work, but for $20, the game is painfully lacking in gameplay outside the story mode. In all honestly, if the game had a better form of replay value, I wouldn't be so negative, the game has more good points than bad, but again, for the price I expect more gameplay outside of 5 hours of narrative gameplay. Prehaps I'll revisit this game and this review once an update or two has passed. Only time will tell.

TL:DR - Great gameplay and concept let down by poor replay value.

荷物の梱包を解きながら、持ち主の人生に思いを馳せるゲーム。
プレイヤーは主人公の名前も知らないし、引っ越しのタイミングでしか主人公の人生を垣間見ることができないのだけれど、「前回の引っ越しからこういう事があったのかな」と察することができる。
ゲーム・映画・本はドット絵のグラフィックで、現実にある作品のパロディになっていて、自分の好きな作品を見つけるとなんだか嬉しい。
グラフィックの他に、音がすごく作り込まれていて、モノを置く場所によって音が違う。それに、段ボールをたたむ時のシュッ！という音が気持ちいい。「作業が進んでいる」ことを音で実感でき、荷物を置いていくだけというシンプルなゲームながらやり応えのあるゲームとなっている。

引っ越し先で荷物を整理整頓する荷解きパズルゲーム。
子供時代から大人になるまで、引っ越しを通して主人公の人生を想像させる面白い発想のゲーム。子供時代は家族と住んでて整理できるのは自分の子供部屋だけだが、やがて一人暮らししたりルームシェアになったりと飽きさせない作り。子供時代から持ち続けてるぬいぐるみや引っ越しのたびにゲームソフトが増えたり体鍛えるのにダンベル買ってみたり、人柄や時間の積み重ねを感じさせるのが良いですね。
基本的に「想像」を大事にしてるのか物の名前などは一切わからないのが良くも悪くも特徴的。本とか服とか見たらすぐわかるものは問題ないですがパッと見でなにがなんだかよくわからない物も少なくない。物を置ける正しい場所はある程度それっぽいところに限定されていて例えば服ならクローゼット、食器ならキッチンの棚とか。しかしよくわからない物はどこに置けばいいのかもよくわからないことが多く、正解の場所を求めて右往左往しがち。いちおう設定で配置制限の解除は可能。
値段的にちょっとボリューム不足感は否めませんが作り込みはしっかりしていてプレイして損することはないでしょう。おすすめ出来るゲームです。

[i] "This will be a calm and relaxing game to wind down with..." [/i] You think to yourself at roughly 11 PM.

All is well when you first start pulling items out of boxes. The music is pleasant, and the art is cute. This will surely be relaxing, you tell yourself.
You proceed to pull another item out of a box after delicately placing one earlier, and then another, and then another. . .

[h1] Then the dread settles in; you're completely surrounded. [/h1]

Now, you've got several ponies laying about, action figures, and... Wait why are you not allowed to place that backpack on the floor?
Great heavens, items are scattered [i] everywhere now. [/i]
There is no hope now. You continue to put things away as neatly as possible while also trying to soothe that itch for aesthetic in the back of your brain, all the while trying to simultaneously please the Unpacking gods.

Wait.
What do you mean you can't put those nail clippers in that bathroom drawer? Absolutely vile. [b] Put that back. [/b]

Tl;dr:
A very cute, calming, and soothing game! I highly recommend it.

[h1] 人生×お片付け×シミュレーション[/h1]
荷ほどきを通し、人物の背景について考察するゲーム

[b] [u] ストーリー [/u][/b]
主人公が成長とともに引っ越しを繰り返し、その荷ほどきをしていくストーリーです。
全体として恐らく一つのストーリーがありますが、人の登場や言葉で展開するのではなく、荷ほどきでストーリーを展開していきます。
荷ほどきを通じてその人の背景を考察していくため、人に興味のある方や考察好きの方にはおすすめかもしれません。

[b] [u] 荷ほどき [/u][/b]
ひたすらダンボールから物を取り出し、自分の好きなように配置していきます。
ただし、適切な場所に配置を行わなければストーリーは進行しないため、そこは注意点です。
たまに適切な配置場所がわかりにくいものがあります。

[b] [u] デザイン [/u][/b]
UIは直感的であり、すぐ慣れます。

[b] [u] ボリューム [/u][/b]
全実績解除に大凡2時間半かかりました。
ゲームのボリュームとしてはかなり軽いです。
下手すると返品可能時間の間に全てクリアできてしまうのでは？と心配になってしまうほどです。

[b] [u] おわりに [/u][/b]
ステージをクリアする際、選択している部屋によってアルバム(とそのコメント)が変わります。
各ステージの全てのアルバムのパターンを見たい方は、アルバム画面で写真を押せば部屋を再度選択することが可能なためそこから見てください。

The good:
- This game has very good pixel art.
- I fully understood the story, even though there was no dialogue and very little written text on screen.
- It's a very relaxing game.
- Surprising number of secrets to find for a game about opening boxes. (Still not many, though.)
- The soundtrack was nice and fit the game well.

The bad:
- This game is not worth the current normal asking price.  Got it 50% off, and that felt appropriate, but its normal asking price is just not worth it in my opinion.
- Representation is great and all, but I'm kind of sick how, in all media these days, every heterosexual relationship is a dumpster fire or an insane and awkward struggle and same-sex couplings are the way to fix everything.

I hate to say it, but that cultural trope showing up really soured my opinion of the story and pushed me over the edge from recommending with a caveat to get it on sale to not recommending.  What sucks is that, until you start unpacking clothes, it just seems like our girl found a sane and quirky guy who was going to treat her right.  It feels out of character for the main character to go this route.  This just feels like forced same-sex representation just to have it, especially when the last act baby feels less like adoption and more like somebody got gender-swapped late in the dev process.

Other developers out there, please stop shoe-horning homosexual same-sex couples in every chance you get.  They are not a window-dressing to show off how woke you are.  Also: Can we stop pretending like all relationship problems belong to heterosexual couples and heterosexual couples have nothing but problems, please?  As a species?

[h1]Desempaquetando la Diversión - Reseña de \Unpacking\[/h1]

[h2]Resumen[/h2]
Bienvenidos a una épica aventura de... sacar cosas de cajas. Sí, amigos, \Unpacking\ se lleva el premio al juego más zen y posiblemente menos necesario del milenio. ¿Quién necesita salvar el mundo o correr carreras cuando puedes desembalar objetos domésticos, verdad?

[h2]Aspectos importantes e interesantes[/h2]
Lo majestuoso de \Unpacking\ es su capacidad de convertir algo tan mundano como organizar tu habitación en un rompecabezas sorprendentemente adictivo. Arrastras, sueltas, y de repente, una hora ha pasado y todavía estás intentando decidir si el osito de peluche se ve mejor en la cama o en la estantería.

Y vamos a ser sinceros, la satisfacción de escuchar ese pequeño 'click' cuando colocas un objeto en su lugar perfecto es bastante gratificante. Además, tienes todo un viaje visual a través de diferentes años, viendo cómo cambian los estilos y los espacios vitales de tu personaje.

[h2]Aspectos por mejorar[/h2]
Con tanto foco en la estética y la colocación, a veces desearías un poco más de drama. ¿Quizás un fantasma de una caja anterior o una nana maldita que no puedes sacar de la habitación? Además, una historia más rica daría más contexto y emoción al acto de desempaquetar.
