There is a saying among game developers, that ideas are worthless, because implementation is everything.  Unpacking is possibly the best example of this old saying that I've ever seen.  It starts with what sounds like a terrible idea - moving into a new place and unpacking all the boxes - and turns it into something compelling, emotional and beautiful.  

The game in Unpacking - the entire game - involves taking items out of cardboard boxes and then arranging them in your new home.  But a few very smart design decisions are what make this excruciatingly mundane premise work so well.  Unlike other "home making" games like House Flipper or The Sims, Unpacking doesn't use 3D graphics, instead opting for a fixed isometric perspective and lovely pixel art graphics.  

The satisfying way objects snap into place, or snap together, makes the whole process enjoyable.  You can stack plates together and then move the whole stack with one click.  Clothing automatically attaches to hangers or folds itself up in a way that feels almost magical.  Books automatically stand up, or shift over to make room on the shelf when a new one arrives.  Every click on the cardboard boxes reveals a new item, like a tiny surprise each time.  Manipulating the objects in this game is so pleasurable, it's slightly addictive.  Even the cardboard boxes fold themselves up and disappear with a satisfying swoosh when they're empty.  

The audio is absolutely perfect.  There's an amazing amount of attention to detail that went into rendering the various clicks, clunks and thumps that punctuate the movements of all the household items and bring the little world to life.

I suppose my biggest problem with Unpacking is that I just wish there was more to it, but adding anything more would have probably ruined it.  It has such a singular focus I can't really imagine anyone wanting to play this for dozens of hours.  But for a few hours, it's a gentle delight.

The icing on Unpacking's pixelated cake is a storyline which is a marvel of subtlety.  By examining and placing every single one of the unseen protagonist's belongings, we learn - without words - an amazing amount about her life.  Her hobbies, her job, her relationships, even her health - all of this manifests itself in some really clever and nuanced ways.  

It's one of the best achievements in storytelling I've ever seen in a video game.  And yet, I still feel like the storyline is a bit of a missed opportunity.  I was hoping Unpacking would deal with some of the difficult questions that come with ageing:  should I move to a smaller place?  Is it time to get rid of my childhood possessions?  If my partner dies, should I keep any of their stuff?  And when I die, who's going to deal with the mess I've left behind?

But rather than deal with any of those (admittedly sad) issues, it simply ends - rather abruptly - when the protagonist reaches middle age, suggesting a "happily ever after" from this point forward.  And that's fine, I suppose.  I can understand why they would want to end the game on an optimistic note.  But had the game attempted to deal with those deeper issues, I think the emotional impact would've been fairly breathtaking.  

In any case, I think I can give Unpacking a cautious recommendation.  It's certainly not for everyone, and I would definitely wait for a sale, unless you're comfortable spending $20 on a four hour game.  But for those few hours, it was one of the most unique and memorable experiences I've ever had with a game.

Cada item que tiramos de uma caixa carrega memórias, escolhas e identidades. À medida que encaixamos esses pedaços de vida em novos espaços, nos deparamos com as marcas invisíveis do crescimento, das perdas e das mudanças.

A beleza de Unpacking reside na sua simplicidade: ele nos força a desacelerar e prestar atenção ao que parece banal. Um ursinho de pelúcia que nos acompanha por décadas, uma caneca que não cabe em nenhuma prateleira, um diploma que não encontra lugar no presente — tudo isso reflete nossas vitórias, nossas dores e os ajustes que fazemos para caber nos espaços da vida. Há uma melancolia sutil no ato de arrumar. Em cada nova casa, sentimos a ausência da antiga, mas também a promessa do que virá. O jogo nos lembra que, assim como objetos são deslocados e adaptados, nós também somos. É uma meditação sobre pertencimento, sobre a maneira como moldamos o mundo ao nosso redor e como ele nos molda de volta.

No final, Unpacking não é só sobre organizar; é sobre aceitar que a vida é uma constante reinvenção de nós mesmos, onde cada caixa aberta é uma chance de recomeçar, mas também de carregar um pedaço do que já fomos.
Caríssimo pra poucas horas de jogo, se fosse 10 reais tava valendo a pena

For the content of the game, you consistently unpack your items into different areas as the protagonist grows up and has different life experiences. This game play can get repetitive and you can easily lose interest. I understand that there is a story to every place, but the repetition of the game play doesn't make it enjoyable.

If the game needs to stay at this price, I would suggest that they change their mind about adding DLC, and add something that will make the games value more reasonable. They should add more content to it.

However, there are some positives to this game. The art style has a cutesy-pixel look that gives it charm. The soundtrack is relaxing, and the story line is something you learn as you play each separate stage.

This game has potential, but it needs to have a bit more to it game play wise.

Overall, don't get this game at the $22.79 value, and get it whenever it goes on sale. (doubt it ever will.)

SHORT:
Unless they enable workshop for people to create, it's way overpriced and only good on decent sale. Great concept, but severly lacking in content and wierdly uneaven in execution.

LONGER:
So... while this is  agreat CONCEPT of  game, the plain facts are it's either overpcied or lacks content. It took me 5 hours to complete while having it run in the background as I did many other things, so I'd say real game-time was about maybe around 3 hours?

Yes, you can spend 10+ hours looking over every single item (the attention to detail IS praise worthy - books having voulme numbers, a little fogure getting painted, a cup getting chipped), but that's the same trite plaging RPG with their '300 hour gameplay' which is only true if you gather every single leaf and do every side-quest and achivement.

It's overpriced, even on sale for 10$ but there aren't many games that let you decorate and the artstyle is really nice.

Unpacking is a light puzzle game of block-fitting elements that tells of the life of the individual whose items you’re unpacking. As you go through their life over the years, you go through their hardships, their milestones and everything in between. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2808962706

[h1]Storytelling[/h1]

Akin to what Bioshock did in terms of story telling with audio logs back then by giving life to Rapture as a world that has lived and gone as it lay desolate in its current state, Unpacking does this without spoken words but rather with the items that you unpack. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2808963083

[h1]Relate[/h1]

As you unpack, the more of the unnamed character’s life is revealed, their character, their quirks, their hobbies, their goals, their predicament. Every stage reveals layers of their personality and makes it feel so personal that will leave you reflecting on yourself. The level of one’s personal feelings can vary and it can amplify it further if you lived during similar periods as the character.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2808963104

[h1]Troll & (Wi)i[/h1]

It starts off with you unpacking a room and slowly progresses to more sections of the different houses the character you’re unpacking lives in at different periods of their life. From unpacking Dam Troll to CRT monitor to Wii and more, in every stage you will be unpacking items that fit the timeline well. Each item that you unpack will have a number of unspecified areas which you can put them in, you can hang clothes, fold them into a pile, stack books or place them upright against a leaning surface. There’s multiple ways to store and place items where they belong so the flexibility is very welcoming.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2808963374

As you complete the levels, you’ll unlock stickers which you can collect and use to take a photo of the rooms, with filters and frames also available to be added. There’s some hidden achievements and tasks you can do to unlock more stickers, some are along the lines of common sense or human nature for you to do whereas others are more obscure.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2808963399

Another “add-on” that is present once you’re done with the level is the ability to watch your replay of the whole level or saving and viewing a gif of each room you did, which is a nice touch by the developers.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2808963431

[h1]Growth[/h1]

From unpacking a simple drawing on a paper to a table top Easel stand and a drawing tablet, from boombox to headphones, iPods. From Tamagotchi to a Wii console, a London bus souvenir to  souvenirs of Eiffel Tower, Windmills of Kinderdijk. This shows the subtle progression in the character’s interest, hobby and goals.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2808963576

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]

Besides being a really intuitive and good light puzzle game, Unpacking shines at telling a story with its collection of items that you unpack. You can’t help but try to figure out what the character is going through, what they went through based on previous levels. To me that in of itself is story-telling in its finest form, providing hints and leaving the player to wander and paint a picture of their own.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2808963595

From an empty space, a room, a house that’s lifeless and with no identity but you will always end up in a home that is lived, has a meaningful experiences to tell and and one that will stay with you forever, just like the Pig Plushie

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2808963616

I've been looking forward to this game for a very long time and I just completed it, and still have achievements to find. I took my time with this game, making sure everything was placed exactly where I wanted it to be and trying to be creative with how I displayed things in the levels. It tells a story in a beautiful way, following somebody through their life and telling us about their personality through the items they keep with them, or the new ones they collect. 

Also, try out the replay tool! So much fun!

I personally saw a lot of myself in the main character that we follow, and because of that I made an extra effort to organize their space as if it was my own. It felt very deep and personal, and the creators of the game did an amazing job telling a story so minimally. 

I recommend this game if you enjoy organization and home decor, and if you are the creative type. I think it's worth full price and that the amount of levels in the game tells the perfect story- though some people may find it rather short if they rush it. 

Fun thing to try: Set objects down on different surfaces! Move them around! There's a TON of sound files in the game, everything sounds perfect and it's a joy to play around with.

Therefore take some shortbread! (I love it so much and it only requires 3 ingredients!!!)

Scottish Shortbread

Ingredients

    2 cups butter, softened
    1 cup packed brown sugar
    4 to 4-1/2 cups all-purpose flour

Directions

    Preheat oven to 325°. Cream butter and brown sugar until light and fluffy, 5-7 minutes. Add 3-3/4 cups flour; mix well. Turn dough onto a floured surface; knead for 5 minutes, adding enough remaining flour to form a soft dough.
    On a sheet of parchment, roll dough to a 16x9-inch rectangle. Transfer to a baking sheet, and cut into 3x1-in. strips. Prick each cookie multiple times with a fork. Refrigerate at least 30 minutes or overnight.
    Separate cookies and place 1 in. apart on ungreased baking sheets. Bake until cookies are lightly browned, 20-25 minutes. Transfer to wire racks to cool completely.

[h1] Релаксуй [/h1]

Игра-до не возможности простая. Вот тебе комната, вот бери коробки и раскладывай все. Собственно все! 

Постепенно, ты узнаешь историю живущих людей...Вот маленькая девчонка, которая любит рисовать. Переносимся на пару лет и мы уже проживаем в общаге и не можем лапать не которые предметы. Еще чуточку вперед по времени, и ты уже дипломированный специалист (как свою жизнь описываю =D)....А потом понеслось...Учеба, любимый человек, работа, детишки, отдельное жилье, новые хобби и увлечения. Все это будет понятно по предметам, которые вытаскиваем из коробок и ставя их в комнаты.

Тупо нарисованы не которые предметы, ибо вытаскиваешь и такой...."А ЧО ЭТО? КУДА ЭТО???", то ли в кабинет тащить, то ли на кухню (даже при приближении не понятно). Музыка расслабляет и ненавязчиво играет, что способствует дальше бездумно вытаскивать предметы из коробок.

Если по чесноку, то через 2 часа становится скучно и однообразно. Ибо игра диктует свои правила(положить в то или иное место) и ты должен подчиниться. Но и за эти 2 часа, мой мозг расслабился и не думал ни о чем конкретно (хотя это редко бывает). Так вот, игра подойдет людям с депресухой и всепоглощающей "тьмой"-чуточку забыться

[h1]Не тільки лампово, а ще й зі змістом.[/h1]

Unpacking - ну дуже лампова та атмосферна гра, яка дозволяє нам розслабитися у кріслі і розкладати речі нашої гг після декількох переїздів (тут досить велика свобода волі щодо порядку розкладання, але є певні правила - ну там сковорідки в ванні не лишати, бо якось їм там не місце, і гра вам про це нагадає). Візуал приємний, музика теж додає розслабленої атмосфери. 

Але крім милих пікселів, тут є ціла історія, яка вдало розкривається через певні геймплейні моменти та маленькі, на перший погляд непомітні деталі. Ми проживаємо разом з нашою гг її дорослішання, стосунки, досягнення в кар'єрі - і з кожним разом обмежень щодо розкладання речей стає усе меньше, коли вона стає більш незалежною та зустрічає людину, з якою їй дійсно комфортно будувати майбутнє. Наприклад чого тільки вартий момент, коли [spoiler]ми бачимо, як в перших стосунках вона може покласти свій диплом лише під кровать або взагалі повісити над унітазом, бо хлопець іншого місця не дає, а потім спокійно може повісити його на саме видне місце де завгодно, коли зустрічає свою майбутнью дружину? А ще та дрібничка, що коли вони з'їджаються разом, вона ставить для коханої окрему шафку для речей, докупила стеллаж у вітальню (бо розуміє ці відчуття, коли тебе насправді не чекають, згадати лише тот безлад у квартирі її хлопця)?[/spoiler] 

Тож гра дійсно варта уваги. Вона продумана до дрібничок, медитативна і до неї приємно повернутися, щоб знову розслабитися.

Я ждал выхода этой игры с Летнего фестиваля игр. Еще тогда меня заинтересовал геймплей, - простой, расслабляющий, но при этом не дающий игроку унывать. И в июльской демке игра правда показалась очень любопытной, 2 уровня дали представление об интересной механике "впихнуть невпихуемое" и появилось желание ждать выхода полной версии, в которой обещали еще больше вещей, интересный сюжет и обстановка.

Что же мы получили в итоге?

1. Геймплей - расставление нужных предметов в нужных комнатах. Не дает унывать в начале. Свежий духом, ты расставляешь предметы по полочкам вещи и радуешься жизни. На втором уровне даже приходится подумать, но после того как прошел эти 2 уровня (дублирующиеся из демо), становится очень тяжело играть и появляется желание выйти. Но потом появляется желание пройти еще один уровень и так снова. Это странно, но эту игру не получается пройти за раз.

2. Сюжет. Его нет. Почти. Весь сюжет - записи главной героини в альбоме и фотографии в интерьерах её новых квартир. Но в конце и правда милый момент с отношениями двух девушек.

3. Реиграбельность. Игру можно пройти еще раз, если включить режим свободной расстановки вещей для расслабления или чтобы получить все ачивки.

The game is satisfying to play. The sound effects and snappy grid placement make it feel nice and zen to place things in the world.

That said, I just can't get past the game's opinionated take on the "correct" placement of certain household items, particularly in the kitchen area.

The second level encouraged me to place a skillet far out of reach of any viable cooking surface, which suggests that the creators of this game don't cook. Everyone knows you put skillets and pans *close* to the stove, preferably on racks hanging off the walls. This encourages you to cook. If you put the skillet up high on a shelf, you create more friction between yourself and a nice healthy meal. 

The game is subtly suggesting unhealthy eating habits. At the very least it doesn't punish you for putting the cookies high up on the shelf where they should go, but it definitely didn't want me to put the sugar up there. Salt I understand, but most meals don't need added sugar.

Now I'm not sure if this is a narrative element of the game. It was 2004, my very first apartment before college. And I must admit that I wasn't cooking for myself all that much either back then. But maybe I'm playing the game to relive those years as a better version of myself, one where I take even better care of my health and regularly cook healthy meals. Don't punish me for putting a pan where it obviously needs to go!

The game has the ability to turn puzzle mode off, but it's on by default so you have to dig through menus to freely place items where they should go. I also mistakenly put the large stock pot on the burner, failing to realize the skillet is a valid placement and you can put the stock pot in the cabinet below. The game's trailer even suggests this.

So maybe I'm just impatient. Cleaning materials should go under the sink since you use them with a certain degree of regularity. I'm definitely not going to put the stock pot on the top shelf because I use mine all the time. 

I think I generally disagree with the opinion that any cookware should go on the top shelf. No top shelf placement for pots and pans should be valid, and you should be able to place sugar up there because it is a non-essential cooking ingredient. If you have to climb on the counters to get the sugar and the cookies, you've at least burned off some of the calories you will consume.

And that brings me to mouthwash. It's totally unnecessary, but the game has you place it in a prime position on the bathroom sink. Nobody needs to buy mouthwash. It's only as popular as it is because the Listerine corporation couldn't sell it as a household cleaner, so they invented this narrative about bad breath to scare people into buying the stuff.

Mouthwash goes in the cabinet below the sink, or you can just pour it down the drain. That's the "correct" placement.

Don't be fooled by the claims of it being any kind of puzzle. Most people will find zero challenge in this. That's fine, if you go with those expectations. The only real challenge is that things need to be put in the "right" place. 99% of the time it is obvious. The rest of the time there's no way of telling what the game wants you to do other than trial & error. You've placed all the objects and some of the glow red, which means they're not in an approved place. The diary in the first room has to go in your drawer, not on a shelf. The gamecube has to go on the TV stand, not on the shelf next to the TV. You can't put your diploma on the bathroom wall, you have to put it under the bed. These aren't wrong, exactly, but they feel pretty arbitrary. When you have roommates sometimes you can move some of their things to make room, sometimes you can't, and the only way to know the difference is to try clicking on something.

There's no way to fail, no time limit, no pressure. No real bonuses or achievements other than your own personal satisfaction for organising things in one way over another. Organise your shoes from smallest to biggest: fine. Throw them in a jumble: also fine.

People talk about the "story" but let's be clear: this is pretty trite obvious stuff: girl goes to college, girl graduates and gets roommates, girl moves in with boyfriend, girl breaks up with boyfriend. It is reasonably clever that this is done via environmental storytelling of our stuff. And you do see how our changing possessions reflect us and our changes in life. She gradually picks up souvenirs from her European trips. Her childhood stuffed animals stay with her through life, as other things come and go. Moving into her boyfriend's apartment it feels like there's no room for her stuff...is that a metaphor for how there's no room for her in his life? If that kind of subtle thing strikes as deeply moving storytelling I guess you like what they're trying to do here.

引っ越しした先で段ボールを開封し、可愛らしいドット絵で描かれたアイテムをひたすら黙々「相応しい場所に」収めていくチルめのお片付け作業ゲーム。

とはいえ、所詮はプレイヤーからすれば「他人の荷物」でしかないわけで……そこに親近感を覚えるか、はたまたイラつきを覚えるかは、そのプレイヤー次第なので[b]人によっては逆にストレスが溜まる可能性もあります。[/b]この荷物の主が後生大事に保持している品物ですら、他人からすればただの……。
故に、[u]やや女性向け・どんなストーリーが来ても気にせず聞き流せる人用[/u]という感じはします。
[b]何がとはあえて言いませんが、買う際は「ユーザーが定義したこの製品への人気タグ」を確認する事をおすすめします、お察しください。[/b]

それらの点を気にせず、単純な可愛いお片付けゲーとして楽しむ分にはおすすめです。

A Engenharia do Cotidiano e o Fascínio do Espaço
A análise de videojogos frequentemente subestima obras com fachadas minimalistas. Unpacking, da Witch Beam, é o exemplo perfeito desse equívoco. Sob a superfície de um simulador de organização doméstica, esconde-se uma verdadeira obra de arte da engenharia de puzzles espaciais. Este é um dos passatempos mais mecanicamente satisfatórios da história recente. A experiência flui com graciosidade quase ininterrupta, ancorada em um ciclo de jogabilidade que domina a psicologia da recompensa e a liberação constante de dopamina.

Design Espacial e a Irrelevância Narrativa
Para compreender a genialidade técnica do título, precisamos dissecar o seu alicerce fundamental: o design de espaço. O jogo exige uma leitura geométrica rigorosa. Cada ambiente funciona como um tabuleiro invisível onde a física dos objetos interage perfeitamente com a topografia do cenário. A resposta visual é imediata e o encaixe cria uma satisfação tátil que prende a atenção de forma absoluta.

Embora grande parte da crítica exalte o conceito de narrativa ambiental, é preciso ser honesto. Essa imersão na história pregressa da personagem não funcionou totalmente para a minha experiência. É exatamente neste ponto que o design estrutural prova a sua força, pois a obra não depende da empatia narrativa para ser absurdamente engajante. A força motriz real da experiência é a arquitetura da progressão mecânica.

O Motor da Ansiedade Positiva
A ansiedade e a antecipação palpável para descobrir o que acontecerá no próximo ano atuam como um motor implacável. O jogador é impulsionado pela curiosidade técnica em descobrir qual será a complexidade arquitetônica do novo apartamento e como o volume do inventário vai desafiar a capacidade de otimização. A curva de dificuldade sustenta o peso do jogo magistralmente.

Esse engajamento é elevado por um polimento audiovisual irretocável. A arte em pixels oferece clareza impecável, mas o verdadeiro destaque é o departamento de som. O trabalho de efeitos sonoros responde dinamicamente ao material do objeto e à superfície de contato. Essa resposta auditiva cria uma imersão rítmica e profundamente terapêutica.

Platina, Cansaço e Rejogabilidade
Para os jogadores focados em platinar suas bibliotecas, Unpacking apresenta uma dualidade interessante. O título é facilmente platinável e direto. No entanto, a exigência de retornar a fases anteriores para engatilhar ações escondidas ou manipular itens fora de contexto quebra o fluxo orgânico da organização. Essa repetição mecânica torna o processo final um pouco exaustivo e cansativo.

Felizmente, os desenvolvedores implementaram álbuns rejogáveis que mitigam esse cansaço. Eles funcionam como um modo criativo, permitindo experimentar novas configurações sem punições. Isso adiciona um excelente fator de rejogabilidade para quem deseja apenas organizar os cenários livremente, sem compromisso com a campanha.

Veredito
Em conclusão, Unpacking é um triunfo monumental do design focado na experiência do usuário. Mesmo que a narrativa silenciosa não estabeleça uma conexão emocional profunda, a estrutura lúdica sustenta a obra de forma autônoma. A excelência técnica na manipulação espacial, a maestria do feedback sonoro e a vontade constante de desbravar a próxima caixa justificam absolutamente cada minuto investido. Um título altamente recomendado para qualquer pessoa que saiba apreciar a beleza da ordem surgindo do caos.

Es una joya minimalista que demuestra que no se necesitan diálogos para conmover profundamente. A través del simple acto de sacar objetos de cajas, el juego teje una narrativa silenciosa y poderosa sobre el crecimiento, los cambios de etapa y la búsqueda de un lugar propio en el mundo.
Es increíble cómo el diseño de sonido y la estética pixel art logran que sientas una conexión con alguien que nunca ves.

Cada habitación cuenta un capítulo de vida: desde la emoción del primer dormitorio hasta las decisiones difíciles de la adultez.

[h1] ▶️ Gameplay[/h1]
https://youtu.be/Z8bM65RJ9Co?si=2REj_ddTqx0yDHGZ


[h1] 👍 Pros  [/h1]
+ Adorable graphics -- very cute, love the pixel art
+ Cozy vibes with relaxing music 
+ Fun to explore, especially as you watch them grow up
+ The story is subtle, but quite emotional as you slowly get attached to the MC
+ Photoshoot function for the rooms is pretty cute heheh
+ Toilet roll can be rotated (lol)


[h1] ❗Cons [/h1]
- Some items, I feel, should be possible to be placed in other rooms (but that's probably personal preference) 
- The isometric nature of the game and how it auto-rotates in certain angles when you're gliding makes it confusing to navigate sometimes.


[h1] 🤔 Conclusion [/h1]
This is a lovely game perfect for days when you wanna get in the feels. It's sweet and relaxing, but also strangely empowering because as you are 'helping' them unpack MC's life in the spaces she is in, you also witness her wins and the challenges she is facing at the time.

I would highly recommend it for those who appreciate cozy, wholesome games where you take your time to play it (especially if it's on discount).

本作是一款将“拆箱整理”玩出极致治愈与情感深度的禅意益智游戏，没有激烈的对抗、没有紧迫的计时，仅以8次搬家场景，就用最细腻的“物品叙事”陪玩家走过一位普通人从独居宿舍到成家立业的人生轨迹。从拆出第一只马克杯到布置完整间家庭住宅，指尖的每一次摆放，都是在拼凑一段藏在物件里的生活，那些被保留的童年玩具、新增的情侣摆件、失意时丢下的旧照片，没有一句台词，却把成长、相遇、离别与温暖讲得动人心弦，玩到结局时，心底只剩被生活细节填满的柔软。
游戏的核心玩法融合了轻解谜与家居布置，将数百种物品按生活逻辑归置到对应空间，从叠餐盘、挂毛巾到摆书籍，每一次精准摆放都能收获满满的成就感。制作组对生活的还原度拉满，插座旁摆电器、橱柜分层放厨具，甚至会有“照片藏起来避嫌”的趣味细节，而像素画风的暖调色彩搭配BAFTA获奖作曲家打造的舒缓配乐，让整个整理过程成为一场沉浸式的减压体验，哪怕是碎片时间玩上一局，也能让浮躁的心情瞬间平静。
当然游戏并非完美，像素风格虽精致却让部分物品辨识度偏低，偶尔会因分不清物件属性陷入反复试摆的尴尬；而部分关卡的摆放判定偏死板，与个人生活习惯相悖时，会稍显束缚感。但这些小瑕疵完全不影响核心体验，更何况无障碍模式支持“随意摆放”，能满足不同玩家的游玩需求。
 整体而言，本作早已超越了“收纳模拟器”的范畴，它是一款用物件讲述生活的治愈佳作，适合每一个喜欢慢节奏游戏、渴望在虚拟世界中寻找生活暖意的玩家。在这个快节奏的时代，能有这样一款游戏让我们静下心来整理、感受生活的点滴美好，本身就是一种难得的体验。

Una experiencia que todos deberían disfrutar alguna vez, crear una cercanía con personajes que nunca hablaron ni se mostraron, sino que en cambio mostraron lo más intimo que también puede resultar una simpleza, una mudanza. Sin embargo el sentimiento que logra transmitir, de familiaridad al ver objetos y como se nota el desgaste en base a cada etapa de la vida, y cómo en cierto nivel se nota la diferencia de no ser un hogar sino un lugar al que se intenta adaptar, la sensación de no encajar, para finalizar encontrando tu propio hogar tiempo después. Un juego que logra transmitir tanto sin decir nada, una carta de amor a los juegos y a la vida, transmitida en silencio, y haciendo te participe de una historia que es ajena, pero se vuelve cercana con el pasar de los años (niveles).

史低入库的，从刚发行就一直放在愿望单的游戏。
玩到最后片尾曲出来的时候有点感触，就仿佛真的陪她经历了从小到大的历程。
女主是个很念旧的人，缝补的玩偶，用到缺一块的杯子，总是跟着搬走的巴黎铁塔等，这些都很有代入感...
其中搬进男友家结果属于自己荣耀的证书只能放在床底，而分手后证书能在墙上有一席之地，这些小细节我都很喜欢。
这是少有我不需要看攻略就能通关的游戏，质量方面我觉得蛮好的，只是如果物品能加上名称之类的会更好，因为有些东西我不太清楚是什么，比如我家没有把药品放在卫生间的习惯，会让没有相同摆放习惯的人感到confused，这应该也是一种文化差异？
史低价格来说，性价比是不错的，可入；原价还是有点太贵了哈。

Unpacking é uma obra-prima minimalista que transforma uma tarefa simples, desempacotar caixas e organizar objetos em uma experiência emocional profunda e significativa.
O jogo prova que não é preciso diálogos nem textos para contar uma boa história. Cada item que o jogador tira da caixa carrega memórias, fases da vida e mudanças internas da personagem principal. Ao organizar os objetos em cada novo ambiente, o jogador também reconstrói a história de alguém, percebendo conquistas, decepções e recomeços de forma sutil e tocante.

Practically, unpack boxes and place items in different rooms and places where they belong. Tidy up, organize, and make the most of the space you're given.
But Unpacking is about more than placing items where they go. It's about pulling a life out of a box and putting it together again. It's about the things we've collected along the way, and what they mean to us. It's understanding who we are by the things we would bring with us to the end of the earth. It's a story.

游戏是好游戏，接着打开箱子把家具搬进家中这样一个简单的操作，一点点地带你了解一个人（或者说，这就是你）的生活，从幼年的孩子到初入大学，再到迫于经济压力去合租，与人坠入爱河又分别，最后找到了一个属于自己的家。ed里有句歌词唱得很好，让你的房子成为你的家，拿来概括整个游戏再适合不过了。
作为一个现在已经离开家外出求学的人而言，看到愈加破旧但始终陪在身边的小猪玩偶时，眼睛和喉咙确实有点酸酸的。
不过游戏虽好，价格实在是有些昂贵了，全价70的基础之上，我没记错的话我是打八折时购入的，但还是小贵，尤其是考虑到我两个小时就全流程打完，甚至成就还解锁了七七八八的情况下，实在是有些不值了。
如果定价能再便宜一些，或者体量再增大一点就好了。

[b]Unpacking[/b] is a game about... unpacking stuff…
Who would’ve guessed huh?

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Click… Clickity click click.
You click on packages, take out items, and place them around the house, do that and go back to move about the last items you left out of place, I mean, maybe placing a toaster in a bathtub is a bad idea, come on now.

[h1]Story[/h1]
You’ll follow a girl moving in, onto the various homes of her life from childhood to adulthood and discover what kind of person she is though all the items she brings along.

Very simple and sweet and shows that telling a story isn’t strictly by outright telling you

[h1]X-Factor[/h1]
A simple “unwind” type of game where there’s a zen-like appeal into the simple act of Unpacking™.

The game also packs (heh) great environmental storytelling as, beside a little text snippet at the end of each stage, the story can only be inferred through the various items you’ll be moving around the house.

The pixelart style is lovely and has that right amount of complexity, giving each item shape and depth, and simplicity, making it distinct from its surroundings, anyone who tried their hand at the style themselves can really appreciate how subtly masterful its use is here.

[h1]Downsides[/h1]
Maybe an object name is needed as a right click option, the squeezed down pixel artstyle often jumbles some detail making you unsure if the rectangle you’re holding is a cleaning product, medicine, or something else entirely.
(and totally not because the culture difference had me never seeing some stuff, no sire)

Unpacking turns the simple task of organizing boxes into an unexpectedly emotional experience. You play as a character moving through different stages of life, unpacking boxes filled with meaningful items. Each level, from dorm rooms to shared apartments, reveals the character’s growth through the objects they’ve collected.

What makes this game special is the way it tells a story without words—just the process of deciding where to place each item. It’s a soothing, meditative journey, and the satisfaction of seeing a room come together is oddly fulfilling. The joy comes from the tiny details: a stuffed animal, a favorite book, or even kitchen gadgets that mark a chapter in life.

If you’re looking for a relaxing, feel-good game that’s all about finding the perfect spot for each item (and discovering a character’s story in the process), Unpacking is a cozy, emotionally rewarding experience.

非常棒的游戏，很快就可以把内心带入到游戏中，我从好奇这是谁的房间到，我欣慰的看着自己的孩子长大了，后面又进入一段新的未知关系的紧张和期待。从细节中你感受到时间的痕迹，最爱的娃娃一点点变旧破损，磁带越来越多，曾经画的角色动物变得越来越多每一部分都见证了主角的成长。

而游戏在感受和进入一段关系的思考上耶十分出色，和人合租时我们不可以触碰和移动对方的物品，即便混乱也尊重对方不去触碰。而第一段关系，我感受并不好，我感觉我好像入侵了对方的生活，必须移动对方的物品才可以挖掘自己的空间，这表示进入一段深入的关系可以触碰彼此生活，但这样局促的空间让我感到不安和一种被压制的感觉。我没有很多空间可以摆放绘画物品和书籍，对方原本的轨迹也必须移动才可以让我进入。而最难过的是我完全找不到地方挂我的毕业证书，我只能将它隐藏在床底，这感觉像是我要将自己收起来才可以小心维持这段关系。

而回到第一个房间时，我感到既熟悉又陌生，但慢慢又安心下来，我想知道发生了什么，一点一点的把东西拿出来，看着那张照片我随手把它挂到墙上，但我发现男人的位置被图钉钉起来，最后发现挂起来其实是错误的，主角并不想看见它。这是应该伤心的时期，但她回到了她安心的家。

第二段关系我开始并没有立刻发现，一切好自然就像是主角和好友一起去快乐的旅行带回来很多纪念品装饰家里。直到一些私人物品逐渐出现我才发现可能是新的感情要进入了。而这次不用担心空间，因为早已经准备好了空间和空位迎接新物品的到来。

随着游戏的推进我仿佛一起走完了主角的一生，最喜欢的玩偶，从未放弃的绘画，获得的奖杯，出书的喜悦，低潮和振作，以及一个家慢慢建成的期待。在最后布置时我甚至在自言自语模拟两个人彼此开着玩笑布置家里。
“hi~你看你把东西装到这里来咯！”
“看！这个衣柜好大，我们可以把衣服都放进去了！”
“哦！我想想，这是你工作房的东西我帮你搬过去了咯~”
......

This is a very charming little game, I enjoyed it quite a bit. I think you could absolutely finish it much faster than I did, especially with the accessibility option to allow placement anywhere, but that kinda defeats the point of the puzzle. It already allows for a lot of personal variation, so I don't think the option really helps with that. Some of the achievements are way more cryptic than I think they should be though, and one of them feels a bit too strict on its vision as compared to the rest, which are largely fairly free placement or encouraging finding easter eggs. The worst achievement, though, requires you go far beyond what the hint in the achievement description would imply, and I genuinely think it's pretty unlikely you would find it without a guide. That aside, as I said, the game is very short, but the puzzle elements make it quite fun in addition to the laid back atmosphere. I do have one complaint with the puzzles though, the last couple of levels go hard on a mechanic that mainly appears in the second level, and is then mostly absent for the rest of the game, that being items that cannot be placed in the room you find them in. I wasted a good few minutes trying to find places for items that couldn't go in the room I was looking through, which was kind of annoying. Overall, for a cozy little puzzle game with a lot of heart, I'd give it a score of 8.75 out of 10, a solid game, but certainly with some room for improvement.

Unpacking : un jeu cozy et nostalgique avec une touche rétro
*Unpacking* est un petit bijou du genre cozy gaming. L’ambiance rétro est parfaitement réussie et donne une sensation agréable de nostalgie. Le concept est simple mais incroyablement satisfaisant : déballer et ranger des objets tout en découvrant, pièce par pièce, des fragments de vie et d’histoire.  

Avec une durée de vie d’environ 5 heures, le jeu est relativement court, ce qui peut être un frein pour certains, surtout compte tenu de son prix plus élevé de 20 €. Cependant, il compense par une rejouabilité intéressante : à chaque partie, on peut réarranger les objets différemment, ce qui apporte un petit vent de nouveauté.  

Ce qui est dommage, c’est qu’il n’a reçu aucune mise à jour ni DLC depuis sa sortie en 2021. Ajouter de nouvelles pièces, des années d’aménagement, ou des défis supplémentaires aurait pu prolonger la durée de vie et enrichir l’expérience.  

En résumé : *Unpacking* est parfait pour les amateurs de jeux cozy et relaxants, avec un charme rétro et une ambiance unique. Il reste un peu cher pour sa durée de vie, mais il offre une expérience mémorable et rejouable. Un vrai plaisir, malgré l’absence d’ajouts post-lancement !

You just moved in and your stuff is in the cardboard boxes. Time for unpacking. 

Unpacking is an isometric click-and-drag game, where you help the same woman unpack at different points ih her life, taking her from childhood all the way to fufilling ultimate millenial fantasy of moving into your own house. Do not be deceived, however, as the game is not devoid of story. It is a masterclass of enviromental storytelling, that functions as a puzzle you can solve, by observing which things have been carried over to your new home, what appeared or what was lost. In a way it nails aspects of various stages of life. My favorite level by far is 2007, the feeling on moving in to live with your nerdy rommates, playing d&d game nights, having your first job after college. The later part of the game, starting with slowly emotionally crushing 2010 level all the way to the end, are a hurricane of emotions, once you realize how is the protagonist's life unfolding.

Unpacking is a simple, but extremely effective way that you could, if you want, finish in one sitting, but I recommend taking your time and getting to really take things in. Highly recommended.

This game was so fun and soothing to play. I only expected that you'd be organizing things and, as the title suggests, unpacking things in random rooms. But I was happily wrong, you follow the main character and their life from childhood to adulthood in all the places they live. Not only are you being fed puzzling ways to fill and decorate rooms but you're discovering the life story of this character the further you progress. 

The game itself is impressive and very detail oriented, you can tell a lot of love and work went into it. The only thing I have to say that is disappointing is how fast this game can be finished. I know some players finished it in one sitting in a few hours, as for myself I spread it out over a few days, and sadly was met with a very quick end. With that in mind, I think it's a game that easily can be played over and over again without becoming dull, and you also have achievements that you can aim for that you probably won't get all of them in one play through. I also would add that In the beginning of the game you choose a photo album and begin your unpacking journey, I have hopes that in the future they may add more albums to follow more character's lives and allow for further content. I think there is so much potential for the game and room for further content and stories. Honestly it's a wonderful game and I'm glad it exists, I was happily surprised by how much I enjoyed it!

После прохождения, игра оставила после себя какую-то безысходное послевкусие с нотками грусти: "Неужели это всё? Только одна история?" Эти вопросы пролетали в голове, пока я кликала мышкой по меню, убеждаясь в том, что да: история лишь одна. 
Казалось бы, обычная распаковка вещей, которые необходимо раскладывать по своим местам в каждый период жизни главной героини. Но игра после второго переезда девушки заставила обращать внимание на детали: "О, вот эту игрушку она снова взяла с собой! ой, она истрепалась уже от времени, но она всё равно ей дорожит." 
Ух ты, после жизни с девушкой косплеером, она так же увлеклась готовкой и начала шить, лепить фигурки. Переезд к парню сразу вызвал ощущения неуместности главной героини в его жилище: атрибуты своих достижений - диплом, вынуждена была забросить под кровать, где-то едва нашла, куда можно поставить старую приставку или диски с играми. После разрыва отношений она увлеклась музыкой, полюбила кофе: осталась маленькая гитара, и стала брать те же пакеты с кофе, что стояли у него дома.
После переезда к родителям, забросив совместное фото с бывшим под кровать, главная героиня нашла в этом этапе "исцеление для себя" после расставания, даже символично зашила на пузике дырочку у любимой игрушки.
И как же стало тепло на душе, когда гг  впустила в свою жизнь партнера, рядом с которым она чувствует себя собой и расцветает: начитает больше уделять времени своим увлечениям, наконец, докрашивает фигурку девушки с лютней, в доме появляется больше души, больше интересных вещей, больше жизни и, наконец, меняет свой старый многолетний гардероб на множество новых. По мелочам видно, что героини разные, но интересы у них схожи и им хорошо вдвоем.
Спасибо, за такую игру, внимательную к мелочам, деталям, жаль, что её очень и очень мало

I'm glad I got this game on sale. While I recognize that the designers, etc. put a lot of work into making it, I think I would have personally been disappointed if I spent $20 on it.

Pros:
* Cute, nostalgic pixel graphics! I liked the photo mode and filters.
* Short and sweet, if that's the kind of game experience you're looking for.
* I enjoyed how the items you unpacked told a story about the main character's life without words. Moments that reminded me of trying to fit my stuff into a space where someone else already lived, combining my life with another person's. It was cool to learn details about the person's background through the context clues of their belongings.

Cons:
* The pixel graphics also made it so that sometimes it was very difficult to figure out what an item was and where it should go. Most of the time, it's fairly flexible on where you put something as long as it vaguely makes sense (clothing in the closet, bathroom items in the bathroom, etc.) but there were quite a few times where it was hard to know where they wanted you to put something, to get the red outline around an item telling you it's in the wrong spot to go away. The kitchens were especially bad about this.
* Like I said, it's very short. About 3-4 hours of gameplay, depending on how quickly you can unpack the items (I was a little more meticulous with it than some, probably.)
* The extreme usage of 'show, don't tell' made this game sometimes feel a little empty, for me. It didn't quite match the hype of how wonderful and relaxing I heard it was. I also found the end credits song almost unbearably cheesy and grating. 

Bottom line, I can only recommend Unpacking if you can get it for maybe $8 or less. It had cute moments and a unique concept, but for me it has almost no replay value once you've gotten through the 3~ hours of gameplay.

故事线也非常巧妙（下方大概涉及剧透？）
只靠照片定格时的一句话和许许多多生活中的细节，玩家完全可以拼凑出主角这几年的经历——崭新到用旧的鼠标垫，喝水的马克杯搬家后变成了刷牙杯，逐渐有了裂纹也没有扔，越来越多的马克笔和绘画工具，速写本最后多到需要用架子单独放，以及从童年就陪伴自己的小猪，从崭新到破了口子漏出棉花，再一次搬家之后拿出来，口子又变成了补丁……游玩时仿佛我就是主人公，品味着我起伏的人生。
我知道你搬去和恋人住时的苦恼，他的家大得有些冷清，又小得连你的一块证书都放不下；我也知道你搬走后回了老家，一边感叹着 这房间 这张床 小时候感觉更大些，一边从行李里掏出一个前男友家的小玩意；我知道你后来有了自己的房子，事业也取得了成功，又认识了喜欢穿波点连衣裙的可爱妹妹，她搬来你家住，装行李的纸箱还是你帮她开的呢；再往后你们有了婴儿房，你用心准备着小孩子需要的一切，期待着这个生命的到来，游戏的最后你们一起坐在院子里看夕阳，你弹着尤克里里，为她唱了一首很棒的歌。
谢谢，玩完尸体暖暖的了……

Dlatego że (przynajmniej z pozoru) nie epatuje dramatyzmem i pełną napięcia akcją? Odmienność nigdy nie była prosta, i potwierdza się to w każdej niezależnej grze, którą trudno dopasować do któregoś z głównych nurtów.

[i]Unpacking[/i] uderza nas od samego początku poczuciem ogromnej melancholii za czymś, czego tak naprawdę nigdy nie przeżyliśmy. Jest to z jednej strony piękne, a z drugiej przytłaczające, wręcz dołujące. Czy więc gra z takimi konsekwencjami naprawdę zasługuje na miano przytulnej? Oj tak, bezsprzecznie. Rozpakowywanie pudeł nigdy nie było tak przejmujące, jak teraz, gdy w praktyce rozpakowywałem coś więcej – własne emocje.

Chociaż proste w formie (ale okraszone przesłodką oprawą graficzną i wyjątkowym soundtrackiem), ta gra to filozoficzne doznanie, które poruszy w nas głębokie struny i zmusi do rozmyślań nad poczuciem przynależności do czasu i miejsca, do osób które do naszego życia trafiły i z niego odeszły; nad tym co właściwie czyni nas – nami.

Odpowiadając na zadane na początku pytanie – oczywiście, że nie. Cieszę się, że żyję w czasach, gdy każdy może znaleźć dla siebie tytuł, który naprawdę go oczaruje. Oby tylko nikt nie oczekiwał, że wszystko musi być dla wszystkich, bo tak nie jest.

[h1] REVIEW [/h1]
[b] Unpacking [/b] is a casual sorting puzzle game.  
[h3] STORY [/h3]
You seem to be following a female protagonist as she moves into different places through her life. There are a total of 8 puzzles to unpack and place objects.
[h3] GAMEPLAY[/h3]
The puzzles deal with unpacking boxes and finding a home for each item unboxed.
[h3] PLAYTIME [/h3]
The game is not complicated and each map takes around the same amount of time, until you get to the last board, which seems to triple the amount of unpacking needed to happen. Play time is ~4-5 hours to complete the campaign and get all achievements.
[h3] COMPLAINTS [/h3]
There is nothing specific to complain about for this game.
[h3] REPLAYABILITY [/h3]
There is NO replayability on this game, unless you want to unpack the same boxes and find different places for items.
[h3] RECOMMENDATION [/h3]
I recommend this game to anyone that likes casual games or is an achievement hunter.

I loved everything about Unpacking. Looks inconspicuous and yet it's so full of detail and has an amazing story. You get to learn the character's life's story without ever meeting them. Unpacking the boxes and placing things neatly is, on its own, very satisfying and relaxing, and at first I though that was all it was, and I was still very happy about it, but boy was I wrong.
First of all, it takes you down the memory lane, with the old-time consoles, toys and boombox (at least me), but what really got to me was how much I understood the life of the character just by looking at her stuff! I don't want to give any spoilers, but let me just say, it's happy and sad and so beautiful.
The music also shows the mood of a situation, which I appreciated a lot and the final song made me tear up a bit.
It's a short game that can be finished in one evening, but I come back to it every now and then. It's very cozy and chill, good relax before bed. I also loved the small details, such as right-clicking an object let's you interact with it.
Definite recommend. Love, love, love! <3

This game is really cute. It does everything it wants to do, with some annoying aspects.

Unpacking is a casual game where you literally unpack boxes and arrange the pieces throughout different rooms, throughout a girl's life. The overall narrative is actually really nice, and the continuity between each session is packed with detail (a poster 3 years later will have a corner torn, or a stuffed animal will be noticeably dirtier, or she'll have more of the same type of plush next year). Overall, it was very fun, though I got bored quickly and Jade took over and had a ton of fun.

There is also a supreme attention to detail, things like the cup full of paintbrushes will make a sound if you shake them by moving the mouse, there are achievements for little easter eggs (I got one for organizing the boyfriend's sock drawer when she moved in), or the album caption changing depending on which room you decide to make the scrapbook photo for that year.

That being said, it is annoying to not be able to change the room angle, but the worst part is the game shoehorning you into certain aspects (for example, you can't leave things on the floor, or pots in a cabinet with their handles poking out). Most of them make sense, but figuring out what they want at all can end up being frustrating, it makes you feel like you don't have the creative freedom you were promised.

[h1] Unpacking [/h1]
[code][b] Gatunek: [/b]relaksacyjny symulator
[b] Dla kogo: [/b]dla wszystkich
[b] Poziom trudności: [/b]bardzo łatwa
[b] Czas gry: [/b]5h
[/code]

Uwielbiam studio Humble Games za to, że potrafią stworzyć tak kolorowe, casualowe gry jak chociażby Lost Nova czy Forager. Takie, że siadając do komputera po ciężkim dniu wiemy, że się przy nich zrelaksujemy i nic złego nam się w nich nie stanie. Taki jest też Unpacking, czyli produkcja skupiona na, dosłownie, rozpakowywaniu rzeczy i układaniu ich na miejsce,

[b][u]Historia[/u][/b]
Czy gra tego typu może mieć w sobie jakąkolwiek fabułę? Okazuje się, że tak! I to właśnie ona czyni Unpacking tak dobrym. Świetne jest to, że przez rozpakowywanie rzeczy możemy poznać życie naszej głównej bohaterki. Gdzie się wprowadzała, jakie pamiątki trzymała ze sobą przez całe życie, czym interesowała się w dzieciństwie i czy przełożyła w późniejszym czasie te hobby na pracę?
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3108972395
[b][u]Oprawa audiowizualna i klimat[/u][/b]
Gra posiada bardzo prostą, pikselową grafikę i ambientową oprawę audio. Szkoda, że twórcy nie zdecydowali się na trójwymiarowe sprite’y i dioramy z grafiką przypominającą stylistycznie chociażby jedną z najnowszych produkcji Humble Games - Coral Island albo The Sims Project Rene. Myślę, że całość byłaby jeszcze bardziej klimatyczna i przytulna.

[b][u]Rozgrywka[/u][/b]
Nie ma tu większej filozofii - każdy poziom składa się z kilku pomieszczeń, w których znajdują się kartony pełne rzeczy do rozpakowania. Fajne jest to, że poziomy są bardzo zróżnicowane, np. raz wprowadzimy się do akademika, w którym nie możemy przestawiać przedmiotów innych lokatorów. Innym razem zamieszkamy u chłopaka w małej klitce, w której prawie nic się nie mieści, a jeszcze kiedy indziej dostaniemy do dyspozycji całe, wielkie i całkowicie puste mieszkanie. Bardzo ucieszyły mnie również wyzwania poboczne, bo miło w tak prostej i krótkiej grze mieć jakiś powód do zagrania w dany level ponownie po przejściu gry. Nie są one skomplikowane, bardziej na zasadzie easter eggów, dla przykładu - prawym przyciskiem myszy zwykle obraca się przedmioty, ale kostka rubika działa inaczej i klikając kilka razy sprawimy, że się ułoży. Za taką akcję gra wynagrodzi nas naklejką. Czasami też gra wymaga od nas zabrania przedmiotu z jednego pomieszczenia i umieszczeniu go w innym. Super, że wyzwania nie są tylko osiągnięciami na steamie, a także wbudowanymi w grę naklejkami. Dzięki temu cieszyć się będzie mógł nimi każdy, bez względu na jakiej platformie gra. Rzeczy rozkładamy jak chcemy, więc dla niektórych Unpacking może być tylko relaksującą przygodą na jeden wieczór, u kogoś innego za to obudzi się dusza projektanta i będzie starał się, żeby wnętrza były urządzone perfekcyjnie.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3108972301
[b][u]Podsumowanie[/u][/b]
W zasadzie wszystko już napisałem - jeśli lubisz spokojne gry i urządzanie wnętrz, to jesteś idealnym targetem Unpacking. Szkoda, że całość nie jest choć trochę dłuższa, bo nie wydaje mi się by pełna cena gry była adekwatna do zawartości. Prosta rozgrywka i prosta oprawa audiowizualna - niby nic nadzwyczajnego, a mimo wszystko wciąga.

额，忘记这个是多少钱买的，但是通关之后还是有点震惊，真的有点短，我个人觉得这个游戏售价20左右撑死了。

我是在b站上看了c菌玩，挺喜欢的，就买了一个。总体来说挺治愈的，随着主人公的长大，添置了新物品，也保留了很多小时候的物品，和我本人还挺像的，我也有很多充满回忆的小物件舍不得扔，随着搬家保留20年前的东西，有时候看到了还是很感动。

游戏里主要就是从纸箱子里面取东西然后在家里摆好，不知道纸箱子里下一个会蹦出来什么东西，带着未知的新鲜感摆物品，可能之后的东西要归类好还要前面的物品挪一挪，看到熟悉的物品会心一笑，放在熟悉的位置也挺好。然后有些物品有特定的位置，没有摆放正确就需要多尝试几次，其他的剧情基本上靠脑补，总体来说是个轻量休闲小游戏，挺适合摸鱼。

不过现实里搬家才发现东西超多，要是所有东西能这么整齐就好了，真 • 游戏里咣咣收拾，现实里乱七八糟。

[h1][url=store.steampowered.com/app/1135690/Unpacking/]Unpacking[/url] follows a young girl's emancipation into adulthood with the unusual delight of discovering the next item in a box and where to best place it.[/h1]

It is a cute concept that wins in simplicity, delivery and creativity. Sorting items after moving into a new home may technically sound like a boring chore to some but it turned out to be a very enjoyable experience, given the proper laid-back state of mind.

Appreciate subtleties like how your character will not touch her roommate's stuff but she can later easily reorganize her lover's, or how you can place your toothbrush in a cup by the sink. Figure out where mismatched items go, in which room or specific location. Stack things neatly and make your place comfortable and tidy.

Scenes increase in complexity, with new and more rooms available as your character matures through her life stages, gets into new studies, goes through breakups or new relationships, and achieves professional success. Each scene marks a key change in her life. It surprisingly achieves a decent form of minimal storytelling without words or on-screen characters.

I appreciate short, candid experiences but Unpacking still ends rather abruptly. I was genuinely expecting the main character to grow into old age, maybe even end on a bittersweet note, but the developers chose to leave the story in her prime years instead, which gives it a bit of unfinished state.

You can organize items anywhere that makes sense, and while the game is relatively permissive it won't let you leave irregular arrangements untended. Aside from placing things in a temporary location while you figure out where you really want them, there isn't much of a puzzle component.

Without any description of what an item is, few ones were a little more difficult to figure out, but most are easily identified. Anyone who's ever run a household will instinctively know where most things go. There is rarely an occasion where you will run out of place, though a few rooms are more cramped than others. Furniture can't be moved, so the basics of the room have to remain untouched.

Earn stickers for placing special combinations of items together. Take photos of your rooms for the scrapbook.

The game is built on okay pixels but it is not visually outstanding. The pastel art style did not really appeal to me as it felt more functional than inventive, but it also does not detract my appreciation. The soundtrack felt likewise serviceable but relatively bland, despite good sound effects. I was drawn to the game's content and freshness more than its presentation style.

[h3]Positive[/h3]
[list]
[*] Simple and creative concept
[*] A charming and relaxing experience, almost cathartic
[*] Everything in its right place, leave no mess behind
[*] Items stack neatly where appropriate
[*] Stickers earned from special item combinations
[*] Scenes tell a story from key moments in the character's life without words
[/list]

[h3]Negative[/h3]
[list]
[*] Ends rather abruptly
[*] Okay pixels, not visually outstanding
[*] Serviceable but bland soundtrack
[*] No item descriptions
[/list]

Unpacking é um jogo que me emocionou profundamente enquanto eu descobria, pouco a pouco, a história da protagonista através de suas mudanças de vida. Cada fase é uma janela para momentos marcantes de sua jornada, revelados pelos objetos que vamos organizando nos cômodos. Desde a alegria de uma nova conquista até os desafios que ela enfrenta, tudo é contado de forma silenciosa, mas poderosa, apenas pelo que escolhemos guardar ou descartar.

O jogo transmite uma narrativa tão íntima e sensível que é impossível não criar uma conexão com a protagonista. Ver como sua vida evolui, suas paixões mudam e seus desafios são superados me tocou de uma maneira inesperada. Unpacking não é apenas sobre organizar objetos; é sobre reviver memórias, aprender a deixar coisas para trás e encontrar nosso lugar no mundo. Uma experiência simples, mas cheia de emoção e significado. <3

[h1]Unpacking[/h1]

Are you tired of parachuting into warzones and fighting your way through mountains of 
corpses? Does your stomach feel queasy after buying yet another loot-box that won’t fix your childhood trauma? Is boredom a familiar notion you’re having, browsing through the endless list of monster-fighting games on steam?  Is your life stressful?
 
Unpacking is a zenful game about growing up, finding peace and watching life unfold.
By being observant, you pick up changes in her life, things gone wrong, precious memories, places travelled and hints of what the future holds. Even though the game is about opening boxes and placing things where you feel they belong. It’s more about taking a break and observing the beauty of life.
Such a sweet game with a clever, original mechanic that allows for much more narrative than you would expect. I've played through more than once.

Beautiful game with a gentle narrative; a meditation on growing up, moving out and moving on. 

Hyper-specific experience here, but I ended up playing this on Boxing Day with my mum in the co-pilot seat. While she started off telling me she couldn't understand the appeal of a game about unpacking things, she quickly got into the groove and we found ourselves busy arguing about where to keep the spare toilet paper. 
That gave way to discussion about where life has taken me since I moved out of home over a decade ago; each new house to unpack a recognisable step on my own journey. The devs really nailed the rental market experience - as a fellow Aussie I can tell you I have lived in every rental depicted in this game. It was a memorable way to spend a day with her and while perhaps not the intended playstyle it was the most meaningful experience I've had with a game in a while.

Highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a quiet meditation on life that can be finished in a single sitting (and if you can wrangle it, get your mum involved too).

Oyun size bunu anlatmıyor, ama eşyaları koyduğunuz yerden koliden çıkan eşyaların sırası ve nereden çıktıklarına kadar hikâyeyi sizin oluşturmanıza önayak oluyor. Bunu da oldukça zekice yapıyor. 4-5 saat gibi bir sürede bitse de verilen parayı hak ettiğini düşünüyorum. (Diploma yatağın altına gidecek bu arada)

Spoilerlı olarak:
[spoiler]Kızın önce çocukluğundaki odasını düzüyoruz. Elbette koliden hep oyuncaklar çıkıyor. Geçen yıllarda bu oyuncakların sayısı giderek azalıyor, çünkü çocuk büyüyor. Üniversiteye gidiyor, manita yapıyor ve ayrılıyorlar. Ayrıldıklarını da ikisinin fotoğrafını asamadığınızda anlıyorsunuz. Zaman geçtikçe toplanma konusunda ustalaştığı için yanlış koliden çıkıp da farklı odaya götürdüğünüz eşya sayısı azalıyor. Yetişkinliğe ulaştığında artık kendi evine çıkıyor. Eşyalarını diziyorsunuz. Birkaç sene sonra yine aynı evdeyiz, ama bir bakıyoruz eşyalar artmış. Artık bir sevgilimiz var, ve onun eşyalarını sığdırmakta zorlanıyoruz. Onun da bizim gibi bir oyuncağı var. Finalde ise çift katlı bir eve çıkıyorsunuz. Bunu girişi düzenlerken gözünüze çarpan merdivenden anlayabilirsiniz. Yavaş yavaş odaları düzenleyip üst kata çıktığınızda sizi bir sürpriz bekliyor: Çocuk odası! Bebek bekliyorsunuz ve çocukluğunuzdan beri taşıdığınız oyuncağınız ile kocanızın oyuncağı koliden çıkıyor. "Less is more" felsefesini çok güzel kullanmışlar, tebrik ediyorum.[/spoiler]

[b]乍看之下這是一款讓你體驗搬家後歸納物品的遊戲，但事實上它並不只僅僅是如此而已。[/b]
[hr][/hr]
= 推薦原因: 對於喜歡整理歸納的人，這是一款非常輕鬆的休閒遊戲。過程相當輕鬆，沒有任何壓力，是以部分自由的方式進行，並非能完全照自己方式擺放。

= 不推薦理由: 關卡數量很少，對比遊戲價格可能不是每個人都買帳。建議有特價再考慮。

遊戲運用不同關卡和時間的推進，讓玩家一同參與了主角的不同人生時段。從一開始的房間開始，經歷大學、工作、戀愛，漸漸地，需要歸納的東西越來越多，人生負擔越來越重。遊戲也巧妙運用一些物品，讓他們一同陪著主角和玩家成長，例如粉紅的豬豬玩偶、艾菲爾鐵塔裝飾、破損老舊的漱口杯......有些物品隨著人生不斷變化卻依舊擺在相同的位置，但是過了不久他們也許又會消失，取代而知的則是新的物件。

透過場景的變化，也能稍微推斷出主角人生的起伏轉折。主角是一個活潑的小孩，喜歡足球、也獲得許多獎項，從1997的房間中不難看出，主角從小就對美術和電玩感興趣，粉紅的豬豬玩偶也第一次在這個房間亮相。長大後上了大學，主角開始攻讀美術專業，我們能在書房中整理出主角的電腦和各種書籍。2007年，玩家開始可以整理多個房間，這時主角離開大學並和室友同住，有了工作名片也代表主角已經開始接案工作。2010年主角和男朋友同居在時髦的公寓套房，東西開始變多，玩家歸納起來也相當費力。戀愛後主角便不再是一個人，有很多事情和物件無法隨心所欲，她的美術用品悄悄從畫面中消失。2012年她和男朋友分開了，我們重新回到童年的小屋，很多昔年物件如今也變化許多。整理浴室用品時，也可以知道主角明顯有健康上的狀況。2015年，主角和女朋友同居了，空間越來越狹窄，但是主角這次終於不用再從新的空間開始，似乎也代表女朋友願意接受現在的主角，這些新物品有很多都完美融入舊有的物件中。2018年，主角搬進新的房子中，這次有非常多的東西需要歸納。從工作室的物品來看，主角的事業相當成功，如今她已是一名暢銷繪本作者。她和女朋友也有了小Baby，工作和家庭變成了主角的生活，但是現在的她終於擁有了自己的生活空間，一切也正往美好的未來發展。

這款遊戲背後蘊藏成長的故事，作者巧妙運用場景和物件暗示主角的人生發展。空間和物件代表著當時主角的生活風格，有些物件隨著時間依舊存在，有些則因種種原因而離開。
看似簡單的歸納遊戲，打開的不只是紙箱，而是人生。

The visuals, music, and subtle story all lend themselves to making this one of my new favorite games. It's extremely satisfying to unpack all of the boxes and be able to have a certain amount of freedom when it comes to where you place your belongings. The nuances of certain levels- from items that have followed you throughout the years, to only being able to place certain objects in certain, limited places at times- really gives depth to a story with few words. I've played through twice already in two days and I see this game becoming one I return to in times of stress to decompress. My only criticism is that I wish the game were longer. I hope the developers consider listening to the fans that have fallen in love with this lovely game and consider adding levels in the future.

I love this game. 
I love it so much that I'm still trying to get all the achievements, just so I can spend more time playing it. 
I want updates. I want more rooms. I want more of this game. Let me tell you why on a couple, non-gaming levels before I get to the game itself.

1. This game has helped me organize my house. I suffer from treatment resistant depression, along with MCTD. I have little to no energy, and I don't know where to start when it comes to putting all of my unnecessary crap away. I'm overwhelmed immediately when I see a doom pile I need to take care of. 
2. It's extremely straight forward. No grind, no quests, no loading into zones forever. That makes it an excellent cozy game. You can just put stuff away, be in a meditative state and let your brain unpack itself. 

I love the graphics. They're pixel, but not so "zoomed in" that you're staring at blocks. The music is good, but it doesn't seem to loop. I love the little details, like turning on the radio, game systems, move items around and they do something. Things like that are treasures, almost what I live for in games like this. 

Please, please make more rooms. I wanna unpack a town.

So, I've never written a game review before, but I like Unpacking so much I wanted to give it a try.

I wasn't sure I would get anything out of this game since I've watched multiple streamers play it through in its entirety. I caved out of curiosity and it turns out that organizing these little pixel items on my own terms and time was a totally different experience than watching someone else do it!

I definitely considering myself a bit of a connoisseur for cozy games. Although it lacks in any concrete replayability, Unpacking will be becoming part of my "need to relax" rotation. I've played it through almost three times now, and although the story and items don't change, I find myself enjoying trying to organize the items in a way different from the previous times. Something about organizing all the little books and sketchbooks and clothes according to random, arbitrary rules I create for myself, really scratches an itch in my brain. It's already helped me calm down from a bad mental health episode, and I can see myself adding it into my "toolbox" for mental health management as well.

The environmental storytelling is well crafted, the pixel art is beautiful. I can't speak for the soundtrack since I played on mute (as I do most games). 

The price is a bit of a point of contention for myself and it seems other reviewers as well. Admittedly, I find $20 USD pricey for a solid 4 hours of gameplay and achievements to complete it in it's entirety. Anyone who opts not to replay the game for its "cozy" elements as I might is essentially paying $5/hr for a single game. I'll allow anyone curious to do the math themselves in comparison to price points for other indie/small studio games. 

Aside from that: I really loved this game. I love it so much that I wish there was more of it. More levels, more (perhaps optional) challenges, more locations, etc. I hope Witch Beam chooses to expand on this puzzle game niche in the future.

As I was playing this my boyfriend looked over and said "Oh, you're playing a game about tidying up... that's very on-brand for you." He's wrong that the game is about tidying up, but he's right about my tastes.

Organising things neatly is very satisfying. So this game of unpacking objects and finding homes for them was bound to be fun for me. It's so relaxing to play, and the pixel art and music match the relaxing feel (although I have some notes about the song for the closing credits). I only wish it was longer. I would absolutely play some extra levels if any were ever released.

I'm not sure how "clever" the storytelling is. It perhaps feels more innovative to see it in a game, but telling stories through objects is as old as the hills. On the other hand, the sparsity of the story still works well. It leaves the player's imagination to fill in the gaps, and I found myself projecting my own experiences onto the character. It's no surprise that I then felt an emotional connection to a character who we never meet in the game. I hope she's ok.

Be aware- this is a VERY short game. I got it on sale and I'm glad I did. I fully support small and indie artists, but I personally believe $20 is too much for this game. However, I highly, highly recommend it for anyone who just wants a peaceful, quiet, relaxing game to kill some time or release some stress. 

The music is super cute and nostalgic, if you're a nerd like I am, you'll appreciate all the little details (I could tell what some of the games/movies were). Watching this person go through a small story through the small details is adorable too, and the ending made me tear up a little bit. It's PRECIOUS. 

It's open-ended enough that things belong in certain places, but not an EXACT spot. I say it's replayable because I think it's fun to just figure out the many different configurations you can do. I do hope there's an Unpacking 2 or an update or something in the works, because I'd love to be able to come back and do new things, follow a new story line, etc. Overall, it's a very cute and simple game and perfect for casual players.

Where do you put baby toys when there is no toy box? And is it just me or who doesn't put tinfoil on top of the refrigerator ?!?! Is that just me? AM I THE INSANE ONE?

Nonetheless, I learned a lot in the short game (I had to reply it again because clearly, I do not know where objects belong in a home no matter the size of the place). 沒有人物，沒有文字，只有房間、家具及一些私人物品。
意外故事性很棒，敘述性也很好。

在整理屋子之中，從物件的擺放，慢慢的陪伴/理解/探索主角的成長、性格、喜好、交友、職業等等。

沒想過單純的擺放物件，可以講述的事是如此的深而廣，令人思考很多，相當動人的遊戲。厲害在於，隨著玩家的心境/經歷不同，遊戲所帶來的力量為之不同。

帶給我良好體驗的遊戲，就算遊戲結束了，也能常常讓人回想/沉浸其中。

尤其已經出社會的人，想必更能深刻體會。
[hr]
硬要說缺點的話：
故事有點短
價格有點高

Название игры несет в себе тот же смысл, что мы и будем делать на протяжении полутора-трех часов. Несколько бессмысленная и не особо интригующая игра, но на пару часов искренней медитации - самое оно. Если вы играли в какую-нибудь часть The Sims, то вы сразу поймете, что здесь нужно делать. Как раз таки - это расстановка вещей по комнате девчушки - до состояния зрелой лесбухи. Особой свободы расстановки вещей здесь нету, ведь нужно ставить просто в рамках того, что запланировали разработчики; ноутбук на столе, полотенце в ванне, микроволновка в кухонной мебели и не более того. Ни возможности менять обои, ни расстановка шкафов как нас устраивает - здесь не будет. 

Итак, ежели вы не вернули деньги сразу же после прохождение первой главы, не расстроились из-за незначительной скуки и не скупились отдать деньги за что-то столь бессмысленное, как собственноручная расстановка вещей в изометрическом несуществующем мире, то поздравляю! Вы получаете дозу релакса и солнечного штиля в своей голове на какое-то незначительное время.

reviews.review: Мы оказываемся в разных квартирах, где в каждой комнате расставлены коробки. Открываем их, достаём оттуда предметы и расставляем или раскладываем их. Каждая вещь имеет значение, и это не десяток предметов — в некоторых квартирах расставляешь чуть ли не сотню вещей. И каждому объекту уделяешь внимание: достаёшь его, рассматриваешь, чтобы понять, что это такое, и выбираешь для него место. Unpacking не позволяет класть предметы куда попало: одежда должна быть в шкафу, всякие шампуни и полотенца — в ванной, а книги разбрасывать по всей квартире нельзя.

Se estavam com preguiça de fazer isso, poderiam muito bem deixar o jogo aberto na oficina para a criação de novas histórias pelos próprios players, ou uma ferramenta para isso. What an amazing game that has made me more of a minimalist than I thought I was. There is something so relaxing about creating a space for yourself; thus - creativity is genuinely built in a box.
Unpacking has thus helped me ask myself, “Do I need this?” or “Have I worn this in the last year?” Sometimes life is messy, and things fall into our environments, and we must fish them out. I never realized the items we surround ourselves with could tell our story without meeting us; this has stepped up my homemaking game to demonstrate outer world indeed affects our inner narratives.
As one of the top 3 stressors in life, my Father stated were: divorce, moving, and a new job; Unpacking has helped me understand that this game mirrors an essential evil with life; similar to dusting your room, cleaning dishes, discovering acceptance of these are necessary to “living.”
Unpacking is one of those games enhanced by a fantastic soundtrack the way “Stardew Valley” and “Undertale” have been praised to the point where I will do chores with the soundtrack. I find it delightful to be more mindful of tasks we typically dread. My friend has even noticed a difference in how organized my apartment is, calling me out for making it look like a level in Unpacking - guilty.
Thank you very much for the beautiful hours of the first playthrough and for meeting the “play” criteria of not wanting it to end. Luckily, in life, I can keep moving forward at the levels Unpacking has shown that one can get through; if we unpack one item at a time. We might not know what’s inside the boxes, but eventually, we’ll be done Unpacking and enjoying the moments of “living.”

Short, but cute, and packed full of details. The knick-knacks and clutter in the different settings offer enough context clues to get a good idea of what the "protagonist," so to speak, is like and the game paints a charming picture of a life that had some speed bumps but was nevertheless well lived. The gameplay is simple and easy to grasp, and the game is methodical and relaxing. A lot of care and attention went into the details; the DVDs, BluRays, Wii games, and GameCube games were all distinctive despite their similar size/shape, and I could even recognize covers of games/movies I knew. It can be a little persnickety in where you can or can't put some things, but that's really just a minor nitpick.
(And that persnickety-ness actually led to a pleasant surprise. As a cane-user myself, I put the protagonist's cane in the umbrella stand as a sort of 'haha, me' moment, and then was thrilled to realize that's where the cane is supposed to go.)

I love the pixel isometric style so much, the game successfully gives off such a pleasing and comforting look.

Likewise Unpacking is pretty short, finishing in only a few hours. That might be sad for some but it feels like the right amount for this game. After the third or fourth stage, It was starting to feel very samey for me, where i was fiddling with the same junk with only more clutter to fiddle with. The system where everything has be "logical" to be there is somewhat flawed for this kind of game. Having complete freedom to place whatever furniture you want would sound so perfect for this game, something akin to Animal Crossing. Although silly, it would give off a much more personal feel of you "making" the environment than just fitting tiles onto a puzzle. Its a minor nitpick because i was feeling this only half-way through, and i become less invested to actually make it look like how i really wanted it to look than what the game wanted me to make it look. It is understandable though, as placing nonsensical things in different locations would just make it less fulfilling that you can place everything around and still win.

The price tag is pushing it for considering the length of the game and some irritated feelings that same may experience when not allowed to completely shape how they want their rooms to look, wait for a discount.

This game is amazing! I found this game on social media and I am so glad I tried it out for myself. I really enjoyed the artwork. I really loved and enjoyed how I was able to learn from the main character without having to see who they are or hear what they're like. I learned what she was like through her belongings, like how she went to art school because of all the notebooks, markers, and art supplies she had, as well as her degree that I was able to hang up. I also liked how she moved often because I was able to see what kind of people she lived with through their belongings too. For instance, she moved in with a man that enjoyed music because he had some guitars on the wall and some large stereos. However, there was no room for the main character's diploma to be put up on the wall, so it had to be put under the bed. It made me feel like she had to shut that part of herself out by doing that, whereas everywhere else she moved, she always had room to put up her diploma and to express herself through her belongings. It's little things like that. This game told a story without needing much and I really enjoyed that. This game was different than what I normally play, but it was well worth the time it took to play. I even played it again once I finished, not just to experience the story again, but also to get the achievements, which were super easy to obtain. I really loved this game and I definitely recommend it to anyone who wants something a bit different yet relaxing and satisfying.

这几句歌词来自游戏 unpacking 的片尾曲 Unpacking a Life ，当两个人决定要住到一起的时候，她们不同风格的冰箱贴也是会凑到一起的。

unpacking 这个游戏基本就是在几个不同的年份，打开纸箱取出物品，放置在合适的位置。游戏是像素风格，所有物品都会贴格子，强迫症友好。

绘画很精细，细节很多。比如大量有区分度的音效，书籍和卡带声音不同，然后同样的东西放在地上和桌上又或者柜子上声音也完全不一样。很多道具都可以戳，马桶可以冲水，灯可以交互，柜门可以开关。如果你开着衣柜的抽屉再去关衣柜门，会有一个碰撞的效果以及不同的声音。

游戏没有什么剧情，就是从1997年第一个房间，到之后大学，毕业合租，恋爱，分手，再次开启新的生活，每一次的开箱布置。布置房间可以获得极大的精神满足，不过更重要的是你可以通过物品的变化，来猜测物品的主人是一个什么样的人，遇到谁，过着怎么样的生活，见证她的人生。

This is one of my favorite games in my library at this point, and one of the most charming on all of Steam. I am a pixel artist, and some of the pixel art makes me jealous.

The gameplay is really, really simple. But don't let that scare you, because in this case that's a good thing! You take items out the boxes, put them where they need to go, and then you're done! Each time you finish unpacking, the game then points out items you have incorrectly placed and you need to put them where they belong. Then you move onto the next place where you get more rooms organize, more boxes to open, and more items to stow away. Along the way, the game tells you a story about who you are and where you are in life. It's all incredibly intuitive and easy to understand. Only on occasion have I been stumped by a room or an item.

One thing I would change is that sometimes it's not always immediately clear where there is space. I had no idea that you could place items on any of the window sills until I watched a friend play. It's also difficult to tell just how large an item is, so sometimes certain items don't fit together when they probably should.

Overall, very fun. I completed it in one sitting. 9/10

This game delivers a powerful and meaningful message about how we deal with many stages of life, our ups and downs through the simple act of unpacking stuff; we can see through the objects that leave or remain across each move what really matters to our character, and follow her journey through what means finding happiness.

It's a game that will hit close to home for many people.

The gameplay might be short, but it's something that will live on your mind for a longer time than any 500 hour grindfest. It will improve you as a person if you're willing to listen to its message, which is not something that can be said about most games.

The good moments aren't forever, but so aren't the bad ones. We move on and things get better as long as we are open to new experiences, just like our character here. Give a chance.

[h1] Игра, дающая слишком много надежд и вещей, которые нужно расставить по местам [/h1]

Вся суть игры проста: вам даётся пустая (или не очень) квартира или комната, коробки с вещами и ваше воображение и перфекционизм. Задача: расставить все тарелочки, зубные щётки, игрушки и фигурки, книжки и блокноты. Не без определённого челенджа, естественно

Из [b]плюсов[/b] могу отметить 
- Красивый дизайн. Игра здорово стилизована, вещи понятные и милые
- Саундрек. Фон не навязчивый, спокойный и приятный
- Сюжет. Удивительным было для меня, что он тут есть. Конечно, не такой, как вы видите во множестве игр, но вы растёте с главной героиней и видите, как меняется её быт, жизнь, хобби и как, соответственно, меняются вещи вокруг неё
- Милейшие очивки. Я не хочу спойлерить, за них дают определённые бонусы в игре
- Режим создания фото. Сделан хорошо и на него явно уделили отдельное внимание и приятно, когда можешь красиво и по-разному запечатлеть каждый уголок, который ты сделал

Без [b]минусов[/b] не обошлось, если возвращаться в реальную жизнь из этой милейшей игры
- Некоторые предметы. В конце уровня красным подсвечиваются предметы, которые стоят неправильно. Возможно, вы не угадали с назначением предмета, а возможно игра имеет иное от вашего мнение относительно расположения той или иной вещи. Например мне [spoiler]так и не ясно, почему иногда ноутбук нужно сунуть в шкаф, а иногда нельзя даже поставить на ближайшую полку и почему цветы не во всех местах могут стоять на кухне.[/spoiler] Однако, некоторые такие "ошибки" очень здорово обыгрываются в сюжете
- Цена. Я уверена, что над игрой работали долго и кропотливо, ведь все шкафчики, ящички и фигурки проработаны хорошо и ничего не лагает, но 400 рублей за 6 часов геймплея (а я достаточно дотошный игрок, который переставлял всё по сотне раз, только чтобы остаться довольной результатом) это, как говориться, ту мач. Я брала по скидке, но даже 300 достаточно много, как оказалось (сравниваю я с другими инди-играми кликерами, не знаю, насколько это сравнение корректное) 
- Количество "уровней". Это, опять же, увеличило бы игре геймплей. Игра, на мой взгляд, закончилась не совсем логично, но и не на ноте "нам было лень доделывать остальное". Осталось чувство незавершенности, в общем, возможно, только у меня так

Игра понравиться людям, которые любят тыкать что-то на фоне разговора в дискорде, не любят экшн или просто хотят расслабиться.

I'd already played through this on Xbox and now am spreading the love on PC.  I'm not sure how to describe this game except that Witch Beam just knows how to scratch that itch.  Think of it as a walking simulator, and by that I mean it's a narrative journey intertwined with an activity, and that activity is unpacking belongings in a variety of domiciles, the act of which, just like real life, can be tedious and frustrating.  But the real act of genius here is a video game able to do so much with so little.  How can a character's story be told with no dialogue?  Masterfully, apparently.  The pacing is chill and zen, but the journey packs one hell of an emotional punch because the game's subtle delivery forces the player to react organically to the story without cliched mechanics like a voiceover or "found notes" telling them how they're supposed to feel.  Bottom line: it's a masterpiece of storytelling, done in a way you'll never see in another video game.

這遊戲比我想象中的有趣。
Steam上顯示遊玩時間三小時，實際上中間還去吃了個飯，所以實際一週目通關時間大概在兩個多小時左右。
遊戲整體流程內並沒有過多地敘述主人公的所有故事，充其量就是在每關通過後在通關圖片後附上的短短一句話（後來發現在不同的房間裡確認通關顯示出來的句子也會不一樣），但是玩家完全可以隨著收拾每次箱子裡的物品自己拼湊出大概的故事內容，或者說是主人公的每個人生階段。
遊戲物品的細節做得挺好，比如說跟前男友分手後的關卡裡如果把兩人的合照釘上軟木板會發現釘子直接懟前男友臉上了，部分細節還是看成就攻略才知道原來還可以這麼弄的（比如沖咖啡）。也有些物品第一次從箱子裡拆封出來的時候完全摸不著頭腦那應該放在哪裡，最後還是一個一個地方試過去才頓悟那是個什麼東西（對，說的就是貼冰箱上的那個白板，一開始還以為是繪圖板直接放工作桌上了）

遊戲內的BGM挺不錯，但關卡長度比想象中的要少。如果碰巧看見這款遊戲在打折而你又剛好有點興趣的話，就趕緊入手吧，這是一個買了之後不會後悔的遊戲。
