[h1]AKA[/h1]
Lifetime Moving Simulator 2021

[h1]BASICALLY[/h1]
Unpacking.  [i]Seriously.[/i]

[h1]YOU PLAY AS[/h1]
A licensed, commercial telekinetic moving place to place, quietly making sense of what makes a home.

[h1]WHAT YOU DO[/h1]
What you dare not have time to do in real life: find a place for everything and put everything in its place. 

[h1]RENDERED AS[/h1]
If all the world was a stage on a SNES.

[h1]TUNE IN FOR[/h1]
The sounds of an acoustic guitarist and a Commodore 64 forming a band at your local coffee shop.  Also a cute song about Stanley™ tools for some reason.

[h1]MAY CONTAIN[/h1]
[list]
[*]Moving boxes that, when emptied, collapse into singularities without warping space-time.
[*]Flushable toilets
[*]7.2 quintillion sounds of putting things on other things. Ever wonder what putting a tiny bus on a toilet seat sounds like?  Wonder no more.
[*]Reasonably accurate pixel art recreations of vintage consoles and BIOS screens.
[/list]

[h1]AWARDED[/h1]
Best alternative to organizing that closet you dare not open.

I recommend this game, but I don't think it's worth the price I paid.
What I liked - the fact that you get to know this person throughout her life, from when she was a child to an adult, going through the ups and downs of life. There are many clues as to what is going on even before you see her annotation on each photograph in the album. I loved seeing the things that she carried with her in every place she lived, and you got so many clues to her personality and I wanted to hug her many times! It felt like she was a real person. I liked the challenge of putting the items away, had to rearrange things so many times (especially in the kitchen!) and get creative. A really lovely concept overall.
What I didn't like - I was disappointed by the fact that it was only ONE storyline here. I assumed there would be multiple. Would love to peek into more than one life. Even if it was just a single room at a time! It took me just over 5 hours to work through it. I'm not sure if I would play it again in a hurry.

É um jogo bem rápido e relaxante que a principal mecânica envolve guardar e organizar suas coisas depois de uma mudança. Ele conta uma história muito agradável de uma jovem, e sua respectiva jornada de seu crescimento e amadurecimento à medida que ela vai se mudando para outras casas no decorrer de sua vida.

Esse é um jogo tranquilo. Não tem ação, não tem tempo limite pra fazer as coisas, é pra você fazer do seu ritmo e organizar do seu jeito (alô perfeccionistas) e eu gosto muito disso. 

Particularmente, também gosto da temática de "show, don't tell", ou seja, não precisamos de um narrador, textos ou descrições para descobrir um pouco mais sobre o desenvolver da trama. Isso significa que fazemos essa descoberta através dos itens e fotos disponíveis no jogo.

Podemos interagir com alguns itens, como por exemplo um Rubik's Cube, videogames, lâmpadas e até vasos sanitários. Pena que são apenas interações passivas, os desenvolvedores poderiam ter aproveitado pra fazer alguns minigames ou interações inesperadas de diferentes itens dentro do jogo.

Uma coisa que fiquei com medo seria largar uma fase pela metade, tendo em vista que fazer uma nova casa do zero poderia se tornar uma atividade cansativa. Felizmente, além de existirem fases curtas, posso parar a qualquer momento que o jogo salva meu progresso (inclusive os itens colocados ou cômodos finalizados) e os achievments são bem fáceis de serem conquistados. 

Gostaria de destacar que o preço do lançamento, no entanto, é um pouco salgado em comparação com o conteúdo que o jogo pode nos oferecer. Recomendo aguardar quando o mesmo estiver em alguma promoção da Steam entre uns 20% a 50% de desconto. 

Tirando esse detalhe, no geral curti bastante, e se esse jogo chamou a sua atenção, seja pela temática, arte ou qualquer outro motivo, vale a pena verificar por você mesmo(a)!

I found this game to be a fun and very calming experience. 
 Some of my highlights from this game are:
-Using the level’s environment  & unboxing items to tell a story about the MC
-The oh so satisfying noises and sound effects when placing things in certain places
-The simple yet high quality pixel art
-The graphics
-The OST for every level
-Very low system and hardware requirements (I played this on my 2020 MacBook Pro and works just fine)
-The gameplay is very simple
-Quite nostalgic (I was born in ‘04)
-Friendly for all ages even little kids


Some of the cons I have about the game:

-Even though there are 3 photo albums there is only 1 story to follow with no twists or differences 

-Some players could find it difficult or could take longer to place things where they are supposed to

-The game can get boring at times because there aren’t really that many mechanics, other than open boxes, take items out, place it somewhere in the house or apartment. Repeat again and again until the level is finished

-The story is short, most of the time in this game is spent on placing things where they should be and continuing to the next time period to repeat the whole process over. There are a grand total of 8 stages. Depending on who you are it could be enough but some people such as myself it really isn’t

-The price, I got this game for $8.19. Personally when I get games less than $10 I don’t really expect much, especially this is an indie game but I do find it a little bit too expensive, considering the amount of content there is for this game at the moment. 


Things this game can add to improve it:

-Allow modding to be accessible and community made levels and stories on the steam workshop

-Add more levels to the first story or make new stories with the other albums

-Have a gamemode where players can make their own level and place down furniture and decorations of their own choosing

-Allow people to make their own custom assets 

-Maybe have room competitions it can be themed and stuff (Like Pewdiepie Tuber Simulator)

An absolutely charming little game. A mix of meditation, puzzle, and self-expression through the mundane act of unpacking boxes when moving into the new homes someone lives in through their early-to-mid life. There's a surprising amount of emotion that can be, um, packed into little situations like where do you put your old D&D rule books, or how do you find space for your own things in a cramped apartment? How do you fill your own space after a stifling relationship? And how do you intermingle your things with a true partner?

The music is lovely, the story is light but moving, and every house I was excited to see how my favourite plushies and action figures were holding up. I got a tiny bit stuck with a couple of items, but some guess work and trial-and-error saw me through. (Unpacking kindly highlights objects that aren't in suitable locations once you have emptied every box of a new move.)

At full price, Unpacking is far from the most hour-per-money around but I would definitely recommend picking it up in a sale. Or paying full price if you're rich like that.

Unpacking é um jogo que mostra a vida de uma garota através de mudanças necessárias da vida, como a mudança para o primeiro quarto, depois uma mudança para sua primeira casa sozinha e assim por diante. 
A cada mudança podemos mexer livremente com os utensílios que vêm com as caixas, deixando onde você bem entender desde que siga algumas regrinhas, como não poder colocar garfos dentro da banheira. Ao final da mudança, tiramos uma foto do cômodo que quisermos e deixamos uma frase escrita. Cada frase representa uma parte da história da garota e, quando terminamos todas as mudanças do álbum, encontramos um vídeo que resume a história da garota em uma relaxante música com as fotos tiradas dos quartos.
----
Unpacking é altamente recomendado pela sua soundtrack relaxante, o seu traço relaxante, os efeitos relaxantes e a sua própria aura relaxante. Este é um jogo perfeito para você que sempre volta para casa estressado, incomodado com algo e precisa deixar isso de lado. Ele também serve para termos uma noção de como podemos fazer nossas mudanças no futuro, tendo uma ideia de base através desse jogo.
Particularmente eu não joguei muito este jogo, mas posso garantir que ele me ajudou muito quando eu estava estressado e ansioso com coisas pessoais e precisava relaxar um pouco. as poucas horas que eu tenho deste jogo provavelmente me salvaram de algo que poderia acabar comigo no futuro.

A chill, organizing game for those who enjoy order, organization and and puzzles!
This is basically a glorified unpacking and organizing game. Great for those who enjoy a relaxing game. Plus, it’s way more fun than unpacking in real life!
My own things might not be organized in my real life, (I’ll be honest, I’m a slob) :-P but I do enjoy playing these types of chill puzzle games nevertheless!

As you progresses through the game, you fill out a photo album, with each page a highlight of some big change [moving to a new place] the character has going on in their life for a specific year.
For each “section” of the photo album, 
You go through a select number of rooms in a house & unpack the boxes that have been placed in each room. Meanwhile, there’s a story going on in the background that you the player can interpret on your own as you play & finish each section of the memory book. It’s actually pretty relaxing! 
Every object has its place and it’s up to you to place them in the correct room and place. There’s even an option to put the items wherever you please, if you prefer.

What I liked about this game: not only is the art style reminiscent of Stardew Valley and calming music, but the sorting and placing of each object is such a neat, fantastic experience! The SOUND DESIGN is SO GOOD!! Each item makes a unique sound whenever you place it on different surfaces, and some objects (the rattling of a pill bottle, a salt shaker, etc) will make noise! It heightens the experience & adds to the overall atmosphere of the game.
The developers even added some realistic details: some objects will be mixed in with a completely different box in another room—like the missing partner of a shoe being packed in a box with the dishes placed in the kitchen, or a hairbrush that’s been packed with office supplies…

You’ll fall in love with this relaxing organizing puzzle game that you can play on your computer OR on the go from your Nintendo Switch (if you have one).
You could probably knock this out in a day if you get sucked in & can’t stop playing. I took my time & played one or two chapters/sections a day.

I REALLY REALLY hope there will be more stories added in the future! This is such a unique game and I’m borderline obsessed with it, I might go back and replay & reorganize the rooms for fun! 🤣
 I wish there were more games like this out there!!
I’ll be following this game & the developers closely to see what they do with it next! I hope they add more!

[h1] Context [/h1]
I played the demo a few months before the game released, so I already had a grasp of the gameplay and general vibes before going into the full game. As someone that A.) loves organizing things, B.) likes puzzle games, C.) prefers chill and comfy games, and D.) loves when games experiment with storytelling methods, this game is completely up my alley and I enjoyed the experience.

[h1] Controls and Accessibility [/h1]
The controls are point and click, so they're very easy to pick up. The accessibility options are enlarging icon sizes, changing the visual transition when you swap rooms, changing the highlight color of invalid items, and allowing items to be placed anywhere. Additionally, any text used (mostly in menus) is already large and in a simple sans-serif font. I did my play through with all the default settings.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]
So far, I've just finished my first full play through. I probably did 5.5-6 hours of actual game play and the whole time it ran smoothly without bugs or crashes. There was a point after the 5th chapter where putting things into places started getting a bit tedious but I'm going to chalk that up to me playing it all at once. Plus, this game is all in the details and the small moments of joy (or sorrow) you get from discovering, and that's what kept me engaged throughout my 6 hour run. Since I didn't recognize a few of the items, it meant I just had to keep guessing until I got it right, and this game luckily does not penalize you for that.

I really do love how, in the absence of people and interactions between characters, this game uses almost everything else at its disposable to give us a rich sense of the main character's life. There is a strong sense of place and story, and the important points of the story land well in terms of clarity and emotion. The music and sound design were great to listen to and further supported the story. I don't think I recognized all the references made with certain objects (like books and DVDs) but it didn't take away from my experience.

Also spoiler: [spoiler] I just wanna say that my gay senses were tingling before she even broke up with her boyfriend and the satisfaction I felt after the ending cut-scene was immense. [/spoiler]

Raro juego del 2 de Noviembre del 2021. ¿Como puedo definirlo? Mmmm… No se: es un juego de mecánica muy repetitiva, simple y de temática plana (debemos desempacar, y ordenar).
A pesar de su simplicidad, se siente tan real y tan palpable que te deja inmerso en la historia (aunque no se narre una); solo con el mero hecho de ver los cambios de espacios, los objetos que uno desempaca y sentir las emociones que transmite la banda sonora, nos percatamos de lo que está pasando, y de la línea narrativa que está sucediendo a lo largo del tiempo… De esta forma no solo conocemos una historia, si no que conocemos al personaje (aunque ni su sexo este claro), su evolución, su madurez y hasta pensamientos, llegando a sentirnos dentro del juego, como si nosotros fuéramos los que cambiamos de casa y tenemos que desempacar.
El tema Soledad, fluye en el aire, cuando vemos como se va deshaciendo uno de cosas que le recuerdan a otra persona, cambia de cama de dos plazas a una, se achica el armario, y hasta el mero hecho de tener solo las pertenencias propias y no tener que hacer encajar las tuyas en la dinámica de alguien más.

이삿짐 정리가 컨텐츠의 핵심인데, 단순한 조작을 반복하는 지루함을  Unpacking만의 감성적인 맥락으로 연결시킨 게 정말 기발하네요. 물건을 하나하나 정리하며, 물건 안에 스며있는 추억을 유추해보는 독특한 매력이 있어요. 자세한 것은 플레이해보세요. 게임 안에서 업적(스티커)을 달성하는 것도 재미있습니다.

사운드도 정말 훌륭합니다. 물건과 물건을 놓는 바닥면의 재질에 따라 각자 미묘하게 다른 소리가 납니다. 또, 물건을 흔들 때 나는 소리도 아주 섬세하게 구현되어 있어요. 이런 사소한 부분들이 몰입을 돕고 반복적인 플레이가 재미있게 여겨지도록 만들어요. 

스테이지를 완료하면 현재 있는 방에 한정해 이삿짐 정리 타임랩스를 영상과 gif로 저장할 수 있습니다ㅋㅋㅋ 인코딩에 시간이 오래 걸리지만, SNS로 공유하는 용도로 적당한 품질에 가벼운 용량으로 앵간한 gif 생성 프로그램보다 훨씬 좋더라고요ㅋㅋㅋ 저장된 타임랩스를 보면 착착 정리되는 과정에 쾌감도 느껴집니다.

아쉬운 점은 딱 하나네요. 더 하고 싶은데 끝나버렸어... 
Unpacking의 감성에 흠뻑 젖어있을 때 엔딩을 보게 되어있는 것 같아요. 
아끼고 아껴가며 플레이 했는데도 7시간이면 엔딩을 보고 마네요... 
퍼즐 컨텐츠 볼륨이 작다는 이야기는 아니에요. 후반부는 방이 한 두개가 아니라서 한 스테이지를 깨는데 시간이 꽤 걸립니다. 그런데 스토리텔링은 스테이지 단위로 풀어가다보니, 더 자잘하게 구성되어있으면 감성적으로 훨씬 만족스러웠을 것 같습니다. 이런 면이 살짝 아쉽네요.

[/h]Recommended with caveats[/h]

[b]did you like "Gone Home?"[/b] Do you like hidden object games? If so, and you're looking for a casual experience [b]on your mobile device[/b] you've found your game. The problem being, the game isn't on mobile... yet! It screams mobile though, and Witchbeam ported their last game to every electrical device on which it can operate. They're likely to do that with "Unpacking" too. Wait for that, because it will be inevitably cheaper, a better fit for this type of game, and they're likely to add more content between ports. On PC right now, it's not a good buy.

What you have here is the reverse of a hidden object game in isometric perspective. It's entirely mouse driven. You draw ordinary household objects from a deck as you unpack boxes, and you have to find an appropriate place to put them away in each room. You play as a young woman... or the guy she keeps calling to help her move, depending on how you want to interpret it. She moves every three years starting in 1997 (though it feels more like 1987) until 2018. The objects you unpack, and the spaces you unpack it into tell you the story of this woman's life.

The story is sweet, and a little sad in places. It does have some odd elements. I don't want to spoil, but objects come up in some of the later stages that seem meant for an older woman. 1997 to 2018 is only 21 years, and the character is maybe twelve at the oldest when the game begins. It feels like the game wants to tell the story of an entire life, but the time-frame is at odds with this. I suspect the game was meant to be longer, including more stages. I think it was supposed to start in 1987, maybe 1977 would have been better. This is why I recommend waiting for ports. There's a lot of re-use of the same assets, which is to be expected to a degree, but it's on an excessive level. This lady is unpacking pairs of underwear she was wearing when she was twelve years old twenty years later, that kind of thing. With their last game "Assault Android Cactus" Witchbeam added content with every port, and kept refining the game as time went on. I think you'll be happier with the mobile port, if and when they get around to it.

[b]speaking of Cactus[/b] if you're interested in this game because of that one, save your money. It's not just that it's a different genre, it's a different ethos. There's little room for player expression here, you're very much being led. The puzzles aren't challenging, and there's very little replay potential. There are a few optional puzzles to solve and achievements to get in a second play-through, but it won't feel worth doing. Cactus keeps you playing forever, You'll feel done with Unpacking when you complete the last stage. You'll have been playing for a few hours. To test for replayability, I went through a second time, and put everything away as differently as the game would let me, to see if it changes anything. It does not. When asked on his Ask.fm page about the possibility of a sequel to Cactus, he mentioned that his team was working on "Unpacking" without even trying to promote it. He knew he was speaking to the wrong audience.

Nach zwei Runs kann ich das Spiel grundsätzlich empfehlen (MIT ABSTRICHEN - KAUFWARNUNG UNTEN) - Ein tolles Zen Game mit grandioser Pixelgrafik, narrativem Storytelling, das mal unglaublich glänzen kann (da in Punkten aber sogar mehr hätte bieten können) einem wirklich angenehmen Soundtrack - und einem schon recht happigen Preis, wenn ich es in Relation zu anderen Spielen in dem Segment betrachte.

Das Spielprinzip:
Im Grunde, das was die Trailer zeigen, nicht mehr, nicht weniger. Man packt Kisten aus und verstaut Dinge. Alles ohne Zeitdruck, es ist gut durchdesigned und kommt nur selten zu Trial and Error Momenten. 

Die Story:
Wir begleiten eine junge Frau auf ihrer Reise durchs Leben zumindest einem Abschnitt von Kind sein zur Familiengründung. Auf Details will ich nicht weiter eingehen. Im Grunde, fast wie in echt, spiegelt immer eine neue Wohnung oder ein neues Zimmer einen neuen Abschnitt in ihrem Leben dar. Wir sehen sie nicht, wir wissen nicht, was zwischen dem letzten Abschnitt und diesem passiert - aber durch das Auspacken der Dinge und die Räumlichkeiten können wir recht tief eintauchen und sie kennenlernen. Das funktioniert soweit auch sehr gut. Es gibt einen Punkt, wo es sogar uns aktiv fordert. Leider kommen diese aktiven Punkte viel zu selten, wir können vieles aus der Umgebung mitnehmen, aber da wäre mehr drin.

Zur Grafik:
Wunderschöne Pixelart. Anders kann ich es nicht sagen. Unpacking hat ein enormes Level of Detail - obwohl natürlich alles verpixelt ist. Das geht soweit, dass man sogar die Cover einzelner DVDs meint, wiederzuerkennen und selbst die Fotos am Kühlschrank erzählen eine Geschichte.
Ich bin normal gar kein Pixelart Fan, aber das ist wirklich unglaublich gut geworden.

Zum Soundtrack:
Angenehm, gelassen, stört nie - und das Outro ist wirklich süß und rundet das Spielerlebnis ab. Wäre zwar nichts, was ich mir jetzt extra kaufen würde, aber im Spiel funktioniert er hervorragend.

Kritikpunkte:
Umfang/Preis. Die narrative Erzählung bricht ziemlich unerwartet einfach ab, wo man sich eigentlich noch mehr Levels ausgemalt hätte. Das wirkt etwas seltsam, ich weiß nicht, ob die Entwickler da was weggestrichen haben, es fühlt sich stark danach an. Nach knapp 4 Stunden ist ein Run durch, das sollte allen bewusst sein.

Erneutes Spielen funktioniert was den Zen Faktor angeht allerdings immer noch gut. Doch das narrative Erlebnis lässt stark nach, auch wenn man immer noch wieder mal Kleinigkeiten entdeckt (wo man auch die Detailverliebtheit nicht zu viel loben kann), aber jedem sollte Bewusst sein:
Nach den 4 Stunden bleibt eben "nur" ein sehr gutes Clicker Spiel - das man sicher alle paar Monate mal rauskramen kann.

Und hier dann auch eine Warnung. Wenn ihr bereit seid, 20€ für einen atmosphärischen Zen-Clicker auszugeben oder auch für 4 Stunden narrative Erfahrung, dann solltet ihr es tun. Die Entwickler haben durchaus Unterstützung verdient. Aber der Preis ist eben auch happig, 20€ ist für viele Menschen viel Geld - ich würde den Titel real eher im 10€ Segment sehen. Wenn ihr euch entsprechend nicht in dieser Zielgruppe seht, dann wartet auf nen Sale und gebt dem Game dann ne Chance - unter 10€ kann man nichts falsch machen, wenn euch das Grundkonzept nicht schon abgeht ;)

  这个游戏做到了，这个游戏真的做到了，我布置到最后一关的时候直接忍无可忍破防大骂：他X的这个是什么东西我凭什么不可以放在这里？开发者为什么要教我玩游戏？？？

  我在现实里算是一个真的很喜欢整理的人，我为了整理多余的东西会再去买一块洞洞板挂墙上甚至买一个柜子，所有东西不在自己该在的位置会被我整理回该在的位置。所以我当时这个游戏刚出的时候就很期待，但是一直忘记买，前段时间看到打对折满心欢喜的入了，大概对折35元吧，本来要80元...刚玩的时候翻评论有人说时长有点太短了不值这个价格我还有点担心，现在我通关了倒反而松了一口气：我谢谢开发者三个小时就肯放我走，这段近四小时的痛苦的旅程真是对我人生的一次磨砺，随着时间的推移一次又一次地冲击我的大脑摧毁我的精神，他是伪装成红烧肉的姜，是一盘三文鱼刺身里的一根鱼骨，是一坨无敌的镶金的史！我这辈子不愿再有一段和玩伟大的unpacking一样的游戏经历，我这种三流俗人欣赏不来这等绝世大作

  一个宣传点是收纳整理的游戏却会限制你东西该放在哪，包括但不限于放不下，不准放，你不知道这个画的很好看的像素图是什么，该放哪，只能一直试一直试还会一直有一个红框来提醒我你这个傻子这玩意不能放这里你必须放在这个地方！！可能是我和制作组的文化有差异所以我看不懂这是什么该放哪，但是你到底，你凭什么，你哪来的权利，教我这个东西我只能放这————我请问这不是我的相册吗？你们制作组自己开头写的，这本相册是属于我的，这是属于谁的故事，你凭什么要干涉我凭什么指指点点我要把这些东西收纳在哪里？这到底是谁的故事？你到底想做什么游戏你想表达什么？你凭什么这么高傲？？我付了钱来玩的欸？？

二编：我写完去看了一下游戏简介，确实不是玩家的故事，那麻烦别让玩家在开头相册取名造成误解，而且凭什么要因为你这点所谓比较巧妙新颖的叙事手法限制物品摆放，[spoiler] 男友家那关你说奖牌没地方放只能放床底，还有分手后照片不能挂墙上诸如此类的我当时还觉得设计的很有意思，最后一张图我把婴儿车放在角落一点的地方也要管，绘本没放在柜子上也要管…还有一个大概是浴缸的防滑垫，我家不用浴缸根本不知道放哪，摆来摆去摆了五分钟…… [/spoiler]设计者觉得很精妙的叙事手法根本不是教玩家玩游戏的原因。玩家根本没必要非要顺着设计者的思路玩的

  So有看到这条差评的，真的很想玩的话打折再买，没打到50%以下不要买，喜欢的会觉得四小时时长太短不够玩，讨厌的话会觉得制作组教你做事毕竟你本来是抱着收纳整理布置来的。哦对了，还有对欧美那边 引号 潮流新文化 引号 不能接受的也千万不要买，我一直是属于这些内容不骑玩家脸就忍忍算了的人。我翻评论看到一个老哥退款了说虽然分类卫生棉和胸罩挺好的但是他是个男的实在是没有沉浸感，我看完觉得真的是又搞笑又可怜的，我是女的还好点，男的玩这游戏不配有沉浸感了吗，就非要当那个主角吗万一玩家不想呢他们就活该被你的宣传片骗进来杀吗…不过反正不是我的故事了，还是祝游戏主角生活幸福吧……

I am not someone who minds "the grind" in games, but this was just manual labor. I enjoyed the first two levels or so, but it quickly became repetitive to the point of being mind numbing. I didn't see the fun in "decorating" when the number of items grew exponentially while still also remaining the same (this woman had the same pieces of clothing her entire life) all while staying within the small space limitations. Seeing how cluttered some spaces like the bathroom had to be to get to the next level actually gave me anxiety rather than take it away. 

In what is an unfortunate conundrum the game is both blessedly and unfortunately short. For someone who wasn't enjoying it the content being done in a matter of a blink was a relief, but considering the normal price of this game? OOF. That is definitely not enough content - let alone even slightly varied content - to justify that high of a price tag. 

Unfortunately, not for me. And unfortunately for others, not long enough for them.

Unpacking es un juego que algunos podrían considerar "corto", tal vez incluso simple. Sin embargo, eso no fue lo que más me atrajo de este juego. Me gusta la temática de los rompecabezas, aunque eso tampoco fue lo que más me cautivó. Lo que realmente me enamoró fue su historia. Observar el crecimiento del personaje principal a lo largo de los cambios de casa, ver las diferentes etapas de su vida, sus logros y cómo eventualmente forma una familia, así como la separación que marca su progreso como ilustradora. ¡Uf! ¡Qué juegazo!.

Me divierte mucho organizar las habitaciones, la verdad. Aunque quizás podría haber más historias alternativas, otra "vida", más "opciones". Pero supongo que ese no era el objetivo de este pequeño juego. UwU

Я думала это классная игра, где раскладываешь вещи и всё орошо, удовлетворяешь своего внутреннего перфекциониста, дизайнера и тд. Но после того как ты, казалось бы разложишь вещи, так как тебе нравится, или ты думаешь что это должно быть тут, игра не хочет заканчивать уровень, пока ты не положишь вещи так как думает надо она. И это дико раздражает, может я очень глупая, но на некоторых вещах я гуглила прохождение игры, чтобы понять куда надо поставить тот или иной предмет чтобы завершить уровень.

An sich ein nettes Spiel. Eine Story in dem Sinn ist nicht vorhanden. Man erfährt etwas über das Leben der Person, indem man ihre Wohnung nach einem Umzug einräumt. An sich war es für die wenigen Stunden ganz schön. Aber das wars dann auch. Für einen aktuellen Normalpreis von 19,99€ absolut überteuert. Hätte ich es nicht mit 50% Rabatt gekauft, hätte ich mich echt geärgert und selbst der Preis ist für das sehr kurze Spiel zu teuer. In weniger als 5 Stunden habe ich das Spiel durch und alle Erfolge gemacht. Gäbe es mehr Räume, mehr Aufgaben.. Für den Preis fehlt einfach Inhalt. Zudem ist es schade, dass man beim Einräumen keine komplette Freiheit hat. Das Spiel gibt oft vor, in welchem Raum Sachen zu sein haben und wo in diesem Raum die Gegenstände nicht stehen dürfen.

Pro:
- Liebevolle Gestaltung, ansprechende Grafik
- Entspannendes Spiel

Cons:
- Viel zu kurz (definitiv weniger als 5h)
- Viel zu teuer (aktueller Vollpreis 19,99€)
- Story quasi nicht existent
- Keine komplette Freiheit beim Spielen

休闲游戏某种程度上确实不需要玩法引导，但游戏内的整理条目却又对应着不同的功能区域（例如浴巾需要挂在卫生间内），而如何定义某个项目却又依赖个人的主观判断，就导致当你对某个项目无法判断其归属时，穷举试错就变成了似乎唯一的解法。
另外游戏内的收纳与展示空间的比例或者说自由度也令人感到困惑，主角卧室中过多的小配饰必然导致风格上的迥异，而收纳空间的不足就必然会导致将其全部摆在台面上，于我而言这种风格上的混乱十分影响观感，但是在厨房等位置，展示空间的不足则导致了所有东西会被一股脑的塞进柜子里，反而影响了场景的设计思路。
说是自定义空间，但是可供玩家选择的地方自由度又没有设计的很足，真的让人玩起来莫名火大

I reaaaally wanted to like this game. Unpacking stuff in a low-stress environment is exactly the kind of thing my brain likes to do to relax, so this seemed like the perfect game to unwind. Also, I'd heard that the game had a nice story to follow as well, so that sounded like a lovely cup of tea. But. This game is so stressful, and I don't even know where to start unpacking (ha) my problems with it. 

One: the rooms you're unpacking stuff into *aren't empty*. You have to try to jam the heroine's stuff in around other people's things. So it's not a beautiful clean slate that you paint with belongings, but more like a messy jumble of someone else's things that you have to work around and hope they don't mind. Some items are even locked in place and can't be moved! I was actually surprised by how much stress this triggered, and I wanted to call a house meeting to discuss the toilet paper situation.

Two: many of the items are tiny, blurred, or otherwise unclear what they are or where they go. I would have preferred the interface have a label and location for what something is when you pick it up. Turns out the game has Strong Opinions on where you can store certain things. Can I put the tiny guitar in my bedroom under the bed? NO. It must go in the living room. Often it's hard to tell where something goes because you can't tell what it is. I had to google how to get past the first level because a cute little purple notebook was actually a *diary* and I had to put that in a secret drawer rather than on the shelf with the other notebooks. I'd foolishly gone and filled the drawer with erasers and rulers and scissors, but those are supposed to go on TOP of the desk, which is how I know that the devs don't have cats. 

I quit when I moved back into my childhood room and I was supposed to know that one of the photos wasn't supposed to go on the corkboard with all the other photos but was instead supposed to go in a cabinet where the heroine won't see it (unless she...opens the cabinet??). I was supposed to realize that the tiny photo was of a romantic ex because there was a tiny thumbtack through his tiny face, and I was supposed to guess that instead of "throwing it in the trash" or "storing it in a file folder" that the right answer was to lay it face-up on a cabinet shelf where it will be seen every time the she opens the cabinet. Intuitive! 

Three: The story. There isn't one, not really. We're supposed to construct a story ourselves based on wild assumptions regarding the things our heroine owns--it's like walking into a stranger's house and trying to construct a Sherlockian narrative over why they own what they do and then calling that a "story". 

Whilst consulting google to figure out what to do with the previously-mentioned photo, I was startled to realize that I was supposed to assume that our room occupant is a world traveler because she collects tiny Eiffel Tower and Leaning Tower of Pisa figurines. WHAT?? I had just assumed that she liked those places! Maybe she collects the figurines because she *can't* afford to travel (if you can't see the real thing, you can at least see the replica) or maybe her dad travels for work and brings back souvenirs for her. I used to have an impressive collection of shot glasses from around the world for that very reason; it doesn't mean I've ever left the country!

We're apparently supposed to chart the "changed interests" of the main character based on which belongings she keeps and which she trims out of her life over time, but having just lost a lot of personal items of my own to a basement flood, I am too aware of how many factors other than "loss of interest" can cause a beloved stuffie or photo to leave one's life. It's strange and frustrating to feel like I'm supposed to access the story through a series of unintuitive logic leaps. Maybe the heroine kept the pink pig stuffie and trimmed the other animals because she loved that one best, or maybe the others were destroyed in a flood, or the thumbtack ex threw out her things, or maybe one of her roommates accidentally stole the stuffies during a move out when they packed them by mistake. Sherlockian analysis is a myth, as Sir Terry Pratchett demonstrated far better than I ever could:

"Samuel Vimes dreamed about Clues. He had a jaundiced view of Clues. He instinctively distrusted them. They got in the way. And he distrusted the kind of person who'd take one look at another man and say in a lordly voice to his companion, "Ah, my dear sir, I can tell you nothing except that he is a left-handed stonemason who has spent some years in the merchant navy and has recently fallen on hard times," and then unroll a lot of supercilious commentary about calluses and stance and the state of a man's boots, when exactly the same comments could apply to a man who was wearing his old clothes because he'd been doing a spot of home bricklaying for a new barbecue pit, and had been tattooed once when he was drunk and seventeen and in fact got seasick on a wet pavement. What arrogance! What an insult to the rich and chaotic variety of the human experience!" --Terry Pratchett, Feet of Clay

The gaming experience is unique, as it uses different time periods to help the female protagonist tidy up her room, subtly depicting her life experiences. Some details are meticulously crafted. For example, the sound effects change depending on the surface where items are placed, the door won't open if items are blocking it, and the contents of cardboard boxes might belong to different rooms, closely mirroring real-life scenarios.

The narrative is enriched with elements like the teddy bear, a toy chicken that gains one more chick each year, the protagonist’s awards, pain relief patches for back pain, various low-resolution photos, and more. Of course, the specific storyline is left to the player’s imagination.

It's a good game, so why not recommend it? Spoiler: [spoiler] This seemingly harmless and zen game ends up incorporating LGBT elements just to keep up with trends. I'm not against having homosexual elements in game narratives, but forcing it into the ending is perplexing. Whose child is it in the end? Is it her ex-boyfriend’s or did the protagonist discover she's bisexual, get a surrogate, and live with another woman? It feels nonsensical. Are Western developers incapable of making games without adding LGBT elements? To top it off, I didn’t notice a single piece of male clothing upon reflection.[/spoiler]

I find this kind of dramatic twist hard to understand.

I bought for the hype and realy disliked the game. I mean, is fun to put stuff in the scenario the first time you do it, but the game makes you do it again and again in other houses. ANOTHER room, ANOTHER BATHROOm, ANOTHER KITCHEN and even some of the objects are still the same. There is even once that scenario is the same, it just comes more objects fo put in. I played the thing wanting it to endup almost enterily. It doesn't help that the game actualy makes some rules about objects needing to be place in certain places. You may think "yeah you cant just put a knife in the floor or something" but is more than that, is a personality thing. Your character loves certain things, so certain things can't be not in the table. Is part of the subliminal history.

Also, I REALY disliked the message of the history of this game. If I knew it was a LGBT game I would probably not bought it. but turns out it have a very not great message for kids. The history (spoiler alert) goes something like this: Your male boyfriend treats you like trash? Well go lesbian and somehow you will have child, everthing will match, the partner will only complement you. The game literaly makes living with the man horrible and living with another girl fell like you are soulmates. And this is basic the only story it tells. Again: there is a public that want this kinda stuff, ok, but I was not expecting it and saw no reason to search on LGBT propaganda in a game about literaly unpacking.

What makes me particular worried is to find out that part of the popularity of the game is not from the game aspect of it, but the political agenda of it. We can see that in other movies or games sometimes, like being prease in part by ideology issues. Like "the game is repetitive, kinda boring, have no actual history BUT THE SUBLIMINAL MESSAGE IS LGBT IS AWESOME" and I can see a lot of people giving high score to it because of it. Like, objectivity being destroyed.
"but aren't your review being afected by your political point of view" - Yes, because it wasn't a game I expected to hear about ideology in the first place. Who expect to be doctrinated when playng a game about umpacking? I was expecting something amazing made with simple mechanic

Is also important to understand my review as a review of a game that is very popular. I came for the hype, so my expectations where very high. So if you are coming for the hype, if you are expecting a very amazing subliminal story (even a lgbt one, if is your thing), if you are expecting something amazing made out the experience of tryng to make cloths fill in your closet, don't. You will put things in their place and THAT IS IT. 3 hours worth of puting things in the place the devs allow you to

Pros:
* Pretty solid idea for a game that is fairly well executed
* Pretty art
* Definitely fulfills the "satisfying" kind of feeling if that's what you're looking for

Cons:
* Not a lot of content, and not a lot of diversity of different rooms / different stuff to unpack.

Unpacking is a delightful and unexpected journey through the life of an unnamed protagonist, told solely through the act of unpacking boxes. What initially seems like a mundane task evolves into a poignant exploration of memories, growth, and change.    

Unpacking. I wasn't really expecting much, you know? I mean, unpacking boxes? How fun can that be? But it was actually pretty chill. Like, it's one of those games where you don't really do much, but you still get sucked in.

You’re just unpacking this person's life, one box at a time. It's kinda weird how you start to feel like you know them through their stuff. Like, finding a bunch of old books makes you think they were probably a nerd or something. And then there’s the satisfaction of fitting everything perfectly in the space. It’s like a puzzle, but with stuff.

The graphics are nice and simple, and the music is really relaxing. It’s one of those games you can play when you just wanna chill out. But don’t get me wrong, it’s not all sunshine and rainbows. Some of the puzzles can be a bit tricky, and the ending made me feel kinda empty, like a cardboard box after you’ve taken everything out.

Overall, it’s a strange little game, but I’d say it’s worth a shot if you’re looking for something different. Just don’t expect any explosions or aliens.

Si les pidiera que intentaran narrar una historia como la de Unpacking, estoy seguro de que más de uno terminaría arrancándose los pelos. Pero si, además, les prohibiera usar hasta la más mínima palabra para hacerlo, probablemente el pelo se les caería con solo intentarlo. Bueno, Unpacking lo logra a la perfección.
El juego utiliza un recurso más que conocido, el famosísimo "environmental storytelling" o narrativa ambiental, para los amigos. Títulos como los de FromSoftware son grandes exponentes de esta forma de narrar y, fuera de los videojuegos, otros medios como el cine, la pintura y la arquitectura nos ofrecen numerosos ejemplos de ella. Sin embargo, hasta el momento, nunca había encontrado una obra en la que la narrativa ambiental dejara de ser un recurso entre muchos otros para convertirse en el verdadero núcleo que impulsa toda la historia. Si bien hace bastante tiempo tengo incorporado este concepto, siempre lo entendí como un complemento narrativo, una herramienta más de las cientos que se necesitan para construir una casa. Verlo convertido en el mecanismo principal de una obra fue... 🤯. Y resulta fascinante que un juego construido sobre puzles tan simples consiga semejante hito.
Llega un momento en el que empezamos a atar cabos. En la cuarta habitación que ordenamos, el juego llega a su clímax. Ese es, para mí, el instante del eureka, donde aparece ese famoso "¡Ah, claro!".
De momento, lo único que hicimos fue acomodar objetos. Y, de repente, entrecerramos los ojos y decimos: "Un momento...". Algunos objetos pueden moverse. Podemos reorganizar cajones, cambiar el lugar de los libros o hacer espacio para nuestras pertenencias. Sin embargo, los cuadros de la pared son inamovibles. En efecto, nuestro mayor logro hasta ese momento, el título universitario por el que seguramente tanto trabajamos, no tiene lugar donde ser exhibido. En mi caso, terminó relegado al suelo, debajo de la cama.
¿Cómo puede ser posible? ¿Y nuestro cuarto?
Qué triste no contar ni siquiera con un lugar en el que apoyar nuestras herramientas de dibujo y tener que hacerlo sobre una mesita de luz. Tendremos que exigir, por lo tanto, como nos enseñó Virginia Woolf, una habitación propia. Se pueden quedar con sus 500 libras anuales, pero, a cambio, queremos lo importante: un lugar en el que crear, un lugar en el que podamos ser nosotros, sin que nos veamos influidos por ajenos que no nos dejan ni siquiera tener un escritorio. Una habitación propia en la que poder colgar nuestro título en la pared.

i rarely write reviews, but after playing this through, I had to say something. Unpacking is as casual as they come, you can go at your own pace, unpacking boxes, placing them in different rooms, and once you've done that, the game will tell you if where you put it is an appropriate spot. Then you have to scramble to find the right place for everything to go. You can go as fast or as slow as you want to, taking a break whenever you need to, which as a mom to a teenaged son and 3 furry kids, being able to stop on a dime is necessary at this stage in my life. I've been playing for 5 hours, and I've already played through the game, the life of the main character. You get to see them go to college, move from place to place, go through a breakup, find love, move in together, and start their family. It's a really fun game, but it does finish quickly. You can play it again to try to unlock the other achievements, which is what I'm doing now. I don't know if it would have been worth it at full price, but I definitely think it was worth it at the discount I got it for.

[h1] Überraschendes kleines Indiegame! [/h1] 

Zunächst einmal muss ich sagen, dass ich nicht gedacht hätte eine Review zu einem kleinen Indiegame zu schreiben, welches ursprünglich nur meiner Ablenkung vom Alltag als Gelegenheitsspiel diente. Völlig blind hab ich daher Unpacking gespielt und während des Games gemerkt "Warte mal, man spielt doch immer die selbe Person, oder?". Das kleine Game Unpacking entpuppte sich plötzlich für mich als kleines Storygame und da ich sowieso Storygames liebe, war ich echt überrascht von dem Inhalt. Mir war vorher nie bewusst, dass man nur anhand einer Wohnung und den damit verbundenen Umzügen sooo viel über eine einzelne Person bzw. den Charakter erzählen kann. Und das ganz ohne Dialoge, Aussehen des Charakters etc., sondern nur anhand von Gegenständen sowie dem Fotoalbum, was einen durch die Level begleitet. Ich war auf jeden Fall von der Story sehr angetan, aber seht gerne selbst. :)

Zum Spiel selbst: Man ordnet und platziert Gegenstände in der neuen Wohnung nach einem jeden Umzug. Grundsätzlich ist man sehr frei bei der Platzierung, sofern Gegenstände von der Größe etc. dort hin passen. Dennoch müssen diese in einer bestimmten Logik im Raum angeordnet werden, hier kommt also ein kleiner Rätselaspekt hinzu. So kann man logischerweise keine Tassen oder Teller ins Bad platzieren oder einfach auf den Boden. Sobald man fertig ist, zeigt das Spiel einem, welche Gegenstände fehl am Platz sind. Auch hier wird die Story einem geschickt "verpackt", denn manche Gegenstände dürfen auch nicht dort sein, wo es der Charakter nicht möchte, werd hierbei aber nichts spoilern. ;)

Mit insgesamt knapp 6 Stunden Spielzeit ein kleines aber feines Game mit Tiefe, dass ich jedem empfehlen kann. :)

Unpacking: Милый симулятор распаковки коробок

Привет, друзья! Сегодня я хочу рассказать вам об игре Unpacking, которая стала моим новым увлечением. Это милый и расслабляющий симулятор, где вам предстоит разбирать коробки с вещами и обустраивать свой дом.
В игре нет сложных задач или напряжённых моментов. Здесь вы просто наслаждаетесь процессом распаковки и любуетесь тем, как ваш дом наполняется уютом и теплом. Вы начинаете с простых вещей, таких как одежда и посуда, и постепенно переходите к более крупным предметам, таким как мебель и техника.
Но самое интересное в Unpacking — это то, что каждая коробка хранит в себе кусочек истории. Вы узнаете больше о жизни главной героини, её увлечениях и интересах. Это делает игру ещё более увлекательной и интересной.

В целом, Unpacking — это отличный способ расслабиться и провести время с пользой. Я рекомендую эту игру всем, кто любит уютные симуляторы и хочет окунуться в атмосферу домашнего уюта.

Un petit jeu détente excellent pour se reposer après une journée bien remplie. Entre le calme des musiques, la liberté dans les placements et le temps illimité pour le faire, rien dans ce jeu ne saurais vous stresser.
   Pour ceux tout de même un peu plus compétiteurs [i](comme moi)[/i], vous pouvez toujours essayer d'obtenir tous les autocollants possibles qu'offre le jeu, en plus des succès Steam bien évidemment qui vont de paire.

   Si je devais résumer, j'ai beaucoup apprécier l'expérience et passer des heures sur ce jeu ne m'a absolument pas dérangé et je pourrais encore y passer plus de temps. Le seul bémol, c'est la vitesse avec laquelle il se termine. Il est en réalité extrêmement court et même si il y a déjà beaucoup de contenue et une histoire captivante malgré l'absence de textes [i](c'était vraiment une expérience très intéressante !)[/i], cela n'en reste pas moins un jeu... qui laisse sur sa faim. Je ne sais pas s'ils comptent faire un deuxième volet [i](ce que j'aimerais beaucoup à coup sûr, avec la vie d'une autre personne ?)[/i] mais je fus un peu déçue quand on s'arrêta après la chambre du bébé dans la grande maison. On aurait pu voir la suite avec l'enfant qui grandit, peut-être un second qui arrive ou bien encore le départ de la maison car il va à la fac [i](?)[/i], la retraite, la vieillesse jusqu'à la mort de la personne partageant sa vie ? Ce ne sont que des suggestions, et l'absence de tout cela n'enlève [b]EN AUCUN CAS[/b] la beauté de ce jeu et le plaisir qu'il m'a procuré.
   J'aime donc énormément Unpacking, et je pense y rejouer même après l'avoir terminé. Cela reste agréable de ranger et reranger, encore et encore. On n'a pas terminer même une fois l'histoire achevée.

   Je le conseille donc vivement pour plusieurs raisons: l'ambiance détente et zen, la satisfaction dans les possibilités offertes au joueur, les musiques [i](j'en profite pour noter mon admiration pour la chanson de fin où j'ai l'impression que c'est le point de vue de la compagne de notre perso qui parle à travers les paroles, très beau)[/i], l'expérience unique du jeu avec cette histoire pleine d'informations sans avoir à utiliser de mots, et enfin, les graphismes tout simplement adorables, rétros et magiques.
   Je n'imagine même pas tout le travail qui a dû être fait pour pouvoir réaliser et sortir ce jeu, mais c'est un immense succès.

[b]9/10[/b]  [i](juste un peu trop court mais sinon parfait !)[/i]

I have been waiting months for this game to be released and can say that it worth the wait. The game is peaceful and well thought out in terms of how they tell a story without words. Самое странное в этой игре — то, что к ней вроде бы и не придерешься. Я ведь прекрасно знал, что покупаю симулятор распаковки коробок. Никаких иллюзий насчет жанра не было. Но когда пошли финальные титры, в голове остался только один вопрос: «И ради этого я потратил три часа жизни?».

Нас обманывает не маркетинг, нас обманывает сама концепция. Игра пытается выехать на дешёвом уюте — этот пиксельный чайничек, этот милый щелчок, когда ставишь книжку на полку. Нас усердно пытаются погрузить в чужую жизнь, заставить сопереживать взрослению пиксельного человечка через его кружки и плакаты. Но за этим нет ничего. Это стерильная, искусственная драма, сделанная по всем канонам безопасного инди-дизайна.

Инструменты здесь работают как строгий надзиратель. Игра притворяется медитативной, но стоит тебе проявить хоть каплю индивидуальности и положить вещь туда, где она кажется логичной тебе, интерфейс начинает истошно мигать красным. Нас заставляют разгадывать чужую, порой весьма сомнительную логику расстановки обуви и сковородок. Зазор между объектами раздражает, хитбоксы кривые.

В итоге вместо расслабления ты получаешь три часа рутинной работы чужим грузчиком. Если это и есть то самое «высокое инди-искусство», о котором все кричат, то индустрия окончательно свернула куда-то не туда. Хотя и тут странно. Зато захотелось спать. Из плюсом. Всем пис. можно идти спать. получается наврал - медитативная. сюжет лол конечно.

I find this game particularly hard to enjoy because it perpetuates a myth of a completely unattainable life and lifestyle without being upfront that the story depicted in this game is fantasy. For each person that discovers a passion/skill and succeeds in it well enough to comfortably support themselves ( and a partner, and a child) there are thousands who will try and fail and settle for their lot in life. However, those thousands who fail may be led to expect too much of themselves with the story presented in this game. 
Other fantasy games make clear that everything is taking place in a separate universe, whether by having outlandish personalities, over-the-top visuals, or outright stating the game is fantasy. However, this game treads too closely to reality, so an impressionable player might actually interpret the story in this game as a statement on how life works, which is very misleading. Please make it more apparent that this game is fantasy by adding outlandish elements.

[h2] 家政模拟器× 人生轨迹相册√[/h2]
游戏玩法非常简单，收拾整理房间，点点点把各类物品放在合适的地方【此处小小吐槽一下：为什么厨具一定要收进抽屉啦！我就想把它们放在我触手可及的地方不可以吗？放在架子上也不可以嘛！主创团队：是的，不可以哦^ ^】
但这就是这款游戏的全部吗？Nonono，正如游戏简介里所说，主创团队是在以“整理行李、打造舒适空间”的方式，间接地讲述”行李主人”（也就是本作没露脸的主角）的人生故事。是的，本作是有剧情的！以下内容涉及剧透↓↓↓
[spoiler] 主角是一名女性（行李中有月经用品和bras），曾经在超市or咖啡店（根据衣服里的绿色围裙推测）工作，故事末尾时的工作是儿童绘本画家（墙上的海报、很多本一模一样的绘本，应该是出版社寄来的样书）。她喜欢的颜色是紫色，爱好包括美术/足球/瑜伽/健身/旅行（各国纪念品）/DND（20？面骰）/电子游戏（且疑似任天堂铁粉）。会烤小饼干。 家庭成员包括父母和妹妹，小时候会和妹妹吵架。她曾经和两名大学同学合租，其中一名是女性coser（假毛+疑似是水手金星的cos服）。大学毕业后交往过男友，后来分手，之后交了亚裔女友。女友喜欢的颜色是红色，喜欢植物，从事影视行业（那两个黑白的小东西应该是对讲机？吧？加上玻璃相框里装裱起来的电影票）。故事的最后和女友一起买了双层住宅并有了一个孩子。（[/spoiler]
在故事的开头，主角只有一间卧室可供收拾；而在故事的最后，主角可以收拾一整栋小别墅的每个房间。空间的扩张也直观地反映了她的成长轨迹。

[h2] “无用”的细节 [/h2]
由于像素风+文化差异，有些物品不太容易辨认。然而根据Unpacking Wiki（放外部链接容易被锁评测，在此就不放了，感兴趣可自行搜索）以及讨论区内分析细节的帖子，每本书、每张卡带的封面都不是胡乱设计的，全是现实里真实存在的作品，而且几乎与本作中的年代完美对应（例如出现在2010年图的《飞屋环游记》&《阿凡达》DVD碟片，都是2009年的知名影片）。另外，随着时间推移，主角持有的设备也越来现代化了。不得不感慨主创团队的认真细心。

[h2] 没有标明“女性主角”，却处处体现女性视角 [/h2]
从1997年的房间布置，已经不难推测出故事的主角是一名女性了。而在后续的每一个场景里，主创团队都在不断强化这一设定。请不要误会，我的意思并不是“本作带有强烈的性别刻板印象”，恰恰相反，主角的爱好并不十分“女性化”，性格也不太符合传统刻板印象中的女性形象（可能是我过度解读，但早期她的搬家箱子真的很混乱hhh各种日用品混着放，【轻微剧透】[spoiler]在刚搬到属于自己的小房子时也没清理过窗台的积灰 [/spoiler]）。但玩家只要稍稍注重一些细节，就能很清晰地感知到：哦，这是以一位女性的视角展开的故事。
首先是值得被我大夸特夸的，行李中包含月经用品（卫生巾和卫生棉条)的设计。可能是我见识短浅，但这是我第一次在游戏里见到对月经的直接or间接刻画（苦笑.jpg）。非常生活化的设计，直接点明主角性别。
其次是一直陪伴主角的小猪玩偶。作为游戏封面，它的重要性不言而喻（笑）。我个人的猜测是，它的变化影射了主角自身的心态变化。一开始，它是一个系着红色领结的崭新玩偶；后来，红色蝴蝶结不翼而飞；再后来，它的身上有了破洞和缺口；之后，缺口被补好了；故事的最后，它系上了金色的丝带。这是否意味着，成长路上，怀着童心的主角曾经感到迷茫和痛苦，但最后奔向了属于她的幸福人生呢？
【以下剧透】
[spoiler] 然后是大家都懂的“不要靠近男人会变得不幸”环节。主角曾和男友同居，而这也是我玩得最不舒服的一节。不适感源于两点：1. 这个男人的房子并不小，却已经被他堆得满满当当，根本没有为即将入住的女友特意腾出一些空间。主角的心爱的画具和瑜伽垫无处安放，而主角还得收拾他乱堆的内裤和袜子:(；2. 主角非常珍视她的学位证书，大学毕业后的每次搬家都会带着，每次都可以骄傲地挂在墙上显眼的位置。然而，在男友家里，她竟然只能被迫将证书塞到床底。所幸最后分手了，但姐啊我觉得你只是把他的照片收进柜子里还是太温柔了，应该扔进马桶里冲掉然后触发一个新的成就^ ^ [/spoiler]
最后是一个不知道是不是主创团队的小巧思：在1997年的房间里，带锁的紫色小本子（日记本？）是可以藏在枕头下面的（不知道游戏机之类的可不可以）。天呐这简直就是少女の心思！
我相信主创团队中，一定存在拥有较高话语权的女性制作人，才可以做出如此细腻又舒适的作品。

[h2] 满是意外的全成就 [/h2]
本作的25个成就都是隐藏状态，因而无法从成就名称猜测其达成方式，在游玩途中也大概率不会抱着一些“完成任务”的心态去解锁成就（除非看攻略）。解锁非流程成就的方法非常有趣，可能只是好奇地用右键多点了几下，就猝不及防地跳出了成就，对成就党有激励作用，也让非成就党忍俊不禁（【剧透】[spoiler] 比如我只是好奇游戏机能不能打开，就多戳了几下，结果电视上出现了画面并跳了成就；只是单纯觉得玩偶在床上排排坐很可爱，把老虎和小猪放在了一起 ，又跳了成就[/spoiler]）。

[h2]总结：非常好小甜品，爱来自瓷器❤  [/h2]

VERY DISAPPOINTED!  I bought this for my 8 year old daughter who was VERY excited to get it. It was her first ever Steam game. She spent lots of time unpacking but in the end was extremely frustrated to the point of tears that the game would not let her save her world the way she wanted! TURNS OUT there are only pre-approved ways of setting up a room. It's not about setting it up YOUR WAY. It's about setting it up THERE WAY. For instance she wanted to put a boom-box on the floor but the game won't allow this. She set up the whole house but it wouldn't let her save it when she was done the way she wanted it. After hearing her crying, I asked her to show me the problem. she showed me. That took a bit of time. I requested a refund but Steam won't allow the refund because the time it took her to set up her house and find out she couldn't save it and then show me why she was crying, it took us over the 2 hour refund limit. The game is advertised as a game that lets you create a satisfying living space. But, not, apparently if you are 8 and want it set up your way.

游戏的剧情表达形式很新颖，用收纳互动代替文字邀请见证了女主人生几段最重要的回忆。
游玩过程像是做了个心灵spa，通过开箱子投放物品，像是拆盲盒，每次看到老朋友的瞬间都会很亲切~收纳过程是类似作画般的自由拼图，随性的有序摆放源源不断产生清单完成的解压感。几乎没有设置难度障碍，只在部分场景为了传递剧情信息做了些摆放限制。比如小卧室中没有容纳奖状的地方只能摆在床下，已经分手男友的合影不能钉在留言板上...生活就是这样，没那么慷慨给你珍视的东西全都都留个位置。
虽然讲的是别人的故事，却猝不及防被自己的回忆击中。和爷爷奶奶一起生活的老家小房间 自己独立的卧室 刚毕业合租的单间......再后来有了能容纳我所有杂物的家。 真好啊，谢谢! 祝所有人的生活，都有永远有一头小粉猪陪伴。

This is a good game, and I think it is very interesting... having said that, it was not for me. 

    Before I get to that, I want to get into what I love.  

       First, it should be noted that the protagonist is presented as female.... though I cannot confirm if that was the intent, it is coded to be that way. While there is nothing wrong with that on its face, it contributed to my difficulty in more personally connecting with the character.     That is the primary reason for why I didn't continue to play.   Though it did not speak to me personally, that does not mean that it is a bad game. 

      Second: Environmental storytelling at its finest.  Though many would find this to be a negative, I found the novel way in which the story was left for us to find, to be fascinating. I wasn't spoon-fed the contents of the story, rather, I was given subtle hints, Environmental clues and deduction were the primary way this interesting story came to me.... however, that brings me to one of two criticisms...

     The story is left too much up to interpretation. I felt that there was information to be gleamed, but did not get the sense that I was having a narrative slowly pieced together. While the snapshots we receive in the game are lovely, they feel too disconnected.  The glimpses it gave were interesting enough to catch my interest, but discovering they would never be fleshed out saddened me... 

       Ultimately, for the snapshots we were given, it was a tad too short, in my opinion....  

I hope the developer has a bright future ahead.

Cozy game about unpacking the moving boxes as we follow someone through different stages of their life, from 1997 to 2018. Unpack every box, place the items where you think they should go, and after all the boxes are unpacked and the misplaced items are highlighted in red/white, rearrange as needed. You can take photos of each room to get more of the player character's comments, and lock in your favorite before moving on to the next stage. Can be time-consuming if you're a bit of a perfectionist, but super satisfying when you get the option to watch back your tidying of each stage sped up once it's completed. 

It's really interesting to see what items the character holds onto as the years go by, which get worn with age and/or later fixed up, and which were set aside as the character grew out of them. You can tell a lot about a person by what items they keep, set in a place of importance, or tuck away in the nooks and crannies of a place. You can also tell a lot by how much or as little space someone makes for the player character and vise versa when you cohabitate. I felt uneasy for the player character during one difficult stage, and then later excited as I realized by their office that their career was picking up by the clues in the room. It's surprisingly easy to get attached considering we never really see their face in detail.

[h3] Unpacking [/h3]

[u]Gameplay:[/u] 7/10
- This game's premise is super unique. I've seen "sorting" type games before, but what Unpacking offers is novel in the best ways. You unpack boxes full of household items and place them where you think they belong. There are a handful of levels with hundreds of items to unpack, so it can get a little repetitive. However, the game introduces new and unique items every so often, and the environments differ enough to keep the player engaged with the story. Speaking of...

[u]Story:[/u] 7/10
- The story isn't anything revolutionary. If you're not paying attention, it would be hard to notice that it's even there. However, the game drops subtle hints through what you're unpacking and where so you could piece together some sort of story. I won't drop any spoilers, but it's a cute and simple story with it's ups and downs and ties it up nice conclusion.

[u]Graphics:[/u] 8/10
- The graphics are super charming. It feels like a modernized version of an old, pixelated isometric city builder game, but zoomed into only a handful of rooms. The colors are charming and, despite the low resolution, you can tell what (most) items are.

[u]Sound Design/Soundtrack:[/u] 9/10
- The soundtrack is bit-crushed, but phenomenal. van Dyck did a wonderful job making a super cute, retro soundtrack that accompanies the graphics well. The only small complaint I have with it is that it can get grating after a while if you're on the same level, and some songs are reused across levels. (There are some radio easter eggs too, if you're looking for some different music).

[u]Replay Value:[/u] 7/10
- Given the very simple story and gameplay, this game can be replayable, but it's hard to re-live that magic after the first playthrough. There are only ~5 levels with no differing unpacking items or rooms, so after maybe 2-3 playthroughs you've seen almost all you could see. There are some easter eggs and hard-to-get achievements that can stretch out that time, but after that you've milked the game completely dry. If there was some level builder, or maybe even a DLC, or more Unpacking content in general, I think that could help.

Overall, it's a very pleasant, cute game with a soundtrack to fit. It's perfect to pop open after a long day and unwind with virtual moving. I wish there was more content and variety of content, especially to justify the $20 price tag, but it's a good experience.

While I did like the graphics, if it had the drawn/painted art feel that it has on a title art, not only would it have fit the storyline, but it would have looked amazing, too. The game starts off very therapeutic, with you putting things away in one small room, with plenty of opportunities to organize your own way and make it look really nice. That does not continue for long, and I began to just plop a lot of things on the floor and wait for the "wrong" outline to pop up before I haphazardly placed things in the right spot. For the final level, my second favorite (behind the first one), there were ten rooms and tons of boxes to unpack. However, this time, there was enough space for me to be able to organize well again, which is where the game gets its fun from— you organize in your right way, but sometimes it's annoying when the game tells you that "you can't put something there." One issue I have is that some of the items are hard to tell what they are, and the game doesn't tell you either. The thing that was done really well was the UI. Your album is your save, and navigating it and photo mode are very easy. Everything within is simple to navigate, which makes the game far less stressful.

"Unpacking" is a relaxing puzzle game where you organize and unpack after moving in homes at varying stages of life. The game has you put away various items whether it be regular things like clothes, toiletries, or cookware or even storytelling items like plushies, photos, and hobby related items. You essentially grow up with the off-screen main character and watch how they change in life! The game wants you to place items in specific places, but you can enter a mode that lets you place items anywhere you would like as well. A good purchase for those that enjoy puzzles and decorating!

Unpacking is a game that I love coming back to as a comfort game, Outside of the freedom to decorate how I like while also following few restrictions, the story-line is what I come back for. I feel as if each time I play this, I see different things and make new connections across the album entries. Watching this character grow up over and over also lets me see these things, I change where I put things based on what story points I'm getting from this new run. 

I feel there is something very cozy being able to watch this character grow up, live life and find happiness in ways I know others feel. The graphics and items chosen for the game work so well together, it makes even the mundane items of life like paper towels and hangers seem cozy and comforting. Part of me wishes I could follow the story more, see where else life takes our character but the other side of me sees the positive of leaving the story right when their life is about to really start.

[h1] 물건에는 주인의 인생이 깃든다 [/h1]

이사를 온 집에서 짐정리 하는 게임입니다.
특별한 기믹이나 요소 없이 그저 방에서 짐을 풀며 나오는 물건들을 제자리에 배치하기만 하면 되는 간단한 게임입니다.

짐정리를 하면서 주인공의 인생을 단편적으로나마 따라가며 지켜보는 재미가 있습니다,
어릴때부터 사용한 물건들이 세월이 지나면서 조금씩 해지거나 깨진듯한 디테일이 소소하게 공감되어 다가오는것이 정말 매력적입니다. 
가끔 느닷없이 제자리가 아닌듯한 위치에 짐을 놓는 경우가 있는데 이것 또한 곱씹어 생각해보면 왜 여기에 두는것인지 이해가 되고 그 이유때문에 형용할 수 없는 기분이 들고 씁쓸함을 느끼기도 합니다.

스크립트도 없으며 주인공의 얼굴을 게임중에 단 한번도 볼 수 없음에도 주인공이 어떤 인간인지, 취향은 어떠한지, 좋아하는것은 무엇인지 알 수 있었던게 정말로 신기한 경험이었습니다.

삽입곡과 효과음 등으로 힐링하면서 시간 보내기에 정말 좋은 게임입니다,
게임 볼륨 대비 가격이 저렴한편은 아니므로 개인적으론 할인 할 때에 구입하시는걸 추천드립니다.

非常好的像素小游戏，在摆设家具的过程中和风细雨地描述了一个女性的一生。相比起直接用长篇小作文或者小剧场告知你她所经历的故事，这种无言却又像徐徐道来的感觉，更让人在游玩时如同相识许久的老友一般，对眼的时候就默契一笑。其中很多互动也很有意思，例如说摇一摇都会发出水声的暖水袋，又或者碟碗放置在不同材质的平面上会产生不同音效（这游戏的音效做得很细节我很喜欢）。

当然缺点也不是没有，首先是这个体量原价售卖70元，还是稍显昂贵了， 打折后入手倒是不错。
另外因为像素画的原因，部分体积小的物品尤为抽象，只能凭借联想或者瞎蒙去判断这究竟是什么玩意[strike] 例如换大房子的时候多了三个一个单位的爱心星星啥的图案，当时我摸不着头脑这究竟是什么东西啊只能全塞厨房抽屉，结果通过看评论区才发现你吗原来是冰箱贴，太他吗抽象了吧！ [/strike]

[strike] 另外就是那个，我诚挚建议外国友人们，无论房间多小都买个鞋柜吧。当我发现外出的鞋只能放衣柜或者床底时不由得发出了尖锐爆鸣声 [/strike]

From my understanding, you help a youth girl unpack her belongings for each stage in her life. You start off unpacking her childhood room, then you move on to a college dorm, and so on (trying not too spoil too much). Each round of the game is a few years in the future, where you notice small changes in her belongings that tell her story - wear and tear of childhood items, change in hobbies and interests, gain and loss of relationships, and so on. 

As a bonus, I loved the decorating part of the game and having the choice of where things go, it was relaxing. As you unpacked more and more items, you had to re-evaluate and make changes so everything could fit. Then you have the hidden achievements that pop up like a scavenger hunt. The music was calming and the sound effects were satisfying too

I would recommend!

If you have [b]a pathological need for organization[/b], maybe with an aesthetic flair, this game is for you. Here you can setup and decorate several homes with loads of items and [i]without[/i] having to pay back any loans to raccoons. There [i]is[/i] a story told here - you unpack the many moves in a young woman's life over the course of a few decades - and you'll piece it together all while listening to a fantastic, mood-filled soundtrack. (I wish the story aspect had a bit more "meat" to it, but that didn't detract from my enjoyment of the overall experience.) Each residence is full of expertly crafted pixel art of everything from a Rubik's cube to a Wii and many of these items are interactive. This makes hunting for "stickers" (achievements) rewarding. I managed to get 100% after about 16 hours of play, which makes it definitely worth the $20 (and a sale price even better).

ALE. jak dla mnie gra jest bardziej stresująca niż odprężająca. podchodząc do tej gry nie wiedziałam, że będziemy towarzyszyć podczas przeprowadzek jednej i tej samej osobie i choć pomysł jest świetny, to jednak wolałabym zobaczyć różne osobowości podczas odpakowywania. np. poziom gdzie wprowadzamy się do chłopaka, jego styl mieszkania jest bardzo minimalistyczny i harmonijny, fajnie by było móc pomóc wprowadzić się komuś takiemu, móc poznawać ludzi o różnych gustach. zamiast tego śledzimy życie tej samej osoby i z jednej strony jest to czarujące, widząc te same przedmioty i to jak oddziałuje na nie czas, a z drugiej ile razy mogę segregować te same majtki. w dodatku (jak dla mnie) zamiast zżyć się z bohaterką, miałam jej już dość. to ile gratów musiałam rozstawiać zaczęło mnie stresować zamiast relaksować, męczyło mnie to "upychanie" przedmiotów po szafkach, coś w tym jest z prawdziwego życia, ale nie po to chciałam w to zagrać. w pewnym momencie zaczęło mnie denerwować to ile szkicowników lub pluszaków muszę umieszczać, jedna wielka graciarnia. nie przeszkadzałoby mi to aż tak, gdyby nie to, że każdy poziom wygląda tak samo (bo dotyczy tej samej osoby!!!). fajnie jest domyślać się jak obecnie układa się życie naszej bohaterki, ale przyjemniej by było móc poznawać historię różnych osób, ale to natomiast wiązałoby się z większą ilością przedmiotów do stworzenia, także rozumiem ten wybór.

ogólnie gra ma swój urok, ale nie polecam perfekcjonistom, bo z taką ilością pstrokatych gratów ciężko mieć jakąś satysfakcje z ich ułożenia

[h1] A life story disguised inside a tetris-like game [/h1]

It's hard to define this game but it's a mix between a life story, tetris, Sims and puzzle game.
You open cupboard boxes full of objects and have to put them in specific places. You can obviously put everything on the ground but to clear a level, the items needs to be put in its logical place which means a magnet on the fridge or clothes in a cupboard.

The game is not difficult at all. Some items are hard to place but once you find their place it makes sense and is satisfying. You can only progress to the next place to unpack once everything is in its adequate place but the game clearly indicates what would be wrongly placed.
The hardest part is getting some optional stickers which requires some deduction skills.

The art is really good and only a few times I was left perplexed and clueless regarding an object (but managed to place it correctly in the end). The music is also good and fits perfectly the game.

The best part of this game is actually being attached to some of the items and seeing the life story of the main person as you unpack across various places as she gets older.
You will see how that person grows, gets friends, gets new hobbies, work, gets rewarded and even more personal stuff.
It's really well done and some key moments of her life is told in a very intelligent manner which i won't spoil but if you also unpack often, you will understand it!

I recommend this game for every fan of puzzle, easy life story games. It's a nice concept and the satisfaction of organizing a house is always good, especially how easy it is compared to real life!
It's a bit short though, you could easily finish it in 4-5 hours, finding all the achievements makes it a bit longer so some people would wait for a sale, I guess.

Eu amei esse jogo! É bem tranquilo e gostoso de jogar. A trilha sonora e a arte do jogo são muito fofinhas e ajudam a te deixar na vibe certa de arrumar as coisas sem se frustar ou cansar. Uma das melhores partes pra mim é conhecer a personagem principal por meio dos pequenos detalhes sobre a vida dela que descobrimos a cada mudança, enquanto abrindo as caixas. Eu não tive problemas ao tentar encaixar os objetos no lugar certo porque isso é bem fluído e natural, então apesar de ser um puzzle game não é frustante em momento algum. O único ponto que esse jogo me incomoda é o preço em relação à duração do jogo. [h1]This game reminds me of why I love video games[/h1]

Unpacking tells a brief story about a person growing up and experiencing life through the years and this story is told only through the environments you visit and the items you unpack. So much exposition is given through the objects in this game that tell you about the personality and hobbies of the protagonist and I found myself quite attached to them by the end of the game.

Another highlight of this game for me is the sound/foley design. Each object has a distinct sound when you move it around and place them on different surfaces, which really adds to the substance of the world and makes it feel very physical and solid.

It's a very short game, with my play-time clocking in at 3 hours, and while I'm personally happy to pay the $29AUD price tag, I can understand how it may be a stretch for some people.

Потому что всё, что нужно делать в этой игре - распаковывать бесконечное множество коробок с вещами и расставлять их по местам в разные комнаты, что невероятно залипательно и расслабляюще. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3172941594 Сюжета, как такового, здесь нет, но вещи и обстановка в доме на самом деле могут многое рассказать о человеке, его интересах, предпочтениях и даже событиях в жизни. Такой жизненный сюжет без сюжета, повествование без слов.
Игра именно про распаковку и расстановку, а не про дизайн: здесь не предполагается кастомизация предметов на свой вкус, а расставить вещи куда попало не получится, в конце они будут подсвечиваться красным, не позволяя перейти к следующему периоду жизни.

I bought this game a while ago but never got around to finishing it. My recent development reminded me of it so I revisited it. It turned out to be surprisingly helpful and therapeutic at the same time. Gonna be one of those casual, relaxing games that I'll always recommend.

[h1] Unpacking -  милая инди игра о лесбиянках и ОКР. .[/h1]

Игра рекомендована к ознакомлению, суть игры помочь главной героине с переездом. Причем с несколькими и в разных масштабах. Сначала у героини появляется своя комната, затем она взрослеет, идет в универ, встречает свою первую любовь, возвращается в родные края и встречает свою судьбу. И в каждый момент времени и места с нами переезжают наши вещи, новый хлам и новые увлеченья. 

Геймплей сводится к простому, достаем предмет из коробки и ставим его туда, где он будет уместен. Иногда в коробке в одной комнате, может по ошибке затесаться предмет из другой комнаты. Некоторые объекты интерактивны, например консоль можно включить, плакат повесить, кубик рубика собрать…

Атмосфера у игры приятная. Игра медитативная, выполнена в приятной рисовке и на фоне играет расслабляющая музыка.

Сюжет в игре не дается явно и в лоб. Мы можем только догадываться и строить теории по предметам интерьера и увлечений главной героини. То она внезапно начинает заниматься футболом, то бросает это дело и находит страсть в рисовании. И знаете, за этим действительно приятно следить.

Как вывод, игра дешевая, но атмосферная и увлекательная. Реиграбельности нет, проходится за 2-3 часа, а платину можно выбить с первого раза если смотреть гайды. Поддержка геймпада полная. Отпугнуть может только повесточка в конце игры, но если Вас это не напрягает, то вы получите удовольствие от прохождения.

[h1]Описание:[/h1]
"Распкоуука".  Долго ждал эту игру в своей библиотеке и нет предела моему разочарованию. Мы играем за телочку и ее крайне короткие этапы жизни связанные с переездом. Мы распаковываем коробки и расставляем предметы по квартире/дому. Когда все поставим как хотим игра нам показывает какие предметы мы поставили не туда и мы занимаемся перестановкой. В игре великолепный саундтрек, но что за пауза млиять после его окончания? Саунд отыграл и минута тишины!. Крайне мало предметов в плане асортимента, мы играем за бабу бомжа? 8 тарелок возит с собой 20 лет и не бьет... Некоторые предметы я так и не понял вообще что такое и с чем едят... If you absolutely want to "play" this game, here's what you can do instead: Take a screenshot of a house from the internet, download some images of any items you want, and place them using MS Paint or Krita. Not only it will give you the exact same gameplay, it will also be 100% free (instead of this overpriced product) and will allow you to really customise it however you want.

Don't trust some of the reviews that say "You can place anything however you like". This is completely false, and you can only place items at a very specific place. You can't even place the Cookie Jar on your own desk, it HAS to be on the kitchen's shelf. 

They can't even get the music to properly loop, that's how lazy and boring it gets. You just drag'n'drop with your mouse, with absolutely no sound nor music playing for a solid minute. It's truly sad that a "game" like this is at 93% positive reviews. 

And of course, don't forget the "subtle" woke messaging in it. Can't have a simple cute pixel art without some form of alphabet-soup mixed into it and left-leaning propaganda.

This is genuinely one of the most relaxing games I've ever played.  It is so satisfying starting with a blank room and putting everything in its place.  There's a lot of freedom to put things where you want, though my only complaint is that there are a few restricted placements that don't make much sense to me, though they are few and far between.  It was fun to watch items come back time and time again in new places and new years, sometimes sad to see some not make the cut.  However I beamed when a few things turned up late in the story that had seemingly disappeared earlier... amazing how this game managed to make me excited to see little objects like that, but I truly got attached to some of the items!

The storytelling was far more than I expected, considering you're just putting things away, but there is a definite, obvious story that unfolds as you move through the years and the different homes, as long as you're paying attention.  Not going to lie, I had a big smile on my face all throughout the last level, and I may have teared up a little at the very end.

My biggest wish is that this game was longer!!  It only took me 4 hours to play through the whole game once and get half of the stickers (rewards for doing certain actions), and I wasn't rushing.   This game has so much potential for sequels or DLC, like playing through new character's stories, new items, etc.  There could be a follow up after the end of this story, maybe ten years in the future or something, as well.  I was very disappointed to google it and read that the company isn't in a rush to release a sequel... I just really hope they do revisit it one day.

Anyway even though the game is quite short I think it's worth the money, and you can go back and play it again (there's 3 save slots) to try to get all the stickers/achievements, and try different placements for things.  I really loved it.  If you like zen games, if you like organizing things, if you like subtle but sweet storytelling... I highly recommend.  Just wait for a sale if you don't want to pay full price for the short game time.

День выдался очень длинным, насыщенным и тяжелым, поэтому когда я заходила в эту игру, мысль была только одна: "расслабиться". Это было ошибкой.
Играть начала с зеленого альбома. На момент написания отзыва я не знаю, есть ли какая-то разница или нет, просто если есть возможность выбрать, значит, не особо.

На первых десяти минутах игра правда была расслабляющей: спокойно ставишь вещички на полку, на стол, открываешь шкафчики и местишь предметы туда, куда посчитаешь нужным. А потом тебе выпадает книга. Ты ставишь ее, например, на полку, после рядом ставишь фигурку, копилку, а после выпадает еще одна книга. А потом еще, и еще, и еще... И куда теперь ставить этот набор юного библиотекаря одному разрабу известно. Я сама любитель книг, но ведь в комнатах, в которых ПО ИДЕЕ они должны стоять просто не хватает места. И в итоге ты уже просто куда угодно ставишь эти книги, двигаешь фигурки, теряешь композицию за ради того, чтобы очередная коробка дала тебе книгу, на которой уже и на полке рядом с другими места нет. Приходится оставлять ее на столе. 

Почему я написала "ПО ИДЕЕ"? да потому что ты не можешь положить книгу, например, на кухне, даже при всем желании, если игра сама не предусмотрела это на уровне. Да-да, игра - распаковка. Ставь предметы туда, куда ты хочешь, НО если они не вписываются туда по мнению игры, после распаковки всех коробок предмет загорится красным, пока ты не уберешь его на то место, которое за ранее предусмотрено.

Условные фотографии на разных уровнях игра расставляет по-разному. Где-то можно просто положить их на самую дальнюю полку, где-то обязательно повесить. Вот в спальне весит доска, на нее вешаются все фотографии, а вот эта одна, ОПРЕДЕЛЕННАЯ, загорится на этой доске красным, пока ты не положишь ее в шкаф с настольными играми. Кто-то скажет: "Это такой сюжет комнаты, это фото напоминает о плохих событиях, поэтому гг убирает его в шкаф" или "гг эти друзья напоминают веселое времяпровождение, поэтому и положила ближе к играм", я не знаю, предполагаю. Круто, очень мило, но только не тогда, когда из-за этого куска бумаги нужно передвинуть десяток вещей, чтоб он поместился туда. На этом же уровне из-за переполненности вещей свитер улетел под кровать. 

Переполненность. Дается квадрат комнаты, а вещей, особенно книг, дают так много, будто переезжали из особняка. Вот сюжет одного уровня (как я его поняла): два человека съезжаются вместе - девушка переезжает к парню, и вот через комнаты показывают, что парень перфекционист. Даже трусы через клетку лежат. Ну и вот по логике для комфорта хотелось бы сохранить его идеал, вот только опять проблемы: книг дофига, так что фигурки приходится двигать и сбивать порядок, в шкафу вещи сложить хоть как-нибудь, лишь бы все вместились, но вот опус магнум этого уровня - это диплом. Или что это, грамота в рамке, неважно. Я ну очень долго искала, куда его можно повесить. Там, где у гг висят картины, подвинуть их и повесить его нельзя, на полки он не вмещается, доступных стен больше нет. Может, в сообществе помогут? Да, вот ответ: "Я просто засунул его под кровать, лол". Да... Круто, вот это геймплей. И ЧТО САМОЕ СТРАННОЕ ЭТО ТО, ЧТО ИГРА СЧИТАЕТ ЭТО МЕСТО ВПОЛНЕ СЕБЕ ПОДХОДЯЩИМ ДЛЯ ДИПЛОМА, А ВОТ РАНДОМНАЯ КНИГА ОПЯТЬ ЗАГОРИТСЯ КРАСНЫМ, ПОТОМУ ЧТО НУ ВОТ НАДО ТАК.

Я не закончила. Рай для перфекционистов: лифчиков дают 6-7, шкаф рассчитан на 5. И вот клади один боком и дай своему глазу дергаться. Тампоны ты можешь засунуть в ящик, а вот прокладки туда уже не вместятся. И вот гигиена, что по идее часто лежит в одном месте, вынуждена делиться по разным частям. Понятное дело, что можно найти другое место в шкафу, другие полки и тд, но почему я должна находить другое место для этих вещей, если по моему взгляду они должны находится там. Тем более, что в шкафу специально делают два маленьких ящичка для лифтонов и трусов.
Овощечистка не может лежать рядом с ложками, а вот масло среди кастрюль и посуды вместилось как свое. Ну, потому что на тех уровнях, которые я успела пройти, холодос чисто аксессуар и не открывается.

Я выговорилась, не хотела писать негативный отзыв, тем более, что это мой первый комментарий. Но высказаться очень хотелось, так как игра на первый взгляд зацепила, милая и расслабляющая. По отзывам в стиме большинству она нравится, но разделить этот позитив я не могу.
